| **⚠ Two false-positive classes the first run produced, both excluded with the reason stated** | **(a)** `classpath*:` reaches `target/test-classes`, so a fixture (`StrongPasswordValidatorTest$Holder`) was reported; its constraint *is* enforced, by a programmatic `Validator` in the test that owns it. **(b)** **JPA entities.** `spring-boot-starter-validation` puts a provider on the classpath and the JPA validation mode defaults to `AUTO`, so Hibernate's `BeanValidationEventListener` validates on pre-insert/pre-update — a constraint on an entity field is **not** inert, it fires at flush. Conflating the two would have overstated this finding by six sites. It is still worth knowing: it fires as a `ConstraintViolationException` → **500**, so the caller is told "server error" about their own malformed input. Reported separately as **5 entity-at-flush** sites, not as findings. |
| **The confirmed instance** | `CalendarEventDto` declared `@Pattern(regexp = "NONE\|DAILY\|WEEKLY\|MONTHLY\|QUARTERLY\|ANNUAL")` on `recurrence`. That class is the **outbound** payload, built by `fromEntity()`; both endpoints bind the nested `CalendarEventDto.CreateRequest`, whose `recurrence` had no annotation. Bean validation runs only against a parameter marked `@Valid`, so the constraint enforced nothing — while reading exactly like the guard a reviewer was looking for. Fixed under F2-182 by deleting it and putting the vocabulary in the service. |
| **⚠⚠ Why this is filed and not swept: my scan was wrong and I am saying so rather than shipping its number** | A tree-wide scan for "declares a validation annotation, never appears as a `@RequestBody`" reported **75 types**. The first one checked — `AsmDtos.FindingRequest` — **is** bound and **is** validated: the scan attributed annotations on nested records to their *container* class (`AsmDtos`), because its brace-depth walk did not track the innermost declared type through a multi-line record header. So the 75 is meaningless and is **not** recorded as a population anywhere. 🔑 **Third instance in three findings of a regex over Java reporting a large phantom number** — F2-170's 1,763 endpoints from a javadoc sentence, F2-179's 0-of-389 from `\b=\b`, this. |
| **⚠⚠ The worst instance: the only route that creates a sanctions entry validated none of its fields** | `SanctionsDtos.EntryBulkImportRequest.entries` was `@NotNull` but **not `@Valid`**, and `EntryCreateRequest` is bound **only** through that bulk path — there is no single-entry create endpoint. So on the sole route that creates sanctions entries, none of `@NotBlank entryExternalId`, `@NotBlank primaryNameEn`, `@Pattern entityType` or `@Pattern severity` ran. `SanctionsListService.bulkImportEntries` is a straight setter copy whose only guard is `assertWritable` (tenancy, not fields), and `aml.sanctions_list_entry` has **zero CHECK constraints** — so those two `@Pattern`s were the *only* thing narrowing `entity_type` and `severity`. An entry with an empty `primaryNameEn` passes NOT NULL, is stored, and **never matches a screening query — a sanctioned party that is not flagged**. Probed live: blank name, lower-case `individual`, null external id and an out-of-vocabulary severity now each answer **400 naming the nested path**; all four previously stored a row. |
| **⚙ And it closed a second defect for free, which is why the boundary is the right place** | `bulkImportEntries` skips duplicates via `existsByListIdAndEntryExternalIdAndIsDeletedFalse(...)`. With a **null** external id that compiles to `= NULL`, which is never true in SQL — so every null-id entry was **created rather than skipped, on every re-import**. Refusing null at the boundary makes that query unreachable. 🔑 **A defect that only manifests on input the boundary should have refused is fixed by fixing the boundary; adding a null check in the service would have left the unnamed-entry row.** |
| **The other four cascade repairs, each with its consequence stated at its real size** | `BiaQuantitativeRequest.lossLines` — `time_band`/`loss_type`/`confidence` have no CHECKs either, so the `@Pattern`s were the only vocabulary guard, and `@PositiveOrZero` on `amountSar` never ran. · `TabularExportRequest.sheets` — the 20-**sheet** cap ran; `Sheet`'s own `@Size(max = 50_000)` on `rows` did not, so a caller could post 20 sheets of unbounded rows into an in-memory POI workbook. **A DoS control, not a cosmetic check.** · `AttendanceRequest.marks` — `guestName`'s `@Size(255)` equals `member_name` exactly, so enforcing it converts a truncation 500 into a named 400. · `MatrixUpdateRequest.grants` — ⚠ **not** an authorisation bypass, and the row says so: `putMatrix` already rejected an unresolvable pair with a 400, so the guard was in the service (F2-182's lesson, a third time). What the missing cascade cost is the **diagnostic** — a `null` module reached `g.module().toUpperCase()` and answered **500 NPE**. |
| **🔑 The rule that came out of it, and it is not "add @Valid everywhere"** | A dormant `@Size` **number has never been tested against its column**, so switching it on is a decision, not a repair. Three outcomes: cap **equals** the column length → enable, since the DB already refuses more and this only converts a 500 into a 400 (cannot break a working request); column is **NVARCHAR(MAX)** → the schema deliberately leaves the field unbounded, so enabling **imposes a limit nobody chose**; cap **looser** than the column → enabling protects nothing and the annotation is the thing that is wrong. Measured per site: `coi_note` is MAX, so `AttendanceMark`'s `@Size(1000)` was **deleted rather than enabled** — a cap on a conflict-of-interest declaration is a product change. This is the third variant of one question in this program: [[F2-179]] asked it per field, [[F2-182]] answered it with *does a coercion already exist upstream*, F2-184 answers it with *does anything already refuse this*. |
| **⚙ Why enabling the five cascades broke nothing** | Every enabled constraint was checked against stored data first: all 15 `sanctions_list_entry` rows hold in-vocabulary `entity_type` and `severity`; all 40 loss lines hold in-vocabulary `time_band`/`loss_type`/`confidence` and **0** negative amounts (min 0.00); every `@Size` cap equals its column. So the fix is **latent-defect closure, not a behaviour change** — stated with the query behind it rather than asserted. |
| **⚠ The three deletions, and the one that indicts my own previous slice** | `CalendarEventDto` still carried `@NotBlank` on `source`/`titleEn`/`eventType` and `@NotNull` on `startsAt` — **four more inert constraints on the very class [[F2-182]] had already edited**, sitting directly above the comment F2-182 wrote explaining why it deleted the fifth. 🔑 **Fixing the instance you noticed is not the same as closing the shape, and a class you have already edited reads as one you have already checked.** That is the entire justification for building the instrument instead of trusting the read. · `CommitteeDtos.AttendeeRow` — its own javadoc says *"Output only"*; the constraints are leftovers from when it **was** the input shape, and outlived the demotion. · `PushSubscriptionDtos.DispatchPayload` — an internal service parameter, never bound; its sibling `SubscribeRequest` has identical-looking annotations that are real, which is exactly what makes the inert ones misleading. |
| **⚠⚠ Two of the twelve remaining are not annotation problems at all — they are dark code** | `WhistleblowerDtos.RetaliationTransitionRequest`'s only consumer, `WhistleblowerRetaliationService#transitionTo`, has **no caller anywhere**: the retaliation terminal transition (`VALIDATED`/`UPHELD`/`DISMISSED`) has **no endpoint**, so a retaliation complaint's lifecycle cannot be closed through the API. `VendorBcpAttestationDtos.EscalateRequest` has no usage at all. Deleting their constraints would have *hidden* both. 🔑 **An inert constraint on a `*Request` type is a fingerprint of a dark endpoint** — this scan found from a new angle what [[F2-165]]'s reachability instrument measures directly. Filed as **[[F2-185]]**(a); the fix is to wire the endpoint or delete the dead path, and both are scope decisions rather than repairs. |
| **Gates** | `InertValidationConstraintTest` (1) — the instrument: reflection over 2,941 types, with the tolerated set held as a **named map with a reason per entry, enforced in BOTH directions** so an entry that gets fixed must be removed in the same commit. A decrease-only count of "12" would let a new inert constraint be swapped in for a fixed one, which is the failure CLAUDE.md records for `BARE_EXPORT_CEILING`. Four anti-vacuity legs, two of which prove the *detectors* rather than the population: if the constraint detector breaks, everything looks unconstrained and the test passes over a platform full of inert annotations; if the validation walk breaks, everything looks inert and the failure is noise. Neither half can be trusted from the other's number. · `NestedRequestCascadeTest` (15) — behaviour through a real `Validator`, because the whole finding is that an annotation's *presence* proves nothing about its *effect*; a test asserting "the field carries `@Valid`" would repeat the mistake it checks for. Includes the negative control that a valid bulk import still succeeds, and the deliberate non-refusal of a 5,000-character COI note. |
| **Mutation** | **16/16 caught.** All five cascades removed again; the deliberately-deleted `coiNote` cap put back; an inert constraint re-added to each of the three deleted sites; a real entry dropped from `TOLERATED` and a stale one left in it (both directions of the gate); and **six mutations against the instrument itself** — the entity exclusion, the test-classes exclusion, the `@Valid` cascade walk, the constraint detector, the body-binding walk, and **the phantom-75 bug itself** (attributing a nested type's constraints to its container). The last one matters most: it is the specific defect that made this finding a filing instead of a sweep, and the instrument now fails if it returns. |
| **Live probe (37/37)** | Backend from the freshly built jar on :8084; prod :8090 (PID 6888) untouched throughout. Identity **`compliance`** (GRC_ADMINISTRATOR — real AML WRITE + MANAGE_LISTS, BCM WRITE, IAM WRITE), not `admin`. **A (13):** every dev sanctions list is `organisation_id NULL` — a platform-global OFAC/UN/EU list that `assertWritable` deliberately refuses to a tenant officer ("visible is not writable"), so the probe **created a list this persona owns** and deleted it after; four refusals each naming the nested path, `entries[1].primaryNameEn` among them; **0 rows written by any refusal**; then the negative control — a valid 2-entry import returns `created: 2`, both rows byte-exact under `Latin1_General_100_BIN2`, Arabic names round-tripped. **B (5):** `3d` timeBand, a negative amount and a lower-case `confidence` each 400, and no assessment created. **C (4):** `null` module → **400 naming `grants[1].module`**, where it used to be a 500, with grant count unchanged at 47. **D (2):** a 256-character `guestName` → 400. **E (4):** 50,001 rows → 400 naming `sheets[0].rows`; a normal export still returns a real 3,625-byte workbook. **F (4):** the calendar and the quorum view still serialise after their constraints were deleted. **G (5):** cleanup by the id captured at creation plus a `CHARINDEX` belt, `aml.sanctions_list_entry` back to its 15-row baseline as a **failing** leg, and an anti-vacuity leg proving the probe created rows at all. |
| **⚙ Five probe bugs, all mine, and one of them the exact failure I would flag in someone else's harness** | `bcm.business_processes` is `bcm.critical_processes` · the calendar path is `/api/v1/calendar/events`, not `/api/v1/platform/...` · `AttendeeRow` is served by `GET …/quorum`, not by a GET on the POST-only attendance path · `GET /events` is guarded by `PLATFORM:READ` which `compliance` lacks, so that **one** leg uses `admin` and says why (it tests serialisation, not authorisation, so the bypass is irrelevant) · and **section C printed nothing at all**, because it filtered for `organisation_id = 1` when all 69 dev roles are `NULL`. 🔑 **A silent skip in a harness reads exactly like a section that passed.** It now has a leg that fails if it cannot find a role — and the section needed no owned role anyway, because `@Valid` fires before `@PreAuthorize`. |
| **⚙ Deliberately not probed positively, and why** | `PUT …/matrix` **clears and replaces** a role's permissions, and `POST …/attendance` writes a real meeting's roster. Both ran refusal legs only. House rule 6 — destructive DB operations need the user's explicit OK — and the refusal legs are the ones under test, since `@Valid` rejects before either service runs. |
| **Effort** | M (1 new instrument + 1 behaviour class, 5 cascades restored, 9 inert constraints deleted across 3 types, 16 mutations, 37 probe legs, **0 migrations, 0 frontend change**) |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-11.** Inert constraints **20 → 12**, every remaining one named with a reason and gated in both directions. Backend suite **3,687/0/0**, FE **487/487** + `tsc` clean (0 frontend files touched), mutation **16/16**, live probe **37/37**, `mvn -o clean package` hermetic. Filed on the way out: **[[F2-185]]** — (a) the two dark types, (b) the ten `@Size` caps whose columns still need comparing, with the enable/tighten/delete rule and the measurements already taken. ⚠ **(b) shipped the same day as [[F2-185b]] and three of the measurements recorded here were wrong** — two caps were 8000 not 1000, `archive_reason_en` was an exact match rather than the looser-than-column case this row predicted, and the two "unconfirmed" columns exist under names the field search missed. The measurements were the least-verified thing in the filing, which is why F2-185b's deliverable is a gate rather than a corrected table. |

## F2-185 · The two request types F2-184 could not fix by annotation: nothing reaches them

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-185 *(filed 2026-08-11 as the explicitly-tolerated residue of [[F2-184]]. **Scope narrowed twice**: the ten `@Size` caps became [[F2-185b]] the same day; the retaliation half was **worked and resolved 2026-08-11** and its claim here was refuted. What remains open is the vendor-BCP escalation.)* |
| **Module** | `ethics/whistleblower` *(resolved)*, `tprm/bcp_attestation` *(open)* |
| **Category** | unreachable server capability — the [[F2-165]] family, found from a different angle |
| **Severity** | ~~P2~~ → **P4 for the retaliation half (dead code), P3 for the vendor-BCP half.** See the correction below: the P2 rested on a sentence that is false. |
| **⚠⚠ The severity was wrong because the claim was false, and a live probe settled it** | This row said *"a retaliation complaint cannot be closed through the API at all — a missing statutory capability"*. **It can.** `POST /retaliation/{id}/validate`, `/uphold` and `/dismiss` all exist, are guarded `hasPermission('ETHICS','PROTECT')`, and `WhistleblowerRetaliationPage.tsx` renders a button for each. Probed live 20/20: `RECEIVED → VALIDATED → UPHELD` and `RECEIVED → DISMISSED` both complete, the protector is stamped from the caller, an illegal jump still 409s, and `ranalyst` gets 403. 🔑 **A dark method is not automatically a missing capability** — and the second time in two slices that a filing was right about the code and wrong about the consequence ([[F2-183]] was the first, one day earlier). |
| **⚠ How the wrong claim was written** | By reading `WhistleblowerRetaliationService` and not `WhistleblowerRetaliationController` beside it. The service holds four transition entry points; three are wired and one is not, and the one that is not is the *generic* one. Reading only the service, "the terminal transition has no endpoint" is a natural inference. 🔑 **One file short is the whole error** — the same shape as [[F2-179]]'s "`ExerciseObserverService` is open" claim, and both were mine. |
| **(a) resolved: the retaliation path** | `transitionTo(id, RetaliationTransitionRequest)` and its DTO were **deleted**, not wired. Wiring would have been strictly worse than the three it duplicated: the DTO adds nothing (`terminalStatus` is what the path segment encodes, `assignedProtectorUserId` is the `protectorUserId` query parameter they already accept); it built the F8 trigger by concatenation, correct only because `ALLOWED` happens to gate `to` down to three upper-case tokens; and its audit line read *"transitioned to UPHELD"* where `uphold()` writes *"upheld — disciplinary action triggered"* — the sentence a labour regulator reads, degraded for an identical state change. |
| **(b) still open: the vendor-BCP escalation** | `VendorBcpAttestationDtos.EscalateRequest(reason, escalatedToUserId)` has no usage — and unlike its sibling it has **no live twin**. Campaign-level `POST /bcp-campaigns/{id}/escalate` is a **bulk sweep** over everything past the threshold, with no reason and no named recipient; there is no way to escalate **one** vendor's attestation to a person. Corroborated by the schema: `vendor_bcp_attestation.escalated_to_user_id` is declared in V177, mapped on the entity, and **written by nothing**, while `aml`'s `ScreeningHit` writes its identically-named column from `HitEscalateRequest`. So the DTO, the column and a working precedent in another module all exist and the endpoint does not. ⚠ **Still do not close it by deleting the `@Size`** — adding a write surface is the owner's call. |
| **⚙ Why this half did not ship with [[F2-185b]]** | Because the answer is not mechanical. (b) had a rule to apply per site; (a) had two options per site — and the resolution turned out to be *neither*, which is the argument for measuring before choosing rather than for keeping them apart. |
| **Status** | ⬜ **OPEN on the vendor-BCP half only.** The retaliation entry is **gone** from `InertValidationConstraintTest.TOLERATED` (that test is enforced in both directions, so a resolved entry must be removed in the same commit). The whole measured population now lives in `DarkServiceMethodTest` → [[F2-187]]. ⚠ `FindingsRegisterConsistencyTest.closureClaimedByATestIsHonoured` failed when a draft javadoc claimed this row CLOSED — **the register was right and the javadoc premature**, the mirror of [[F2-185b]]'s experience with the same check. 🔑 **That check does not tell you which side is wrong; it tells you to go and decide.** |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **An inert constraint on a `*Request` type is a fingerprint of a dark endpoint** — but *only* where the dark method happens to take a constrained DTO. One taking primitives leaves no fingerprint, so the annotation scan could never have measured this population, only stumbled on members of it. That is why the deliverable is [[F2-187]]'s instrument and not a second annotation sweep. |

## F2-185b · Ten dormant @Size caps, and the ten did not share an answer

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-185b *(split out of [[F2-185]] and **worked the same day it was filed**, 2026-08-11. Its parent row keeps the two dark types, which are a scope decision.)* |
| **Module** | `compliance/obligation`, `cyber/asm`, `cyber/vuln_sla`, `iam/governance` ×2, `privacy/extensions`, `risk/bowtie`, `tprm/bcp_attestation` ×2, `tprm/outsourcing` |
| **Category** | a validation cap whose number had never been tested against the column it guards — the third variant of [[F2-184]]'s question |
| **Severity** | **P3 as filed, and one site inside it is P2.** The cap work is a 500 where a 400 belongs. But `VulnSlaDtos.RemediatedRequest` was not a cap problem: **the controller bound the note and threw it away**, under a comment asserting the audit log captured it. |
| **⚠⚠ The filing's own measurements were wrong in three places, and that is its most reusable part** | [[F2-184]] recorded per-site measurements so "the next slice starts from data". Re-measured: **(a)** the two `closing_summary_*` caps it recorded as `@Size(1000)` are **`@Size(8000)`**; **(b)** `privacy_notices.archive_reason_en` was recorded as the one case where the cap would be **looser** than the column (500 vs a guessed 1000) and is in fact an **exact match**; **(c)** two columns it called "unconfirmed" do exist — it had searched for the **DTO's** field name, and `approverName` lands in `approved_by_name`, `reviewedByName` in `reviewed_by_name`. 🔑 **A measurement recorded as a guess is not a measurement**, and the only durable difference between the two is whether something re-checks it — which is why this slice's output is a gate and not a table. |
| **The per-site verdicts — and they disagree** | **DELETE the cap (2 sites, 4 fields):** `ObligationDtos.CampaignCloseRequest` + `VendorBcpAttestationDtos.CampaignCloseRequest` — `closing_summary_en/_ar` are `NVARCHAR(MAX)` in both the entity and the migration (V184 186-187, V177 94-95), so switching an 8,000-character cap on would impose a limit the schema declined to impose on the narrative that closes a regulatory attestation campaign. **ENABLE (7 sites, 9 fields):** `CloseCampaignRequest.exceptionNote` 1000 · `AttestationReviewRequest.reviewerCommentEn/Ar` 1000 + `reviewedByName` 255 · `MonitoringEventResolveRequest.actionTakenEn/Ar` 1000 · `NoticeArchiveRequest.archiveReasonEn` 500 · `ApproveRequest.approverName` 255 — every one **equal** to its column, which is exactly what makes enabling safe: SQL Server already refuses more, so the only change is a 400 that names the field instead of a truncation 500, and **no request that works today can start failing**. **FIX THE SERVICE FIRST (1 site):** the SoD override, below. **NOT A CAP PROBLEM AT ALL (1 site):** the vuln-SLA note, below. |
| **⚠⚠ cap == column was TRUE and the write still failed — the SoD override** | `ApproveAccessRequest.overrideJustification` is `@Size(max = 1000)` and `iam.sod_violations.disposition_note` is `NVARCHAR(1000)` (confirmed against `sys.columns`, not inferred from the entity). The structural mirror is satisfied. But `SodService#recordOverride` prepended `"Override justification: "` — **24 characters** — so the effective budget was 976, and a justification the boundary accepts overflows the column by exactly the length of the prefix: SQL Server **8152**, HTTP **500**, and because the violation is written in the same transaction as the grant it authorises, **the whole SoD override rolls back**. Fixed by deleting the prefix rather than lowering the cap to 976: the same row already carries `detection_source = 'OVERRIDE'` and a `detail_en` ending "granted with override", so the prefix was redundant three times over — and it was the only reason the two numbers disagreed. Nothing in the suite had ever asserted it. 🔑 **A length check that stops at the boundary misses everything the code adds after it** — not an annotation, not a vocabulary, not a column, so invisible to every scan in this family. |
| **⚠⚠ The P2 inside the P3: a field bound and discarded, with a comment saying otherwise** | `VulnerabilitySlaController#markRemediated` bound `RemediatedRequest req` and then called `computeService.markRemediated(externalId, currentUserId())` — **`req` was never passed**. Directly above that call sat: *"The optional note in `req` is captured by the F7 audit_log via the service-layer message."* It was captured nowhere. `vulnSla.ts:150` already posts `{ note }`, so the wire carried a value the server dropped in silence, and the `@Size(500)` that should have bounded it never ran either. Now threaded to the service and appended to the audit message, mirroring `ShadowItService#block`. ⚙ Latent rather than active: the sole FE caller (`VulnSlaDashboardPage.tsx:57`) passes no note today, so nothing has been lost — say that, not "data loss". 🔑 **The inert `@Size` was the fingerprint, not the defect**, and deleting the annotation — the obvious tidy-up for an unenforced cap — would have removed the only clue that the field went nowhere. |
| **⚙ The decision F2-184's rule could not make, answered eight lines above the code** | `ShadowItBlockRequest.note` and `RemediatedRequest.note` have **no column at all** — both land in the F7 audit message, which is `NVARCHAR(MAX)` — so "compare the cap to its column" has nothing to compare, and its MAX branch argues for deleting them. The answer was local: the **identical** `note` field on `ShadowItSanctionRequest`, eight lines up in the same DTO file, is bound `@Valid` on the adjacent `/sanction` route of the same controller. The platform already enforces exactly this cap on exactly this field, so 500 here is consistency, not a new limit. 🔑 **Before asking what column a cap guards, ask whether a sibling route already enforces the same field.** |
| **What shipped** | 2 caps deleted · `@Valid` added at 10 binding sites across 8 controllers (three of them the accept/reject/out-of-scope trio on one controller) · the SoD prefix removed · the vuln-SLA note threaded through a widened service signature into the audit message · **0 migrations, 0 frontend changes** (the FE already sent everything the server now reads). |
| **Gates** | **`RequestSizeCapMirrorTest` (4)** — the durable half, and the answer to [[F2-184]]'s unmeasured half: a **declared** (request component → entity field) map verified by reflection, because nothing in the code connects the two — a service copies the value across and sometimes renames it. Same shape as `ClosedVocabularyPinTest` naming its CHECK and `PromotionVocabularyTest` naming its target table. Four directions: cap **==** column length for all 9 mirrored fields; a `columnDefinition` containing `MAX` fails with "delete the cap, do not mirror it" rather than silently comparing against Hibernate's default 255; every `@Size` on the eight enabled types must be **mirrored or explained by name**; and the two deleted caps may not be **re-introduced** — the direction `InertValidationConstraintTest` cannot see, because re-adding a cap *with* `@Valid` is enforced and therefore not inert. Plus **`SodOverrideNoteTest` (3)** — the behaviour test the structural one cannot replace, asserting by **arithmetic** (the longest value the boundary accepts must fit the column *after* the service has touched it) rather than on the absence of a string literal. |
| **⚠ One trap inside the instrument** | `jakarta.validation.constraints.Size` declares **no `RECORD_COMPONENT` target**, so javac propagates it to the backing field and the accessor, and `RecordComponent#getAnnotation(Size.class)` **always answers null**. A sweep that asked only the component would report every cap in these files as absent — and "absent" is indistinguishable from "nothing to check here". It cost one red test: `SodOverrideNoteTest` read the component and NPE'd on a cap that is plainly in the source. |
| **⚙ An instrument in the tree caught the record before the record caught up** | `FindingsRegisterConsistencyTest.closureClaimedByATestIsHonoured` failed the full suite because `InertValidationConstraintTest` now says "F2-185b CLOSED" while the register still read F2-185 as OPEN. That is the check working as designed — and the honest resolution was to **split the row** (F2-07a's precedent) so the executable claim and the register agree, rather than reword the comment until the check went quiet. |
| **⚠⚠ Mutation 19/20 → 20/20, and the survivor was the most valuable result in the slice** | Removing `@Valid` from **one** of the three routes that bind `AttestationReviewRequest` left the suite **green**. [[F2-184]]'s instrument is per-TYPE: it subtracts everything the cascade validates, so a DTO validated on one route drops out of the population on *every* route. 🔑 **A per-type gate over a per-site defect reports the population it can see, and one unvalidated site out of three looks exactly like none** — which is the same failure mode as a ceiling that tolerates a population (CLAUDE.md's `BARE_EXPORT_CEILING`), one level down. Closed rather than documented: a second assertion, `aConstrainedRequestTypeIsValidatedAtEverySiteThatBindsIt`, walks 254 controllers and **186** bare-bound body parameters and reports any whose type (or `@Valid` cascade) declares a constraint. Measured population: **hard zero**, with `PARTIALLY_VALIDATED` empty and enforced in both directions. Mutation 3 re-run against it: **CAUGHT**. ⚙ It is also a second guard on the two deleted caps — re-adding one *without* `@Valid` is invisible to the per-type test (the type would be inert, and inert-but-tolerated) and fails here. |
| **Effort** | S-M (10 DTO/controller/service sites, 2 new test classes, 5 tests extended, **0 migrations, 0 frontend change**) |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-11.** Backend suite **3,698/0/0** hermetic (`mvn -o clean package`, no DB, no secrets) · FE **487/487** in 50 files + `tsc` exit 0 with **0 frontend files touched** — run because "no FE change" is a claim, not an exemption · mutation **20/20 caught, 0 survived, 0 broken, 0 `.mutbak` residue** (6 of the 20 attack the instruments, including the `RecordComponent` blind spot) · live probe **25/25** on a jar built from this tree, **nothing mutated** — every leg used a non-existent id, which `@Valid`-before-`@PreAuthorize` makes sufficient · schema check **14/14** against `sys.columns`, including the SoD overflow reproduced arithmetically against the live column · census refreshed (3,477 / 3,706) · **0 migrations**, head stays V374 · prod (PID 6888, :8090) untouched throughout and re-verified after the probe JVM was stopped. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **"Ten dormant caps" is a population, not a defect — and the ten had four different answers.** A single `@Valid` sweep would have gone green having imposed two limits nobody chose, left one 500 live, and left one field silently discarded. The only reason that was visible is that [[F2-184]] made each tolerated entry carry **its own recorded reason** instead of a count: the reasons are what disagreed. ⚙ Corollary for the next reader of any register row: **the measurements in a filing are the least-verified thing in it** — three of these ten were wrong, and all three were wrong in the direction of looking already-solved. |

## F2-186 · The SAMA quarterly report's top complaint category is decided by HashMap iteration order on a tie

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-186 *(filed 2026-08-11 while working [[F2-183]] — found because a test I wrote **passed or failed depending on run order**, and the right response to that was to ask why rather than to stabilise the fixture and move on)* |
| **Module** | `module/consumer/complaints` (`ComplaintService#generateQuarterlyReport`) |
| **Category** | non-deterministic selection in a regulator-facing aggregate — adjacent to [[F2-183]] but a separate mechanism: the vocabulary is now closed and the *tie-break* still is not |
| **Severity** | **P3.** The number reported is correct; *which* category it is attributed to is arbitrary when two tie. A wrong attribution in a SAMA consumer-protection filing is a real defect, but it needs a tie to fire and both categories genuinely are the joint top. |
| **What is wrong** | `byCategory.entrySet().stream().max(Comparator.comparingLong(Map.Entry::getValue))` over a `HashMap`. `max` keeps the **first** maximal element it encounters, and `HashMap` iteration order is a function of bucket layout and insertion history — so on equal counts the category written to `top_category` is whichever the map happened to yield first. Nothing in the method or the entity records that the result was a tie. |
| **Why it is not merely theoretical** | A tie at the top is an ordinary state for a quarter with few complaints, which is the normal case for a single tenant: dev's 12 complaints already produce `FRAUD_UNAUTHORIZED_TXN` 3, then **`CARDS_DISPUTES` 2 and `TRANSFER_DELAYS` 2** — one more of either and the top is tied. `String.hashCode` is stable across JVMs, so this is not run-to-run random, but bucket order depends on **what was inserted and in what order**, so re-generating the same period after the complaint set changes shape can move the reported category without any complaint changing category. |
| **The decision in it, and why it did not ship with [[F2-183]]** | The tie-break is a **product choice** and every option changes published output: alphabetical (stable and arbitrary), most-recent-complaint-wins (defensible, needs a second pass), highest-severity-wins (arguably the most useful to a regulator), or report the tie honestly — which is the only option that needs a schema change, since `top_category` is a single `NVARCHAR(64)`. ⚠ What is *not* defensible is leaving it arbitrary, so this is filed rather than deferred silently. F2-183 was a closure of ungoverned vocabularies; picking a tie-break is not that. |
| **⚙ How it was found, which is the transferable part** | [[F2-183]]'s first draft of `aCaseVariantCategoryDoesNotSplitTheSamaReportBucket` used a **2-versus-2** fixture and asserted the winner. It failed with `expected "CARDS_DISPUTES" but was "ATM_ISSUES"` — and the tempting reading is "flaky test, pick a different assertion". The fixture was rebuilt as **3-versus-2** so the correct answer is unambiguous, and the tie became this row. 🔑 **A test that depends on a tie-break nobody chose is asserting the implementation rather than the requirement** — and an assertion that only holds by luck is evidence about the code, not about the test. |
| **Effort** | S — one comparator plus a decision, or S-M if the answer is "record the tie" (a migration). |
| **Status** | ⬜ **OPEN** — owner decision on the tie-break rule. Documented in the failing-fixture note inside `ComplaintVocabularyTest` so the next reader of that test does not re-derive it. |

## F2-187 · 38 public service methods nothing invokes — and two reachability instruments that could not see any of them

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-187 *(measured 2026-08-11 while resolving [[F2-185]](a). The third consecutive finding produced by building the instrument the previous one asked for — [[F2-165]]→[[F2-166]], [[F2-184]]→[[F2-185]], this.)* |
| **Module** | platform-wide: 332 `@Service` classes across 59 module packages |
| **Category** | unreachable server capability, measured — not an instrumentation defect this time, but a population no instrument was looking at |
| **Severity** | ~~**P3 as a population**, with individual members worth more … several are the "a row can never leave this state" shape~~ → **P3 as a population, and the "sharpest bucket" claim was wrong.** [[F2-188]] measured all five of those members and **every one was false**; the bucket is empty. Nothing is *broken* except the one narrow defect the audit found (a duplicated OVERDUE transition), and the population is 37 built capabilities with no HTTP surface. |
| **⚠ Why neither existing instrument could see this** | `apiClientMethodReachability.test.ts` ([[F2-165]]) resolves **TypeScript API-client methods** — a Java service method is not in its universe. `FrontendEndpointContractTest` ([[F2-170]]) resolves **endpoints** — a service method with no controller *has no endpoint*, so it is not in that population either. The gap is exactly the intersection: a shipped capability with no HTTP surface at all. 🔑 **Two complete, green reachability gates left a hole the size of "the backend".** |
| **How the one known member was found** | By accident. [[F2-184]] noticed `WhistleblowerRetaliationService#transitionTo` because its DTO carried an inert `@NotBlank`. **That fingerprint only exists where the dark method takes a constrained DTO** — one taking primitives leaves none, which is why the annotation scan could never have measured the population. |
| **The measurement** | **38 public methods on shipped `@Service` classes with no `invoke*` site anywhere in `target/classes`** (39 before [[F2-185]](a)'s deletion), read from the **compiled constant pool via ASM**. Adjudicated, not counted: **9** are a documented expand-contract residue (`PolicyService`'s legacy lifecycle — CH-6/PM-C1 retired it from HTTP, `PolicyManagementService#transition` is the live twin, CH-9 is the named exit); **6** are outbound-integration pushes with no production trigger; **2** are declared test seams; **21** are unreachable capability or helpers. |
| **⚠ The raw number was 51 and publishing it would have been publishing false positives** | A first pass (javap + Python) reported 51 "hard-dark". 16 are `@Scheduled`/`@EventListener` — **the container calls them**; 5 implement a framework interface. Both are invisible in bytecode by nature, which is the honest limit of the instrument and is why the survivors are a **named list and not an assertion of zero**. 🔑 [[F2-165]]'s warning arriving one instrument later: *assume the generalisation has the old blind spot in a new place* — mine had it as "reflection is not a call site". |
| **⚠⚠ And the ASM pass found MORE than the javap pass, not fewer** | The Python pre-pass fell back on a class-agnostic method-*name* check, so common names (`create`, `update`, `delete`) were cleared by any call on any type — hiding **five more `PolicyService` methods**, i.e. the whole legacy write lifecycle rather than the four it reported. 🔑 **A name-based fallback in a reachability scan silently clears exactly the methods most likely to be duplicated elsewhere.** The shipped instrument resolves per owner type, walking supertypes so interface dispatch still counts. |
| **⚠⚠ "The most substantive members" — all five were refuted by [[F2-188]] the next day** | This row claimed `CcmService#recordRun` meant *"a CCM control that fails repeatedly raises no Issue and reads as never having run"*, and that `CommitteeActionItemService#markOverdue` / `ObligationAttestationService#markOverdueForCampaign` had **no caller and no scheduler**. Measured: the CCM ladder runs on a 60-second `@Scheduled` tick *and* has a `run-now` endpoint, both reaching the private `recordRunInternal`; attestations are swept daily by `sweepOverdueForOrg`, whose scheduler javadoc **names the method it superseded**; and the committee sweep was flipping the row itself. The other two in that bucket — `IrPlaybookService#recordInvocation` and `ThreatIntelService#markActioned` — were superseded and a self-declared *"Legacy shim"* respectively. **Four of the five truths were in a comment beside the method.** The members that stand: `MlModelDriftService#listUnacknowledged` — the escalation [[F2-175]] fixed can be filed and never reviewed; `WebPushService#dispatchToUserIds` + `RealtimeBroadcaster#sendToUser` — targeted delivery built and unwired on **both** transports, which is why neither looks like the odd one out ([[F2-38]](d)'s open half); `ServiceNowOutboundService`'s four typed pushes — the controller exposes only `/health`, `/config` and `/test-push`, so the integration reads as working while **no domain event reaches it**. |
| **⚠⚠ "The members that stand" — [[F2-192]] audited those too, and three of the four did not** | The sentence above nominated four survivors of [[F2-188]]'s audit as the substantive ones. Measured against each owner class's **live cross-class surface**: `MlModelDriftService#listUnacknowledged`'s claim that the escalation *"can be filed and never reviewed"* is **false twice over** (`#list` is routed and exposes `isAcknowledged`; the escalation files an **intake record**, and `GET /api/v1/intake` is the review queue — both probed 200); `WebPushService#dispatchToUserIds` is a **self-declared v1 stub** whose javadoc says the VAPID POST is deferred, so *giving it a caller would write a `WEB_PUSH_DISPATCHED` trail for pushes that never left the server* — the reason invited the wrong remedy; `RealtimeBroadcaster#sendToUser`'s *"only BroadcastHelper's tenant-wide path is live"* named the wrong caller (14 services call `#broadcastEntityUpdate` directly) and missed that **no frontend subscribes to `/user/queue/notifications` either**, so it is dark on both ends. Only the ServiceNow four survived intact. |
| **Status** | ⬜ **OPEN as a population; instrument SHIPPED and its reasons since audited TWICE.** `DarkServiceMethodTest` (10 tests) holds **36** methods as a **named map with a reason each, enforced in both directions**: a new dark method fails the build, and one that gains a caller must lose its entry in the same commit (`markOverdue` did in [[F2-188]], `markOverdueForCampaign` in [[F2-191]]). Not a count — CLAUDE.md's `BARE_EXPORT_CEILING` lesson. A third assertion rejects a reason that is a bare label, which fired on six of my own first drafts; [[F2-188]] added a fourth refusing an **unreachability claim** unless a scan verifies it, and [[F2-192]] a fifth requiring every reason to **cite a live method of its own owner class**. Mutation **10 caught / 0 undeclared survivors / 3 declared expected-survivors / 1 compiler-enforced**. |
| **⚠ Each entry must say what a USER cannot do** | Not "unused". The instrument enforces a length floor precisely because my first draft wrote "Unused read helper" six times, and a label is what makes a tolerated entry indistinguishable from a reviewed one. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A green reachability gate certifies the granularity it resolves, and nothing coarser or finer.** [[F2-165]] said this about object-vs-method granularity inside one file; the same sentence applies across a whole tier — two instruments resolving *client methods* and *endpoints* left every method behind an endpoint unexamined. Before trusting a reachability gate, say what unit it resolves out loud and ask what sits between that unit and the code that runs. |
| **⚙ And the mutation harness corrected the test it was written against** | Mutation 6 deleted the `visitInvokeDynamicInsn` handler and **nothing failed** — javac desugars a method reference to a private static into a synthetic bridge invoked with an ordinary `invokestatic`, which `visitMethodInsn` already collects. My new assertion was named `theMethodReferenceCollectorIsLoadBearing` and did not prove that at all. Renamed to `aMethodReferenceTargetIsNotReportedDark`, which is what it does prove. 🔑 **I wrote that test by reasoning about my own code instead of measuring it, and named it after the mechanism I assumed was doing the work** — [[F2-159]]'s shape, and the mutation pass is the only reason it did not ship under a name that lied. |

## F2-200 · MFA enrolment is browser-local, and the shared secret is sent to a third-party QR service

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-200 *(filed by [[F2-199]] 2026-08-12; spec written 2026-08-13 alongside [[F2-202]] because the register is what an external auditor is handed and a finding recorded only in the plan disappears when the plan is superseded.)* |
| **Severity** | **P3 as it stands, and the reason is structural rather than reassuring.** `lib/mfa.ts` persists enrolment to `localStorage` under `grc.mfa.enrolment.v1`; `iam.users.mfa_enabled` exists server-side and **nothing ever writes it**; and the `otpauth://` URI — which carries the TOTP **shared secret** — is placed in a query string sent to **`api.qrserver.com`**. Were the page reachable, that last point alone would be P1: a second factor whose seed has been handed to a third party is not a second factor. |
| **⚠ Why it is P3 and not P1** | `MfaSetupPage` is one of the **8 Sprint 4 §3.3 culled page folders still on disk** ([[F2-199]] filed those separately) — its route was removed, so **no path in the product reaches any of this code**. 🔑 **The grading depends on a fact about routing, not on a judgement about cryptography**, which is why [[F2-199]] wrote "confirm that before grading it" into the filing: [[F2-174]]'s lesson, where a filing's urgency was false because the field it worried about had never once been written. |
| **⚠ What must NOT happen** | Re-routing the page without fixing the two defects. The enrolment must be server-side (`iam.users.mfa_enabled` plus a secret the browser never holds after setup), and the QR must be rendered **locally** — sending an `otpauth` URI to any external host defeats the enrolment it is illustrating. Deleting the folder is also a legitimate answer; it is the [[F2-199]] (d) decision. |
| **Status** | ⬜ **OPEN — filed, not worked.** Nothing has been changed in `lib/mfa.ts` or the culled folder. Treat the P3 grade as conditional on the route staying absent; if anything re-routes `/mfa`, this becomes P1 in the same commit. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **An unrouted defect is not a fixed defect, it is a defect with a missing trigger** — and "the page is culled" is a fact that a later slice can undo without noticing it was load-bearing for a severity grade. |

## F2-236 · Seven registers where the server stamped the clock and the caller named the actor

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-236 |
| **Title** | The nine parameter-borne split attributions: four frontend call sites passed the literal `'admin'`, two controllers defaulted to it, and one register recorded a user id that does not exist |
| **Severity** | 🔴 P2 (live on seven governance registers: SAMA fourth-party validation, ISO 22301 supplier resilience approval, PDPL data-sharing signature, CMA/GRI materiality approval, NCA/NDI maturity review and approval, committee action-item completion) |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · server-owned attribution |
| **Modules** | `scm` (×2), `privacy/dsa`, `sust/materiality`, `ndi/plan`, `ndi/maturity`, `admin/committee`, `common/security`, FE (11 files) |

### What was measured

Executing F2-234's filed nine-entry work list. Every entry was read — the service **and** its
controller, since the wire-ness of a scalar parameter lives at the call site. Adjudication:
**8 confirmed and fixed · 1 BY DESIGN · 0 unread**.

Measured **byte-identical in dev and prod**:

| register | rows | clock set | actor set | what the actor values are |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scm.supplier_resilience_tests` | 11 | 4 | 4 | `CIO` ×2, `CISO`, `CEO` — offices |
| `admin.committee_action_items` | 33 | 5 | 2 | user id `1` |
| `privacy.data_sharing_agreements` | 8 | 8 | 8 / 8 | offices; counterparties are external parties |
| `scm.fourth_party_exposures` | 13 | 5 | 5 | **5 invented person names** (F2-207's cast) |
| `sust.material_topic` | 26 | 10 | 10 | `President of the Authority` ×7 |
| `ndi.improvement_plan` | 2 | **0** | 1 | an attribution with **no clock at all** |
| `ndi.maturity_assessment` | 16 | 8 / **0** | 8 / 8 | `Chair, Data Governance Committee`; `Chief Data Officer` |

🔑 **No surface records a real attribution today**, which is what made the fix safe: the frontend
passed the literal `'admin'` at **four** call sites, the literal `'counterparty'` as a signature, a
`dialog.prompt` at **two**, and nothing at one. Every populated value is a seed.

### The live half — probed 28/28 pre-fix and 28/28 post-fix

As **`compliance`** (GRC_ADMINISTRATOR — holds all six guards these routes carry: `ADMIN:WRITE`,
`PRIVACY:WRITE`, `SCM:WRITE`, `SUST:WRITE`, `NDI:WRITE`, `NDI:APPROVE`) and **not**
PLATFORM_ADMIN, against rows the probe **plants itself** (F2-206).

- `POST /api/scm/resilience/tests/{id}/approve` stored `approverName: "Nobody Who Did This"` beside
  the server's own `approvedAt` — and **an omitted approver was stored as the literal `"admin"`**,
  because the controller read `body.getOrDefault("approverName", "admin")`. 🔑 **`admin` is a real
  PLATFORM_ADMIN username in this platform, not a placeholder**: the default did not leave the field
  blank, it attributed the approval to the most privileged account that exists.
- `POST /api/scm/fourth-party/{id}/validate` defaulted to the literal **`"system"`** — which reads as
  an *automated* validation of a SAMA fourth-party concentration record when a human did it, or when
  nobody did.
- `POST /api/v1/committees/action-items/{id}/complete` stored **`completedBy: 9999`**, a user id that
  does not exist, as who completed a committee action item.
- `POST /api/sustainability/materiality/{id}/approve` **REQUIRED** `approvedBy` — a 400 when omitted —
  and never verified it, while stamping `approvedAt` from its own clock. Fourth register in this
  lineage to demand an attribution and then trust it (after F2-223, F2-224, F2-226).
- `POST /api/privacy/data-sharing/{id}/activate`, `POST /api/ndi/plans/{id}/approve`,
  `POST /api/ndi/maturity/{id}/mark-under-review` and `…/approve` all stored the forged actor.

No privilege escalation anywhere: each route's guard is the same one the register's other writes
carry. The attribution was the only thing at stake, and it was the caller's to choose.

### The correct artefact was in the adjacent controller of the same package

`SupplierResilienceController` — the file beside `SupplierResilienceTestController` — has always
passed `usernameOf(auth), userIdOf(auth)` for `approveAlt` and `approvePlan`. 🔑 **N-th instance in
this lineage of the right pattern sitting next to the wrong one**, and the first where the two are
sibling controllers over sibling registers in one package.

### One primitive, eight call sites

`CurrentActor.requireUsername(act)` / `requireUserId(act)` — added to the class whose
`organisationId()` already establishes the fail-fast idiom, rather than hand-rolling a ninth
null-check. Refusing is deliberately louder than recording a blank: **a governance record whose
approver is `""` or `"admin"` reads as an attribution**, so it is worse than one that could not be
written.

### The BY DESIGN survivor, verified rather than guessed

`DataSharingAgreementService#activate::counterpartySigner` — the *other* organisation's signatory can
never be a principal here. F2-234 filed this as *"plausibly BY_DESIGN … and that is a GUESS"*; it is
now verified against the register: **all 8 live rows in both databases name an external party** — an
NCA liaison officer, a MoCI director, a university dean, a vendor DPO. Its sibling `signerName` is
OUR signatory and was closed, so the verdict is a **field-level boundary inside one method**, not a
whole-method exemption.

### 🔑 The half the OTHER gate found: closing the guarded route makes the update route a bypass

`ServerStampedFieldContractTest` went red on this slice's own fix. Once `markUnderReview` stamped
`reviewerName` from the principal, `NdiMaturityAssessmentService#update` writing the same field from
the request became a contradiction that gate could report **for the first time** — and it is a real
bypass: under the same `NDI:WRITE`, the ordinary edit route could overwrite the recorded reviewer with
anything, making the fix pointless. **Two instruments in series, and the second only became able to
see the site because the first was closed.**

The verdict there is per field **and per window** (F2-222's shape): `reviewer_name` is an
**assignment** before the review — measured, 8 of 16 live rows hold an office with `reviewed_at` NULL
— and the **attribution** after it. So `update` keeps the assignment, refuses a *change* once
`reviewedAt` is stamped, and still accepts an **echo** of the stored value so a form that round-trips
the row keeps working (F2-231).

### An eighth site the gate never reported, found by reading the frontend

`NdiPage`'s compliance-assessment Approve opened a `required: true` prompt for `approverName` and sent
it to `NdiComplianceAssessmentService#approve`, which **takes no actor parameter and never has** — so
the server discarded it on arrival. F2-225's shape: a required field the server ignores tells the
caller their value matters. The prompt and the client parameter are gone.

### The fifth test asserting the defect as correct

`CreateNamesNoDecisionTest` read `assertThat(live.getSignerName()).isEqualTo("Real Signer")` — that
the value the **caller** passed is the value **stored** — **one line below its own comment stating the
rule it breaks**: *"activate() stamps the signature date from the clock — that is the whole reason a
create may not name it."* After F2-159, F2-175, F2-227 and F2-234. Repurposed the way F2-223 and
F2-234 repurposed theirs: keep the half that protects the record, assert the attribution's new source.

### Frontend

11 files. Four `'admin'` literals and one `'counterparty'` deleted; three operator prompts for a name
replaced by a confirmation that says the record will be in your name; the ESG materiality
**approver-name form** retired — its placeholder read *"e.g. Khalid Al-Otaibi"*, the **8th recorded
instance** of an invented officer in a placeholder teaching an operator to type somebody else's name.

### Verification

- Live probe **28/28 pre-fix** (forged values stored, plus both literal defaults) and **28/28
  post-fix**, on a backend deliberately restarted so the probe could not hit stale classes (F2-217).
- `SplitAttributionContractTest` **18/18**, `WORK_LIST` **9 → 0** with the ceiling lowered in the same
  commit; `ServerStampedFieldContractTest` **20/20** with the new per-field verdict.
- `ParameterBorneActorTest` — **9 new tests** for the four registers no gate can assert, because both
  gates read a literal `"admin"` as a server stamp (F2-219: a mutant a gate legitimately cannot see is
  an unasserted behaviour, not a loose instrument).
- Mutation **8 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss**, including a negative control on the gate itself.
- Full backend suite green; FE `tsc` clean; **72 vitest files / 797 tests**.
- Cleanup: **38 planted rows** removed with CHARINDEX, 0 residual, every register back to its measured
  size.

### Filed

- **`ndi.improvement_plan` has 1 row with an approver and no `approved_at`, and
  `ndi.maturity_assessment` has 8 with a reviewer and no `reviewed_at`** — attributions with no clock,
  so those rows never went through the routes that stamp both. Seed-origin, identical in both
  databases.
- **The office-versus-person meaning** in `supplier_resilience_tests.approver_name`,
  `material_topic.approved_by`, `data_sharing_agreements.signer_name` and
  `ndi.*.approver_name`: every populated value is an office title, and the platform now records a
  username. If the product wants to record *which body* authorised something, that is a second field
  and an owner decision — F2-222 filed the same shape for `policy.documents.approver_name`.
- `scm.fourth_party_exposures.validator_name` holds **5 invented person names** on live rows in a
  *server* register (F2-207's measured cast of 65). Repair rewrites live rows: owner decision.

## F2-275 · Six registers are bilingual for what the record IS and monolingual for WHY IT WAS STOPPED

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`510eefff`) |
| **Severity** | **P2** — why an IIA audit engagement was cancelled, why a CAPA was cancelled, why a SAMA/NCA/SDAIA regulatory change was deprioritised, why an approval was delegated, why a board pack was withdrawn and why an NCA ECC filing was cancelled could none of them be recorded in Arabic |
| **Found by** | working [[F2-271]]'s EN_ONLY list and grouping its members by **concept** rather than by module |
| **Fix** | `V389` adds six nullable, width-mirrored `*_ar` columns · six entities, six DTOs (response + `TransitionRequest` + outbound mapper) and six null-guarded writes · a new gate for the half the bilingual ratchet cannot see |
| **Verified** | V389 applied twice; six pairs width-mirrored, nullable, **0** backfilled · live probe **9/9** as `auditor` driving two registers HTTP-to-column · gate **568 pairs / 0 asymmetric** · harness **7 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss** · backend **4405/0/0**, frontend 75/814, `tsc` clean |

### The shape, and why grouping by concept found it

[[F2-272]] closed four members in `privacy` and established the framing: a table already bilingual
for every *other* text column and monolingual for exactly one is [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N, because the
Arabic columns already present are what stop a reader asking about the missing one. Grouping the
remaining 41 by concept rather than by module found that shape at its most systematic:

| register | pairs already bilingual | the one that is not |
|---|---|---|
| `audit_eng.engagements` | title, objective, scope (3 of 4) | `cancellation_reason` |
| `capa.tasks` | title, description, progress_notes (3 of 4) | `cancellation_reason` |
| `regchange.changes` | title, summary, impact_summary (3 of 4) | `deprioritisation_reason` |
| `approvals.requests` | three pairs (3 of 4) | `delegation_reason` |
| `nca_ecc.filings` | title, gap_summary (2 of 4) | `cancellation_reason` |
| `board_pack.packs` | title (1 of 3) | `cancellation_reason` |

🔑 **One concept, six registers, six modules: the happy-path fields were made bilingual and the
exception-path field was not, every time.** That is not six coincidences — it is what happens when
bilingualism is added by walking a form rather than a schema, and the cancel path is not on the form.

### The gate: an Arabic column that EXISTS is not one that can be WRITTEN

`BilingualInvariantRatchetTest` asks two questions — is the `*_ar` sibling **declared**, and is it
**annotated** symmetrically. Both are about the entity. Neither can see what [[F2-272]] found on
`purpose_ar`: a column fillable on create and silently unwritable afterwards, because the update
whitelist named the English field and not the Arabic one, so the edit was accepted with **HTTP 200**
and discarded.

`BilingualWriteSymmetryTest` asks the complementary question — *if a service writes `setXEn` on an
entity, does anything write `setXAr` on that same entity?* Measured **568 En/Ar pairs, 0
asymmetric**, so it ships as a hard zero with an **empty exemption map**: writing the Arabic half
beside the English one is always available, so there is no correct code for it to fail on
([[F2-214]]).

⚠ **Resolved PER OWNER TYPE, and my reconnaissance pass did not.** Matching the setter anywhere in
the tree reported `BcmExerciseScenario.successCriteria` as a violation — but that call writes
`SupplierResilienceTest`, a different entity sharing the field name. [[F2-187]]'s recorded mistake,
and **the tell was that the reported entity had no writer for *either* half.**

### The seventh member, in a module this slice was not about

The gate fired on `CyberSubControl.descriptionAr` on its first run. [[F2-213]] had removed it from
that service's update whitelist because persisting the request object was **deleting** it, and left a
comment: *"Preserved here; offering it means adding the input, which is filed, not invented."*

🔑🔑 **Preserving a field is not protecting it.** Omitting it stopped the deletion and left the
column **permanently uneditable** — F2-272's defect exactly — and **frozen and protected are
indistinguishable from the caller's side.** A null guard gives both properties at once: an omitted
Arabic description leaves the stored one alone, and a supplied one is written.

⚠⚠ **And then a correction to my own correction, which is the more useful half.** I first wrote into
that comment that `CyberSubControlRequest` *"does not exist — its only occurrence in the whole tree
was this sentence"*, having grepped the **Java** tree alone. It exists in **TypeScript**
(`lib/api.ts`), which is precisely what F2-213 meant — and `FullReplaceUpdateContractTest`'s reverse
leg proved it by failing the build the moment the write was added: *the server may not write a column
its only client cannot put on the wire*. 🔑 **"That type does not exist" is a claim about every tree,
and this platform has two.** The fix is both halves in one commit — the guarded write and the field
on the frontend type. Whether the sub-control *form* grows an Arabic textarea stays filed: a field
the type can express and the form does not collect is honest; a field the server writes and the type
cannot express is not.

### The re-scoped ceiling, third consecutive fix

```
asymmetric pairs = 159 (unchanged), EN_ONLY 41 → 35, sum 200 → 194
```

All six English siblings are nullable, so the new pairs are **symmetric** and the sum fell by exactly
the number of members closed. [[F2-271]]'s re-scoping keeps paying: on the old ceiling this would
have read as having done nothing.

### A register's row count is only a measurement if no probe residue is in it

My baseline said `capa.tasks` held **22** rows in dev against **15** in prod, and wrote *"the
databases differ, so that is a measurement"* into the migration. **Both figures were probe
residue.** Dev carried **eight** leftover `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows from earlier slices, which this
slice's own bare-tag sweep removed ([[F2-267]]'s rule), leaving exactly the **14** [[F2-208]]
recorded. 🔑 **"The two databases differ" is the shape residue takes when you believe the first
number.**

⚠ **Prod still carries one** — `CAPA-2026-19F2D8`, soft-deleted and therefore invisible to the API,
so inert. Removing a row from a customer database is not a side effect of a migration (house rule 6),
so it is **reported and left**: an owner decision.

### Two probe corrections, both mine

The transition body key is **`status`**, resolved from each `TransitionRequest`. My first two
guesses (`target`, `to`) both returned **400**, and a 400 from a wrong key reads exactly like the fix
being rejected — so the corrected probe carries **no fallback**, because a fallback hides which key
is real ([[F2-250]]).

⚠ And `mvn -o compile` did **not** trigger a DevTools restart, so my wait loop spun for ten minutes
against a listener still serving pre-V389 code — [[F2-252]]'s recorded hazard, where a probe would
have scored the fix as not working. Killed and relaunched after confirming by `-Djava.io.tmpdir` that
the process was this session's and that :8090 belongs to the prod jar ([[F2-216]]: identify a process
by its arguments, never a log timestamp).

### Filed

- **35 remaining EN_ONLY fields.** The largest single-module cluster is `evidence` with **9** — the
  assurance fabric 14 modules adopt — and it is a *different* sub-shape: `evidence.evidence_reviews`
  has **no Arabic column of any kind**, where the other eight tables are bilingual for their name or
  title and monolingual for their description. `evidence.sub_controls` also carries an
  `evidence_guidance_ar` with **no English sibling**, which is the mirror case and worth a look.
- **`review_comments_en` / `peer_review_comments_en`** (`board_pack.packs`, `nca_ecc.filings`) are
  *what a reviewer said*, not *why something stopped* — a different concept, deliberately not mixed
  into this slice. The NCA ECC one is the sharper: it is the four-eyes peer review on a regulator
  filing and it is the only member of either group with real data (3 of 4 rows).
- The one `[REVIEW-TEST]` row in the production `capa.tasks`.
- Whether the cyber sub-control form should collect an Arabic description.

## F2-274 · The link detector's "every way this codebase expresses a destination" omitted the template literal, and a retired page was relinked through the gap

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`1f0c85d8`) |
| **Severity** | **P2** — a dead control on the PDPL Article 6/29 data-sharing register, and a retired-page gate that was green over a live inbound link |
| **Found by** | re-deriving [[F2-272]]'s filed `ropaTitleEn` item ([[F2-221]]) — which **refuted the filing** and led to the link that carries the code |
| **Fix** | `LINK_KEYS` learns the static template literal · `routeReachability` strips comments through a named helper the self-tests exercise · the ROPA chip repointed at `/data-lifecycle?tab=cbt&ropaCode=…` |
| **Verified** | the retired-redirect leg goes **red naming `/ropa`** the moment the pattern is widened, before the link is touched · 12/12 · harness **6 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss** · browser-verified end to end on real server data · frontend 75/75 files, 814/814, `tsc` clean |

### The filing was refuted first

[[F2-272]] filed `CrossBorderTransfer.ropaTitleEn` as an [[F2-245]] parent-identity-copy member, with
the fix *"derive the label from the resolved ROPA, which yields both languages free"*. Measured, in
both databases: **`ropa_code` resolves to nothing — 0 of 9.** `privacy.processing_activities` has
**no code column at all** (its only reference is a UUID `external_id`), so there is no ROPA to
resolve and nothing to derive from. 🔑 **Executing a filing is how you find out it was wrong, for
the fifth time in this programme — and this one would have sent the next slice to build a derivation
against a join that does not exist.**

What is actually there is [[F2-203]]'s **disjoint code space**, on statutory registers:
`ROPA-001`…`ROPA-007` is used by `cross_border_transfers.ropa_code` (9 rows), and
`linked_ropa_codes` on `data_sharing_agreements` (8) and `privacy_notices` (7) — **no foreign key on
any of them**, and the register they name cannot produce the code. A **name** join recovers 6 of 9
(two null labels, one label matching no activity), which is why reconciliation is an owner decision
and not a side effect of a link fix.

### The instrument: seven patterns under a comment claiming completeness

`routeReachability.test.ts`'s `LINK_KEYS` is introduced as *"Every way this codebase expresses
'somewhere the user can go'"* and lists `to="…"`, `to={'…'}`, `to: '…'`, `href`, `route` and
`navigate('…')`. **Not one matches a template literal** — and `DataSharingPage` wrote
``to={`/ropa`}``.

So `RETIRED_MUST_STAY_UNLINKED`, which F2-199 built precisely because *"a redirect keeps every stale
link working, so nothing breaks and nobody notices they are stale"*, was **green over a live inbound
link to `/ropa`** — a page [[F2-198]] retired for rendering nine invented PDPL activities.

Measured: **6 static** template-literal destinations across **148** template links (142 dynamic),
exactly **1** pointing at a retired redirect. 🔑 **A pattern list whose comment claims completeness
is the hardest kind to doubt** — [[F2-184]]'s shape in a detector's own documentation, and
[[F2-198]]'s at a new depth: the invariant is real, its population is a list of spellings.

⚠ Its sibling gate `tabLinkTargets.test.ts` ([[F2-207]]) **does** resolve template literals — it
found `SocOpsEventsPage`'s `` `/cyber?tab=incidents` `` when it was written. So two link scanners in
one directory disagreed about what a link is ([[F2-190]]'s shape), and the newer one was right.

### The live half: a chip that was dead three ways

The ROPA-code chips on each data-sharing agreement were `` <Link to={`/ropa`} state={{ ropaCode: code }}> ``:

1. `/ropa` is a **redirect**, not a page.
2. `<Navigate>` carries **neither search string nor `state`** ([[F2-207]]), so the code was dropped.
3. The destination — `/privacy?tab=ropa` — has **no ROPA-code filter** to receive it.

And even repaired it can never reach the processing activity, because the code resolves to nothing.
What it can honestly offer is the other PDPL records carrying the same code, which is what
`/data-lifecycle` is built for: it reads `?tab` and `?ropaCode` and narrows the Article 29 register.

⚠ **Verified in the browser, on real server data**: the chip renders
`/data-lifecycle?tab=cbt&ropaCode=ROPA-004`, and following it shows the filter banner *"مُصفّى وفق
سجل المعالجة: ROPA-004"* with a remove-filter control, on the cross-border tab, narrowed to the one
matching transfer (Stripe Payments Europe, SCC). A mutation pointing the chip at `/privacy?tab=ropa`
— the plausible fix — is killed.

### The second hole was mine, and the third was in the leg that caught the second

**The comment written to explain the repointing kept the gate red**, because `ALL` read raw source
and a quoted link counts as a link. 🔑 **The epitaph reads as the corpse** ([[F2-193]]), for the Nth
time here — and it is not a one-off, because this codebase's convention is to document a retirement
by quoting the link it removed. Comments are now stripped, one left-to-right alternation,
newline-preserving. Measured effect **today**: 398 raw destinations against 396, i.e. **2**
comment-only, of which **1** is a declared route — so this is a **latent-hazard closure, not a
defect discovery**, and saying so is the point.

⚠⚠ **Then the mutation making the stripper two sequential passes SURVIVED, twice, for two different
reasons.** The first attempt merely **reordered the alternation**, which is an *equivalent mutant* —
`//` and `/*` can never match at the same position, so leftmost-match takes the line comment first
either way ([[F2-211]] measured this). My own self-test leg says exactly that, and I wrote that
mutation anyway. The second attempt was genuine and still survived: **the leg tested the `STRIP_COMMENTS`
constant while the mutation replaced the call site**, so the production path could stop using the
thing under test with every assertion green. 🔑 **[[F2-205]]'s rule one level over — a leg that
exercises a primitive says nothing about whether the code under review calls it.** Fixed by routing
the stripping through a named `stripComments()` that the self-tests exercise, plus a structural leg
asserting `ALL` builds its bodies through it and that the helper's body is the single-pass form.

⚠ That structural leg's own first draft counted stripping passes **file-wide** and failed on correct
code, because this suite's two-pass *negative control* looks like a production pass — [[F2-192]]'s
rule (scope a scan to the shape of its claim) landing on a leg written minutes after quoting it.

### Filed

- **`ROPA-nnn` is a code space with no producer** — `privacy.processing_activities` needs either a
  human-readable code column (and `ROPA-007`'s label matches no activity, so one row cannot be
  back-filled) or the three child columns need to move to `external_id` (which orphans 24 live rows
  across three tables). Both are **owner decisions** ([[F2-183]]/[[F2-196]]/[[F2-210]]'s rule:
  align a writer to the register's *stored* vocabulary).
- **The cross-border create form asks the operator to type a ROPA code**, `required: true`, free
  text, no picker — [[F2-246]]'s *a form that collects a label instead of a link* — and there is no
  correct value to type, because no register publishes that code space.
- `RopaWorkflowsController` is a **five-route family keyed on `ropaCode` with no frontend client**:
  its client, `lib/ropaWorkflows.ts`, was deleted with F2-198's retirement, so the endpoints that
  bundle a ROPA's notices, transfers and disposal certificates are reachable only by API.
- The other **5 static template-literal destinations** all point at live routes, so widening the
  pattern only ever made them *visible*; none was in `INTENTIONALLY_OFF_NAV`, so nothing was
  tolerated that should not have been.

## F2-273 · The gated copy of a figure being current is what makes the ungated copies credible

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`b55db727`) |
| **Severity** | **P3** — no runtime effect, but a stale pending-migration range is an input to a deployment decision, and reusing a taken version number is a Flyway checksum failure on the deployed server |
| **Found by** | updating the migration census for V388 as [[F2-272]]'s docs step, and finding two of the three CLAUDE.md figures already three versions behind |
| **Fix** | three new legs on `MeasuredBaselineFreshnessTest`: both ungated CLAUDE.md restatements parsed and asserted, the pending cell's **membership** asserted rather than only its count, and a synthetic positive control carrying master's literal stale wording |
| **Verified** | 13/13 · mutation harness **6 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss** · the four never-enumerated migrations added, so the leg is a hard zero rather than a tolerated gap |

### The measurement

[[F2-266]] found that `CLAUDE.md`'s migration line *said* it was gated and was not, and gated it —
parsing exactly one spelling, `V1→V<head> packaged; next free V<next>** (<n> files`. Measured on
`master` immediately before the repair:

| statement | where | status |
|---|---|---|
| `V1→V387 packaged; next free V388 (375 files` | CLAUDE.md:127 | **gated** (F2-266) · current |
| `head **V344**, so **V345–V384 are pending** … 40 files` | CLAUDE.md:140 | ungated · **stale by 3** |
| `Flyway V1–V384 (OFF in dev)` | CLAUDE.md:198 | ungated · **stale by 3** |
| `**375** files, V1–V387 … next free V388` | MEASURED_BASELINE §0 | gated · current |
| `Pending the next jar: **43**` | MEASURED_BASELINE §7-B | gated (count) · current |
| the same cell's *enumeration* of the pending set | MEASURED_BASELINE §7-B | **ungated** · 37 of 43 named |

Both stale figures read **V384** — behind by exactly `V385`, `V386`, `V387`, the three migrations
added *after* F2-266's leg landed. 🔑 **A gate whose population is one spelling of a fact leaves
every other spelling free to rot, and the drift is measurable in units of "migrations added since the
gate".**

🔑🔑 **The gated copy being current is what makes the stale ones credible.** A reader who checks
the packaged-head line, finds it right, and then reads the pending range forty lines up has no signal
that the second sentence is three versions old. [[F2-198]]'s shape at a new depth — the invariant is
real, its population is one spelling — and [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N, since F2-266's own javadoc says
*"CLAUDE.md's migration line said it was gated, and it was not"* having looked at one line.

### The sharper half: a gated count over an ungated membership

`flywayBaselineArithmeticHolds` has always asserted that the *"Pending the next jar"* figure equals
the number of files above the applied head, and on 2026-08-22 that was correctly **43**. The same
cell enumerates the pending migrations one by one — and named **37**. `V359`, `V360`, `V365`, `V380`,
`V386` and `V387` appeared **nowhere in the document at all**.

🔑🔑 **A count and the enumeration it summarises are two artefacts, and gating the count makes the
gap invisible precisely because the number is right.** A reader asking whether the pending set is
described reads the total, finds it correct, and stops. This is the same relationship as
[[F2-264]]'s catalogue-versus-reachability and [[F2-251]]'s coverage report: the verified artefact
sits on top of the unverified one and vouches for it.

All four never-named migrations were **read rather than inferred from their filenames** and are now
enumerated — `V359` (grants the `PLATFORM_ADMIN` permission module, which existed with zero grants),
`V360` (**disables** 43 operator-object automation rules that could never match, so the jar
implementing the operator vocabulary does not arm them at deploy), `V365` (the 46 foreign keys and 11
uniqueness guarantees a fresh install does not enforce) and `V380` ([[F2-255]]'s `AUDIT_LOG:WRITE`).

### The instrument bug that would have failed on correct code

My first draft of the membership leg used the class's own `valueCell()` helper, and it reported **14**
missing where **4** were. This document's prose contains literal `|` characters — vocabulary listings
such as `HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW` — so splitting the row on the delimiter truncates the logical cell at
**15,754 of ~34,000** characters, and every version named after the first embedded pipe read as
absent.

⚠ It **over**-reports, so it fails loudly rather than hiding an omission — the safe direction. But a
gate that fails on correct code is the one failure a gate must never have ([[F2-214]]), so the leg
reads the whole row and says why. That read is deliberately permissive: a version named in a
neighbouring column would count. Acceptable, because the claim is only that a pending migration is
*named somewhere in this row*, and a newly added version will not appear there by accident.

⚠ The mutation that reinstates `valueCell()` is one of the six, so the truncation cannot come back
silently.

### Verification

Six mutations, all killed: reverting each ungated CLAUDE.md figure to its stale value, un-naming one
pending migration, breaking each of the two new detectors so it cannot match, and reinstating the
truncating helper. The two detector-breaking mutations are the load-bearing ones — a pattern that
stops matching reports a clean tree, which is the failure mode this whole class exists for, so both
new detectors are also run against master's **literal stale wording** in a synthetic control and
required *not* to match text that merely mentions Flyway.

## F2-272 · Four privacy registers were each bilingual for every text column but one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`3d7f0719`) |
| **Severity** | **P2** — the PDPL Article 31 purpose of processing, the Article 18 disposal method, a privacy notice's archive reason and a data-sharing agreement's termination reason could none of them be recorded in Arabic |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-271]]'s filed 45-member EN_ONLY work list — **reading each member rather than batching**, which is why it filed them with no verdicts ([[F2-188]]) |
| **Fix** | `V388` adds four nullable, width-mirrored `*_ar` columns · four entities, three DTO records, three writers and one controller follow in the same commit · ceilings `BASELINE_EN_ONLY` **45 → 41** and the sum **204 → 200** |
| **Verified** | V388 applied twice to dev; all four pairs width-mirrored, Arabic nullable, **0** backfilled · live probe as `compliance` (never `admin`) against planted rows: **7/7 post-fix, 5/7 pre-fix** with both discriminating legs failing · gate 5/5 · backend **4400/0/0**, frontend 75/75 files 808/808, `tsc` clean |

### Reading the list beat batching, and the classification is the finding

`privacy` held five of the 45. Each was read:

| member | what else the table already carries | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `ProcessingActivity.purposeEn` (MAX, 11/11 filled) | `activity_name_ar` | **close** — PDPL Art. 31 requires the register to state each activity's purpose |
| `DisposalCertificate.methodDetailsEn` (MAX, 5/7) | `scope_description_ar` | **close** — PDPL Art. 18 |
| `PrivacyNotice.archiveReasonEn` (500, 2/7) | `title_ar`, `purpose_ar`, `retention_period_ar`, `body_ar` | **close** |
| `DataSharingAgreement.terminationReasonEn` (MAX, 0/8) | `title_ar`, `purpose_ar` | **close** (latent) |
| `CrossBorderTransfer.ropaTitleEn` (510, 7/9) | — | **exclude** — see below |

🔑🔑 **Each of those four tables is already bilingual for every OTHER text column and monolingual for
exactly one.** That is [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N **inside a single table**, four times in one module: the
register was made bilingual and one field was missed, and the presence of four Arabic columns on
`privacy_notices` is precisely what stops a reader asking about the fifth.

⚠ **The one exclusion is a different family, and adding the column would have made things worse.**
`ropaTitleEn` is a **label stored beside `ropa_code`** and written from the request
(`t.setRopaTitleEn(body.ropaTitleEn())`) — [[F2-245]]'s parent-identity-copy shape, where a
description travelling beside an id can describe the wrong row. The ROPA it names already carries
`activity_name_en` **and** `activity_name_ar`, so the fix is to **derive** the label from the
resolved parent, which yields both languages for free. Adding `ropa_title_ar` would have created a
**third** place one ROPA's name is spelled. 🔑 **A member of a bilingual work list can belong to
another family entirely, and the fix that closes the list is the wrong fix for it.**

### The re-scoped ceiling was exercised for the first time, and it discriminated

[[F2-271]] moved the ratchet off `BASELINE_ASYMMETRIC_PAIRS` and onto the **sum**, because closing an
EN_ONLY member adds a nullable Arabic sibling and so makes the pair *visible* to the asymmetry scan —
a number that got worse when the codebase got better. This slice is the first fix to run against the
new shape:

```
asymmetric pairs = 159 (unchanged), EN_ONLY = 41 (was 45), sum = 200 (was 204)
```

All four English siblings are **nullable**, so the four new pairs are **symmetric** and never reach
the asymmetry bucket at all — the sum fell by exactly the number of members closed. 🔑 **A
re-scoped ratchet is only proved by the next real fix**: had the ceiling still been on the
