asymmetry count it would have been unmoved by four genuine closures, which reads identically to
having done nothing.

### The column would have shipped inert on UPDATE, and one line above is why it read as covered

Both ROPA routes bind the **entity** (`@RequestBody ProcessingActivity`, F2-210), so adding the field to the entity is the wire change and `purpose_ar` is fillable on create. But `PrivacyService#updateRopa` copies a **seven-field whitelist** onto the loaded row — F2-213's family — and `purposeAr` was not in it, so the Arabic purpose would have been **settable once at creation and permanently uneditable thereafter** — an edit accepted with HTTP 200 and silently discarded.

🔑🔑 **The line immediately above it is `existing.setActivityNameAr(req.getActivityNameAr())`.** So the whitelist already carried *an* Arabic field, and [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N landed a third time in this slice — once across four tables, once inside one table, and once **inside a single method**. A reader who finds an Arabic setter in a whitelist has no reason to ask which other Arabic setters are absent.

⚠ Checked rather than assumed for the other three: disposal certificates have **no update path at all** (create plus lifecycle transitions), and the notice archive reason and the agreement termination reason are both written by one-shot actions. `PrivacyNoticeService#supersede`, the version-copy path, carries every Arabic field in pairs and correctly does **not** copy the archive reason — a new version has not been archived. So `purposeAr` was the only exposure, and it was found by reading the writer rather than by any gate.

⚠⚠ **My first characterisation of it was wrong, and the probe is what said so.** I wrote “wiped on every subsequent edit” into four documents and a code comment, then ran the probe against the pre-fix tree expecting leg 4 to fail — and **it passed**. This method copies its whitelist onto the row it *loaded*, so a field it does not copy keeps its stored value; nothing is nulled. The real defect is milder and a different shape: [[F2-214]]'s *a field the server discards*, not [[F2-213]]'s reset. 🔑 **The leg I first wrote could not tell the fix from its absence, and the corrected one — send a DIFFERENT Arabic purpose and assert it changed — fails 2/7 pre-fix and passes 7/7 after.** Asserting that a value *survives* is not asserting that it can be *written*, and on a whitelist update only the second question has an answer worth having.

### Why nullable and not `@NotBlank`

The same reasoning as V387, restated because it is the question a reader asks first: bean validation
fires on **UPDATE** as well as INSERT, so requiring Arabic would make every row predating V388
uneditable — and nothing can invent Arabic governance text. `V388` therefore backfills nothing and
asserts that it backfilled nothing, and each Arabic column's width is asserted **equal** to its
English sibling's so a longer English statement cannot be untranslatable.

⚠ An existing fixture (`PdplExtensionsServiceTest`) constructs `DisposalCreate` positionally and had
to gain the new component. It was given **real Arabic text rather than `null`**: a null there would
let the assertion below it pass whether or not the writer copies the field, which is [[F2-179]]'s
rule that a fixture satisfying a condition twice cannot tell you which half is load-bearing.

⚠ **`RequestSizeCapMirrorTest` (F2-185b) failed the build on the new `@Size(500)` and was right to.** That gate requires every validated cap on these request types to name a *destination* — the entity field it mirrors and the service that carries the value — in the **same commit** as the cap. The Arabic cap is registered against `PrivacyNotice.archiveReasonAr` with the reason that makes it safe: the cap mirrors the column exactly **because V388 asserts the two columns' widths match**, so a longer English archive reason cannot be untranslatable. 🔑 **A width-mirroring migration and a cap-mirroring gate are the same claim checked from two ends**, and neither is sufficient — the migration cannot see the annotation and the gate cannot see the column's Arabic twin until something declares it.

### Filed

- **41 remaining EN_ONLY fields**, carried forward from [[F2-271]] with no verdicts. The split that
  matters is governance text (`CommitteeMemberTerm.independenceBasisEn`,
  `CommitteeActionItem.completionNotesEn`, `NcaEccFiling.peerReviewCommentsEn`,
  `Vulnerability.descriptionEn`) versus internal labels legitimately English-only
  (`Permission.descriptionEn`, `WorkflowState.descriptionEn`).
- ⚠⚠ `CrossBorderTransfer.ropaTitleEn` — **this filing was REFUTED by [[F2-274]]**, which executed it.
  It read *`derive it from the resolved ROPA, do not add a second copy`*; measured, `ropa_code`
  **resolves to nothing (0 of 9)** because `privacy.processing_activities` has no code column at
  all, so there is no parent to derive from. It is [[F2-203]]'s disjoint-code-space shape, not
  [[F2-245]]'s. 🔑 **A filing naming a fix is the least-verified thing in it, and this one would
  have sent the next slice to build a derivation against a join that does not exist.**
- **Three ungated restatements of the migration census**, all measured stale while the gated line was
  current — see [[F2-273]].

## F2-271 · The bilingual gate names the bucket it skips, in a comment, and the skipped half is the worse one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`73c424dc`) |
| **Severity** | **P2** — a PDPL Article 20 breach record could not be described in Arabic, on a platform whose primary language is Arabic |
| **Found by** | changing the question after [[F2-270]] recorded the reference-minting seam as worked out |
| **Fix** | `V387` adds `title_ar` + `description_ar` · the entity, the writer, the wire and the console follow · `BilingualInvariantRatchetTest` counts EN_ONLY and its **ceiling moves to the sum** |
| **Verified** | V387 applied twice, Arabic round-tripped on a planted row, cleanup re-counted to 17 · gate 5/5 · frontend 75/75 files, 808/808 |

### The instrument

House rule 7: *"user-visible records carry `*_en` **and** `*_ar`; Arabic names are backend-mandatory."*
`BilingualInvariantRatchetTest` (F2-30) is the only thing that checks it, and it pairs each `*En`
entity field with its `*Ar` sibling to find **asymmetric annotation** — mandatory English beside
optional Arabic. When the sibling does not exist it does:

```java
} catch (NoSuchFieldException e) {
    continue;   // EN_ONLY — needs a migration, not an annotation
}
```

🔑 **So the gate names the bucket it skips, understands why it is different, and never counts it.**
The narrowing is the **existence of the sibling** — [[F2-198]]'s shape at a new depth, after a
filename, an allow-list, a module name, an `extends` clause, a field-name list, a claim shape and an
access modifier.

**Measured: 47 EN_ONLY fields**, against 158 asymmetric pairs and 580 pairs. And EN_ONLY is the
**worse** half: an asymmetric pair lets Arabic be supplied and merely fails to require it, while a
missing column means Arabic **cannot be recorded at all** — and it needs a migration, so the
annotation sweep the ratchet measures can never reach it.

⚠ The census independently reproduces four instances that five earlier slices had each filed by
hand — [[F2-209]] (`privacy.data_breaches` has no `title_ar`/`description_ar`), [[F2-245]]
(`risk.scenarios.risk_title_ar`), [[F2-252]] (`cyber.cyber_controls.framework_name`, where the
sibling register carries `name_ar`) and [[F2-213]] (`iam.users.job_title_en`). Four independent
confirmations of a number nobody had produced.

### The member closed

`privacy.data_breaches` — the PDPL Article 20 personal-data-breach register — carried `title_en`
NOT NULL and `description_en`, and **no `*_ar` column of any kind**. 17 rows in dev, 18 in prod (the
databases differ, so that is a measurement).

⚠ **The platform has two breach registers and the one that already supports Arabic is not the
statutory one**: `pages/dataOfficer/BreachPage.tsx` collects `titleEn` *and* `titleAr` for
`data_officer.breach`. [[F2-196]]'s disjoint-register shape with the statutory half the poorer of
the two; V387 does not reconcile them, because choosing which register is authoritative for a PDPL
breach changes what the platform reports to SDAIA and is an owner decision.

⚠ **The absence had been documented three times and closed none.** `lib/api.ts` carried *"There is
no `severity` and no `titleAr` column on `privacy.data_breaches` — … the second is filed as a real
gap against house rule 7"*, written while [[F2-211]] and [[F2-214]] were both working on this exact
register. Corrected in place.

`V387` adds both columns **nullable, width-mirrored** (`NVARCHAR(255)` and `NVARCHAR(MAX)`, checked
against `sys.columns` — a narrower Arabic column would truncate a title the English one accepts, and
Arabic is not shorter), with **no backfill** and **no `@NotBlank`**: nothing can invent Arabic
governance text, so the honest state is absent, and bean validation fires on UPDATE so requiring it
would make all 17 breaches uneditable. The entity, `updateBreach`, both wire types and
`PdplBreachConsole` follow in the same commit, because a column no write path fills is an inert
column ([[F2-198]]'s shape).

### 🔑🔑 The instrument finding: the ceiling was on a number that gets worse when you fix things

Closing an EN_ONLY member means adding a **nullable** Arabic sibling. That makes the pair *visible*
to the asymmetry scan, so `en_only` falls by one and `asymmetric` rises by one — measured, **47 → 45
and 158 → 159**. The decrease-only ceiling on asymmetric pairs therefore **failed on the commit that
fixed the worse half of house rule 7**, with the message:

> *"Add `@NotBlank` to the `*_ar` field — do not raise the baseline."*

which on a populated column is exactly what this class elsewhere warns makes every existing record
uneditable. **The instrument told me to break editing rather than let its count move.**

⚠⚠ **And it had already written the reason down.** The constant's own javadoc ends:

> *"an instrument that asks about **mapped** things cannot see **unmapped** ones, and its green
> reading is not evidence of absence … **Mapping a column made this number worse and the codebase
> better.**"*

🔑 **So the gate documented why its number was the wrong number and stayed keyed on it** —
[[F2-195]]'s shape, the codebase holding the correct rule in prose beside the place it was not
applied, and the fourth instance of that in this session.

Per [[F2-204]] the answer is to re-scope rather than raise. The ceiling is now the **sum** —
*fields where Arabic is not guaranteed*, `asymmetric + EN_ONLY` = **204** — which cannot be gamed in
either direction:

| change | effect on the sum |
|---|---|
| a new English-only column | +1 → **fails** |
| a new mandatory-EN / optional-AR pair | +1 → **fails** |
| adding a nullable Arabic sibling to a mandatory English one | −1 and +1 → **unchanged**, because the defect *moved* |
| adding a symmetric pair, or annotating an Arabic column whose rows hold Arabic | → **falls** |

Both components are still printed and asserted individually as measurements, so a reader can see
which half moved; only the sum is a ceiling. `BASELINE_ASYMMETRIC_PAIRS` is **deleted** rather than
kept — by then its only remaining mention was a message telling a reader to lower it, and its value
(158) was stale against a measured 159, which is an inert constant answering the question a reader
was about to ask ([[F2-184]]).

### Two errors of mine

⚠ **`BUILD FAILURE` with no `Tests run:` line, and it was my working directory.** I ran `mvn` from
`src/test/java/com/tss/grc/common`, which has no POM. [[F2-255]] records this exact tell and the
same cause; the absence of that line is the signal, whatever produced it.

⚠ Two patch scripts missed their anchors because `—` in a Python string stays literal where the
file holds a real em-dash, and one because a `+` was missing between concatenated lines. Both were
loud. The rule this repo already states — **use the Write/Edit tools for content carrying
escapes** — applies to em-dashes as much as to regex backslashes.

### Verification

V387 applied **twice** to dev via pyodbc: both columns exist, widths mirror their English siblings
exactly (510/510 bytes and MAX/MAX), both nullable, **0 rows backfilled**, and Arabic round-tripped
on a row the probe planted (`title_ar = '…اختبار ثنائي اللغة'`) with cleanup re-counted to 17. Gate
**5/5** — `en_only=45`, `asymmetric=159`, `sum=204`, `all_pairs=582`. Frontend **75/75 files,
808/808 tests**, `tsc` clean. Census moved in all three paired artefacts.

⚙ **Filed:** the **45** remaining EN_ONLY fields as a work list with **no verdicts** — two shapes
live in there and they want opposite treatment. A PDPL or committee record's title is governance text
that house rule 7 is about (`CommitteeMemberTerm.independenceBasisEn`,
`CommitteeActionItem.completionNotesEn`, `NcaEccFiling.peerReviewCommentsEn`,
`DataSharingAgreement.terminationReasonEn`); an internal label such as
`Permission.descriptionEn` or `WorkflowState.descriptionEn` may legitimately be English-only, and
deciding which is which is a reading job this number must not pre-empt. Also unchanged: the two
disjoint breach registers, and `privacy.data_breaches.breach_type` still free text with no CHECK
([[F2-214]]'s filing).

## F2-269 · A four-click flow ended by displaying a fabricated National Cybersecurity Authority acknowledgement

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`7267062d`) |
| **Severity** | **P1** — the platform asserted that a Saudi regulator had accepted an ECC filing, with a reference minted by `Math.random()` in the browser |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-207]]'s filed frontend-minter population, re-derived first ([[F2-221]]) |
| **Fix** | `ncaAckRef` deleted (minter, field, badge) · `createThreat` takes the advisory reference instead of inventing it · `authorityReferenceMinting.test.ts` holds a hard zero |
| **Verified** | pre-fix control fires naming all three sites at their true line numbers · frontend 75/75 files, 808/808 tests |

### The live one

`cyberLifecycle.transitionFiling` minted the acknowledgement reference on the `ACCEPTED` transition:

```ts
if (status === 'ACCEPTED') { updated.ncaAckRef = `NCA-ACK-${new Date().getFullYear()}-${Math.random().toString(36).slice(2, 6).toUpperCase()}`; }
```

and `CyberLifecyclePage` rendered it as a green `success` badge, monospaced, beside the filing's
status and year. **Fully reachable** — four buttons, each offered by the status it applies to:
`DRAFT → PEER_REVIEW → CISO_APPROVAL → SUBMITTED →` `cycMarkAccepted` (a `CheckCircle2` primary
button). On that last click the screen shows something like `NCA-ACK-2026-K7QP`.

Measured: there is **no `nca_ack_ref` column anywhere** in either database (the only acknowledgement
columns are `rrp.rrp_cycle.regulator_ack_reference`, `bcm.crisis_regulatory_notifications
.acknowledgement_reference` and `regreporting.regreport_filing.regulator_ack_reference` — three
different registers), no server field, and no NCA integration of any kind. **The value could only
ever have been invented.**

🔑 **This is the top rung of [[F2-199]]'s harm ladder.** A fabricated dashboard misleads whoever is
looking at it, and looking again corrects it; a fabricated export leaves the platform; **a
fabricated acknowledgement asserts that a regulator has accepted a filing** — and a green badge
carrying a monospaced reference is exactly what an operator would screenshot as evidence that it
did.

⚠⚠ **[[F2-205]] edited this file, retired its fabricated exports, and left comments disclosing that
the filing store is browser-local — and left this.** The page carries *"Nothing persists them today
because the filing store is still browser-local"* a few lines above the tab that renders the badge.
🔑 **A disclosure in the code is not a disclosure on the screen.** The operator sees no comment;
they see a green badge. [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N, and [[F2-185]]b's *a class you have already edited
reads as one you have already checked*.

### The latent one, closed anyway

`createThreat` invented the **issuing body's own advisory number**:

```ts
const sourceRef = source === 'NCA-HASEEN' ? `NCA-AD-${year}-${Math.random()…}`
  : source === 'SAMA-ISAC' ? `SAMA-CTI-${year}-${Math.random()…}` : `INT-${Date.now()}`;
```

[[F2-207]] filed exactly this. It is latent because **the single caller passes `'INTERNAL'`**, so
neither authority branch is reachable from any screen — a fact about today rather than a property of
the control ([[F2-182]]), which is why it is closed regardless. `advisoryRef` is a caller-supplied
parameter now, `sourceRef` is optional, and only the `INT-` case — where the reference is ours — is
still minted.

### The fix is deletion, and F2-209 is why

**An authority's reference is received and recorded, or absent — the server may not mint it
either**, so there was nowhere to move `ncaAckRef` to. Same precedent as [[F2-209]]'s `onDispatch`:
*when a control's output describes something the platform cannot do at all, the fix is deletion
rather than rewiring.*

⚠ **Deleting must not assert health** ([[F2-197]]), so the boundary matters: the **status flow is
kept** — recording *"we submitted and they accepted"* is a legitimate operator note, and the real
register is at `/nca-ecc/filings`, which this page already links to. What is gone is the platform
inventing the regulator's reference number for it. And where an advisory genuinely carried no
reference, the row now shows an **em-dash with a bilingual hint** on `title` *and* `aria-label`
rather than a blank ([[F2-209]]'s three states).

### Why this gate is a hard zero where the last three were censuses

[[F2-266]], [[F2-267]] and [[F2-268]] all shipped **counts**, because a caller-supplied reference or
deadline is often legitimate and a ban would fail on correct code ([[F2-214]]). Here there is **no
correct reason for a browser to generate a Saudi regulator's own reference number**, so
`authorityReferenceMinting.test.ts` bans it outright — with two exclusions asserted rather than
assumed:

- **A recorded reference is not a minted one.** The seed corpus carries real received advisory
  numbers (`sourceRef: 'NCA-AD-2026-0148'`); no entropy on the line, so the entropy requirement
  excludes them, and that exclusion is pinned. Banning those would have deleted real data.
- **A label formatted from a server id is not a mint**, and `crypto.subtle.digest('SHA-256', …)` is
  not a reference at all. My first scan counted both — **9 `SHA-256` hits and 5 server-id labels out
  of 38 raw sites** — so the subtraction is 14 of 38 and the exclusion count has its own
  anti-vacuity floor.

The non-authority mints ride a separate decrease-only figure (**26**) with **no verdicts**: those are
our own references, and some of those stores have no server side at all ([[F2-204]]'s
`NO_SERVER_SURFACE` population), where the browser's mint is the only id the row will ever have.

### Three instrument errors of mine

⚠⚠ **My first scan reported line numbers from the comment-STRIPPED text, so every one was wrong.**
The authority hit came back as "line 630", which in the real file is an unrelated field mapping —
I read it, found nothing, and only then noticed the offset. [[F2-242]] records the remedy and I did
not apply it: **strip comments while preserving newlines.** The corrected scan reports 484 / 739 /
740, which the pre-fix control confirms against the raw file.

⚠ **It also counted display labels as minters.** `INC-${'{'}String(i.id).padStart(4,'0')}` formats a
server-assigned id, which is legitimate; the discriminator is whether the string incorporates a
server id or entropy. Raw 38 → 31 mints → 26 after separating the authority bucket.

⚠ **And the path resolution was invented rather than copied.** `new URL('..', import.meta.url)
.pathname` yielded `D:\src` on Windows and every walk failed with `ENOENT`; the house idiom in
`kpiProvenance.test.ts` is `join(process.cwd(), 'src')`. 🔑 **A test-harness convention that already
exists in eleven sibling files is not worth re-deriving.**

### Verification

Pre-fix control: restoring master's two files makes the hard zero fail, naming **all three** sites
at their true line numbers — which is also what proves the newline-preserving stripper works. The
detector's self-test pins both retired shapes as must-fire, a recorded reference as must-not-fire,
and both exclusions. Frontend **75/75 files, 808/808 tests**; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; 0 live
(non-comment) references to `ncaAckRef` remain.

⚙ **Filed:** the **26** non-authority browser mints as a work list with no verdicts. The sharpest
are the ones whose store has a real server side, since there the browser is minting a reference the
server should own — `ACC-` (risk acceptances) and `KRI-BR-` in `riskLifecycle.ts`, `IR-`/`SOC-`/`PT-`
in `cyberLifecycle.ts`, and `CLS-` in `ContractClausesPage` ([[F2-267]] already identified that one).
`RES-`/`ACT-` in `CommitteesPage` mint from a local `seq` counter against a server-backed committee
register.

⚠ **`RES-`/`ACT-` MEASURED AND REFUTED as a corruption risk (F2-270), and with them the seam.**
Both columns already carry a UNIQUE index — `UQ_resolution_code` and `UQ_action_item_code`, on
`(organisation_id, code)`, present in **both** databases with **0 duplicate groups** (22 resolutions
in dev and 20 in prod, 33 actions in each — the two databases differ, so that is a measurement
rather than an assumption). A concurrent filing is therefore **refused, not duplicated**: a UX gap
with no retry on conflict, not a data defect — [[F2-259]]'s verdict, exactly as [[F2-267]] found for
nine of ten members. What *was* wrong is the prose: both minters carried comments claiming the code
*"can't collide with an existing one"* / *"collision-safe"*, which is true of the list the page has
loaded and silent about the database — and the action one **named the index**, which is what made
the claim look checked ([[F2-184]]). Corrected in place.

🔑 **Three slices in, this seam is worked out, and recording that is worth more than finding it a
fourth time.** [[F2-266]], [[F2-267]] and [[F2-269]] closed the genuinely sharp members — a code
with no minter and no unique index, and an authority's reference invented in the browser. Every
remaining candidate has resolved the same way: **ask the unique-index question first, and where one
exists the answer is a naming question.** The next slice should change the question rather than work
down this list.

## F2-268 · F2-202's rule has two halves, and the deadline half had never been counted

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`66feef5d`) — a census, deliberately with no fix |
| **Severity** | P3 — no live defect closed; the value is the measurement and the intersection it names |
| **Found by** | ranking after [[F2-267]]: [[F2-266]] gave the *code* half of [[F2-202]]'s rule a primitive and a census, and the *deadline* half had neither |
| **Fix** | `ServerOwnedDeadlineContractTest` — census (decrease-only, no verdicts), the intersection asserted exactly, and the shape pinned both ways |
| **Verified** | 3/3 mutations killed · the pin caught a real gap in my own detector before it shipped |

### The rule, and the half nobody counted

[[F2-202]]: **only the server may issue a tracking code or a statutory deadline.** [[F2-266]] and
[[F2-267]] gave the *code* half a primitive (`ReferenceCodeMint`) and a census (93 → 92). The
*deadline* half had been applied one instance at a time — [[F2-202]] itself (the PDPL Article 4
30-day DSR clock, minted in the browser), [[F2-172]] (the intake SLA), [[F2-196]] (the DSR sweep
excluding `EXTENDED`), [[F2-250]] (`aml_alerts.sla_due_at`, filed and unresolved) — **and never
counted.** Four findings, no population, which is [[F2-208]]'s shape.

Measured by the gate: **22 create-path sites take a deadline from the request; 11 compute it
server-side.** Published to `target/caller-supplied-deadlines.txt`.

### Why this is a census and not a ban

Three kinds live in the population and only one is [[F2-202]]'s defect, so the gate records **no
verdicts** ([[F2-188]]):

1. **Policy- or statute-derived** — the platform, not the caller, knows the interval.
   `DataSubjectRightsService#createDsr` does `receivedAt.plusDays(30)` (PDPL Art. 4);
   `PrivacyAssuranceService#createBreach` does `detectedAt().plusHours(72)` (PDPL Art. 20);
   `IntakeService` does `now.plusHours(routing.slaHours())`. **The only defect bucket.**
2. **A plan the operator sets** — `ObligationService#create`'s `firstDueDate`,
   `ChangeManagementService#addCondition`'s `dueAt`. There is no interval to derive: the first
   occurrence of a recurring obligation is a date somebody chooses, and refusing it would fail on
   correct code ([[F2-214]]).
3. **An outside party's date** — `ObService#createTpp`'s `certExpiresAt` is on the TPP's
   certificate. [[F2-209]]'s rule for references applies unchanged: a date only an outside authority
   can set is *received and recorded, or absent*, and the server may not compute it either.

### The intersection is the work list

Six properties the platform **already knows how to compute** and takes from a caller somewhere else
— asserted exactly rather than as a ceiling, because a decrease-only count cannot express *the
population was undercounted* ([[F2-204]]):

`dueDate` · `nextReviewDue` · `nextReviewDueDate` · `nextTestDue` · `slaDeadline` · `targetDate`

Two are worth naming:

🔑 **`OutsourcingArrangementService` computes `nextReviewDueDate` as `today.plusMonths(12)` in
`recordReview` and takes it from the request in `create` *and* `update` — one class.** [[F2-215]]'s
two-of-N at its most literal, on a SAMA outsourcing review cadence that is really consumed:
`OutsourcingArrangementRepository` queries `nextReviewDueDate <= :asOf`, and both databases hold 14
arrangements, all dated, **2 already past due**. The sibling `SubprocessorService` names its cadence
(`REVIEW_CADENCE_MONTHS`); this one hard-codes `12`, so nothing else can see it. ⚠ There is also no
`last_review_date` column, so `recordReview` records the next due date without recording when the
review happened.

🔑 **`SupplierResilienceTestService#create :: setNextTestDue` is caller-only while `DrPlanService`
and `ExitPlanService` both default to `LocalDate.now().plusMonths(6)` — and that is the class
[[F2-267]] edited one slice earlier to fix `testCode`.** *A class you have already edited reads as
one you have already checked* ([[F2-185]]b), and the edit was mine.

⚠ **Filed rather than fixed, and the reason is a judgement this gate must not pre-empt.** On a
`create` there is no prior review or test for a cadence to anchor to, so the first date is arguably
kind 2 — but `update` then lets it be pushed out indefinitely, which can empty the reviews-due list.
Whether an operator may exceed a cadence is a product decision about a customer's SAMA obligations,
and inventing an answer to make the register look enforced is [[F2-196]]'s defect.

### It resolves F2-250's recorded uncertainty

[[F2-250]] filed `ethics.aml_alerts.sla_due_at` as *"no server computation anywhere: this line is
its only writer, so the deadline is the caller's **by design rather than by oversight**"* — a
recorded uncertainty. Measured: **no AML SLA is declared anywhere** in the backend or the frontend;
the only statement of one is a comment in a **seed DDL** (`-- usually +30 days from detection`); and
**nothing reads the column** — no sweep, no query, no export, no rendered surface, where `socops`
has `SECURITY_EVENT_SLA_BREACHED` and a scheduled sweep over the same column name. So it is **inert
rather than by design**, and building the SLA is a product decision, not a fix. [[F2-178]]'s rule:
re-measure a recorded blocker before believing its estimate.

### My own detector was too narrow, and the pin caught it before it shipped

⚠⚠ The first pattern required a **capitalised** suffix, so bare `targetDate`, `validUntil` and
`nextTestDue` never matched. Measured in the tree: `setTargetDate` exists in **7** files,
`setExpiryDate` in **8**, `setExpiresAt` in **6**, `setValidUntil` in **3**, `setNextTestDue` in
**3**. The throwaway Python locator used the same regex and reported **16** where the corrected gate
measures **22** — 🔑 **an under-count reads exactly like a smaller population**, and the only reason
it did not ship as the census is that the must-match pin failed on `targetDate` on its first run.
The widening then exposed real false positives in the tree (`dueOffsetBusinessDays`,
`evidenceExpiryWarningDays`, `avgTargetScore`, `expiredEvidence`, `expiringContracts`,
`hasNetZeroTarget`) and each is pinned as a must-NOT-match, because a **count** of days is not a
deadline.

⚠ **The classification order is load-bearing.** `FROM_SERVER` is tested before `FROM_REQUEST`,
because the house fallback shape — `req.x() != null ? req.x() : LocalDate.now().plusMonths(6)` —
reads the request *and* computes, and for this census the interesting fact is that the platform
**can** compute the interval. Breaking `FROM_SERVER` moves those sites into the caller bucket and
the count goes **22 → 27**, which is how the census leg catches a broken classifier rather than
leaving that entirely to the pin.

### Verification

3 mutations, 3 killed. ⚠ **M3 survived its first run and the mutation was at fault, not the gate**:
I replaced **1 of 3 alternatives** in `FROM_SERVER`, and every server-computed site also matches
`plusDays`/`plusMonths`, so the mutated code was not wrong ([[F2-206]] — and the recorded rule to
check the site count before believing a surviving mutation). Against the whole pattern it is killed
by **two** legs.

🔑 **The property that matters here is that a decrease-only ceiling cannot see a detector that
stopped matching** ([[F2-69]]) — so M1, which narrows the pattern, is caught by the pin and the
intersection rather than by the count. That is the whole argument for shipping three legs instead of
one.

⚙ **Filed:** the six intersection properties as a work list with no verdicts — read the two named
above first. `ethics.aml_alerts.sla_due_at` is inert and its SLA is a product decision.
`OutsourcingArrangementService` hard-codes its cadence where the sibling names one, and the register
has no `last_review_date`. ⚠ **`ApprovalRequestService#create :: setSlaDeadline` was filed here as
*"kind 1 or kind 2 depending on whether the platform declares an approval SLA anywhere, which this
slice did not measure"* — MEASURED, and it is kind 2 BY DESIGN.**
`V22__approvals.sql` declares the column *"optional hard deadline"*; **no approval SLA is declared
anywhere** in the backend or the frontend (every `*_sla_hours` in the tree belongs to
`cyber/vuln_sla`, a properly modelled per-severity policy engine with warning and breach
fractions); and `lib/approvalsApi.ts` **already** handles absence with a `NO_DEADLINE` state, under
a comment recording that it is populated on **12 of 22 rows in dev and 12 of 21 in prod** —
measured back at [[F2-201]]. So there is no interval for the server to own, and refusing the
caller's value would break a working request ([[F2-214]]). It remains true that the requester
chooses it on the register [[F2-226]] found accepting a forged `requested_by`, but that is the
column's stated purpose rather than a defect.

🔑 **Recorded at the line rather than raised as its own finding** ([[F2-261]]) — and it is the
second consecutive slice whose most useful output was a correction to the filing of the slice
before it.

## F2-267 · Nine of the ten "sharpest unread" members I filed one slice earlier already had a UNIQUE index

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`696064d0`) |
| **Severity** | P2 on the one real member — a caller-named ISO 22301 / SAMA supplier-resilience test reference with no minter and no unique index; P4 correction on the other nine |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-266]]'s own filed work list, re-derived first ([[F2-221]]) |
| **Fix** | `SupplierResilienceTestService` mints via `ReferenceCodeMint` · `V386` filtered UNIQUE index · the `testCode` form input deleted · census 93 → 92 |
| **Verified** | 9/9 probe legs (3 index + 6 API) as `ranalyst` against planted rows · V386 applied twice · cleanup re-counted to 11 |

### The correction

[[F2-266]] filed *"sharpest unread members are kind 3: `subprocessorCode` (PDPL Art. 30), `kriCode`,
`bowtieCode`, `arrangementCode` (SAMA outsourcing), `noticeCode`"* — the implication being that they
were `alertCode`-shaped, i.e. **a duplicate is storable**. Measured across ten candidates, asking
the unique-index question *first*:

| property | table.column | UNIQUE index? | caller |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subprocessorCode` | `privacy.subprocessor` | **YES** (`UQ_subp_code`) | overrides a fallback minter |
| `bowtieCode` | `risk.bowtie_analysis` | **YES** | overrides a fallback minter |
| `kriCode` | `risk.kri_definition` | **YES** | overrides a fallback minter |
| `noticeCode` | `privacy.privacy_notices` | **YES** | caller-only |
| `arrangementCode` | `tprm.outsourcing_arrangement` | **YES** | overrides a fallback minter |
| `campaignCode` | `tprm.vendor_bcp_campaign` | **YES** | overrides a fallback minter |
| `scenarioCode` | `sust.tcfd_climate_scenario` | **YES** | server-only |
| `clauseCode` | `scm.contract_clauses` | **YES** | caller-only (**the FE mints it** — [[F2-207]]'s filed population) |
| `planCode` | `scm.exit_plans` | **YES** | — |
| **`testCode`** | **`scm.supplier_resilience_tests`** | **no** | **caller-only, no minter anywhere** |

🔑 **Nine of ten are F2-259's verdict, not F2-253's**: a caller can choose a *well-formed* code and
cannot create a duplicate, so it is a naming question rather than a defect. [[F2-253]]'s filing of
`subprocessorCode` as [[F2-172]](d)'s family never mentioned that `UQ_subp_code` exists — and
[[F2-266]] carried that reading forward to four more members without re-checking. **Ask the
unique-index question first; it is the difference between "a duplicate is storable" and "a caller
picked the string".**

### The one real member

`scm.supplier_resilience_tests.test_code` — the reference an ISO 22301 / SAMA reviewer cites for a
supplier resilience test. `create` does `e.setTestCode(req.testCode())` with **no generator anywhere
in the owning class**, the column is `nvarchar(80)` **nullable** with **no unique index** (4 indexes,
none unique on it), and 11 rows in dev and prod carry 11 distinct codes across **two disjoint code
spaces** (`SRT-2026-00n` ×8, `SRT-GOV-00n` ×3 — [[F2-203]]'s shape in miniature).

⚠ **The collector was the form, with the same placeholder shape three slices have now removed.**
`ResilienceTestsPage` offered a free-text `testCode` box placeholdered **`'SRT-2026-009'`** — the
next number in the server's own sequence — so two operators typing it both succeeded. And because
the create had no minter, a **blank** input stored null: a resilience test with no reference at all.

🔑 **The service's own comment listed what is server-controlled** — *"status/outcome and all
attribution, audit, soft-delete and rowVersion columns are server-controlled (SEC-FIN-004) — never
taken from the request body"* — and `setTestCode(req.testCode())` sat **two lines below it**, with
[[F2-246]]'s vendor-resolver comment directly above, so the create read as audited. [[F2-215]]'s
two-of-N, and [[F2-213]]'s rule that naming two fields to rescue is what a reader does when the
editable list is implicit.

⚙ **This slice is also the test of [[F2-266]]'s claim** that the next application would be *a call
rather than a new generator*. It was: one import, one `ReferenceCodeMint.mint("SRT-" + year)`.

### Four instrument errors of mine, every one caught by running something

⚠⚠ **My batch script mis-attributed two setters by not resolving the owner type.** It reported
`scenarioCode → generateScenarioCode()` and `planCode → code` by taking the **first match across all
services**, which is [[F2-187]]'s recorded mistake verbatim (*"a method-NAME fallback silently
clears the methods most likely to be duplicated elsewhere — resolve per owner type"*). It also
reported `testCode` as having a fallback minter; the owning class has none — that fallback belongs to
**CCM's** `testCode`, an unrelated register. Its FE column mixed the two for the same reason.

⚠⚠ **[[F2-264]]'s landmine recurred and its own remedy is what I skipped.** My probe's payload
omitted `@NotBlank scenarioDescriptionEn`, so the caller-supplied-code leg and the no-code leg both
got an identical bean-validation 400 — and **the refusal leg scored a PASS on it**. `@Valid` fires
before the service, so the refusal never ran. F2-264 wrote *"resolve every mandatory field from the
DTO before reading a write probe's result"*; I did not, one slice later.

⚠⚠ **A sed-derived probe inherits the original's assumptions about a DIFFERENT table.** Deriving
this probe from F2-266's carried over a `description` column `scm.supplier_resilience_tests` does not
have; my guard against that (`assert "description" not in s`) then matched
`scenario_description_en`, rejected the patch, and the old file ran **again** — planting rows twice.
🔑 **A guard whose token also occurs innocently rejects the fix and leaves the defect**, which is
this register's substring-satisfied-by-something-else shape, in a patch guard.

⚠ **And I cleaned by the probe's own tag rather than the house prefix.** The earlier runs planted
`[REVIEW-TEST] V386 probe`; my sweep looked for `[REVIEW-TEST] F2-267`, so three rows survived and
the table read 14 against 11. House rule 5's tag is the **bare** `[REVIEW-TEST]` for exactly this
reason. Swept by the prefix across every text column and re-counted to 11.

### Verification

V386 applied **twice** to dev via pyodbc: the index exists, is unique **and filtered**, keyed on
`(organisation_id, test_code)`; a duplicate is refused with `uq_srt_test_code` **named in the
message**; a fresh code is accepted; two NULL-coded rows are accepted, so the filter is load-bearing
(the column's nullability is reachable — the create used to store a blank as null). Live probe as
`ranalyst`, **9/9**: caller's code → **400** naming the field and the mint; no code → **201** with
`SRT-2026-6X3K-WXY4`; a second create → `SRT-2026-RE4G-RNVX`. Cleanup swept by the house tag and
re-counted: 0 tagged, table back to 11.

⚙ **Filed:** the census is **92**. `clauseCode` is a **frontend** minter
(`ContractClausesPage.tsx: nextClauseCode(category)`) and therefore belongs to [[F2-207]]'s filed
population of 14 client-side reference minters, not to this one. `subprocessorCode`'s generator is a
**check-then-insert over 899 values** (`SUBP-YYYY-001..899`, `Math.random`) with a 50-attempt retry —
so a concurrent duplicate becomes a 500 rather than corruption, because `UQ_subp_code` backstops it;
replacing it would change the format of a **public** PDPL transparency reference, which is a product
decision with no defect behind it. And the two `SRT-*` code spaces are left unreconciled
deliberately: both are legal and distinct, and collapsing two seeded notations on a register a SAMA
reviewer reads is an owner decision, not a side effect of adding a constraint.

## F2-266 · A gate that correctly refuses to ban a shape leaves it uncounted, and six slices each filed one instance by hand

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`e180fae8`) |
| **Severity** | P2 — the reference an FIU submission cites was caller-named, with no minter and no unique index; a duplicate of a real code was storable |
| **Found by** | ranking the next slice after [[F2-265]]: three consecutive candidates in the guard/instrument seam had come back latent-or-refuted, so the question was changed to *"which filed-one-at-a-time family has nobody counted?"* |
| **Fix** | `common/reference/ReferenceCodeMint` · `AmlAlertService` mints `alertCode` · `V385` filtered UNIQUE index · the `alertCode` form input deleted · `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest` +3 legs |
| **Verified** | 12/12 live legs as `auditor` against planted rows · V385 applied twice to dev, index proven to refuse a duplicate *by name* · suite green |

### What was NOT the finding

`ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest` keys on `\bset(?:ExternalId|RefNumber)\s*\(`. My first framing
was that this is [[F2-248]]'s *a gate key is a spelling*. **Reading refuted it.** The class's own
javadoc records the narrowing as a decision, with the right reason:

> *"Deliberately not `setCode` or `setSlug`: those are frequently the caller's to choose (a KB slug
> is checked for uniqueness and belongs to the author), and banning them would make this gate fail
> on correct code, which trains the next reader to edit the assertion instead of the code."*

🔑 **That is correct, and it is not the whole job.** The narrowing settles what may be *banned*; it
says nothing about what should be *counted*. Nobody counted it — so the family has been closed one
instance per slice: [[F2-250]] (`aml_alerts.alert_code`, probed: a duplicate of a real code
accepted), [[F2-253]] (`subprocessorCode`), [[F2-258]] (three `AiLifecycleService` creates),
[[F2-259]] (`snapshotCode`, read → collision-safe), [[F2-260]] (`regulatorAckReference`, read →
CORRECT), [[F2-264]] (`CreateAssetRequest.reference`). **Six survivors after six filings is what a
population looks like when nothing counts it** ([[F2-208]]).

### The measurement

**93 create-path sites write a business reference from the request**, across 59 distinct setter
names — measured by the gate, in Java, over the same tree ([[F2-213]]'s rule). My Python locator
said 91: **third consecutive slice in which the throwaway locator under-counts what the shipped
gate finds**, so the census is the gate's number.

🔑 **Why the ban's zero reads as complete: 118 tables declare `external_id` — server-minted and
covered — *beside* a caller-named `*_code`.** The covering mechanism is visibly present on the same
row, so a reader has no reason to ask which of the row's **two** references it covers. [[F2-215]]'s
two-of-N at its most literal, and `ethics.aml_alerts` is exactly that shape.

### Three kinds, and only one is a defect

The census therefore carries **no verdicts** ([[F2-188]] measured what happens when a slice writes
reasons for sites it has not read: five claims, five false):

1. **Authority-issued — correct to be caller-supplied.** `regulatorAckReference`, `samaLicenceRef`,
   `samaNonObjectionRef`, `lawEnforcementReference`, `strReference`. [[F2-209]]'s rule: a reference
   only an outside authority can issue is *received and recorded, or absent* — the server may not
   mint it either. [[F2-260]] verified one of these individually.
2. **Names another record** — `linkedAssetRef`, `ropaCode`, `retentionRuleRef`, `contractRef`. That
   is [[F2-242]]/[[F2-252]]'s question (does the reference resolve, and to what?), not minting.
3. **The record's own identifier** — `alertCode`, `subprocessorCode`, `bowtieCode`, `kriCode`. The
   only [[F2-172]](d) bucket.

⚠ **Two scoping errors of mine, both caught by re-measuring.** The first pass put `\w*Id$` in the
reference shape and swallowed every foreign key (`setVendorId`, `setRiskId`, `setApproverId`),
reporting **135** — a scan scoped wider than its claim reports a population it never measured. And
`ObService#recordApiCall` writes `setStatusCode` from the request, which is an **HTTP status on an
API-call log**: it is now the gate's must-not-match negative control, because that is precisely how
a `*Code` pattern over-reports.

### The member closed end-to-end

`ethics.aml_alerts.alert_code` — the reference an FIU submission cites. Verified structurally rather
than assumed: the table has **no upstream-source marker of any kind** (no `source_system`, no
`ingested_at`), one caller (`AmlAlertController`, a plain `@PostMapping`, no ingest route), and it
declares `external_id` *beside* `alert_code`. So this is the platform's own reference, not an
upstream engine's — which is the distinction [[F2-260]] established matters, and getting it wrong
would have meant minting a value an outside system owns.

Measured identical in dev and prod: **10 rows, 10 distinct codes, 0 duplicate groups**,
`nvarchar(100)` nullable, **no unique index**.

- **`common/reference/ReferenceCodeMint`** — extracted **from** `IntakeService`, which now delegates
  to it, so the second register calls the primitive instead of copying it ([[F2-190]]). Entropy, not
  a sequence: a per-tenant sequence needs a read-then-write, so two concurrent creates race, and
  [[F2-48]] already had to fix a collision in a generator with an effectively constant suffix.
  ⚠ The intake output shape is **unchanged** and asserted — an intake tracking code is quoted to the
  public on the whistleblowing and breach-report portals, so a code somebody is holding must keep
  resolving.
- **The create refuses a caller-supplied code** rather than silently dropping it, so the caller
  learns the value is not theirs; the update accepts an **echo** and refuses a **change**, so a form
  that round-trips the row keeps working ([[F2-231]]/[[F2-234]]).
- **`V385`** — a **filtered** UNIQUE index on `(organisation_id, alert_code)`. Filtered is not a
  style choice: the column is nullable and SQL Server treats NULLs as **equal** for uniqueness, so a
  plain unique index would permit at most one code-less alert, refusing a state the column's own
  nullability allows. Tenant-scoped, because a global unique index would let one tenant's reference
  block another's — a multi-tenancy defect dressed as strictness.
- **The frontend collector is gone.** `EthicsPage`'s create form offered a free-text `alertCode` box
  placeholdered `'AML-2025-0042'` — a placeholder teaching an operator to invent somebody else's
  reference, the shape [[F2-236]] and [[F2-245]] each had to remove. The code is still rendered.

### Two of my own errors that only running things caught

⚠⚠ **My first index probe printed *"duplicate REFUSED as intended"* when the insert had actually
failed on `description` being NOT NULL.** `except pyodbc.IntegrityError` cannot tell one refusal from
another. 🔑 **A refusal thrown for the wrong reason is indistinguishable from the right one in a
pass/fail line** ([[F2-261]]) — the corrected probe builds its INSERT column list from `sys.columns`
and asserts the error **message names the index**, and it now also proves a *fresh* code is accepted
and that **two** NULL-coded rows are accepted, so the filter is demonstrated rather than described.

⚠ **The gate would not compile because `argumentAt` already existed in the class** — I hand-rolled a
helper the file already had, which is [[F2-190]] catching the slice whose own primitive is an
extraction. Removed, and the census leg adapted to the surviving helper's empty-string contract
rather than the null one mine returned.

### And a second one, found by asking why the suite had gone green

Fixing the census figures for V385 meant editing three artefacts —
`MEASURED_BASELINE.md`, `baseline_census.py`'s `PUBLISHED` dict, and `CLAUDE.md`'s migration line.
`MeasuredBaselineFreshnessTest` failed on the first two and **not** the third. Checked: no test in
the tree reads `CLAUDE.md` at all (every hit is a comment *mentioning* it), so its own sentence —
*"`Appendix/scripts/baseline_census.py` prints it and `MeasuredBaselineFreshnessTest` gates it"* —
is true of the **figure** and false of **that line**.

🔑 **[[F2-265]]'s finding inside the file that records [[F2-265]]**, one paragraph after a
warning that this exact line had gone stale by **54 versions**. Proved rather than argued: adding
V385 and updating only the other two artefacts leaves the suite green with `CLAUDE.md` reading
`V384` and `372 files`.

Closed with `claudeMdMigrationLineMatchesTheTree`, which parses head, next-free and file count out
of the line and compares all three against the tree. The figure is **not** deleted — a reader of
the house rules needs the next free version to hand — so the copy is made checkable instead, which
is the other half of [[F2-265]]'s answer. ⚠ Anti-vacuity: the line must be **found**, because an
unparsed line reports a clean tree ([[F2-69]]). Control run: reverting the line to `V384`/`372`
fails the leg naming the exact drift.

### Verification

V385 applied **twice** to dev via pyodbc (Flyway is off in dev), then: the index exists, is unique
**and filtered**, keyed on both columns in order; a duplicate is refused with `uq_aml_alert_code`
named in the message; a fresh code is accepted; two NULL-coded rows are accepted. Live probe as
`auditor` (COMPLIANCE:WRITE — `admin` proves nothing about authorization), **12/12**, against rows
the probe planted: caller's code → **400** naming the field and the mint; no code → **201** with
`AML-2026-NQ6K-9UZS`; two creates → different codes; echo → 200; change → 400; omission → stored
code unchanged. `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows cleaned with `CHARINDEX` in a `finally` and **re-counted** — 0
left, table back to its 10 live rows.

⚠ **[[F2-223]]'s stale-test-classes landmine fired, in a new shape.** The full run reported **22
`NoClassDefFound` errors** across the two intake test classes, including anonymous inner classes
(`...$1`, `...$2`). Nothing was broken: Maven's incremental test compiler keys on **test** source
timestamps, so editing a *main* class leaves previously-compiled test classes referencing the old
shape. F2-223 met this by changing a DTO; here it was removing a private field and its import, so
the trigger is wider than that record suggests — **any** main-class edit will do it. 🔑 The
output reads as N broken tests rather than as *the tests were never recompiled*. Remedy is still
`rm -rf target/test-classes`, which forces it **without** `mvn clean` — the command that kills the
dev backend.

⚙ **Filed:** the **93**-site census as a work list with no verdicts — read the site and classify it
into one of the three kinds before touching it, and do not write 93 reasons. Sharpest unread
members are kind 3: `subprocessorCode` (PDPL Art. 30, [[F2-253]]'s filing), `kriCode`, `bowtieCode`,
`arrangementCode` (SAMA outsourcing), `noticeCode`. Also: `ethics.aml_alerts.sla_due_at` still has
**no server computation anywhere** — that line is its only writer, so the deadline is the caller's
([[F2-202]]'s rule that only the server may issue a deadline), unchanged by this slice; and **225 of
383** reference-shaped text columns in dev carry no unique index, most of them legitimately (kinds 1
and 2), so that figure is a starting point for reading rather than a defect count.

## F2-265 · The cell that says "re-derive it, never edit by hand" drifted through four re-derivations, because an instruction is not an enforcement

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`394fb9cd`) |
| **Severity** | P3 — no runtime defect; the artefact an auditor is handed, and the list that gates scheduling |
| **Found by** | ranking the next slice after [[F2-264]] — three consecutive candidates in the guard/instrument seam had landed on latent-or-refuted findings, so the question was changed |
| **Fix** | `FindingsRegisterCoverageTest` publishes `target/findings-register-coverage.txt`; `theDocMapCellPointsAtTheGateRatherThanRestatingIt` refuses a restated count |
| **Verified** | 10/10 mutations killed · pre-fix control fires on `master` · two holes in my own gate found by the harness · suite green |

### The measurement

§0's doc-map cell in `UNIFIED_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` states the rule for this register's coverage
and publishes the figures behind it. Re-derived with **the gate's own patterns** (`F2-(\d{2,3})`
over the plan, `^## F2-(\d{2,3})` over the register — never a hand-written variant, because my own
scan has already been refuted once in this programme for treating sub-slice ids as distinct where
the gate parses them to an `Integer` and rolls them up):

| | cell claimed | measured 2026-08-22 |
|---|---|---|
| plan references | **94** distinct ids | **264** |
| register specs | **57** | **235** |
| specs owed | **40** | **29** |
| orphan specs | — | **0** |

Every figure wrong, and the owed one **overstates** the debt — the pessimistic direction, which is
the less likely of the two to be reported, because *"we owe 40 specs"* invites no question while a
suspiciously low number does ([[F2-210]]).

### The consequence: the list that gates scheduling omitted 76% of what it gates

The cell does not merely report a count. It states a **rule** — *"Write one before scheduling any of
them"* — and publishes the list a reader consults to obey it:

> *"`F2-55` `F2-56` `F2-57` `F2-58` `F2-59` `F2-60` `F2-62` `F2-63`"*

Measured against the real owed set: that list **omits 22 of the 29** and **names `F2-57`, which
already has a spec**. So a slice scheduling `F2-74` would consult this cell, not find it, and
proceed believing the rule satisfied.

🔑 **That failure is not hypothetical — the cell records it happening.** Its own 2026-07-31 entry
says *"**F2-61, which an ordering pass scheduled straight into the live queue without a spec**,
breaking the rule stated in this very cell"*, from the same cause: a stale owed list.

### The shape

🔑🔑 **A count in prose is a COPY of a measurement, and an instruction not to copy it is not an
enforcement.** The cell has been re-derived **four** times — 2026-07-29, 2026-07-31, 2026-08-01 and
now — and **every one of them added a warning rather than making the figure checkable**:

- 2026-07-29: *"⚠ This line is itself a recurring drift site — **re-derive it, never edit it by hand.**"*
- 2026-07-31: *"**A line that warns 're-derive, never edit by hand' was neither re-derived nor edited: it was left alone while the thing it counts grew by twelve.**"*
- 2026-08-01: *"Current, and every figure here is script output"* — and *"Re-derive with the script in the commit message of this change; do not hand-edit the counts."*

The 2026-08-01 generation is the sharpest: it names a script, and the script is **in a commit
message**, so *"re-derive it"* was an instruction whose subject a reader could not reach. It also
asserts its own freshness (*"Current"*), which is the one property prose cannot hold.

This is [[F2-52]]'s `AttachmentAccessPolicy` shape at the level of a document: an instruction with no
enforcement, ignored by every author who read it. Nothing in the tree could contradict it, because
the gate that owns this measurement (`FindingsRegisterCoverageTest`, [[F2-79]]) ratchets the owed
**count** and asserts its own **instrument**, and had no opinion about a document restating either.

### And the gate's own javadoc disagreed with its own constant

`FindingsRegisterCoverageTest`'s class javadoc opened *"Why a ratchet and not zero. **31 specs are
owed today.**"* while `BASELINE_SPECS_OWED` three paragraphs below read **29** — and that constant's
own javadoc narrates the walk 33 → 31 → 30 → 29, so the class-level sentence was left behind by the
paragraphs beneath it. House rule 3's named hazard (*"read the constant, never a prose summary of
it"*) **inside the file that owns the constant**, which is [[F2-258]]'s shape.

### The fix, and why it is not "re-derive the numbers a fifth time"

A fifth hand re-derivation would drift a fifth time. So:

1. **The measurement is published.** `target/findings-register-coverage.txt`, this tree's own
   convention (`target/permission-usage.txt`, `target/mass-assignment-risk.txt`,
   `target/server-stamped-fields.txt`), written on every `mvn test` with the three figures, the
   owed list, and a per-id closure **hint**.
2. **The cell states the rule and points at the artefact.** The figures and the stale list are
   gone. ⚠ Deleting them *without* the pointer would have left a reader nowhere to look, which is
   how they came to be written into prose in the first place — so the gate asserts the pointer as
   well as the absence.
3. **The restatement is refused.** `theDocMapCellPointsAtTheGateRatherThanRestatingIt` requires
   exactly one cell carrying the rule, requires it to name the gate and the artefact, and requires
   `COVERAGE_COUNT` to find nothing in it.
4. **The retired figures survive as quotations.** This register's convention is that a correction
   quotes the sentence it replaces, which is exactly why the detector strips double-quoted spans
   first ([[F2-193]]) — and it is pinned in both directions, because a detector that cannot tell a
   quotation from a claim forces every correction to paraphrase away its own evidence.
5. **The class javadoc no longer states a count its own constant owns.**

⚠ `COVERAGE_COUNT` matches **`referenc(?:es|ed)`**, both stems. The pre-fix cell carried
`referenced **74+**` as unquoted history, and a present-tense-only pattern would have missed it —
passing for a reason unrelated to its claim. Measured: **4 unquoted hits** on the pre-fix cell.

### What was deliberately NOT built, and why that is the finding arriving from the inside

The obvious next step is a second decrease-only figure for *owed **and** open* — the number the rule
actually wants, since a spec for a closed finding is retrospective documentation while a spec for an
open one gates the work. It was measured and **rejected**, and the reason is this finding's own
lesson:

🔑 **Two independent parsers of the plan's status markers disagreed on four ids.** Mine classified by
the first marker found across every row mentioning the id; the gate's hint takes the row's last
non-empty cell. Reading the four settled them — `F2-35`'s trailing cell is an **owner** and
`F2-53`'s a **migration** column (both are `✅ CLOSED` one cell earlier), `F2-65` ends
*"⬜ (b) still not to be swept"*, and `F2-68` leads `🔁` over four `DONE` sub-items.

🔑 **My own draft of the corrected sentence claimed "22 of the 29 are closed or refuted and 6 are
open", and it was wrong in both operands. What caught it was the two parsers disagreeing — not
either of them being checked.** A ratchet built on that parser would have been an
authoritative-looking artefact nobody could keep true, which is precisely what [[F2-188]] measured
at five claims, five false. So the classification ships as a **hint, gated on nothing**, with the
row named as the adjudicator, and the cell gives **no total** — a total here would be a fifth figure
with the same lifespan as the four this slice retired.

### The debt itself, unchanged

**29 specs owed**, of which `F2-32`, `F2-34`, `F2-36`, `F2-37`, `F2-74` and `F2-85` are open (one
scheduled into a later round), `F2-65` is half-closed with its remaining half a recorded decision,
`F2-55` was refuted, and the rest are closed — retrospective documentation, real debt because the
register outlives the plan, and not a gate. ⚠ Writing all 29 in one batch is [[F2-188]]'s failure
mode: 29 paraphrases of plan rows would be 29 fluent unverified artefacts. Pay them where a slice
touches the finding.

### Two holes in my own gate, both found by running it

⚠⚠ **The gate's ANCHOR was not quote-aware, and its own plan entry broke it.** I quote-stripped
`COVERAGE_COUNT` and not the resolution of the cell itself — so the moment this finding's plan
bullet quoted the rule sentence, **two** lines matched and the uniqueness assertion failed on a
correct tree. 🔑 **The quotation problem is a property of the whole detector, not of the part
whose claim happens to be about counts** — and the same defect then appeared a third time in the
mutation harness's own locator, which found two cells for the identical reason. Three copies of one
omission in one slice, each written after quoting [[F2-193]].

⚠⚠ **The publish leg was satisfied by the PREVIOUS run's artefact.** The mutation replacing the
write with a branch that never fires **SURVIVED**, because `target/findings-register-coverage.txt`
was still on disk from the run before and still carried the right numbers. This tree's recurring
*an artefact on disk answers an older question* — one artefact over from the stale surefire report
landmine. Closed by deleting the file first and asserting the content on disk **equals the string
this run wrote**, which also catches a partial write.

### Verification

The three new legs passed on their first run, which is also what a rotted regex looks like — so
the pre-fix control ran them against `git show master:UNIFIED_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md`, where the
restatement leg fires. (`theRegisterDoesNotInventFindings` fires there too, and that is expected
noise rather than a second finding: master's plan does not reference `F2-265` while the working
register carries its spec.) **10 mutations, 10 killed, 0 survived, 0 anchor-miss** — after two
rounds in which the harness's own anchors were the fault, which is why an anchor miss is a distinct
non-zero outcome here ([[F2-212]]).

The ratchet then did its own job unprompted: filing this finding took the owed count to **30** and
**failed the build** until this spec was written, which is the pay-as-you-go mechanism its javadoc
describes, on its third occurrence.

## F2-264 · "MODULE has no catalogued permission" has two opposite consequences, and three slices carried the conflation forward

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-21 (`3bc6c2ac`) |
| **Severity** | P3 — a filing's severity claim, refuted; no runtime defect |
| **Found by** | ranking [[F2-257]]'s filed catalogue gap as the next slice, re-derived first ([[F2-221]]) |
| **Fix** | `PermissionCatalogueUsageTest.theCatalogueGapHasTwoKindsAndOnlyOneIsALockout` |
| **Verified** | probed live 4/4 modules, read **and** write tier · 3 discriminating controls · suite 4,388/0/0 |

### The claim, and what it is actually about

[[F2-257]] filed:

> *"`DATACLASS`, `OUTSOURCING`, `REGINSPECT`, `REGREPORTING` and `RRP` have no `WRITE`/`APPROVE` row
> in `iam.permissions` at all, so five of the ten registers are reachable only through the
> PLATFORM_ADMIN code bypass."*

[[F2-258]], [[F2-259]] and [[F2-260]] each named it as the remaining work. [[F2-260]] closed the
`RRP` member and it **was** a real lockout — with *no administrator remedy*, because nothing could
be granted since nothing existed to grant.

The other four are not. Probed live, `admin` as a control column only:

| module | write route | admitted persona | off-tier persona |
|---|---|---|---|
| DATACLASS | `POST /dataclass/assets` | `compliance` **200** | `rmanager` **403** |
| REGINSPECT | `POST /reginspect/inspections` | `rmanager` **201** | `auditor` **403** |
| REGREPORTING | `POST /regreporting/obligations` | `compliance` **201** | `auditor` **403** |
| OUTSOURCING | `POST /outsourcing/arrangements` | `rmanager` **200** | `auditor` **403** |

On the read tiers, **4–5 of 7 personas** answer 200 in every module. Nothing is
administrator-only, and the guard discriminates in every case.

🔑🔑 **The sentence was true about the CATALOGUE and reads as a claim about REACHABILITY, and the
two coincide only when the guard is a PERMISSION guard.** All 57 of these routes are `hasAnyRole`,
which never reaches `ModulePermissionEvaluator` — so an uncatalogued module costs **nothing at run
time** and an administrator can already satisfy the guard. That is [[F2-05]]'s conversion backlog,
not a lockout, and [[F2-253]] is explicit that the distinction is the one that matters: *"a role
nobody holds has an administrator remedy — a remedy, not a defence"*, while a permission nobody can
hold has none.

### And the list was half the population

Derived from the tree rather than recalled: **57 module packages carry at least one
`@PreAuthorize`, and EIGHT cite no `(MODULE, ACTION)` pair at all** —

`auth` · `ccm` · **`dataclass`** · `governance` · `opres` · **`outsourcing`** · **`reginspect`** ·
**`regreporting`**

Four were named; **`auth`, `ccm`, `governance` and `opres` are the same shape and were never
mentioned.** [[F2-198]]'s narrowing one more time, in a filing rather than in an instrument.

⚠ `auth` is mixed and correctly so — 3 `isAuthenticated()` self-service routes plus one role guard.
The other seven are **83 role-guarded routes** with no permission leg anywhere.

### 🔑 Why no instrument could see it

`PermissionCatalogueUsageTest` extracts the pairs guards **cite**, and asserts a hard zero over
those the catalogue does not define ([[F2-255]]). **A module citing no pair is outside that
population by construction** — so the gate was green over all eight, correctly, while saying nothing
about them. That is why the claim sat unchecked through four slices, and it is the gate-shaped half
of this finding.

`theCatalogueGapHasTwoKindsAndOnlyOneIsALockout` derives the classification **by reflection** over
`@PreAuthorize` — the class javadoc's own rule, *"because a source regex has twice under-counted a
security surface in this codebase"* — and asserts the eight **exactly** rather than as a ceiling
([[F2-204]]): a decrease-only count cannot express *the population was undercounted*, and raising it
would be indistinguishable from tolerating a regression. Converting a module to `hasPermission`
removes it from the set and the assertion must be edited in the same commit, which is the point.

### Refuted while ranking, and each refutation is why this is a correction and not a conversion

* **No examiner reaches any write.** All four are cleanly tiered read/write/approve, and
  `AUDITOR`/`INTERNAL_AUDITOR` appear only on reads. [[F2-259]] recorded both directions of this
  question and warned they look identical in a summary — converting can *drop* the examiner whose
  independence is the point, or *admit* a reader to a write. Neither is present here.
* **Every tier has a live non-admin holder in BOTH databases.** Prod differs only in `CIO` and `CRO`
  being **absent** from `iam.roles` rather than merely unheld, since V373 is pending there — the
  F2-253 distinction between the two databases, re-confirmed rather than assumed.
* **The fatal kind is at zero.** No guard anywhere cites a pair whose module the catalogue does not
  define, which is what [[F2-255]]'s leg asserts and what [[F2-260]]'s V383 achieved for `RRP`.

### Controls, and the one that does not count

4 mutations, 4 killed — **and M4's kill is an artefact, recorded as one.** AssertJ's
`containsAnyElementsOf` fails on an empty actual, so the inverted disjointness leg died on
*emptiness* rather than on the property it is named for. 🔑 **An assertion protected by a different
part of itself than the part it is named after** ([[F2-262]]'s `\b` lesson): that leg is a **pin**
whose tripwire is a future regression, not a discriminating detector today, and saying so is
cheaper than discovering it later. The three that matter all discriminate — the extractor stopping
(57 instead of 8), the module segment taken from the wrong end (sub-packages stop collapsing), and
the scan resolving nothing (exact-equality passes over an empty set).

### My own errors, both caught by running things

⚠ **Two probe payloads were missing mandatory fields, and the resulting 400 arrived identically for
the admitted and the refused persona.** `@Valid` fires **before** `@PreAuthorize` (recorded
landmine), so an incomplete body cannot distinguish them — and that pair of identical 400s reads
exactly like a lockout if you do not know the ordering. It is the same false signal the filing being
refuted asserts, arriving from my own harness.

⚠ A cleanup column guessed again: `outsourcing.outsourcing_arrangement` has `service_title_en`, not
`title_en`, so that delete matched nothing. Resolved from `sys.columns`, and the cleanup now
re-counts across **every** text column of all four schemas rather than trusting its own report —
**0** tagged rows remaining.

### Filed

* **`module/auth`, `ccm`, `governance`, `opres`** join the F2-05 conversion backlog with the four
  already named. Each is the same two-step [[F2-260]] performed (catalogue the tiers in a migration,
  convert the guards), and none is urgent, because none is a lockout — which is the whole finding.
* **`CreateAssetRequest.reference` is `@NotBlank` and caller-supplied**, so a `dataclass` data-asset
  reference is named by the client. [[F2-172]](d)'s family in [[F2-258]]'s *mandatory* shape — no
  null-coalesce, so outside `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest`'s key. Unmeasured for uniqueness.
* **`RegInspectController`'s `WRITE_GUARD` and `TRANSITION_GUARD` recite identical role lists** —
  two constants, one audience. Duplication rather than a defect ([[F2-177]]'s shape), and it becomes
  a real question the moment one of them is converted.

## F2-263 · The file that coined "a regex matching nothing passes forever" required its guard constant to BE a bare `hasPermission` string

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-21 (`f399f4ca`) |
| **Severity** | P3 — a gate failing on correct code (no runtime effect) |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-262]]'s own top filing, re-derived first ([[F2-221]]) |
| **Fix** | `GuardExpressions.permissionPairsIn` / `permissionPairsInConstant` / `permissionPairOfConstant`; ten copies converted; six new gate legs |
| **Verified** | pre-fix control 4/4 legs discriminate · census unmoved on all five figures · mutation harness 12/12 killed · suite 4,387/0/0 |

### The population the filing named, and the one that exists

F2-262 filed *"the `hasPermission('MODULE','ACTION')` pair extractor: 7 hand-rolled copies."*
Re-derived with F2-262's own concatenation walk:

| | filed | measured |
|---|---|---|
| regexes | 7 | **11** |
| files | 7 | **10** |
| spellings | 2 | **4** |
| divergence between them | — | **none** |

All four spellings return the **identical 131 pairs** over **1,314** guard expressions carrying a
two-argument call, and **no guard in the tree splits a `hasPermission` call across a Java string
concatenation**. So every divergence is latent — the same position the role question was in, and
the same argument: 🔑 **what made four independent regexes harmless was that they happened to
agree, and nobody was maintaining that** ([[F2-177]]).

### The sharp edge is not the duplication

`ObLifecycleTest.permissionIn` and its `sharia` twin compiled

```
CONST\s*=\s*\n?\s*"hasPermission\('([A-Z_]+)'\s*,\s*'([A-Z_]+)'\)"
```

and asserted `m.find()`. The closing `\)"` requires the constant's initialiser to **END right after
the pair** — so give either guard a second leg and the build fails with *"guard constant X must be
a hasPermission string"*: **a gate refusing correct code** ([[F2-214]]), blaming the guard rather
than the test.

That is F2-262's mechanism 3 **mirrored**. There the pattern required a `hasAnyRole` literal and
broke when a module *converted*; here it requires a bare permission literal and breaks when a guard
*gains a leg* — and gaining a leg is the documented direction of travel for this platform's guards
([[F2-159]]/[[F2-161]] ownership, [[F2-177]] seats, admin overrides). ⚠ **Measured rather than
hypothesised: 12 of the platform's 94 permission-bearing guard constants are already that composed
shape**, every one of them `"hasPermission('NDI','APPROVE') or hasRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN')"` —
written with the **singular** `hasRole` that F2-262 recorded as invisible to a `hasAnyRole\(`-only
spelling at 67 sites. The shape exists; it is simply not in those two modules yet.

### 🔑🔑 Why the two survived F2-262, which is the reusable part

They had **already replaced** their role extractor with a permission one when their modules
converted, so they were **never members of the role-name population**. F2-262 read
`ObLifecycleTest`'s javadoc, quoted its rule as its headline lesson —

> *"a regex that matches nothing satisfies every downstream assertion forever, so the anti-vacuity
> check belongs in the **helper**, where every caller inherits it"*

— and **did not convert the method the rule is written on**, because it asks a different question.
🔑 **The `find()` they built to be safe is the same `find()` that makes them fail on correct code.**
[[F2-195]]'s shape at its sharpest: the codebase held the correct rule, in prose, on the line that
broke it.

### Refuted before writing code

* **The constant-form hypothesis.** **585 of 2,203** `@PreAuthorize` sites name a constant rather
  than an inline string, and the platform's authoritative consumer
  (`PermissionCatalogueUsageTest`) resolves them by reflection *and says so in its javadoc*. But
  resolving the constants adds **ZERO** pairs to any of the seven source-scanned subjects: the
  constants sit in the **same file** a whole-file scan already reads. A complete, plausible
  divergence that does not exist.
* **Two of F2-262's other three filings.** *"`sharia` and `openbanking` no longer ask the role
  question"* is true and **harmless**: `RoleGuardConversionRatchetTest` scans every controller
  reflectively, so the platform-wide ghost check covers both modules, and their remaining
  `hasAnyRole` hits are **comments describing the retired guards** ([[F2-193]]'s
  epitaph-as-corpse). Filed as a coverage gap, refuted as one.

### The primitive, and what it deliberately excludes

`permissionPairsIn` takes the **widest correct reading** on every axis, so consolidating can only
ever *add* a pair — whitespace anywhere (`hasPermission ( 'X' , 'Y' )`), tokens of any shape
(`ISO27001`). Judging whether a token is well-formed is a **separate** question and
`PermissionCatalogueUsageTest` owns it; a narrow extractor answers it by silently dropping the
evidence.

⚠ **The trailing `\)` is the whole of the three-argument exclusion, and the two forms are refused
for different reasons.** `hasPermission(#externalId,'ML_MODEL','OWNER')` is refused at the opening
quote. `hasPermission('AUDIT_COMMITTEE','COMMITTEE','SEAT')`'s first argument **is** quoted, so
**only the closing paren separates it from a pair** — and matching it would publish
`AUDIT_COMMITTEE:COMMITTEE` as a catalogued permission, which [[F2-255]] recorded as a false ghost
on correct code.

### One population where there were two

`PermissionCatalogueUsageTest` held **two** pair regexes: a strict `[A-Z_]+` one for extraction and
a loose `[^']*` one for the well-formedness leg. The contrast was the design (extract widest, then
judge) and **it did not need two patterns** — the helper already takes the widest reading, so the
judgement moved to one `WELL_FORMED_PAIR` and both legs now consult one population. 🔑 **That is
not tidiness: with two, the extraction silently dropped a malformed pair from
`target/permission-usage.txt` while only the other leg could see it.**

⚠ **`MeasuredBaselineFreshnessTest` keeps its own `stripComments` and only its extraction moved.**
Its javadoc records that the equivalent regex alternation **throws `StackOverflowError`** on this
codebase's larger files — Java's engine recurses per iteration of `[\s\S]*?` — so the helper's
stripper is *not* a drop-in replacement. A latent hazard in the shared helper, now named there.

### My own instrument errors, both caught by running things

⚠⚠ **The pair classifier was INVERTED on its first run, because an escaped `\(` counts as a capture
group.** Every one of the four real spellings opens `hasPermission\(`, so counting bare `(` scored
them at **3**, and the only neighbour the classifier admitted was
`ChangeDocumentationFreshnessTest`'s one-group pattern at 2 — **the gate reported the four members
as clean and the one non-member as an offender.** 🔑 **And my own reconnaissance scan had *printed*
`groups=3` beside each spelling; I read past it because the number was not the answer I was looking
for.** `(?<!\\)` is the fix, and M6 pins it.

⚠ A javadoc `@link` naming the *role* leg as the pinner of the *pair* clauses — a comment
describing a check that does not do that ([[F2-199]]), self-inflicted, in the same commit.

### Verification

* **Pre-fix control** against `git show master:` — **4/4 detector legs discriminate**: 10 of 10
  named files declare a pair regex; **master's own `permissionIn` pattern, recovered from source
  and executed, REFUSES the composed shape in both files**; the five-copy spelling misses **3 of 3**
  legal shapes; 0 of 10 call the helper. ⚠ **Two further legs are PINS whose tripwire is a future
  widening, and they are labelled as such** rather than counted as passes — a green pin and a green
  clean tree are indistinguishable from outside ([[F2-225]]).
* **The census does not move, which is the point.** 131 pairs / 1,784 guard sites / 74 composed /
  363 pure role sites / 38 role names — measured identical on master and here. **A helper that
  changed them would be changing findings rather than sharing code.**
* **Mutation harness 12 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss.** ⚠ Both first-round survivors were
  **real untested clauses, not equivalent mutants** ([[F2-206]]): removing
  `permissionPairOfConstant`'s size check left it throwing out of an iterator — **the anti-vacuity
  property the whole consolidation rests on** — and the class-stripping clause was never exercised,
  because no spelling in the tree happens to put a comma inside a character class. Both closed by
  assertion rather than recorded as equivalent.
* **A synthetic self-test** added to the malformed-guard leg: it is a *collect the violations,
  assert the list empty* shape, and on a clean tree an empty list is what **both** a working
  detector and a dead one produce ([[F2-257]]).
* **No live probe, said out loud rather than skipped.** This slice changes no main source and no
  runtime behaviour, so house rule 4 has nothing to observe; the pre-fix control stands in its
  place. Suite **4,387/0/0** (up 6). No migrations, no frontend change.

### Filed

* **Two test-support packages for one purpose** — `com.tss.grc.support` (`MigrationVocabularies`,
  `GuardExpressions`, 20 importers) and `com.tss.grc.testsupport` (`StateMachineContract`, 8
  importers). [[F2-190]]'s shape one level up, and this slice made it visible by putting both
  imports on adjacent lines in four files. Housekeeping, no defect.
* **`GuardExpressions.stripComments` is the regex form** and `MeasuredBaselineFreshnessTest`'s
  javadoc records that it throws `StackOverflowError` on this codebase's larger files. Nine callers
  use it today on controller sources small enough not to hit it. A character-scanner variant on the
  helper would remove the hazard; nobody has been bitten yet, which is exactly the position the four
  spellings were in.
* **`PermissionCatalogueUsageTest`'s well-formedness leg rejects a token carrying a digit**
  (`ISO27001:READ`) although `ModulePermissionEvaluator` would match `ISO27001_READ` perfectly well.
  Latent — 0 such tokens exist — and whether upper-snake-only is a house convention or an
  over-narrow check is a **product decision**, not a side effect of an extractor change.

## F2-262 · A filing that names its members by module inherits that slice's module list

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| **Severity** | P3 — instrument consolidation closing three latent gate defects, two of them queued behind the next two conversions in this programme's own backlog |
| **Status** | ✔ **CLOSED 2026-08-21** (`8dd0bf73` + `8c09a797`) |
| **Area** | test instruments · `src/test/java/com/tss/grc/support/GuardExpressions` · nine former copies across `security`, `module.bcm`, `module.audit_committee`, `module.rrp`, `module.dataclass`, `module.outsourcing`, `module.data_officer` |
| **Discovered by** | Executing [[F2-260]]'s filed *"shared role-name extractor"*, re-derived first ([[F2-221]]) |

### What was filed, and what was true

[[F2-260]] filed: *"**5** hand-rolled copies across the test tree — `sharia` and `openbanking` were
quietly updated when F2-145(e) converted them, and `cpty` is still latent."*

Re-derived before a line was read:

| | filed | measured |
|---|---|---|
| members | 5 | **9** |
| mechanisms | 1 (implied) | **3** |
