| spellings | 1 (implied) | **6** |
| slices already bitten | 3 | **5** |
| named members that were real | — | **2 of 5** |

🔑 **The three modules it named hold `hasPermission('MODULE','ACTION')` *pair* extractors — a
different question — so they were never members of this population; and the one copy that still
carried the defect (`CrisisRoomGuardTest`) was not in the list at all.** Every error ran in the
reassuring direction: two recorded as already fixed, one as latent, none ever in scope.
**A filing that names its members by MODULE inherits the module list of the slice that filed it.**

### One defect, three mechanisms, failing in opposite directions

| | mechanism | on a converted guard |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | reflective quoted-token scan, scoped | reports `MODULE`/`ACTION` as **ghost roles** |
| 2 | source-text quoted-token scan, scoped | same |
| 3 | source-text, requires the initialiser to **BE** a `hasAnyRole` string, splits on comma | **hard-fails the build**: *"guard constant READ must be a hasAnyRole string"* |

Both are a gate failing on correct code ([[F2-214]]); **only one looks like a bug report.** And
mechanism 3's two copies are `DataclassLifecycleTest` and `OutsourcingLifecycleTest` — `DATACLASS`
and `OUTSOURCING` being two of the four modules [[F2-257]] filed as having no catalogued
permissions, **i.e. the next two conversions in this programme's own backlog. The fourth failure
was scheduled, not possible.**

### Six spellings, every divergence latent, measured against 1,721 guard expressions

| axis | narrowest spelling could not see | live sites |
|---|---|---|
| whitespace before the paren | `hasAnyRole (` | **0** |
| singular form | `hasRole(` | **67** (0 in that copy's own subject) |
| inner token `'([A-Z_]+)'` | a name with a digit | **0** of 38 recited names |
| `hasAuthority('ROLE_X')` | a role said longhand | **2** authority sites, **0** naming a role |
| no scoping at all | every `hasPermission(` argument | **1,392** guards |
| no comment stripping | a javadoc quoting a retired guard | live shape in `RrpController` |

🔑 **What made them harmless was nine independent regexes happening to agree, and nobody was
maintaining that** ([[F2-177]]). The helper takes the **widest correct** reading of every axis, so
consolidating can only ever *add* a name — which is why the verification is that
`RoleGuardConversionRatchetTest`'s census does not move: **363 pure role sites and 38 role names,
identical before and after.** A helper that changed them would be changing findings, not sharing code.

### The rule was already written down, in the file that coined it

`ObLifecycleTest`'s javadoc, explaining why its own conversion produced a legible failure:

> *"a regex that matches nothing satisfies every downstream assertion forever, so the anti-vacuity
> check belongs in the **helper**, where every caller inherits it."*

Correct, and for four more slices there was no helper for it to belong to — [[F2-195]]'s shape.

### The hard zero cannot see the member that had the live defect

The ban is on *hand-rolled role-call regexes*; run against master it finds **8** of the **9**.
`CrisisRoomGuardTest` is invisible to it **by construction** (no scoping ⇒ no regex to ban) and was
precisely the copy that would have reported `BCM` and `READ` as ghost roles on the conversion its own
fourth test is written to adjudicate. 🔑 **A ban on hand-rolled extractors cannot see the copy that
never wrote one.** The complement, `everyFormerCopyCallsTheHelper`, names all nine; the pair is the
contract, because a hard zero over a population the instrument cannot see is the most reassuring
possible artefact ([[F2-205]]).

### My own gate refuted my own census, three ways, on its first run

1. It found a **ninth** member (`DataOfficerLifecycleTest`) — **a detector scoped to the shapes you
   have already seen returns a SMALLER population, which reads exactly like a complete sweep**
   ([[F2-198]]).
2. The reverse exclusion leg reported my own gate file as *not* declaring a role-call regex — an
   exclusion for something never in the population ([[F2-199]]), the direction nobody writes first.
3. The detector could not see mechanism 3 at all: it read only the **first** string literal after
   `Pattern.compile(`.

⚠⚠ **(3) is the reusable instrument bug.** `Outsourcing` interpolates its constant **second**, so its
first literal already carries the token; `Dataclass` interpolates it **third**, so its first literal
is `"String "`. A first-literal detector finds one twin and misses the other — **1 of 2, measured**.
Concatenate every literal in the statement, and bound the window to the enclosing statement rather
than paren-balancing (a Java regex literal contains real parens).

⚠⚠ **And the discriminator is `has` AND `Role`, never `Role` alone.** Keyed on the token alone it
fired on `RoleNameSurfaceRatchetTest`, whose `ParentGuard\.(?:roles|permOrRoles)\s*\(` contains
`Roles` — `AttachmentAccessPolicy`'s **Java** role lists, the second surface whose drift [[F2-52]] and
[[F2-177]] each had to find by hand, and the one CLAUDE.md warns no `@PreAuthorize` scan sees. It
asks a different question and keeps its own extractor.

### Verification

- **Pre-fix control** against `git show master:` — **6 of 6 legs discriminate**, including that the
  bare copy's `namesIn("hasPermission('BCM','READ')")` returned `[BCM, READ]`.
- **Census unmoved**: 363 / 38 / 457 / 94 / 28, identical before and after.
- **Mutation harness**: see the plan entry.
- **No live probe, and that is stated rather than skipped**: this slice changes **no main source and
  no runtime behaviour** — nine test classes and one new test-support class. House rule 4's live
  probe has nothing to observe; the pre-fix control is what stands in its place.

### Filed

- **The `hasPermission('MODULE','ACTION')` pair extractor: 7 hand-rolled copies** in at least two
  spellings (`'([A-Z_]+)'` vs `'([^']*)'`). Same argument, one slice over. Deliberately **not**
  shipped as an unused method on the helper ([[F2-184]], [[F2-201]]).
- **Two test-support packages for one purpose** — `com.tss.grc.support` (`MigrationVocabularies`,
  `GuardExpressions`) and `com.tss.grc.testsupport` (`StateMachineContract`). [[F2-190]]'s shape one
  level up; consolidating them is a rename across the test tree.
- **`sharia` and `openbanking` no longer ask the role question at all** — both replaced their role
  extractor with a permission extractor when their module converted. Legitimate per module, and it
  means the ghost-role check silently left those two modules when they were converted.

## F2-261 · The attribution quality decreased as the authority increased

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-261 *(measured 2026-08-21. Provenance is [[F2-260]]'s filing — §B2b's last two rows — via [[F2-254]]'s recorded blocker and [[F2-152]]'s filing. Re-derived first ([[F2-221]]), which corrected the filing before any code was written.)* |
| **Category** | Attribution — a server-owned clock with nobody owning the actor beside it, at the **top** of a three-stage approval ladder whose two lower stages both record theirs |
| **Severity** | **P2.** Every board sign-off of a quantitative Business Impact Analysis recorded the moment, the board-minutes reference and **no person**. That is the artefact an ISO 22301 or SAMA business-continuity reviewer reads to accept that a named body approved the loss model. |
| **Provenance** | [[F2-152]] filed *"a board approval with no signer, and a CFO approval whose signer is whatever the request says"*; [[F2-254]] recorded the four-eyes bar as *"not buildable today"* because `sys.columns` showed no `board_approved_by` column. |
| **Current State** | ✔ **FIXED 2026-08-21** (`e9c5f466`). **V384** adds `board_approved_by`; `boardApprove` stamps it from the authenticated principal and refuses without one; the field is on the wire. `QuantitativeBiaFourEyesTest` (5 legs). Probed **13/13 pre-fix and 13/13 post-fix**. **Closes the real half of [[F2-152]]** and discharges the technical half of [[F2-254]]'s blocker. The four-eyes bar itself is **withdrawn to a filing** — see below. |
| **Problem** | `QuantitativeBiaService.boardApprove` wrote `boardApprovedAt` from `LocalDateTime.now()` and `boardMinutesRef`, and took no actor parameter — there was no column for one. |
| **Root Cause** | RC-attribution — [[F2-256]]'s shape (the server owns WHEN and nobody owns WHO), landing on the highest tier of a ladder rather than at its edge. |
| **Evidence** | `sys.columns` and the live row in **both** databases; the three guards read from the controller; `iam.user_roles` for the two zero-holder roles; live probe 13/13 in both modes, discriminating on `stage3=None` vs `stage3='admin'`; V384 applied twice to dev with both databases pre-flighted |

**Finding.** Three stages, three different attribution mechanisms:

```
POST …/bcm-review     -> setBcmLeadReviewedBy(actor)                  the controller's actor()
POST …/cfo-approve    -> setCfoApproverName(CurrentActor.username())  since F2-223
POST …/board-approve  -> setBoardApprovedAt(now()) + minutesRef       AND NOTHING ELSE
```

🔑 **So the attribution quality decreased as the authority increased**, and the tier with none was
the board sign-off. Stage 0 already demonstrated the correct shape — `preparedByUserId` beside
`preparedByName` — and each approval stage degraded from it.

⚠⚠ **A correction, and it had been repeated into three artefacts.** [[F2-152]]'s filing said *"a CFO
approval whose signer is whatever the request says"*; F2-52's javadoc on `BOARD_APPROVE_GUARD` said
it; [[F2-254]]'s javadoc repeated it eight paragraphs later. **F2-223 had already converted
`cfoApprove` to `CurrentActor.username()`, with a comment saying so.** Only the board half was ever
real. 🔑 **A claim about a consequence is the least-verified part of a filing** ([[F2-192]]), and this
one propagated through three readings without anybody opening the service.

**V384** adds `board_approved_by NVARCHAR(255)`, mirroring `cfo_approver_name` and
`bcm_lead_reviewed_by` in type, width **and** nullability — check 2 asserts that mirror, because the
comparison the column exists for treats all three parties as strings and a narrower column could
truncate one and make two different people compare equal. ⚠ An id would be the better shape in the
abstract, since a username can be renamed and the history then lies; converting all three together is
filed, because **doing one of three is what produced the divergence being fixed** ([[F2-190]]). It
backfills nothing and refuses nothing: measured in dev and prod, the table holds **one row**, at
`CFO_APPROVED`, with `board_approved_at` NULL — so no completed approval's approver has to be invented
([[F2-196]]), and there is deliberately no check refusing such a row either, because on a customer's
database that is a pre-fix approval to disclose ([[F2-209]]'s third state) and not a reason to block
their migration chain ([[F2-183]]).

⚠⚠ **THE FOUR-EYES BAR WAS WRITTEN, PROBED AND WITHDRAWN, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** With the column
in place the comparison is finally **writable** — board signatory ≠ CFO approver ≠ BCM lead reviewer,
on three now-comparable parties, which is exactly the prerequisite `BiaQuantitativeController`'s
javadoc said was missing. It was implemented, unit-tested and probed. Then measured, from the guards
and `iam.user_roles` in both databases:

```
bcm-review     hasAnyRole('BCM_MANAGER','CISO','PLATFORM_ADMIN')       live: so_officer, admin
cfo-approve    hasAnyRole('CFO','PLATFORM_ADMIN')                      live: admin ALONE
board-approve  hasAnyRole('EXECUTIVE_REVIEWER','PLATFORM_ADMIN')       live: admin ALONE
```

`CFO` and `EXECUTIVE_REVIEWER` are held by **nobody** — they are §B2b's last two rows. **So the only
way to complete this chain today is `admin` taking both approvals, which is precisely what the bar
must refuse.** Probed live with the bar wired: `admin` board-approving what it had CFO-approved
answered **409** — correct, and the only path that works. The post-fix row makes it visible without
any bar at all: `stage1=so_officer, stage2=admin, stage3=admin`.

🔑🔑 **So the missing column, the missing bar and the two zero-holder roles are ONE problem, not
three.** [[F2-254]] wrote that *"the guard lockout and the missing attribution are one problem and
F2-52 filed them as two"* — there is a third. Enforcing the bar without closing the lockout yields a
correctly-controlled feature **nobody can use**: [[F2-112]]'s shape inverted, not a control that
cannot fire but one that can only ever fire. Closing the lockout without the bar yields a usable
feature with no separation. Doing both means deciding who may give a board-level approval, which is a
governance decision about a customer's organisation and not a side effect of an attribution fix.
**What ships is the half that breaks nothing.**

⚙ **The recorded blocker was two claims stacked in one sentence, and only one was a blocker.**
[[F2-254]]'s javadoc read *"the four-eyes bar that would make that safe is not buildable today: …
there is no identity for either tier to compare. Fixing F2-152 is the prerequisite, and choosing who
holds a financial versus a board approval is an owner decision plus a migration."* (a) no identity
exists, and (b) who may take which approval is an owner decision. **(a) was a blocker and is now
closed; (b) is a question.** Stating them as one sentence made the whole thing read as owner-gated,
which is how it survived F2-52, [[F2-152]], [[F2-254]] and [[F2-260]]. [[F2-178]]'s rule — re-measure
a recorded blocker before believing its estimate — with the estimate right about (b) and wrong about
(a) being permanent. The correction is written where the claim is, because **a stale blocker is the
input to somebody's next estimate**.

⚙ **The gate asserts the withdrawal in both directions**, so the next reader cannot add the bar
without also closing §B2b: the attribution must be stamped from the principal, **and** neither
approval method may contain a segregation refusal. A one-directional gate here would have let the
bar reappear and the feature quietly stop working.

⚠ **Three of my own errors, every one caught by running something.** Two guessed names —
`bcm.business_process` (it is `bcm.critical_processes`, and the register's own `process_id` was the
better source) and `bia_id` on the loss-line table — the recurring guessed-name family; and a fixture
whose plain-String principal made `CurrentActor.requireUsername` throw its **no-actor refusal**,
which reads exactly like the four-eyes bar not firing. 🔑 The last is worth keeping: a refusal thrown
for the wrong reason is indistinguishable from the right one in a pass/fail line, and only the message
separated them. ⚠ Also [[F2-203]]'s landmine: `mvn -o compile` restarts DevTools **while the listener
stays bound**, so `netstat` says LISTENING through a window where every request is refused — a
`sleep` is not a substitute for polling `/actuator/health`, and a refused connection reads exactly
like a dead backend.

**Verification.** Pre-fix control **13/13** and post-fix **13/13**, discriminating on `stage3=None`
versus `stage3='admin'`, with L7 — `admin` still board-approves at 200 — the load-bearing
non-regression leg passing in **both** modes · V384 applied **twice** to dev, idempotent, both
databases pre-flighted (0 completed board approvals, so no backfill and no disclosure gap) · cleanup
restored the 1-row baseline on both runs · suite **4,367/0/0**.

**Filed.**
- **§B2b's last two rows are unchanged and now have a sharper description**: both `module.bcm`
  approval tiers are administrator-only, and closing them is the *same* decision as enabling the
  four-eyes bar. Enabling the bar alone breaks the feature; converting the guards alone removes the
  separation; the two together decide who may give a board-level approval. One owner decision, three
  symptoms.
- **The three attribution columns hold usernames, not ids.** A rename makes the history lie, and the
  bar (when enabled) would compare stale strings. Converting all three to `BIGINT` with derived
  labels is one coherent slice ([[F2-249]]'s `TenantUserDirectory` is the primitive); doing one is
  what produced this divergence.
- `bcm.bia_quantitative` has **zero CHECK constraints** and its status vocabulary lives only in
  `guardTransition` — [[F2-221]]'s shape. Not cheap here: this slice touched one writer of one
  column, and a constraint lands in the commit that closes a column's writers ([[F2-183]]).
- The live row's three parties are **invented officers with titles** (`'Faisal Al-Subaie (Group
  CFO)'`, `'Abdulrahman Al-Ghamdi (BCM Manager)'`, `'Layla Al-Otaibi (BCM Lead, Risk & Resilience)'`)
  — seed-origin, [[F2-207]]'s measured cast of 65. Repair rewrites a live governance row: owner
  decision.

## F2-260 · The finding that coined "existence is weaker than holding" was one of the sites still open

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-260 *(measured 2026-08-20/21. Provenance is [[F2-259]]'s filed §B2b work list. Re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]) mattered twice: [[F2-130]]'s recorded measurement `"CRO does not exist"` had aged — V373 created it in dev and it remains absent in prod — and the block's recorded blocker, `RRP` having no catalogued permission, turned out to be a migration this slice could write rather than an owner decision.)* |
| **Category** | Authorization — a role guard admitting the platform administrator alone, on a module with **no catalogued permission of any kind**, so there was no tenant remedy either |
| **Severity** | **P2.** `POST /api/v1/rrp/cycles/{id}/submit` — the route that lodges the Recovery &amp; Resolution Plan with SAMA — was reachable by the platform administrator and nobody else, in both databases, with no configuration that could change it. |
| **Provenance** | [[F2-259]] filed the three remaining §B2b guards, naming `module.rrp` 1 as *"the SAMA recovery-and-resolution filing V373 itself calls the sharp case, blocked on `RRP` having no catalogued permissions"*. |
| **Current State** | ✔ **FIXED 2026-08-21** (`682052ee`). All three tiers converted to `hasPermission('RRP', READ│WRITE│APPROVE)` across 17 routes — the largest single conversion `BASELINE_PURE_ROLE_SITES` has recorded (380 → **363**); **V383** catalogues the module and grants it; `RrpGuardConversionTest` (6 legs); census §B2b **3 → 2**; MEASURED_BASELINE permission modules 37 → **38** and zero-`hasPermission` packages 10 → **9**. Probed live **13/13 pre-fix and 13/13 post-fix**. **Closes [[F2-130]].** |
| **Problem** | `APPROVE_GUARD` was `hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','CRO','CFO')`. `CRO` and `CFO` are held by **no user** in dev or prod, and `CRO` is **absent from prod's `iam.roles` entirely** because V373 is pending there. A role guard never reaches `ModulePermissionEvaluator`, so it never reaches the PLATFORM_ADMIN bypass either. |
| **Root Cause** | RC-B — object-level authorisation expressed as a role name rather than a permission, compounded by RC-catalogue: the module the guards would have to cite did not exist. Fifth closure of [[F2-253]]'s holder-attrition shape after [[F2-253]], [[F2-254]], [[F2-258]] and [[F2-259]], and the first where the ordinary remedy was unavailable rather than merely ineffective. |
| **Evidence** | `iam.roles` / `iam.user_roles` / `iam.permissions` in **both** databases; the migration set for the catalogue ([[F2-255]]'s rule); the cycle state machine read from `RrpService.ALLOWED`; live probe 13/13 in both modes with pre and post validating each other; pre-fix control RED naming the routes; mutation harness 11 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss; V383 applied twice to dev, prod pre-flighted |

**Finding.** `RrpController` carried three pure role guards over 17 routes:

```
READ     hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','RISK_MANAGER','COMPLIANCE_OFFICER','INTERNAL_AUDITOR',
                    'BCM_MANAGER','BOARD_SECRETARY','CFO','CRO')     -- 7 routes · 3 live non-admin
WRITE    hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','RISK_MANAGER','BCM_MANAGER','CRO')  -- 9 routes · 1 live non-admin
APPROVE  hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','CRO','CFO')                    -- 1 route  · ADMIN ALONE
```

🔑 **Why the APPROVE tier bit rather than merely being narrow.** `/cycles/{id}/transition` carries the
WRITE tier, which `RISK_MANAGER` holds, so a risk manager can drive a cycle
`DRAFT → IN_PREPARATION → BOARD_REVIEW → APPROVED`. `RrpService.transition` then **explicitly refuses**
the `SUBMITTED` edge — *"Use the dedicated /submit endpoint to lodge with SAMA"* — and
`ALLOWED.get("APPROVED")` is `{IN_PREPARATION}`. So for every non-administrator **APPROVED was a dead
end: its only forward edge was the administrator-only submit, and its only other move was backwards
into preparation.** Measured identically in dev and prod: 5 cycles (3 `IN_PREPARATION`, 2 `CLOSED`), 46
critical functions, 31 indicators, 32 recovery options, 14 events — and **no cycle has ever reached
`SUBMITTED`**, for which this guard is a sufficient explanation. Probed live: `rmanager` drove a planted
cycle to APPROVED (200/200/200) and was refused the filing at **403**; so was `compliance`; `admin`
lodged at **200**.

🔑🔑 **THE HEADLINE: [[F2-130]] found this in full on 2026-08-06, coined the distinction the whole
[[F2-253]] → [[F2-259]] lineage rests on, and was itself one of the sites still open.** Its Lesson cell
reads *"Ask of an authorisation list not do these names exist but **can anybody satisfy it today**.
Existence is a weaker question than holding, and the weaker question is the one four findings had been
asking."* That is precisely the question the last five slices have been closing one guard at a time —
and the row that wrote it down stayed 🔴 OPEN for fifteen days. Its stated reason was correct as far as
it went: *"converting to `hasPermission` is F2-05's ratified direction, which makes the names
irrelevant… This is the fourth data point for sequencing F2-05, not a fourth patch."*

⚠⚠ **And its exit condition pointed at the remedy that does not work.** The pin's own trigger read
*"When CRO is created or CFO is granted, close the finding and update this"* — **seating**, and only
that. V373 then chose exactly that remedy for exactly these two roles, and [[F2-258]] measured what it
achieved: seating creates a role and assigns it to nobody, so 79 guard sites became *satisfiable*
rather than satisfied. **`CRO` was created and this finding stayed open**, because creation was never
the thing that mattered. 🔑 **A pin that names three remedies in its prose and phrases its tripwire in
terms of one of them points the next reader at that one** — and the one it named is the one this
register has since had to write two findings to correct.

**What made this different in kind from the four attrition sites.** [[F2-253]] is explicit that an
unheld role *"has an administrator remedy — a remedy, not a defence"*. Here there was no remedy at all:
`RRP` had **no row in `iam.permissions` of any kind**, so nothing could be granted because nothing
existed to grant. [[F2-257]] filed five such modules (`DATACLASS`, `OUTSOURCING`, `REGINSPECT`,
`REGREPORTING`, `RRP`); this closes the first, and it is the first entry in
`MEASURED_BASELINE`'s permission-module row whose module had no catalogue at all beforehand rather than
a partial or mis-derived one. 🔑 Note the direction of travel is the **opposite** of `ETHICS`'s: there
the catalogue existed and no guard consulted it, here the guards existed and there was nothing to cite.
Both end up in that column and only the order tells you which failure it was.

**V383 catalogues exactly the three tiers the controller declares** — read off its three guard
constants, never inferred from method shape, which is V362's landmine (it classified by shape and
promoted whole WRITE tiers to APPROVE in four of six modules, and V367/V368 had to undo it). Check 1b
refuses a fourth `RRP` action so a later tier is a decision rather than a default.

**Grants, per role, measured before converting rather than after** (V362's landmine), identical in both
databases. READ and WRITE are **population-preserving**: every role the old lists named is granted,
including the four held by nobody, so a tenant administrator assigning one still gets what the shipped
guard promised. `RRP:APPROVE` goes to `CRO`, `CFO` and `GRC_ADMINISTRATOR` — the last being the unlock
and the only live holder admitted, chosen because it holds `APPROVE` on `BCM`, `RISK` and `ADMIN` alike
rather than because it was convenient. **So the live audience change is one role on one route.**

⚠⚠ **`RISK_MANAGER` is deliberately withheld from `RRP:APPROVE`, and that is the sharpest decision in
the slice.** It holds `RISK:APPROVE`, so convention argues for it — and the shipped guard pointedly did
not name it: WRITE and APPROVE overlapped on `CRO` and nothing else. Granting it would let the persona
that prepares *and board-approves* the cycle also lodge it with the regulator, retiring the one
separation this controller expresses. V383's **check 4** fails the migration if a second role ever
holds both, and the probe asserts it from the outside: post-fix `rmanager` still gets **403** on submit
while driving the cycle to APPROVED at 200. `AUDITOR`, `VIEWER` and `REGULATOR_VIEWER` are likewise
withheld from READ although all three hold `BCM:READ` and `RISK:READ` — a resolution plan is the most
sensitive document in a bank's contingency set, and the shipped read guard names none of them.

⚠⚠ **A MIGRATION MAY ASSERT ITS OWN WRITES AND MUST NOT ASSERT TENANT DATA.** The natural fifth
self-check was the one this file exists for — *does any active user now hold a role granted
`RRP:APPROVE`?*, [[F2-253]]'s satisfiable-versus-satisfied distinction. It was written and **removed**:
a brand-new deployment runs this chain with a bootstrap administrator and no `GRC_ADMINISTRATOR`
seated, so it would THROW and block V383 and every migration after it — a self-check that fails on
correct usage, which is [[F2-214]] at the schema. The roles V383 *grants* are safe to require because
migrations before it create them (V362 seats `BOARD_SECRETARY` and `CFO`, V373 seats `CRO` — resolved
from the migration set, not assumed); who *holds* them is not. For the same reason check 6's catalogue
floor is **50** rather than the ~140 both live databases carry: [[F2-255]] measured that a fresh Flyway
install from V1 builds only **93** pairs, because 36 core pairs exist in dev and prod solely because
the Python bootstrap made them. So "did this unlock anybody?" is proved by the probe and held by the
gate, and `RrpGuardConversionTest` asserts the absence structurally so the next author does not re-add
it.

⚠⚠ **THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE DETECTOR BUG, IN A THIRD MODULE.**
`RrpLifecycleTest.rolesIn` scanned `'([A-Z_]+)'` across the whole guard initialiser, so
`hasPermission('RRP','READ')` parsed as two role names — `RRP` and `READ`. [[F2-254]] repaired exactly
this in `BiaApprovalChainGuardTest`; [[F2-259]] repaired it in `AuditCommitteeGuardTest.namesIn`; and
here again. 🔑 **A quoted-token scan over a guard expression flags every role-to-permission conversion
[[F2-05]] exists to make**, and each instance has bitten on the slice that converted its own module —
so **the shape recurs once per module because there is no shared primitive.** Measured at **5**
hand-rolled copies across the test tree: `sharia` and `openbanking` were quietly updated when F2-145(e)
converted them, and `cpty` is still latent because its module has not converted. Extracting one helper
is filed ([[F2-190]]: do not hand-roll a fifth).

⚠ **[[F2-225]]'s lesson, arriving from the other side.** F2-130 was held by a **pinned known-defect
test**, which passes on a defective tree by design — so the codebase's own record of this defect was
invisible to every scan, and the finding had to be made twice. Its tripwire then worked exactly as
designed: it failed the build the moment the guards were converted, and `FindingsRegisterConsistencyTest`
required the register cell to move in the same commit. Two instruments in series, both doing their job.

⚙ **Verified correct in passing, and worth recording because this family usually gets it wrong.**
`SubmitCycleRequest.regulatorAckReference` is `@NotBlank` and **caller-supplied** — which is right, not
F2-172(d): a SAMA acknowledgement reference is *received from the authority and recorded*, never minted
by the server, and [[F2-209]]'s own rule says so (*"a reference only an outside authority can issue is
not one the server may mint either"*). `title_ar` is `@NotBlank` on the create, so house rule 7 holds.

**Verification.** Pre-fix control RED naming the routes · live probe **13/13 pre-fix and 13/13
post-fix**, the two runs validating each other because all three tiers are population-preserving by
design and the *only* behavioural difference is the submit unlock (so post-fix code loaded during a
"pre" run would have failed leg 11 rather than passing for the wrong reason) · mutation harness **11
killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss** · V383 applied **twice** to dev, idempotent, with prod
pre-flighted (its `CRO` refusal is check 0 working, since Flyway runs V373 before V383) · cleanup
restored the exact 5/14/31/32/46 baseline in all five `rrp` tables on both runs · suite **4,362/0/0**.

**Filed.**
- §B2b is down to **2**, both `module.bcm`: `BiaQuantitativeController#boardApprove` and
  `#cfoApprove`, [[F2-254]]'s two BIA tiers. Still blocked on a migration rather than on effort —
  `bcm.bia_quantitative` has a caller-supplied `cfo_approver_name` and **no `board_approved_by` column
  at all**, so the four-eyes bar that would make one shared `BCM:APPROVE` safe cannot be built yet.
  [[F2-254]] already recorded that the guard lockout and the missing attribution are one problem that
  F2-52 filed as two.
- **The shared role-name extractor**: 5 hand-rolled copies, 3 of which have now failed on a correct
  conversion, one per converting slice. One test-support helper would make the fourth impossible.
- **[[F2-257]]'s catalogue gap is down to four**: `DATACLASS`, `OUTSOURCING`, `REGINSPECT` and
  `REGREPORTING` still have no `WRITE`/`APPROVE` row in `iam.permissions`. All four are in
  `MEASURED_BASELINE`'s zero-`hasPermission` column, so each is the same two-step this slice was.
  Separately `COMPLIANCE:APPROVE` exists with **0 grants** in both databases — [[F2-253]]'s attrition
  one level up, at the permission rather than the role, like `CPTY:APPROVE`.
- The whole **`rrp` schema has zero CHECK constraints**, so `rrp_cycle.status` is narrowed only by
  `RrpService.ALLOWED` — [[F2-221]]'s shape, and now cheap, since this slice touched the module's
  guards but not its writers ([[F2-183]]: the constraint and its writer land in the same commit).

**Finding.** The controller carried three tiers:

```
READ    hasAnyRole('CISO','RISK_MANAGER','COMPLIANCE_OFFICER','INTERNAL_AUDITOR',
                   'EXTERNAL_AUDITOR','BOARD_SECRETARY','PLATFORM_ADMIN')     -- live: 4 non-admin
WRITE   hasAnyRole('BOARD_SECRETARY','PLATFORM_ADMIN')                        -- live: ADMIN ALONE
ATTEST  hasAnyRole('EXTERNAL_AUDITOR','INTERNAL_AUDITOR','BOARD_SECRETARY',
                   'PLATFORM_ADMIN')                                          -- live: 1 non-admin
```

Probed live pre-fix, 13/13: `compliance` (GRC_ADMINISTRATOR) and `auditor` (INTERNAL_AUDITOR), **both
holding `AUDIT:WRITE`**, answered **403** on all three routes while `admin` generated at 201.
`audit_committee.dashboard_snapshot` holds **0 rows in dev and prod**, and the lockout is a
sufficient explanation for that: the register that exists to hold the committee's reporting artefact
is empty, and the only persona who could ever have filled it is the platform administrator.

🔑🔑 **The headline: this guard had already been corrected for this exact family, and the correction
said so.** F2-52 audited it, found `hasAnyRole('AUDIT_COMMITTEE_CHAIR','COMPANY_SECRETARY',
'PLATFORM_ADMIN')` — two of three names in no database — replaced the ghost `COMPANY_SECRETARY` with
the real `BOARD_SECRETARY`, and wrote into the constant's javadoc:

> 🔑 **`COMPANY_SECRETARY` was a near-miss.** The platform ships `BOARD_SECRETARY` ("Board
> Secretary"), which is that person, and the guard did not name it. Corrected, **which restores one
> of the two intended personas**.

It restored nobody. **Asking whether a recited role EXISTS is not asking whether anybody HOLDS it** —
[[F2-253]]'s distinction, and the same one V373 missed one level up when it chose *seating* as the
remedy and made 79 sites *satisfiable* rather than satisfied ([[F2-258]]). The class-level javadoc
then said the snapshot was *"mutated by the Board Secretary and the platform administrator"*, so
every artefact a reader would consult described a two-persona audience that had only ever been one.

⚠⚠ **And this is why a corrected site is worse than an uncorrected one.** F2-52's own heading on that
constant is *"this said 'restricted to the Chair + Secretary + Platform Admin' and admitted the
platform administrator alone"* — so the file contains a precise description of the defect, immediately
above the defect, presented as history. A ghost name looks wrong in the source; **an unheld real role
looks correct**, and `MEASURED_BASELINE.md` listed the package in its *"zero `hasPermission` usage"*
column with a guard that read as fixed.

**The target was settled by measurement, not preference.** Every peer controller under the same
`@RequireModule("AUDIT_LC")` SKU — `AuditLifecycleController`, `FindingController`, `IaController`,
`AuditEngagementController` — guards with `hasPermission('AUDIT', …)`: **55 of 55 guarded routes**,
unanimous. ⚠ **The SKU code is not the permission module**, and taking it from `@RequireModule` is
what made this look unconvertible: `AUDIT_LC` and `AUDIT_COMMITTEE` have no catalogued permission at
all, and *"none catalogued"* reads exactly like [[F2-255]]'s catalogue gap. The catalogued module is
`AUDIT`.

**Audience diff, measured before converting rather than after** (V362's landmine), identical in both
databases: nothing live dropped; `GRC_ADMINISTRATOR` and `INTERNAL_AUDITOR` admitted; containment
holds (everything admitted also holds `AUDIT:READ`). Internal audit is admitted **deliberately** —
`AUDIT:WRITE` already lets it author the findings, engagements, annual plans and working papers this
snapshot aggregates, and the artefact is internal audit's own reporting pack to its committee. That
is the opposite case from **V380**, where `INTERNAL_AUDITOR` was withheld from the audit-log integrity
seal because operating it would make internal audit the author of the evidence it examines. Stating
which of the two you are in is the whole of that decision.

⚠ **V382 exists because converting alone would have narrowed the shipped audience.**
`BOARD_SECRETARY` held `AUDIT:READ` **and `AUDIT:EXPORT`** and not `AUDIT:WRITE` — so the platform
already let that role read and take out the audit register and withheld only the ability to prepare
its own committee's snapshot. Converting without the grant retires the persona the guard was written
for, which is a policy change disguised as a refactor ([[F2-258]]'s precedent, now a recognised step
rather than a one-off). Live effect **none** — nobody holds the role — so what changes is what a
tenant administrator gets on assigning it, which is exactly the remedy §B2b describes and exactly why
that remedy is not a defence. ⚠ The pre-existing `AUDIT:EXPORT` grant was found by **check 1
THROWing** on a first draft that assumed the set was `{READ}` alone: the migration refused rather
than proceeding on a wrong premise, which is the argument for writing self-checks rather than
comments.

⚠⚠ **Two tiers were measured and deliberately NOT converted, and the reasons point in opposite
directions.**

- **READ** — `hasPermission('AUDIT','READ')` is held by **7 live roles including `VIEWER` and
  `AUDITOR`**, so converting it would widen a governance dashboard's read to any authenticated
  reader. That is precisely the defect `ROLE_GUARD_CENSUS.md` §B3 records against
  `BoardPackController`, where ghost roles sat above a comment saying reads were for *"a
  board/governance audience, not any authenticated principal"* while `REPORTING_READ` admitted
  `viewer`. Four live non-administrator roles already read this dashboard, so there was no lockout
  here to fix.
- **ATTEST** — converting would **drop `EXTERNAL_AUDITOR`**, which holds no `AUDIT` grant at all and
  is the one signatory whose independence is the point; an external auditor may not be a platform
  principal ([[F2-256]]'s `EXTERNAL_AUDIT` rule). It is not a §B2b site either: `INTERNAL_AUDITOR` is
  named and held.

🔑 **A side effect worth naming: the attest tier was WIDER than the tier producing the artefact it
attests to.** Probed pre-fix, `auditor` signed an attestation at **201** against a snapshot it was
refused permission to generate at **403** — so the only reason nobody hit that inversion is that the
register is empty. The conversion closes it, because `INTERNAL_AUDITOR` holds `AUDIT:WRITE`.

⚠⚠ **A PRE-EXISTING GATE FAILED ON THE CORRECT CONVERSION — BOTH ITS LEGS — AND IT IS F2-254'S
FINDING VERBATIM IN A SIBLING FILE.** `AuditCommitteeGuardTest`'s `namesIn()` ran a quoted-token
regex over the **whole** guard expression, so `hasPermission('AUDIT','WRITE')` parsed as two role
names, `AUDIT` and `WRITE`, and `noGuardNamesANonexistentRole` reported them as ghosts. [[F2-254]]
repaired the identical defect in `BiaApprovalChainGuardTest` — **same author slice (F2-52), same
purpose, and this sibling kept the bug**, so a ghost-role detector written as a bare quoted-token
scan flags **every** role-to-permission conversion [[F2-05]] exists to make. Scoped to the argument
list of `hasAnyRole(…)` / `hasRole(…)`, which is the shape its claim is about. 🔑 **A gate that fails
on correct code is worse than no gate: it trains the next reader to edit the assertion rather than
the code** ([[F2-214]]) — and here the assertion it would have trained them to edit is a *ghost-role*
assertion.

⚙ **The control for a detector repair is mechanical now, not argued.** [[F2-254]]'s rule is that the
repaired detector must still answer the same on the tree the original passed on; a new leg asserts
exactly that, against the **literal pre-fix and post-fix guard shapes** plus a composed guard (whose
role leg must still be seen — the shape [[F2-159]]/[[F2-161]] controls are built from) and a
three-argument ownership guard (which names no role). Its anti-vacuity floor moved 13 → **11** with
the reason recorded, because the write tier now recites no role at all.

⚙ **`role_guard_census.py` took `--database`**, closing a gap [[F2-253]] and [[F2-258]] each filed:
`DATABASE=TSS_GRC` was hardcoded, so every holder figure the report has ever published described
**dev** while reading as a statement about the platform. The report now names the database it read,
and says why that matters — two databases differ by **absence** as well as by holders, because a role
a pending migration has not seated is missing from `iam.roles` on the deployed server and merely
unheld in dev.

⚠ **The mutation harness found one real weakness in my own gate.** The peer-convention leg was
`anyMatch(guard contains "hasPermission('AUDIT',")`, and moving **two of `FindingController`'s five**
routes off the permission left three still citing it, so the leg **SURVIVED while the convention it
certifies was eroding**. The mutated code was not wrong about the claim I had written — the claim was
weaker than the leg's purpose. Replaced by the negative form that actually holds (measured 55 of 55):
**no peer route may be a *pure* role guard**, which kills the mutation, tolerates a legitimate
composed or record-ownership guard ([[F2-254]]: never ban `hasAnyRole` outright), and tolerates
routes being added. An anti-vacuity floor of 50 rides with it so a renamed or emptied peer class
cannot make every assertion above it pass over nothing.

**Verification.** Pre-fix control RED naming all three routes · live probe **13/13 pre-fix and 13/13
post-fix** as `compliance`/`auditor`/`viewer`/`rmanager` against a snapshot the probe plants itself
([[F2-206]]), cleaned back to the measured 0/0 baseline in a `finally` by `CHARINDEX` with the child
rows removed by parent id ([[F2-257]]) · mutation harness **9 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss** ·
V382 applied **twice** to dev with prod pre-flighted clean · suite **4,356/0/0**.

**Filed.**
- The **three** remaining §B2b guards, still a work list with **no verdicts** ([[F2-188]]):
  `module.bcm` 2 (`BiaQuantitativeController#boardApprove`/`#cfoApprove` — [[F2-254]]'s two BIA
  tiers, blocked on a migration, since `bcm.bia_quantitative` has no `board_approved_by` column) and
  `module.rrp` 1 (`RrpController#submit`, the SAMA recovery-and-resolution filing V373 itself calls
  the sharp case, blocked on `RRP` having no catalogued permissions — [[F2-257]]'s gap).
- **[[F2-151]] is unchanged and is now the only thing standing between this surface and a real
  committee control.** The Chair leg still cannot be expressed: `admin.committee_member_terms
  .member_user_id` is NULL on **all five** audit-committee seats in **both** databases, so
  [[F2-177]]'s `hasPermission('AUDIT_COMMITTEE','COMMITTEE','SEAT')` would answer false for everyone
  ([[F2-178]]'s measurement, re-confirmed) — a control that cannot fire ([[F2-112]]'s shape). And
  `AttestRequest.attestedRole` is still **self-declared**: an admitted `INTERNAL_AUDITOR` can record
  an attestation as `CHAIR`, because the signer's identity is stamped from the principal and hashed
  while the capacity they signed in is checked against nothing. Both halves need the same roster
  linkage; seating those five terms is a **tenant data task**, not a jar.
- `GenerateSnapshotRequest.snapshotCode` is caller-supplied — F2-172(d)'s family on a code an
  auditor cites. ⚠ **Read, not assumed: it is collision-safe** (`UQ_ac_snap_code` exists and the
  service appends a uniqueness suffix rather than throwing, deliberately, because "two snapshots in a
  day" is a legitimate workflow). So it is a naming question, not a defect.
- `audit_committee` has **2 CHECK constraints** and both agree with their DTO `@Pattern`
  ([[F2-180]]'s check, performed rather than assumed): `CK_ac_snap_meeting_type` and
  `CK_ac_att_role`. Nothing owed here.

## F2-258 · The remedy chosen for these routes in a migration, and the reason it did not move them

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-258 *(measured 2026-08-20. Provenance is [[F2-255]]'s filing. Re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]) changed the answer twice: the filed conversion target `AI:APPROVE` **does not exist**, and the population is **six** routes rather than the three the filing named — the three creates share the defect at one role's distance.)* |
| **Category** | Authorization — a role guard whose named roles are held by nobody, where the platform's *chosen remedy already shipped* and left the route exactly as closed as it found it |
| **Severity** | **P2.** Three `POST …/transition` routes on the ISO/IEC 42001 AI model-lifecycle register were reachable by the platform administrator and **nobody else**, and the three creates beside them by one other role. All six are wired to routed pages, so the Move control on `AiLifecycleValidationsPage`, `AiLifecycleRetrainingsPage` and `AiLifecycleRecertificationsPage` answered 403 for every non-administrator, over 16 validations / 11 retraining events / 13 recertifications identical in dev and prod. |
| **Provenance** | [[F2-255]] filed *"`module.ai`'s three transitions are still administrator-only (`CRO`/`CIO`/`DPO` all 0 holders, `CIO`/`CRO` ghosts in prod) with 15 live rows in each database"*, and reasoned that collapsing them onto `AI:WRITE` retires nothing. |
| **Current State** | ✔ **FIXED 2026-08-20** (`1d074539`). Six routes converted to one `hasPermission('AI','WRITE')`; the READ tier deliberately left as a role guard; **V381** grants `AI:READ` + `AI:WRITE` to `CIO` and `CRO` so the conversion drops nobody; `AiLifecycleGuardConversionTest` (6 legs) and `BASELINE_PURE_ROLE_SITES` 389 → 383. Probed live 13/13 pre-fix and 13/13 post-fix. |
| **Problem** | `hasAnyRole` tests for a **granted authority** and gets no `PLATFORM_ADMIN` bypass, so a role assigned to no user admits nobody. `CIO`, `CRO` and `DPO` are held by no user in either database. |
| **Root Cause** | RC-B — object-level authorisation expressed as a role name rather than as a permission, where the role's holder set is the thing nobody measured. Third recorded instance of [[F2-253]]'s holder-attrition shape being closed, after [[F2-253]] itself and [[F2-254]]. |
| **Evidence** | `iam.user_roles` / `iam.role_permissions` in **both** databases, the migration set for the catalogue ([[F2-255]]'s rule), live probe 13/13 both modes, pre-fix control firing on 1 of 6 legs naming all six routes, mutation harness 8 killed / 0 survived |

**Finding.** `AiLifecycleController` carried three tiers of role guard:

```
READ     hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','RISK_MANAGER','COMPLIANCE_OFFICER','AUDITOR','CISO','DPO','CIO','CRO')
WRITE    hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','RISK_MANAGER','CIO','DPO')          -- the three creates
APPROVE  hasAnyRole('PLATFORM_ADMIN','CRO','CIO','DPO')                   -- the three transitions
```

Measured in dev **and** prod ([[F2-253]]'s rule — the census script hardcodes `DATABASE=TSS_GRC`, so
every figure it has ever published is a statement about dev): `CIO` **0 holders**, `CRO` **0**, `DPO`
**0**; `CIO`/`CRO` are additionally absent from prod's `iam.roles` because V373 is among the pending
migrations. So the APPROVE tier admitted `PLATFORM_ADMIN` alone and the WRITE tier admitted it plus
`RISK_MANAGER`.

Probed live before the change (13 legs, personas resolved from `iam.role_permissions` rather than
guessed, against rows the probe planted itself — [[F2-206]]):

| leg | persona | route | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | `rmanager` (holds `AI:WRITE`) | validation `IN_PROGRESS → PASSED` | **403** | 200 |
| T2 | `compliance` (holds `AI:WRITE`) | retraining `PROPOSED → APPROVED` | **403** | 200 |
| T3 | `rmanager` | recertification `DUE → IN_REVIEW` | **403** | 200 |
| C1 | `compliance` | create a validation | **403** | 200 |
| N1 | `auditor` (READ tier, no `AI:WRITE`) | transition | 403 | **403** |
| N2 | `viewer` (neither) | create | 403 | **403** |
| A1 | `admin` | transition | 200 | 200 |

**🔑 The platform had already chosen a remedy for these exact routes, and it shipped, and it did not
move them.** V373 — *"F2-52: seat CIO and CRO, the two executive identities 79 guard sites already
recite"* — names `AiLifecycleController#transition` in its own header and describes it, before the
fix, in the words this finding would use: *"the same shape"* as `RrpController#submit`, which it
calls *"reachable by the platform administrator and nobody else"*. It chose remedy (3), seating,
over remedy (1), conversion. Seating creates the **role**; it assigns it to **nobody**. Its closing
line is the tell — *"79 guard sites and 4 attachment role lists are now **satisfiable**"* — which is
[[F2-253]]'s distinction exactly: satisfiable is not satisfied, and `hasAnyRole` asks for a granted
authority. Dev has held `CIO` and `CRO` with **0 grants of any module** ever since.

**🔑🔑 And the reason it picked the wrong remedy here is that the measurement it made was about four
other modules.** V373's reasoning:

> *"Unavailable: DATACLASS, OUTSOURCING, REGREPORTING and RRP have **NO catalogued permissions at
> all** (measured against `iam.permissions`), so converting means first cataloguing four new
> modules, which is a V362-scale decision about who may do what and not a name fix."*

True of those four — verified, all four still have no `WRITE`/`APPROVE` row in `iam.permissions`
today ([[F2-257]] filed that half). **Not true of the fifth**, which it swept in by resemblance one
sentence earlier (*"`AiLifecycleController#transition` … is the same shape"*), and then justified on
a **different and circular** ground:

> *"of the five modules involved only AI is catalogued at all, where AiLifecycleController is
> role-guarded anyway, so any grant would be inert."*

The grant was inert **because the guard was a role guard**, which is the half that could change.
`AI:READ`/`WRITE`/`EXPORT` have been catalogued since **V313** and `AI:WRITE` is held by **8 live
roles** in both databases. This is [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N at the level of a *remedy*: the same defect
shape across five modules, four of which genuinely could not be converted, and the sentence that says
*"the same shape"* is what stops a reader asking whether the same remedy applies.

**The fix, and the two things it deliberately does not do.**

Six routes now carry one constant, `hasPermission('AI','WRITE')` — the module's own convention, which
`AiSuggestionController` has used since it was written.

*One constant and not two.* Deciding a validation is a different act from filing one, and this
controller no longer distinguishes them, so it says so with one name rather than two identical
strings. Merging retires nothing that existed: the two role sets already overlapped on `CIO` and
`DPO`, and no transition in `AiLifecycleService` compares the acting principal against the record's
author — checked, not assumed. A real maker/checker bar needs an `AI:APPROVE` the catalogue does not
define **plus** an actor comparison, which is a V362-scale access decision. **Filed.**

*The READ tier stays a role guard, and this is the load-bearing measurement.* `AUDITOR` is named on
it, **is** held, and holds `AI:EXPORT` and **not** `AI:READ` — the only role in either database with
that shape, and deliberate, since `MlModelController.EXPORT_GUARD` is
`hasPermission('AI','EXPORT') and hasAnyRole(…,'AUDITOR',…)`. So `hasPermission('AI','READ')` here
would take the tier from five live roles to four and **drop the examiner**. That is [[F2-253]]'s
asymmetry — correcting a role guard on the write side widens access and doing it on the read side can
narrow it, so the two halves are not one sweep — and
`AiLifecycleGuardConversionTest.theReadTierIsDeliberatelyStillARoleGuard` fails the build if somebody
finishes it, the same leg [[F2-254]] added for the BCM reads after making the same measurement.

**V381, and why a guard conversion needed a migration.** Of the names the retired lists carried,
`DPO` already held `AI:WRITE`; `CIO` and `CRO` held **no module permission at all**. Converting
without a grant would therefore have **narrowed the shipped audience by two roles**, and narrowing a
shipped default is a policy change rather than a fix. V381 grants `AI:READ` + `AI:WRITE` to both, as
**declared literals** with five self-checks that `THROW` (the repo's grant landmine: the
`INSERT … SELECT … JOIN … WHERE NOT EXISTS` idiom grants nothing when either side is catalogued later
and cannot tell *already granted* from *nothing matched*). Live effect today: **none** — both roles
are held by nobody, so nothing about who can act changes; what changes is what a tenant administrator
gets when they assign one, which before this was 79 role guards and no permission-driven screen at
all. The one measured widening is stated rather than left as a side effect (the V362 landmine):
`AI:WRITE` also opens **7** `AiSuggestionController` routes these two were not named on.

**Instrument.** `AiLifecycleGuardConversionTest`, six legs, **reflective over `@PreAuthorize`** rather
than a source scan — the annotation takes a compile-time constant, so reflection sees the resolved
expression and cannot be fooled by a constant being renamed or moved ([[F2-187]]). It asserts the
write tier by **claim** (a permission guard citing `AI`/`WRITE`) rather than by banning the word
`hasAnyRole`, because [[F2-254]] had two pre-existing gates fail on a *correct* conversion for exactly
that reason and a gate that fails on correct code trains the next reader to edit the assertion
([[F2-214]]). It also resolves `AI:WRITE` from the **migration set**, never a database ([[F2-255]]),
and requires V381's four triples to still be literals.

⚠ **Two of my own gate legs were wrong, and the mutation harness found both.**

1. `contains("THROW 51381")` **SURVIVED** the mutation that removed check 0 — V381 carries **five**
   THROWs, so deleting the one that matters left four satisfying the assertion.
   [[F2-194]]'s substring-satisfied-by-something-else, in a gate written after quoting it. Replaced by
   a **count** plus check 0's own message anchor.
2. The mutation making the guard reader skip unguarded methods **SURVIVED**, and the mutated code was
   not wrong on this corpus — every route is guarded, so it returns the identical map ([[F2-206]]).
   That is an equivalent mutant, and the fix is a **synthetic fixture**: a nested controller with a
   mapped, unguarded method, asserted to be *reported* rather than skipped ([[F2-195]]). 🔑 **A reader
   that omits what it cannot explain shrinks its own population, and a smaller population reads
   exactly like a cleaner tree.**

After both: **8 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss**, and the pre-fix control fires naming all six
routes exactly.

⚠ **A third of my own errors were in the harness, not the gate.** The escape-collapse landmine fired
**twice in one slice** through inline `py -c` inside Bash — once producing `\(\s*` in a Java string
(a loud `javac` error) and once a raw newline inside a Python string literal (a `SyntaxError` that a
`sed` filter then swallowed, so the harness appeared to produce no output at all). The recorded rule
is to use the Write/Edit tools for any file content carrying escapes; it applies to inline `py -c`
exactly as it does to a heredoc.

⚠ **And one assertion of mine was wrong about the codebase rather than the reverse:**
`contains("'AI', 'WRITE'")` failed because V313 writes `('AI','WRITE',` with no space. An assertion
that depends on a formatting choice fails on a correct tree the day somebody reformats the file, so it
is now a whitespace-tolerant parse.

⚙ **Also corrected, in passing:** `RoleGuardConversionRatchetTest`'s javadoc stated
*"`BASELINE_PURE_ROLE_SITES` is 404"* while the constant read 389 — the prose-versus-constant drift
CLAUDE.md warns about, in the file that owns the constant. And the ceiling is lowered to **383** in
the same commit as the conversion, re-derived from this build rather than subtracted, because
[[F2-207]] recorded what happens when a sweep lands and its ceiling stays: a tolerated guard becomes
indistinguishable from a reviewed one.

**Filed.**

- **The four-eyes question this conversion makes askable.** Creating an AI model validation and
  deciding it are now one permission. They already were, in effect — the role sets overlapped and no
  transition compares the actor — but a real separation is now a small, well-defined change:
  catalogue `AI:APPROVE`, guard the three transitions with it, and compare the deciding principal
  against `validator_user_id` / `owner_user_id` / the creator. Whether an ISO/IEC 42001 recertification
  *should* require a second person is an **owner decision**, and [[F2-256]] already filed that
  `model_validation` has no completer column and `retraining_event` no approver column at all.
- **§B2b is now 6, and it is a work list with no verdicts** ([[F2-188]]): `module.audit_committee` 3
  (`BOARD_SECRETARY`, 0 holders — a committee-seat question, so [[F2-177]]'s
  `hasPermission('AUDIT_COMMITTEE','COMMITTEE','SEAT')` may be the right mechanism rather than a
  module permission), `module.bcm` 2 (the two BIA approval tiers [[F2-254]] measured and left, blocked
  on a migration — `bcm.bia_quantitative` has no `board_approved_by` column), `module.rrp` 1
  (`RrpController#submit`, the SAMA recovery-and-resolution filing V373's own header calls the sharp
  case — blocked on `RRP` having no catalogued permissions, i.e. [[F2-257]]'s filed catalogue gap).
- **`AiLifecycleService`'s three creates honour a client-supplied `reference`** — `@NotBlank String
  reference` on all three request records, `setReference(req.reference())` in all three creates, on the
  register an ISO/IEC 42001 assurance reader cites. F2-172(d)'s family in the
  `SubprocessorService.create` shape [[F2-253]] filed: the field is *mandatory*, so there is no
  null-coalesce and it sits outside `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest`'s
  `setExternalId`/`setRefNumber` key. No UNIQUE index on any of the three `reference` columns, so a
  duplicate is storable.
- **`role_guard_census.py` still hardcodes `DATABASE=TSS_GRC`**, so §B2b and every holder figure it
  publishes is a statement about **dev**. [[F2-253]] filed this; it cost a re-measurement here (prod
  has `CIO`/`CRO` absent rather than unheld, because V373 is pending). One parameter.
- **`ai_governance` still has zero CHECK constraints** on all three registers' `status` columns
  ([[F2-256]]'s filing). Now cheaper for the three that this slice's converted routes write, but the
  vocabularies are declared only in `VAL_ALLOWED`/`RET_ALLOWED`/`REC_ALLOWED` and
  `StateMachineColumnMirrorTest` would be the instrument.

## F2-257 · Ten timeline registers recorded WHICH user acted and never WHAT they are called

| Field | Content |
|---|---|

Re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]) corrected it twice: the filing said **nine** registers and its own javadoc **listed ten**, and it claimed *"every timeline entry renders a blank actor"* when no screen in the platform renders any of these ten actors.)* |
| **Category** | Attribution — a register that records WHICH user acted and never WHAT they are called, publishing a response field nothing can fill · and the question of whether a label is a **copy** of the id's identity or information the id cannot express |
