## F2-252 · Editing a cyber control destroyed its framework link, and a five-name dropdown stood in for the register

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-252 *(measured 2026-08-20 while executing [[F2-251]]'s filed 28-member census — re-derived from the shipped gate's own stdout first, per [[F2-221]])* |
| **Category** | Data integrity — a full-replace write whose payload builder omitted the field · an unresolved, untenanted soft foreign key · a hard-coded vocabulary standing in for a live register |
| **Severity** | **P1 for the destruction.** `framework_id` is populated on **75 of 75** live cyber controls in dev and prod, and editing any control through the platform's own screen NULLED it at HTTP 200 — while leaving `framework_name` standing, so the register still rendered the framework and only a join could tell. A control with no framework link is invisible to every coverage question asked of the register, which for an NCA ECC self-assessment is the question. **P2** for the unresolved reference (another tenant's framework accepted) and **P3** for the dropdown. |
| **Provenance** | Not sought. [[F2-251]]'s filing named 28 census members and said *"classify before reading"*. Ranking them by the cheapest universal fact — id NULL while the label is populated ([[F2-250]]) — put every remaining `change_mgmt` member at **0 rows in dev and NO TABLE in prod**, so the live weight was elsewhere. `cyber.cyber_controls :: framework_id + framework_name` was the largest fully-populated member and had been filed by [[F2-247]] as *latent*. Re-measuring a recorded blocker before believing its estimate ([[F2-178]]) is what found the destruction, which is not in that family at all. |
| **Current State** | ✔ **FIXED 2026-08-20.** `CyberFrameworkReferenceResolver` resolves the reference in-tenant; `CyberControlService.applyFrameworkReference` is the pair's single writer, derives the label from the resolved framework, refuses a contradicting label and accepts an echo; an omitted id on UPDATE leaves the stored link alone. `CyberPage` carries `frameworkId` in both payload builders and picks from the tenant's real register. |
| **Problem** | Three defects on one pair. **(1) The destruction:** `CyberPage`'s `CONTROL_EMPTY` and `controlToReq` carried `frameworkName` and **no `frameworkId`**, while `applyEditable` wrote both columns unconditionally — so an omitted key arrived null and was written null. **(2) The unresolved reference:** a nonexistent id (999999) and **another tenant's** framework were both stored at HTTP 200. The column carries no FOREIGN KEY, and `CyberFrameworkRepository.findByIdAndOrganisationId` has existed since SEC-CYB-001 and was never called from this path. **(3) The lying label:** `frameworkId = 1` ("NCA ECC") stored beside `frameworkName = 'ISO 27001'`. |
| **Root Cause** | An entity-bound full-replace `PUT` (one of the 94 [[F2-239]] measured) whose client type declares a field the client's payload builder never sends. `CyberControlRequest` has always declared `frameworkId`; nothing asserted that anything sent it. |
| **Business Impact** | A cyber control's framework attribution is what makes the register answerable — *"how many ECC controls are implemented?"* is a join on `framework_id`. Every edit silently removed one row from that answer while the screen kept showing the framework, so the register degraded in the flattering direction with no visible event. The cross-tenant half is a dangling reference rather than a leak (the row is still stamped with the caller's org), but it points a Saudi tenant's control at another tenant's framework record. |
| **Technical Impact** | `FullReplaceUpdateContractTest` passes over this: its structural leg bans a method that loads a `T` and persists its own `T` parameter, and `updateControl` persists the loaded row; its coverage leg asks whether a written field is *declarable* by the frontend type, and `frameworkId` is. **That is [[F2-212]]'s headline exactly — a wire-contract gate proves the TYPES agree and cannot prove the payload BUILDER sends what the type permits, and on a full-replace verb that gap is silent data destruction.** |
| **UX Impact** | The control form's framework dropdown was five hard-coded names: NCA ECC, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST CSF, SAMA CSF. The tenant's register holds six: NCA ECC, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, **NCA CCC, NCA CSCC, NCA OTCC**. Only three were in both — `NIST CSF` and `SAMA CSF` name frameworks this register does not have, and three registered frameworks with real controls filed against them could not be selected at all. [[F2-180]]'s shape in both directions at once, and the page's own comment 400 lines below says *"the register carries four NCA frameworks (ECC 29, CCC 24, …)"* while the dropdown offered one. |
| **Recommendation** | 1. As shipped. 2. **An owner decision remains: which framework register is authoritative for a cyber control.** There are two, and they are disjoint (see Trade-offs). 3. Add a FOREIGN KEY on `cyber.cyber_controls.framework_id`, now cheap because this commit closed the column's only open writers ([[F2-183]]'s rule) — but it must wait on (2), since the constraint names the register. |
| **Alternatives** | Relinking by NAME when the caller sends a label and no id was considered and rejected: this pair's whole hazard is that two registers share an id space and carry near-identical names ("NCA ECC" here, "NCA Essential Cybersecurity Controls" there), so a name lookup is the least safe operation available. A caller that wants a different framework sends its id; an echo of the stored label is accepted so a round-tripping form keeps working ([[F2-231]]/[[F2-234]]). |
| **Trade-offs** | ⚠⚠ **Two disjoint framework registers with OVERLAPPING id spaces**, both live and identical in dev and prod: `cyber.cyber_frameworks` (6 rows, tenant-owned) and `compliance.frameworks` (24 rows, **global** — no `organisation_id` — W2-1a-i's ratified regulator catalogue). Ids 1–6 exist in both and name **different frameworks**: id 2 is "ISO 27001" here and "NCA Cloud Cybersecurity Controls" there. V342 added a FOREIGN KEY on `framework_id` for the five tables that point at `compliance.frameworks` and this column got none, because it points at the other one. Picking a winner rewrites live rows and changes what the platform reports about NCA ECC coverage — **an owner decision**, [[F2-196]]'s shape. |
| **Effort** | **S** — one resolver, one writer, one client, one picker. No migration; V379 remains head. |
| **Priority** | Done. |
| **Verification** | Live probe **8/8 pre-fix and 8/8 post-fix** as `so_officer` (`CYBER:READ` + `CYBER:WRITE`; `admin` proves nothing about authorization) against controls the probe **planted itself** ([[F2-206]]), hard-deleted with `CHARINDEX` in a `finally`, residue 0, and the 75 seeded rows byte-identical after all eight legs. Pre-fix: the form's own payload NULLED `framework_id` (200), a lying label was stored beside a real id (200), 999999 was stored (200), **another tenant's framework was stored (200)**, and an id with no label stored a NULL label. Post-fix: 400 for all four, the label DERIVED, the link preserved on an omitted id, a bare label still legal. `CyberControlFrameworkReferenceTest` **14/14**. Pre-fix detector control **8/8 discriminating, 0 silent**. Mutation harness **10 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss**. Backend suite **4,305/0/0**, frontend **805/805** in 74 files, `tsc --noEmit` clean. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-20** — the three defects. The authoritative-register question and the FOREIGN KEY are filed as owner decisions. |
| **References** | `module/cyber/service/CyberFrameworkReferenceResolver` (new), `CyberControlService#applyFrameworkReference`, `CyberControlService#applyEditable`, `module/cyber/controller/CyberController` (`POST`/`PUT /api/v1/cyber/controls`), `tss-grc-ui-v2/src/pages/cyber/CyberPage.tsx` (`CONTROL_EMPTY`, `controlToReq`, `submitControl`, `CONTROL_FIELDS`), `lib/api.ts` (`CyberFrameworkDto`, `cyberApi.frameworks`), `CyberControlFrameworkReferenceTest`, `ParentIdentityCopyContractTest` |
| **Lesson** | 🔑🔑 **A SOFT FOREIGN KEY WHOSE ID SPACE IS VALID IN TWO REGISTERS DEREFERENCES CLEANLY AGAINST THE WRONG ONE AND LIES.** [[F2-246]] established that a scan locates and *the pairing is the measurement*; this gives that rule a mechanism. My first divergence pass guessed `compliance.frameworks` as the parent and reported **75 of 75 rows divergent** — a complete, plausible, entirely false finding, with example rows naming real frameworks. Measured against the register the rows actually use, the same 75 **agree**. A wrong pairing here cannot fail loudly: it joins, and it produces a name. **So derive the parent column — compare the child's label against EVERY text column of every candidate parent and report the agreement rate — rather than picking the column whose name looks right.** Done that way the answer was unambiguous (75/75 with `cyber.cyber_frameworks.name`, 0/75 with anything in `compliance.frameworks`), and it also refuted three of my other four apparent divergences: `evidence.evidence_items.collector_name`, `bcm.mtpd_inheritance_finding.vendor_name` and `change_mgmt.change_approvals.approver_name` are **not copies of any parent column** — they hold offices and role descriptions, which is [[F2-251]]'s third kind of census member. **4 of 4 of my guessed pairings were wrong.** 🔑 **And the finding that mattered was not in the family I came to fix.** The census pair turned out to be latent-and-correct on all 75 rows; the P1 was one line above it, in a method whose javadoc had already been written by [[F2-213]] to explain why *this* register was the safe member of *that* family (*"the one member of the family that was NOT losing data"*). It was safe from the defect F2-213 measured and not from the one its own client caused. **A javadoc certifying a method against one family reads as certifying it, and the next reader does not ask which family.** ⚙ Two smaller ones. The mutation harness produced one **EQUIVALENT** mutant worth keeping rather than counting: taking the tenant from `c.getOrganisationId()` instead of the caller's `orgId` survives, because the stamp precedes the resolution — which is exactly how [[F2-246]]'s 404-on-every-linked-create was safe in three registers "by accident of statement order", so it is now banned structurally. And **`JAVA_HOME` unset made a stale surefire report read as a fresh failure**: `mvn -o test` on JDK 11 dies in `build-info` before running anything, leaves the previous run's report on disk, and prints `BUILD FAILURE` — so the four failures I read were the *earlier* run's, and I nearly fixed them twice. |

## F2-251 · Capturing one party's id retired the only bar that could decide another

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-251 |
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-20 |
| **Severity** | P2 |
| **Area** | `module/change_mgmt` — `change_mgmt.change_requests`, the ITIL change register, and its five self-review refusals |
| **Found by** | executing F2-250's filed census work list; ranking by *id NULL while the label is populated* put the change register's two people pairs top among the unblocked members |

Re-deriving the census (F2-221) gave **48 pairs, 32 unadjudicated**. Ranked by the cheapest
universal fact — *id NULL while the label is populated*, which needs no parent pairing (F2-246) —
`change_mgmt` held **13 of the 32**, and its two change-register pairs were the sharpest unblocked
members.

### The measurement changed the fix

Identical in dev and prod, measured 2026-08-20:

| | |
|---|---|
| live changes | **17** dev, **15** prod |
| `requested_by_id` populated | **2** of 17 dev, **0** of 15 prod |
| `change_owner_id` populated | **0 of 17** and **0 of 15** — the column has **no writer anywhere in the platform** |
| requester labels | 15 populated, 13 distinct, **0 resolving to a platform user** |
| owner labels | 15 populated, 15 distinct, **0 resolving to a platform user** |
| the labels themselves | `'CIO Office'`, `'Group Legal'`, `'AppSec'`, `'FCC Head'`, `'Head of IAM'`, `'Chief People Officer'`, `'AppSec on-call'` |
| live rows whose label equals an active username | **0** — so a fix that refuses *more* cannot break a working request (F2-214) |

🔑🔑 **On these two pairs the label is NOT a copy of the id's identity, and
`create()`'s own CE-15 comment says so:** the id is who keyed the change in, and
`requested_by_name` is *"whatever the tenant typed, since a team ('CloudOps') is a legitimate thing
to record as the requesting party even though it is not a person."* So deriving one half from the
other would **destroy information**, and the defect is in the **READERS**.

🔑 **That is a third kind of member for this census, and the census's own framing is what
disguised it.** `ParentIdentityCopyContractTest` measures *"a parent id AND a copy of that parent's
identity"*; here the second half is an independent fact, so every earlier remedy in the family
(derive the label — F2-245, F2-246, F2-250) is the wrong move. **Ask whether the label is a copy
before reaching for the fix that worked last time.**

### The live defect: three refusals, three different ways of keying the fallback

`change_owner_id` has no writer, so the owner is nameable **only** by label. Of the module's five
self-review refusals:

| refusal | how it compared | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `assertNotSelfWaiver` | `ChangeSoD` with **merged** `Party(id, label)` | the owner's label bar worked (its id is always null); the *requester's* did not |
| `assertNotSelfSatisfaction` | `ChangeSoD` with **merged** `Party(id, label)` | latent — `change_condition` holds 0 rows in dev and does not exist in prod |
| `assertPirReviewerIsNotImplementer` | one name bar | **correct**, and only because `implementer_name` has no id column at all |
| `recordApproval` (CM-C2, the CAB vote) | **hand-written**, fallback keyed on **both ids being null** | dead from the commit that began stamping `requested_by_id` |
| `requireRatificationSeparation` (ADR-017 D-3) | **hand-written**, fallback keyed on **the ACTOR having no id** | dead for **every** caller — `GrcUserDetails` always carries an id |

Probed live as `rmanager` (`CHANGE:APPROVE`) against **planted** rows (F2-206), **8/8 pre-fix**:

| leg | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| the change **OWNER** casts a CAB vote on their own change | **HTTP 201** | 409 |
| the identical vote, identical shape, `requested_by_id` NULLed | 409 | 409 |
| the **OWNER** ratifies their own emergency change (legacy row — no id excuse) | **HTTP 200** | 409 |
| the adjacent **waiver** gate refuses the same person on the same change | 409 | 409 |

🔑🔑 **Capturing the raiser's id — CE-15's improvement — is what switched the owner's
bar off.** The two legs differ in exactly one column, and the one that refuses is the one where
*less* was captured. A change that strictly improves the record removed a refusal.

🔑 **And the gate that held was the one routed through the primitive.** `ChangeSoD` exists,
in its own words, as *"the platform's one answer to 'is the acting principal the same person as
this named party?'"*, and its class javadoc says **a second copy *"lies the first time one copy
learns something the others do not."*** One of three gates over the change's people was converted
to it; **the two that were not are the two that lie.** The prediction and the failure are in the
same file.

⚠ **The rule the copies broke is stated in the primitive's own javadoc**, under
`compareAny`: *"the caller build one party **per bar** rather than per person — `Party(id, null)`
and `Party(null, label)` as separate entries, **never `Party(id, label)`**. Merging them re-engages
rule 1 … which is a refusal removed by a change that looks like a tidy-up."* Every caller in the
module was building the merged form or a hand-written equivalent of it. **A rule with no
enforcement is a rule two of five sites follow.**

### The fix

One predicate, one party per bar. `selfReviewBars` / `cabDecisionBars` / `conditionOwnerBars` each
build an **id bar and a name bar per person**, so no bar can be switched off by another party
carrying an id. The conversion only ever *adds* refusals — asserted in both directions, and safe
because 0 live rows have a label equal to an active username.

⚠ **No escalation to report, and say so.** `CHANGE:APPROVE` guards the CAB vote, the ratification
and the waiver alike; `CHANGE:WRITE` guards create/update. Nothing crossed a permission boundary —
the object-level machine was the only control and two of its three bars were inert (F2-219's shape).

### The instrument: a report whose population was a list somebody wrote

`GET /api/v1/changes/sod-coverage` was built by CE-15 to answer *"which of these gates can actually
decide anything?"* — the question F2-112 needed asked after a shipped refusal turned out never to
have been able to fire. It published **four** gates. The module enforces **six** refusals, and
🔑 **the two absent were the two that could not fire.** Both were enforced, unit-tested and
shipped, so nothing looked unfinished, and the one artefact that would have surfaced them had them
outside its scope **by construction**.

🔑 **The instrument was real; its POPULATION was `ChangeSoD.GATES`.** This codebase has been
caught by that narrowing at a filename, a three-entry allow-list, a module name, an `extends`
clause, a field-name list inside a fix and a claim shape in a gate; a gate list is the next
spelling. `ChangeSodGateCoverageContractTest` now **derives** the population from the refusals
themselves — a method that throws on a `ChangeSoD` verdict — enforced in both directions, with
`GATES` grown to seven: `GATE_CAB_VOTE_NOT_REQUESTER`, `GATE_RATIFIER_NOT_REQUESTER` and
`GATE_RATIFIER_NOT_APPROVER` join the four that were there. The ratifier's two are **separate on
purpose** — ratifying a change you raised is one conflict and ratifying your own emergency approval
is another, and a merged test would report the wrong one.

⚠ **`Coverage`'s javadoc described `labelOnly` as *"records where it carries only a free-text
label, so the gate is UNVERIFIABLE"*. That is false** — rule 2 compares a label-only party by name
and returns SAME or DIFFERENT, which is the whole reason a legacy row can be refused at all.
🔑 **And that false sentence is exactly the belief the two hand-written copies encoded as
"legacy fallback only": a description that answers the question a reader was about to ask is how a
wrong belief propagates into code** (F2-184's shape, in an instrument's own documentation).

### What my own instruments caught, and what that cost

- ⚠⚠ **The derivation refuted my map on its first run: 5 refusals, not 3.** Two of my three
  exemption reasons said the refusal *"sits outside `selfReviewBars`"* — **true, and not the
  question the scan asks**, which is whether the method throws on a `ChangeSoD` verdict. Both do.
  🔑 **An exemption that answers a different question from the one the scan asks reads exactly
  like a correct exemption.** Two in three fell, against this programme's usual ~2-in-10 (F2-188,
  F2-192, F2-204, F2-211, F2-250). The **reverse** leg caught it — the direction nobody writes
  first (F2-199).
- ⚙ **Correcting it paid immediately:** promoting `assertNotSelfSatisfaction` into the population
  surfaced a **fourth** merged-party site that no reading of the module had found. Latent (0 live
  conditions), fixed in the same commit anyway — reachability is a fact about today, not a property
  of a control (F2-182), and fixing the instances you noticed is what leaves the rest looking
  covered (F2-215).
- ⚠⚠ **The mutation harness found a real hole, and it was this slice's own finding in my own
  gate.** The per-bar leg iterated `List.of("selfReviewBars", "cabDecisionBars")` — a list two
  names long because those were the two builders I had written — so re-merging the fourth site
  **SURVIVED the whole build**. The population is now derived by signature. **10 killed / 0
  survived / 0 anchor-miss** after.
- ⚠ **The stripper control failed on correct code**, which is the one failure a gate must never
  have (F2-214). My synthetic pathological input used a **complete** `/* … */` inside a `//`
  comment, and the two-pass form handles that correctly — the block pass removes the self-contained
  span. The corruption needs an **unterminated** delimiter plus a closer downstream. A red leg is a
  finding only if the code is actually wrong (F2-206).
- ⚠ **A name-bar detector keyed on the receiver `c.`** could not see `cond.getOwnerName()`, so
  the leg went red the moment its population became derived. **The receiver is not part of the
  claim** (F2-197's local-alias rule).
- ⚠ **The pre-fix control tripped on my own quotation.** The detector for `Coverage`'s retired
  sentence matched raw text, and this register's convention is that a correction **quotes** the
  sentence it replaces — which is what makes it auditable. Strip double-quoted spans first
  (F2-193's `unquoted()`), and note that a detector whose claim is about **prose** cannot share the
  comment-stripping harness. **8/8 discriminate** after.
- ⚠ Two probe legs failed for reasons unrelated to their claims (F2-244): the transition body key
  is `target` not `to` (**resolved from the controller** — the guessed-key family since F2-198,
  and F2-250 recorded this exact one), the CAB decision vocabulary is `APPROVE` not `APPROVED`,
  `EMERGENCY_APPROVED` needs `CHANGE:APPROVE` so `ranalyst` cannot drive it, and the emergency
  approval had to be cast by a **third** persona or `selfApprover` fires first and masks the owner
  leg.

- **28 remaining census members** (32 − 4: two closed here, two recorded as F2-248's), no verdicts

## F2-250 · A soft foreign key whose label travels beside it, and the PUT that performed two other routes' controls

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-250 |
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-19 |
| **Severity** | P2 |
| **Area** | `module/ethics` — `ethics.aml_alerts`, the SAMA/AML alert register, and its parent `ethics.kyc_subjects` |
| **Found by** | executing F2-249's filed 33-member census work list; the sharpest unblocked member was the SUBJECT pair of the entity whose ANALYST pair F2-249 had just closed |

Re-deriving F2-249's work list (F2-221) gave **33 unadjudicated members**, and ranking them by the
cheapest universal fact — *id NULL while the label is populated*, which needs no parent pairing
(F2-246: a guessed pairing manufactures phantom findings) — put most of the label-only rows inside
members already blocked or closed. The sharpest unblocked one was `ethics.aml_alerts :: subject_id +
subject_name`: **the same entity F2-249 closed the other pair of, eight lines away.**

Measured in dev and prod, identically:

| | |
|---|---|
| `ethics.kyc_subjects` | **16** registered subjects |
| `ethics.aml_alerts` | **10** live — 2 linked (both labels agreeing), **8 label-only** |
| labels that would have resolved | **8 of 8**, matching a registered subject **exactly** |
| dangling / cross-tenant / diverged | 0 / 0 / 0 |
| `FK_aml_subject` | **exists**, on `subject_id → kyc_subjects` |
| CHECK constraints on the table | **none** |

🔑🔑 **The register knew which of the 16 registered subjects each alert was about and
could not join to it.** There is even an index for the join — `ix_aml_alerts_subject_id` — and no
query anywhere that performs one. That is F2-249's *honest but unjoinable* symptom in its strongest
form: the link was available and was not made, because the create form asked for a label.

**The collector was the form.** `EthicsPage`'s AML tab offered `{ kind: 'text', key: 'subjectName' }`
and no picker, and `onCreate` never sent `subjectId` — so every alert the platform's own screen
produces is exactly the label-only shape, which is what the 8 rows are.

⚠ **And the same blanket `apply()` gave the entity-bound PUT two other routes' work.** Probed live
as `auditor`, who holds `COMPLIANCE:WRITE` — the permission on the create, the PUT, `/assign` and
`/transition` alike, so **there is no escalation to report**: the object-level controls were simply
the only ones, and this route sat beside them. Pre-fix **8/8**, post-fix **10/10**, every victim row
planted by the probe (F2-206):

| leg | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| a label with no id (the screen's own shape) | 201, `subject_id` NULL | **201** — still legal |
| an id **plus a contradicting label** | 201, both halves stored | **400** naming the subject |
| **another tenant's** KYC subject | 201 | **400** |
| a nonexistent subject id | 409 (the FK) | 400 (the resolver, naming the field) |
| `PUT {"analystName": …}` after a real `/assign` | 200 — **id 4 beside a label naming somebody else** | **400**, and an echo still 200 |
| `POST {"status":"STR_FILED"}` | **201** — an STR filed outright | **400** |
| `/transition` on the same edge | 400 | 400 |

🔑 **The PUT re-opened F2-249's fix, and the result is WORSE than pre-F2-249** — before, there
was no id for the label to contradict. `analystName` was writable and `analystId` was not, so the
row could assert two different analysts. **A fix at a dedicated route is not a fix while an adjacent
route writes the same column** (F2-246's rule that an update must not re-open what the create closed).

🔑 **The STR bypass is F2-220's still-open filing, instantiated.** `ServerStampedFieldContractTest`
cannot see it: `transition(Long id, String target, …)` writes the status from a **scalar parameter**,
so `status` never enters that gate's stamped set — the recorded transition-by-parameter blind spot.
`AmlAlertService` appears nowhere in its output, either way.

### The fix

Per F2-213's own prescription — **name the editable set, so everything omitted is closed by
construction. A scrub is a list of fields somebody remembered; an allow-list is the set of fields
that exist.**

- **`KycSubjectDirectory`** resolves the subject in-tenant and derives the label from what resolved.
  `KycService.require` is **converted to delegate** the resolution rather than keeping a second copy
  (F2-190); only its 404 stays local, because those routes address a subject by path variable while a
  register naming one in its body gets a 400. Bean name distinguishing, not aliased (F2-247).
- **A label with no id stays legal.** The schema keeps `subject_id` nullable beside a nullable
  `subject_name`, which is it stating that an unregistered party is representable (F2-246) — and it
  is right: an alert can concern a party nobody has onboarded, which is why `counterparty_name` has
  no id at all. All 8 live rows are that shape, so refusing would break every request that works
  today (F2-182). The row is **disclosed as unlinked** instead, in three states (F2-209).
- **Editing only the label of an already-linked alert is refused**, not silently unlinked: an entity
  binding cannot tell `subjectId: null` from an absent key, so "unlink" is not expressible here, and
  treating a label edit as one would quietly undo a resolved reference.
- `status` and `analystName` are held to an **echo** on both write paths (F2-231/F2-234), so a form
  that round-trips the whole row keeps working — which was mandatory, because `reqFromDto` is
  `{ ...a }` and every edit sends both.
- **The entity's `status = "OPEN"` initialiser is removed** and the create owns the default, derived
  from the machine's only root. It was doing two wrong things: a second literal for a state
  `TRANSITIONS` already declares (F2-217), and — on an entity binding — making an **omitted** key
  indistinguishable from a supplied `"OPEN"` (F2-237), so the echo rule would have refused every
  partial PUT. Registered in `NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest`'s moved-initialiser map.
- **The create form offers a picker over the real KYC register**, measured reachable *first*:
  `GET /api/v1/ethics/kyc` is `COMPLIANCE:READ` and **all 13 roles holding `COMPLIANCE:WRITE` hold it
  too**, in dev and prod — so unlike F2-249, where `/linkable-users` is `ADMIN:WRITE` and a picker
  would 403 on open, this one cannot. **The same measurement that blocked a picker one slice ago
  permits one here.**

### What went wrong in the doing

- ⚠ **My own gate leg was wrong about the codebase, not the reverse.** A ban on every `"OPEN"`
  literal in the service reported 4; reading them found **one** real second literal (`assign`'s
  `"OPEN".equals(…)`, now `INITIAL_STATUS`) and two legitimate ones — the analytics bucket list and
  its `getOrDefault` key, which enumerate the whole vocabulary for a KPI strip and ask a **different**
  question ("awaiting disposition", deliberately narrower than the machine's non-terminal complement).
  A red leg is a finding only if the code is actually wrong (F2-206); the leg was rescoped to the
  claim that was meant — *nothing compares a status against a literal root*.
- ⚠ **The pre-fix control reported one detector SILENT, and the cause is the finding's own
  mechanism.** D1 asked whether master's service contained `requireLabel(` at all — and it does:
  `directory.requireLabel(…)`, which **F2-249 added for the analyst**. So the control tripped on the
  very artefact that made this half look covered (F2-215's two-of-N). Scoped to the subject, 8/8
  discriminate.
- ⚠ **A helper for method bodies silently returned the wrong method.** `body()` walks to the first
  brace after a signature; a **field initialiser has none**, so asserting against the `TRANSITIONS`
  declaration read the next method's body — a leg failing for a reason unrelated to its claim
  (F2-244). Sliced to the initialiser instead.
- ⚠ **A probe leg passed for the wrong reason.** L8 sent `{"to": "STR_FILED"}` and received a 400
  reading *"target is required"* — the wrong body key, resolved from the controller afterwards
  (F2-244, and the guessed-route family since F2-198). With `target` it refuses for the right reason:
  *"Cannot transition from OPEN to STR_FILED"*.
- ⚠ **The empty-heredoc landmine fired again**, hanging the shell for two minutes and swallowing the
  `sed` chain behind it. The recorded rule — write file content with the Write/Edit tools, never an
  inline heredoc — covers a *pointless* heredoc too.
- ⚠ **`BUILD SUCCESS` over an app that never bound a port**, for the recorded reason: the old PID
  still owned :8084 and answered `/actuator/health` **UP** while serving code from a `target/classes`
  that `clean package` had deleted and rewritten. **Poll health, then check who owns the port, then
  restart** — a stale listener is the most misleading possible result for a fix-verification probe.

## F2-249 · A register that declares a person id beside a label wrote only the label

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-249 |
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-19 |
| **Severity** | P2 |
| **Area** | `module/iam` · `module/ethics` · `module/bcm/cycle` · `module/signature` · `module/admin/committee` — five registers whose parent reference is a PERSON, one shape |
| **Found by** | executing F2-248's filed 38-member work list, reading the eight actor-attribution members whose parent is a person (F2-221, F2-248's classification) |

Executing F2-248's 38-member work list, the eight actor-attribution members whose parent is a
**person** were read in full. The same absence produced **two opposite symptoms**, and which one a
register showed depended entirely on where its label came from. Measured identical in dev and prod:

| register | id populated | label writer | symptom |
|---|---|---|---|
| `platform.signatures :: signer` | 4/4 | **derived from the id** | the exemplar — REFUTED |
| `privacy.dpia_review :: reviewer` | 0/6 | `CurrentActor` | already closed — REFUTED |
| `bcm.plan_review_attestations :: attested_by` | **0/5** | the acting principal | honest, unlinkable |
| `bcm.bcp_plans :: last_attested_by` | **0/8** | derived from the attestation | honest, unlinkable |
| `bcm.plan_acknowledgements :: distributed_by` | **0/8** | the acting principal | honest, unlinkable |
| `ethics.aml_alerts :: analyst` | **0/10** | **caller free text** | a claim |
| `ethics.cases :: investigator` | 6/30 (seed) | **caller free text** | a claim |
| `evidence.evidence_items :: collector` | 77/78 | **no writer at all** | latent |

🔑🔑 **THE REUSABLE RULE: F2-245 established that a description travelling beside an id can
describe the wrong row. This is the case where the description travels ALONE — and the two ways that
fails look nothing like each other. Where the label comes from the principal the record is honest and
UNJOINABLE; where it comes from the caller the record is a CLAIM. Both are the absence of the same
half, so a reader who fixes one symptom will not recognise the other.**

**0 of the 3 stored analyst labels and 0 of the 14 investigator labels resolve to any real user**
(matched against `iam.users.username` and `full_name_en`), and `bcm.plan_review_attestations` names
`'Khalid Al-Mutairi'`, who resolves to nobody — F2-207's measured cast of 65 invented officers, in a
**server** register.

Probed live as `auditor` (a `INTERNAL_AUDITOR` holding `COMPLIANCE:WRITE`), pre-fix **10/10**:
an AML alert moved `OPEN -> INVESTIGATING` naming an analyst who does not exist, and a misconduct
case entered `INVESTIGATION` with an invented investigator. Both HTTP 200.

⚠⚠ **THE SCREEN WAS THE COLLECTOR, AND F2-223 DELETED THE ONE BESIDE IT.**
`EthicsPage` called `window.prompt(t('amlAssignPrompt'))` — it asked a human to **type** the analyst's
name, and whatever they typed became the register's record of who was investigating an AML alert.
F2-223 removed this page's `amlDecidedByPrompt` (the AML *decider*) and left this one; and
`decidedByName` twenty lines below in the same service has resolved from `CurrentActor` ever since.
🔑 **F2-215's two-of-N is why it looked covered: a reader who finds `CurrentActor` in a service
does not then ask which of its other people-columns still comes from the body.** CH-8 ("replace
window.prompt/confirm") is a completed task and this prompt survived it.

⚠⚠ **FOUR HAND-WRITTEN COPIES OF ONE PREDICATE, AND NO TWO AGREED.** Before writing a
fifth, the population was measured: `CoiService.requireOwnUser` (F2-244),
`CommitteeMemberRegistryService.requireUserInTenant`, `SignatureService.resolveSignerName`, and the
committee registry's own error text. **Two of them differed on whether a BLANK `full_name_en` falls
back to the username** — so a user whose display name was the empty string rendered as an empty
register cell in one place and as their username in the other. 🔑 **What made that duplication
harmless was two copies happening to agree, and nobody was maintaining that** (F2-177).
`module/iam/service/TenantUserDirectory` now owns both the predicate and the label spelling, and the
three existing copies were **converted rather than exempted** (F2-190, F2-246's precedent).

⚠ **`module/iam`, not `common/`, and that was checked rather than assumed.** `iam` owns
`users`; `X -> iam` is an ordinary business edge (`UserRepository` is already read from ten modules
outside `iam`, and `ModuleGraphRatchetTest`'s `KERNEL_ISH` is only `platform | integrations |
dashboard`). Putting it in `common/` would have been **worse**: that package sits outside the
ratchet's population entirely, so the dependency would be neither forbidden nor measured.

⚠⚠ **A BARE LABEL STAYS LEGAL, AND THE SCHEMA DECIDES THAT — NOT TASTE.** A nullable id
*beside* a nullable name column states that an unresolvable party is representable (F2-246's rule),
and the live data proves the registers mean it: `'Financial Crime Unit'`, `'Head of FCC'`,
`'Internal Audit'`, `'External Investigator'`, `'Forensic Accountant'`. Several are deliberately
outside the platform — an external investigator has no login by definition — so **requiring a
resolvable user would refuse exactly the ethics cases where independence matters most.** That is a
fix failing on correct usage, the one failure a fix or a gate must never have (F2-214). Contrast
F2-244, which refused: `coi_recusal_event` declares a NOT NULL id and **no name column at all**, so
there the opposite holds. What is closed here is the **appearance** of a link — an id is resolved
in-tenant, the label is DERIVED from what resolved, and a label contradicting a supplied id is
refused while an **echo** is accepted so a round-trip form keeps working (F2-231/F2-234).

⚠⚠ **MY OWN GATE HAD TWO REAL HOLES AND ONLY THE MUTATION HARNESS SAW THEM — both are
failure modes this register already names.** (a) The id-half leg carried a blanket fallback —
*"if the file calls `directory.requireLabel` anywhere, accept it"* — written because
`EthicsCaseService` assigns the resolved id to a local first. Deleting `c.setInvestigatorId(userId)`
**SURVIVED**, because the file still holds `c.setInvestigatorId(null)` in the no-assignee branch
*and* still calls `requireLabel`, so the presence check and the fallback were both satisfied by
something that was not the claim. F2-217's failure mode, inside the leg written to be load-bearing.
(b) `setAnalystName(label != null ? label : derived)` **SURVIVED**: the contradiction check is
case-INSENSITIVE, so the mutation's only observable effect is the **caller's casing** winning over
the server's — a register whose spelling of a person's name depends on how a caller typed it, which
is F2-179's collation family at one character's depth. 13/13 after both were closed.

⚠ **The gate's load-bearing assertion is the POSITIVE one** (F2-247): on a path that never
wrote the field, *"the service does not write X from the request"* is **vacuous** — there is no
setter for a negative scan to find, so that leg would pass forever over the defect it was written
for. `theIdHalfIsWrittenEverywhere` asserts the id half **is** written, from the resolver or the
principal, and that it is not merely *cleared*.

⚠⚠ **A HARD ZERO ON THE OBVIOUS RULE WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED.** *"Nobody may hand-spell
a tenant-narrowed user load"* returns **25 sites across 9 files**, and most are correct —
`UserService` resolving its own aggregate, `WorkflowRequestService`'s recipient reach. Measuring
before writing the assertion is the only reason that did not ship as a gate failing on working code.

⚠ **F2-244's gate then went red on correct code, and the response matters.**
`CoiUserReferenceResolutionContractTest` asserted the tenant filter inside `CoiService`'s own
`requireOwnUser` body; the predicate had moved into the shared primitive. The claim is unchanged and
still true, so the leg now **follows the delegation** — and, because the predicate is split across
the primitive's `resolve` (tenant) and `require` (refusal), each half is asserted where it actually
lives. 🔑 **Deleting or relaxing the assertion always passes and proves nothing** (F2-206/F2-235).

⚠ **Nineteen existing tests failed on `directory is null`**, and the fix was a **real**
`TenantUserDirectory` over each test's mocked repository, never a mock of it: a mocked resolver
returns empty and every refusal leg would go green asserting nothing (F2-237, F2-246's precedent).

⚙ **No picker was built, deliberately.** `/api/v1/committees/registry/linkable-users` is
guarded `ADMIN:WRITE` and the AML operator holds `COMPLIANCE:WRITE`, so a picker there would **403
on open** — offering an affordance the caller cannot use is F2-246's own browser finding. The id
path stays on the wire and the gap is filed. The register now shows the analyst in three states
(F2-209): a resolved person; a label with an announced `role="status"` *unlinked* badge and a
bilingual hint on `title` **and** `aria-label`; or an em-dash.

⚠ **A probe leg of mine failed for a reason unrelated to its claim.** The investigator id-path
leg re-used the case the label leg had just moved to `INVESTIGATION`, and the machine has no
`INVESTIGATION -> INVESTIGATION` edge — so the 400 read exactly like the fix refusing a valid id.
Fixed by planting a second and third case. F2-244's rule, and it cost one iteration.

⚙ **Verification.** Pre-fix probe **10/10**, post-fix **20/20** against planted rows including a
planted organisation-2 user (F2-206 — never a seeded governance row); pre-fix detector control
**14/14 discriminating, 0 silent** against `git show master:`; mutation **13 killed / 0 survived /
0 anchor-miss**; suite **4,259/0/0** (up 15); FE **805/805**; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean. Seeded
registers unchanged. **No migration — V379 remains head, next free V380.**

⚙ **Filed:**
- **The 33 remaining census members** (38 minus the 5 closed here), no verdicts (F2-188). The
  classification stands: the **person-reference** family is now largely closed, so what remains is
  weighted toward **register references** — `cyber.vulnerabilities :: asset_id`,
  `cyber.cyber_incidents :: affected_asset_id`, `socops.*_id`, `bcm.dr_plans`.
- **`evidence.evidence_items :: collector_id + collector_name` has no writer of either half** —
  77 of 78 rows populated by the seed, 0 dangling, so it is honest data behind no code at all
  (F2-247's shape). It is latent and cannot regress; it also cannot be maintained.
- **No user-listing endpoint is reachable by `COMPLIANCE:WRITE`**, so neither the AML nor the ethics
  register can offer a picker. A `LinkableUser`-shaped projection behind a lighter guard would close
  the id path on both screens at once — an owner decision about who may enumerate colleagues.
- **The unresolvable live labels** — 3 AML analysts, 14 investigators, `'Khalid Al-Mutairi'` on the
  BCM attestations — repair means deciding per row which real person an office label meant, in two
  databases, with no mapping. **Owner decision** (F2-183/F2-196's rule).
- **`ethics.cases.investigator_name` has no `*_ar`**, so an investigator is English-only on an
  Arabic-primary UI (house rule 7); and `ethics.aml_alerts.analyst_name` likewise.

## F2-248 · Two agent nouns the risk ranking could not spell

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-248 |
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-19 |
| **Severity** | P2 |
| **Area** | `module/change_mgmt` · `module/ethics` · `module/admin/committee` — three governance registers, one shape |
| **Found by** | executing F2-247's filed 40-member work list, after re-deriving and **classifying** it (F2-221, F2-245) |

### What was measured

F2-245's own rule says to classify before reading, because roughly half its census is the
**actor-attribution** family (`*_by_id + *_by_name`) whose answer is the authenticated principal,
not a derived copy — a different question from a register reference. Classifying the 40:

* **22 actor-attribution**, of which **13 are in `change_mgmt` alone**.
* **18 register-reference**, the family F2-245/F2-246/F2-247 have been closing.

That concentration is what made the module worth reading, and reading inverted the expectation:
**11 of the 13 already resolve from the principal.** `recordApproval` resolves `approverId` and uses
it as the CM-C2 segregation input under a comment reading *"Now evaluated on the resolved USER ID,
which the caller cannot choose"*; `create` captures `requestedById` through `ChangeSoD` (CE-15 /
F2-112); `stampImposer` and `stampCloser` resolve both halves. The module is largely exemplary.

Two were not, and they are **the same defect presenting as opposite symptoms**:

| register | rows dev / prod | id populated | what the FE sends | symptom |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `change_mgmt.change_comments` | 45 / 46 | **0 / 0** | `authorName: getUser()?.username ?? 'You'` | records a **claim** |
| `ethics.case_actions` | 15 / 15 | 10 / 10 (seed only) | **nothing at all** | records **no actor** |

`author_name` matches no `iam.users` username or `full_name_en` on **45 of 45** and **46 of 46**
rows; the stored values are office labels (`'Change Mgr'`, `'CISO'`, `'Implementer'`, 15 each).
`actor_name` likewise resolves to no user on **15 of 15** (`'HR Investigations Lead'`,
`'Compliance / الالتزام'`).

⚠⚠ **AND PROD HOLDS A ROW WHOSE AUTHOR IS THE LITERAL STRING `'You'`.** That is the
frontend's `?? 'You'` fallback having fired in a production register — under a comment reading
*"CH-8: attribute the comment to the signed-in user, not a hardcoded 'You'"*, three characters from
the fallback it claims to have removed. F2-184's shape, and the reason this is not a latent finding.

### The live defect

Probed live as **`ranalyst`** (a `RISK_ANALYST`, the least-privileged of the seven `CHANGE:WRITE`
holders — `admin` proves nothing about authorization) against a `[REVIEW-TEST]` change request the
probe planted itself (F2-206). **8 of 8 legs pre-fix:**

* `{"authorName": "so_officer", ...}` → **HTTP 201**, stored `author_name = 'so_officer'`. A risk
  analyst posted a comment on a CAB-approved change **as the CISO**.
* `{"authorId": 8, ...}` → **201**, stored `author_id = 8` — mass assignment onto a column NULL on
  every row of both databases, so nothing had ever written it and there was no server-owned half at
  all.
* `{}` (no author) → **201**, stored `'Unknown'`. `if (getAuthorName() == null) setAuthorName("Unknown")`
  is a **default, not a guard** (F2-218): it discards nothing the caller sent.
* `{"authorName": "You"}` → **201**. The prod row is reproducible on demand.

🔑 **The audit row contradicted itself on one line.** `platform.audit_log.user_username` held
`ranalyst` — the framework already knew who acted — while the message this module composed read
*"Comment added to change 273 by You"*. F2-223's rule that quoting the claim is what makes a forged
attribution invisible to whoever audits it, with the sharper twist that **the truth was already in
the row beside it**.

For `ethics.case_actions` the probe (as `compliance`, a real non-admin holder of `COMPLIANCE:WRITE`)
showed **7 of 7 pre-fix**: a forged actor stored verbatim on a misconduct case action
(`actor_name = 'so_officer'`, `actor_id = 8`), and — the payload `EthicsPage` actually sends —
`actor_name = NULL, actor_id = NULL`. **The action log of a whistleblowing investigation recorded
what happened and when, and not who did it.**

🔑 `action_at` is `insertable = false`, so the **database** owns WHEN while the caller owned WHO.
That is F2-223's split attribution with the server-clock half arriving through the one filling
mechanism a setter-matching scan cannot see (F2-226's fourth mechanism) — which is why no existing
instrument reported it.

### ⚠⚠ The instrument finding: a generalisation is itself a vocabulary

`MassAssignmentRatchetTest` ranked **both** endpoints **LOW**. Of 214 entity-bound writes only
**five** were in that tier, and these were two of them — so the platform's own mass-assignment
ranking filed its two forgeable attributions in the smallest, least-attended bucket.

The cause is exact. F2-217's headline is that *"a risk ranking built from a literal field-name list
finds exactly the spellings its author had already seen"*, and its remedy was to replace the list
with a **shape**. But `AGENT_SHAPE` is an alternation of **twelve agent nouns** and
`AUTHORITY_SHAPE` of **twenty-nine verbs** — the shape's stems are themselves a literal list.
`author` and `actor` are ordinary English agent nouns ending in `-or` and neither is among the
twelve. 🔑 **F2-217's own headline, one level up: generalising a vocabulary into a pattern leaves
the pattern's stems a vocabulary, and nobody re-reads a rule that looks like a rule.**

A **third** name was then found by *reading* the single row the widening surfaced:
`admin.committee_meeting_papers.circulated_by` is a user id, bound straight from the request, never
written by the service, and **NULL on all 21 live rows in both databases**. `circulated` is not among
`AUTHORITY_SHAPE`'s twenty-nine verbs either — so this one is an unspelled **act verb** rather than
an agent noun. Two vocabularies, two blind spots, one slice: **assume a fourth spelling exists.**

⚠⚠ **A SHORT stem cannot share a long stem's prefix rule, and my first draft proved it.** Putting
both new stems into `AGENT_SHAPE` — whose prefix is `(?:.*[a-z0-9])?` — made `actor` match inside
`f·actor·Name`, and the **negative half** of the vocabulary leg caught it on the first run.
`contractorName` and `benefactorId` are the same trap. The twelve original stems are long enough
never to have hit it, which is exactly why the rule was safe to write and is not safe to extend. The
two short stems therefore get `SHORT_AGENT_SHAPE`, anchored to a camelCase boundary, with **9
must-pair and 8 must-not-pair** cases asserted — because a widening that is too wide silently
re-tiers the platform and one that is too narrow silently shrinks the work list.

### The fix

* **`ChangeCommentRequest(body)`** and **`CaseActionRequest(actionType, title, description,
  isConfidential)`** replace the entity bindings. The actor fields are not validated, they are
  **absent**: a field the bound type does not declare can never arrive (F2-233), which is a stronger
  closure than any guard — and it is what `MassAssignmentRatchetTest` already demanded of
  `ChangeConditionRequest` by name, *"a scrub is a list of fields somebody remembered, a DTO is the
  set of fields that exist."*
* Each service resolves the actor from **its own module's declared primitive** — `ChangeSoD.actor()`
  in `change_mgmt` (the class whose javadoc states the rule: *"the id is the part a gate can stand
  on, and only the server can know it"*), `CurrentActor` in `ethics`. Never a second mechanism beside
  an existing one (F2-190).
* Both **refuse** rather than record a blank: a comment whose author is `""` or `"Unknown"` still
  reads as an attribution, which is worse than one that could not be written (F2-236).
* The audit line reads off the **saved row** and now names the resolved user id, so the column and
  the message agree.
* `circulated_by` is stamped from the principal. `authorName` beside it is **PRESERVED** — verified,
  not reasoned: there is no `author_id` column, `author_role` holds an office
  (`'Company Secretary'`), and **21 of 21** rows in both databases name a *body*
  (`'COM-BOARD Secretariat'`) resolving to no user. A committee paper's author is its **preparer**, a
  third party, and the schema's own separation of `circulated_by` from `author_name` is what settles
  it (F2-236's `counterpartySigner` precedent). `circulatedAt` stays a **fallback**, stated rather
  than glossed, because back-dating a past circulation is legitimate and F2-233(d) established that a
  fallback is not an ownership claim — so this endpoint was never the split-attribution shape, it
  was a column with no writer.
* **Frontend:** the comment client sends only the body and the `?? 'You'` fallback is deleted; both
  DTOs now declare the id half the wire always carried (F2-198's `crossBorderTransfer` shape, which
  is *why* the register could not tell an attributed row from a label); and both surfaces disclose
  the three states — attributed, pre-F2-248 label, no actor at all — rather than blanking the name
  and letting an unattributable row read as the tidiest (F2-197 / F2-209), in **both languages**
  (house rule 7).

### Instrument changes, and why one is a census rather than a zero

`BASELINE_UNADJUDICATED_NEW_CRIT` **stays 48 and is not raised.** The two widenings together add
**exactly one** new CRIT row — the committee paper — adjudicated in the same commit with a
**per-field** verdict, because three fields there have three different answers and a per-endpoint
verdict has to say which is which (F2-231). House rule 3: a ceiling left in place after a sweep makes
a tolerated row indistinguishable from a reviewed one.

A new leg asks the complementary question the entity-bound ranking **cannot** ask: does a bound
**request type** declare the actor? That population is invisible to everything above, and 🔑 **the
strongest available fix — bind a narrow record — is precisely what moves an endpoint across that
boundary**, so without this leg, re-adding `authorName` to `ChangeCommentRequest` would go unnoticed.

⚠⚠ **My first draft made it a hard zero, and reading the output showed the ASSERTION was wrong.**
It reported **28** types, and a large share are **round-trip** DTOs — `BoardPackDto`,
`CapaTaskDto`, `DsrCaseDto`, `NcaEccFilingDto` — used for the response as well as the request. Such
a type **must** declare `decidedBy` in order to return it, and whether the write path honours the
inbound value is `ServerStampedFieldContractTest`'s question. So it ships as a **decrease-only census
with no verdicts** (F2-188: twenty-eight fluent reasons for unread code is the artefact that measured
five-of-five false), and F2-204's rule applies to my own leg: when a figure cannot honestly be zero,
ask whether the QUESTION was wrong.

The per-type enforcement lives beside each fix instead — `ChangeCommentProvenanceTest` and
`EthicsCaseServiceTest` assert **by reflection** that the two new request types declare no actor
component at all.

### Verification

| | |
|---|---|
| Backend suite | **4,244 / 0 / 0** (was 4,232) |
| Frontend | **805 / 805** · `npx tsc --noEmit` clean |
| `ServerStampedFieldContractTest` | green — the gate F2-236 says to re-run after converting an attribution |
| Pre-fix detector control | **18 discriminating · 0 silent-on-master · 0 broken** |
| Probe 1 (`ranalyst`) | **8/8 pre-fix**, **8/8 post-fix** |
| Probe 2 (`compliance`) | **7/7 pre-fix**, **7/7 post-fix** |
| Seeded registers | unchanged: 45 comments, 15 actions, 21 papers |
| Migration | none — V379 remains head |

Probe 2's pre-fix run was taken by checking out master's three service files onto a committed
branch, recompiling and restarting — not by reasoning about them. F2-244 recorded a leg that passed
for the wrong reason on **both** trees, and only the pre-fix run could expose that.

⚠ **`ChangeCommentProvenanceTest` is the twin `CabVoteProvenanceTest` never got.** That class is
DF-4's forged-actor test for the CAB-approval path *in the same service*; the comment thread beside
it had **no test of any kind**. A path with no test is not a path somebody decided was safe.

⚠ **The mutation harness found a real hole in my own gate.** Deleting `[Cc]irculated` from the verb
list **survived**, because I had added the two agent nouns to the anti-vacuity
`measuredOnRealEntities` list and forgotten the verb — so the mutation lowers the CRIT count, which
a `<=` ceiling reads as progress. That is the exact failure mode F2-217 wrote that leg for,
reintroduced one stem later. Fixed; **14 killed · 0 survived · 0 anchor-miss** after, with one
mutation **withdrawn as invalid** rather than counted (it weakened one of my own assertions, and you
can always delete an assertion — F2-206, F2-235) and one recorded as **NO GATE** (the
`circulated_by` stamp is asserted by the live probe only).

### Filed

- **The 38 remaining census members** (40 − 2 closed here), still with no verdicts (F2-188). The
  classification is the useful part to carry forward: **20 actor-attribution** and **18
  register-reference** are different questions. Recorded exclusions stand: the two `socops`
  `application_id` members are **unwireable**, and `bcm.dr_plans` needs owner decisions on both
  halves.
- **The 28-type request-DTO census** in `MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s printed output. Read the
  service before writing a reason: a round-trip DTO must declare the field to return it.
- **`ethics.case_actions.action_type` is free text with no CHECK** — nine distinct values over 15
  rows, and the whole `ethics` schema has none. Cheap now that this slice closed the register's only
  open writer (F2-183's rule: the constraint and its writer land in the same commit), but it needs
  the F2-221 finding resolved first, since **11 of 30 ethics cases already hold a status no route can
  advance**.
- **The 45 dev / 46 prod comment rows and 15 action rows whose author is an office label**, plus the
  one prod row authored by `'You'`. Repair rewrites live governance rows in two databases and there
  is no mapping from an office to a person: **owner decision** (F2-183 / F2-196's rule).
- **`change_mgmt.change_condition :: owner_id`** has no writer at all and the table holds **0 rows in
  dev and does not exist in prod** (prod is ~35 migrations behind). An owner is an *assignment*
  (F2-226), so free text is defensible; the unwritten id is the F2-247 unlinkability shape, latent
  with no data.
- **A fourth spelling.** Two vocabularies were found short in one slice, by two different routes
  (a widening, then reading its single new row). The next reader should assume there is another.

## F2-247 · A second register, a second resolver, and a bean name that would not boot

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-247 |
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-19 |
| **Severity** | P2 |
| **Area** | `module/tprm/cyber` · SAMA/NCA third-party cyber assessment · one create form |
| **Found by** | executing F2-246's filed 45-member work list, after re-deriving it (F2-221) |

### What was measured

Re-deriving the census by **reach** in both databases split the population into two disjoint
sub-shapes, which is the useful result before any code is read:

* **fully linked** registers can only exhibit F2-245's *divergence* — `cyber.cyber_controls`
  75/75, `admin.committee_meetings` 34/34, `iam.sod_violations` 9/9,
  `bcm.mtpd_inheritance_finding` 8/8 (twice), `ethics.aml_alerts :: rule_id` 10/10.
* **unlinked** registers can only exhibit F2-246's *unlinkability* — `socops.sbom_component`
  20/20, `bcm.dr_plans` 16/16 (twice), `socops.appsec_finding` 10/10,
  `bcm.strategy_roi_analysis` 3/3, `tprm.third_party_cyber_assessments` 8 of 16.

Three of the fully-linked registers turned out to be **already correct by construction**, and they
are the exemplar this family's fix copies: `CommitteeService` writes
`m.setCommitteeCode(parent.getCode())`, `SodService` writes `v.setRuleCode(rule.getRuleCode())`,
and `MtpdInheritanceService` writes `f.setVendorName(vend.getVendorName())` — every label derived
from a resolved parent.

⚠⚠ **MY OWN FIRST PAIRING MANUFACTURED A 75-ROW PHANTOM, AND F2-210 HAD JUST WRITTEN THE RULE.**
`cyber.cyber_controls` stores `framework_id` beside `framework_name`, and paired against
`compliance.frameworks` by NAME it reported **all 75 rows diverging**, with ids and labels
apparently naming different frameworks (`id=5` labelled `NCA CSCC` resolving to *ISO/IEC 27001
ISMS*). `CyberController` owns a `/frameworks` route and `CyberFrameworkService` resolves
`cyber.cyber_frameworks` with `findByOrganisationId` — so **that** is the parent, and against it
**75 of 75 AGREE**, 0 dangling, 0 cross-tenant. 🔑 *A scan locates; **the pairing is the
measurement**, and a guessed pairing manufactures phantom findings* (F2-210), landing on the slice
one after it was recorded. There are also **two** framework registers (`compliance.frameworks` 24
rows, `evidence.frameworks` 16), neither carrying an `organisation_id`, which is why the wrong one
resolved so plausibly.

Two candidates were **excluded on measurement rather than fixed**: `socops.sbom_component` and
`socops.appsec_finding` both carry an `application_id` populated on **no live row**, and **`socops`
declares no application register at all** — so the id has no target and this is the *unwireable*
case (F2-204's shape), not a fixable one. `bcm.dr_plans` is blocked on owner decisions on both
halves: no critical-system register exists, and `linked_bcp_id`'s parent is the already-filed
two-plan-register ambiguity (`bcm_plans` vs `bcp_plans`, F2-196). Neither of its two id columns has
**any** writer at all — `DrPlanService` writes only the labels.

### The live defect

`tprm.third_party_cyber_assessments` — 16 live rows, byte-identical dev and prod:

| | rows |
|---|---|
| **unlinked** (`TPC-2026-001..008`), label only | **8** |
| linked and agreeing (`TPC-GOV-001..008`) | 8 |
| diverging | 0 |
| dangling | 0 |

The unlinked labels are annotated prose — `'New vendor — Sentry IO'`, `'Legacy vendor — Backup Tape
Logistics LLC'` — which is *why* they can never join. `ThirdPartyCyberAssessmentService.create`
binds the **entity** and touched neither half, so both came straight from the caller's body with no
resolution and no tenant check, and the wire contract said so: `vendorId?: number` (optional)
beside `vendorName: string` (required). `ThirdPartyCyberPage`'s form was a `required: true`
free-text vendor box with **no picker**, and `onCreate` sent **no id at all** — so the rows the
platform's own screen produces are exactly the unlinked ones, and the 8 that are linked came from
the seed.

Probed live as `compliance` (holds `TPRM:WRITE`, not `TPRM:APPROVE`, resolved from
`iam.role_permissions` — `admin` proves nothing about authorization) against a **planted** org-2
victim cloned from a real org-1 vendor (F2-206, F2-246):

| leg | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| label-only create | 201 | **201** — deliberately kept |
| another tenant's vendor id | **201**, stored | **404** |
| `vendorId: 999999` | **201** | **404** |
| real id + **lying label** | **201**, lie stored | **201**, label derived `'Cisco Systems'` |

The last row is the load-bearing leg. **The two legs that expect a refusal cannot tell a correct
refusal from one caused by a null tenant** — F2-246's fix was wrong in one of its four registers for
exactly that reason, and only the derived-label assertion could see it. Note also that leg 4 answers
201 pre-fix: the column carries **no FOREIGN KEY**, so the database refused nothing either.

### The module already knew

`TprmService.createAssessment` resolves its vendor with `getVendor(req.getVendorId())` under the
comment *"verify org ownership"*. That is the correct artefact, one service over in the same module
— and `tprm/cyber` imported **nothing** from `tprm/*`, so it had no `VendorRepository` at all and
could not have resolved a vendor if it had wanted to. F2-215's two-of-N. `getVendor` now delegates
to the shared resolver, because what made the duplicate harmless was two copies agreeing and nobody
maintaining that (F2-177).

### ⚠⚠ The bean name that would not boot

Naming the new class `VendorReferenceResolver`, mirroring F2-246's, **stopped the application
starting**: two `@Component` classes with the same simple name claim the same default bean name and
Spring throws `ConflictingBeanDefinitionException` while parsing the configuration class.

🔑 **All 4,229 unit tests passed over it.** Nothing in the suite boots a Spring context, and
`mvn -o clean package` is deliberately hermetic — no database, no secrets — so the build never
starts the app either. The only instrument that could see this was launching it, and the launch
printed **`BUILD SUCCESS`** over the failure (the recorded landmine that `BUILD SUCCESS` is not a
start signal under `spring-boot:run`, because DevTools' `RestartLauncher` swallows it). The visible
symptom was a health probe that never answered.

F2-222 filed the duplicate-simple-name hazard for **entities** and measured it as latent — 15 of
433 names in two packages, *"and nobody is maintaining that"*. For a Spring bean it is **fatal**, so
it gets an invariant: `UniqueBeanNameContractTest` (**744** component-scanned beans measured, hard
zero, no exemption map — an explicit `@Component("name")` is always available, so there is no
correct code for it to fail on). The `Tprm` prefix is also the honest name, for the same reason
`loadTprmVendorOptions` carries one: there are two vendor registers for one concept and reaching
for the wrong resolver is the easy mistake.

### What was deliberately NOT done

* **`vendor_country` is not derived.** It looks like a third identity copy and is not: the
  assessment stores `'SA'` where `tprm.vendors` stores `'Saudi Arabia'` — two notations for one
  concept (F2-203's shape) — and the form caps the field at `maxLength: 3` with the placeholder
  `'SAU'`. Deriving it would write a country *name* into a three-character field. Filed.
* **The unlinked case is preserved and disclosed**, not refused: nothing rejects a label-only
  create today and 8 live rows were made that way, so `require` would break working requests
  (F2-182), and an assessment of a supplier that is not in the register is a real thing to want.
* **No migration.** V379 remains head.

### The census gap this slice closed

`ParentIdentityCopyContractTest` held its closures as a **single `String`**, so F2-246 closed four
registers and **all four still printed `NEEDS-READING`**. 🔑 *A member left on a work list after a
sweep is indistinguishable from one nobody has looked at* — house rule 3's warning about un-lowered
ceilings, arriving inside the artefact that carries the work list. Now a `CLOSED` map of six
entries, each naming its slice and mechanism and each asserted to still be a member the scan finds
(F2-199's reverse direction). Work list **45 → 40**.

### Instrument errors of mine, all caught by running things

* The guessed pairing above (75 phantom rows), and a guessed column — `compliance.frameworks` has
  no `organisation_id`, and the answer was printed by my own script one line above the query that
  failed on it.
* **A vacuous invariant.** My first gate leg asserted *"the service does not write the vendor
  reference from the request"*, and the pre-fix control showed it **SILENT ON MASTER**: an
  entity-bound create has **no setter for a scan to find**, because Jackson had already bound both
  values onto the entity. The leg would have passed forever over the defect it was written for.
  🔑 **On an entity-bound endpoint the load-bearing assertion has to be the positive** — both halves
  *overwritten from the resolver* — which is the only shape that can see a create doing nothing at
  all.
* **A gate failing on correct code**, the one failure a gate must never have (F2-214): a file-wide
  ban on `approverName` fired on the RESPONSE type, which legitimately declares it because
  `approver_name` is a real column. **F2-225 recorded this exact mistake** and I repeated it;
  re-scoped to the function body.
* An anti-vacuity floor **guessed at 800** against a measured **744**, so the leg failed on a correct
  tree — F2-195's rule that a baseline lifted from something other than the measurement is worse
  than none, because it looks measured.
* ⚠⚠ **A docs script destroyed the 1.79 MB findings register**, and the mechanism generalises:
  `io.open(p, "w")` **truncates on open**, so an exception during `.write()` leaves the file at zero
  bytes. Every subsequent grep then answered *"not found"*, which reads as the anchor having moved
  rather than as the file having been destroyed. Restored with `git checkout --` because it was
  tracked and uncommitted. **Build the content, write a temp file, assert the round-trip, then
  replace.** The encode failure itself was lone surrogates — `\ud83d\udd11` written as two escapes
  is two unpaired surrogates, not a character.
* A sibling of that: a patch script whose write handle was **never closed**, so its own verifying
  `assert` re-read an unflushed file, found nothing, and passed vacuously.
* Small ones: a probe fixture giving a `uniqueidentifier` column a plausible string; `mvn` needing
  `mvn.cmd` on Windows, so the mutation harness raised `FileNotFoundError` instead of reporting a
  result; and a non-ASCII character in a bash `grep` pattern, which does not survive the shell.

### Verification

Backend **4,232/0/0** · frontend **805/805** · `npx tsc --noEmit` clean · pre-fix control **14
discriminating, 0 silent-on-master, 0 broken** · mutation **13/13 killed, 0 survived, 0
anchor-miss** · live probe **7/7 post-fix against 6/7 pre-fix**, run twice with cleanup verified and
the seeded register unchanged at 16 rows.

### Filed

* The **40-member work list** that remains, still with no verdicts (F2-188). The two `socops`
  members are **unwireable** (no application register exists) and `bcm.dr_plans` needs an owner
  decision on both halves — recorded so the next slice does not re-measure them.
* **`cyber.cyber_controls` is latent, not clean**: the create and update both take `framework_id`
  and `framework_name` from the request with no resolution and no tenant check on the framework, so
  divergence and a cross-tenant reference are representable. 0 rows exhibit either today.
* **`ethics.aml_alerts :: rule_id + rule_name`** — `AmlAlertService` writes the label from the
  source rather than from a resolved rule.
* **`tprm.third_party_cyber_assessments.vendor_country`**, the two-notation column above: which
  notation governs is an owner decision, and the form's 3-character cap disagrees with the parent's
  stored value.
* **The 8 unlinked live rows** in both databases — repair means deciding per row which registered
  vendor an annotated label meant (owner decision), and the missing FOREIGN KEY is blocked on it.
* **Two vendor registers for one concept** (`scm.vendors` 31 rows, `tprm.vendors` 28) and therefore
  two resolvers, because ADR-012/018 keep the modules' internals apart. **That the shape recurs once
  per module because the primitive cannot be shared is the structural finding**, and it is the same
  argument as the `CyberInputValidation` situation. Owner decision.
* **`tprm.vendors` exists for organisation 1 only**, so the picker is empty for any other tenant —
  the same gap F2-246 filed for `scm.vendors`.

## F2-246 · A form that collects a LABEL instead of a LINK produces a row nothing can join

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-246 |
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-19 |
| **Severity** | P2 |
| **Area** | `module/scm` (resilience + fourth party) · SAMA outsourcing · four create forms |
| **Found by** | executing F2-245's filed 47-member work list, after re-deriving it (F2-221) |

### What was measured

F2-245 established that **a soft FK which also carries its parent's identity is making two
claims, and only the parent can answer the second**. Its filing left a 45-member work list.
Re-deriving that list before touching anything gave two results before a line of code was
read:

* **22 of the 24 parent-register pairs carry no FOREIGN KEY at all** — the shape lives
  overwhelmingly on unconstrained soft links.
* The striking column is not divergence but **a stored label with no id**.

Four registers in one module share one concept — the vendor — and all four had it:

| register | live | with id | **label, no link** | joined by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `scm.exit_plans` | 13 | 6 | **7** | `ExitPlanRepository.findByOrganisationIdAndVendorId…` |
| `scm.alternate_suppliers` | 16 | 6 | **10** | `AlternateSupplierRepository.findByOrganisationIdAndPrimaryVendorId…` |
| `scm.supplier_resilience_tests` | 11 | 3 | **8** | — |
| `scm.fourth_party_exposures` | 13 | 6 | **7** | — |
| **total** | **53** | **21** | **32** | |

Byte-identical in dev and prod. **Divergence is 0** of the 21 linked rows — unlike F2-245,
where 11 of 11 diverged — so here the divergence is latent and the *unlinked* half is live.

🔑 **The DTO declared the defect.** All four create requests read
`Long <x>VendorId` (no annotation) beside `@NotBlank @Size(max = 255) String <x>VendorName`:
**the label was mandatory and the link was optional.** A caller supplying only what was
required produced a row nothing could join, and all four create forms did exactly that — a
`required: true` free-text vendor box, no picker, and no id in the payload. So the 32
unlinked rows are precisely the ones the platform's own screens produce; the 21 linked ones
came from `seed_real_data.py`.

The consequence is a coverage question. *"Which vendors have an exit plan?"* is a SAMA
outsourcing question, `byVendor` is how it is asked, and **7 of 13 real exit plans could
never be returned by it** — 10 of 16 for alternates. Both coverage clients
(`plansForVendor`, `alternatesForPrimary`) are also declared dark, so the query exists, the
client exists, and 60% of the data could not answer it if a screen called one.

### Live, pre-fix, 17/17

As `ranalyst` (organisation 1, holding `SCM:READ/WRITE/EXPORT` resolved from
`iam.role_permissions` — never `admin`), against a `[REVIEW-TEST]` victim vendor the probe
plants in organisation 2 rather than touching a seeded row (F2-206):

* a label-only create → **201**, unfindable by the coverage query;
* `vendorId` = organisation 2's vendor → **201**, stored (no FK, no tenant check);
* `vendorId: 999999` → **201**, stored;
* a real id with a deliberately wrong label → **201**, the lie stored beside it.

All four registers, all four legs. 17/17 post-fix.

### 🔑 Which half is wrong, and how the schema says so

`AlternateSupplier` declares `primary_vendor_id` **and** `primary_vendor_name` for the vendor
being replaced, and for the replacement only `alternate_vendor_name` — **there is no
`alternate_vendor_id` column anywhere.** `FourthPartyExposure` is the same shape
(`fourth_party_name`, no id). So the schema itself distinguishes them: a substitute or
downstream party is deliberately free text because it need not be a registered vendor, while
the **subject** vendor has an id column *and* a coverage query and is meant to resolve.

🔑 **When a table declares an id beside a label for one party and only a label for another,
the schema is stating which reference is supposed to be resolvable.** That is a mechanical
discriminator for this whole family, and it is what made the fix decidable without a product
call.

### The fix

One `VendorReferenceResolver` owns both halves at all five call sites:

* an id **resolves in-tenant** and the label is **derived from the row that resolved** —
  anything the caller claimed the vendor was called is discarded, because only the vendor
  register knows its own name;
* **no id → the caller's label is kept.** Refusing would break requests that work today
  (F2-182: nothing refuses it, and 32 live rows were made that way). The row is disclosed as
  unlinked rather than reading like a resolved one — F2-209's three states;
* the subject label stops being `@NotBlank`; the two id-less labels **stay** mandatory,
  asserted in both directions so "relax them too" fails (F2-199);
* `FourthPartyExposureService#update` — the one **update** that writes a vendor label, and
  the route by which a linked row's copy could be made to diverge after the fact — accepts an
  **echo** and refuses a **change** (F2-231/F2-234), so a form that round-trips the whole row
  keeps working while an update cannot re-open what the create closed;
* the four forms pick from `GET /api/v1/scm/vendors/all`, which **already existed** — the
  fifth blocker in this programme that was already solved. Its client was recorded dark as a
  `HOLE`; that entry is deleted and the count lowered in the same commit (F2-207);
* `ScmService#requireOwnVendor` **and three hand-spelled copies of the identical predicate**
  (`getVendor`, `updateVendor`, `deleteVendor` — same filter, same message) now delegate, so
  one place answers *"is this my vendor?"* (F2-177). The gate's first draft banned that shape
  too widely and would have failed on `stampVendorOnboarding`, F2-242's deliberately scoped
  write helper; scoping the ban to the **refusal** is what made it true instead.

### Lessons

* ⚠⚠ **My own fix was wrong in 1 of the 4 registers, and the live probe is the only thing
  that caught it.** `FourthPartyExposureService` resolved the vendor **18 lines above**
  `e.setOrganisationId(...)`, so the tenant argument was null, the filter could never match,
  and **every linked create answered 404.** The other three were safe by accident of
  statement order. 🔑 **The two probe legs that expect a REFUSAL passed on the broken code —
  a refusal caused by a null tenant is indistinguishable from a correct one — so only the leg
  asserting the DERIVED label could see it.** Fixed as a class rather than an instance (all
  four read the tenant from the request) and gated.
* ⚠ **Two of my own gate assertions failed on correct code**, which is the one failure a gate
  must never have (F2-214). One asserted the word `organisationId` over comment-stripped
  source where the code says `getOrganisationId`; one banned a load shape a sibling method
  uses legitimately. F2-206's rule applied to an assertion: **a red leg is a finding only if
  the code is actually wrong** — and here it pointed at three real duplicates, which were
  converted rather than exempted.
* ⚠ **Relaxing a type on the RESPONSE is a different claim from relaxing it on the REQUEST,
  and `npx tsc` found it at a display site.** My first type edit hit the four response
  interfaces; `vendor_name` is `nullable = false`, so the server always sends a label and only
  the create request may omit it. `TprmConsolidatedOverview` passing that name into a `string`
  parameter is what surfaced it.
* ⚠ **An existing test's mocked collaborator would have silenced F2-242's cross-tenant legs.**
  `ScmServiceTest` gets a **real** resolver over its mocked repository, because a mock returns
  null and all six of those legs would have gone green while asserting nothing (F2-237).
* ⚠⚠ **FOUND IN THE BROWSER AFTER EVERY GATE WAS GREEN — eighth consecutive slice, and it was
  a promise rather than a figure.** `SearchableSelect` hard-coded its search placeholder as
  *"Search or create new…"* / *"ابحث أو أنشئ جديداً…"* **unconditionally**, while the create row
  130 lines above is correctly gated on `!!onCreate`. So the affordance was conditional and
  only the promise was not: measured, **17 of the 19 `select-searchable` fields in the app wire
  no `onCreate`** — including F2-245's risk picker, shipped one slice earlier — so almost every
  picker in the platform invited an operator to create a record it cannot create. F2-184's
  shape at the level of the text a user actually reads, and no code-scoped gate can see a
  string that is wrong only *in relation to a sibling prop*. Fixed in both languages, because
  F2-208 found this class of drift in the Arabic half alone (house rule 7).
* ⚠ **A probe that plants rows must build its fixture by CLONING a real one.** Hand-built
  placeholder values have to satisfy every CHECK on the table and `scm.vendors` constrains
  `category`; losing that fight one constraint at a time teaches nothing. A clone satisfies
  all of them and only the tenant and the names change.
* ⚠ **A cross-schema text comparison needs an explicit `COLLATE`** — `scm.*` is
  `Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_SC_UTF8` against a `SQL_Latin1_General_CP1_CI_AS` database
  default, so the measurement script died on error 468 (the F2-174 landmine) before it
  produced a number.

### Verification

Backend **4,211/0/0** · frontend **805/805** · typecheck clean · pre-fix detector control
**26/26 fire against master, 0 silent** · mutation harness **11/11 killed, 0 survived, 0
anchor-miss** · live probe **17/17 pre-fix and 17/17 post-fix**, run twice · browser confirms
31 real vendors in Arabic and a placeholder that no longer promises a create. No migration
(V379 remains head).

### Filed

* **The 43-member work list that remains** after this slice takes four — still with no
  verdicts (F2-188). Classify before reading: roughly half of the raw population is
  `*_by_id + *_by_name`, which is F2-236's **actor attribution**, a different question whose
  answer is the authenticated principal rather than a derived copy. Among the parent-register
  members, the ones whose id is populated on **no** live row are the least urgent by reach and
  the most complete instances of this shape: `bcm.dr_plans :: critical_system_id` (16 of 16
  rows name a system by label and link to none), `socops.sbom_component :: application_id`
  (20 of 20), `socops.appsec_finding :: application_id` (10 of 10),
  `bcm.strategy_roi_analysis :: strategy_id` (3 of 3),
  `change_mgmt.change_requests :: change_owner_id` (15 of 17),
  `risk.emerging_risks :: linked_risk_id`, `admin.committee_action_items ::
  linked_entity_id`. `cyber.vulnerabilities :: asset_id` (15 of 20 unlinked) and
