## F2-240 · The residual 19 were all latent-by-caller, so reach could no longer order them — and the gate refused this slice's own fix

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-240 |
| **Title** | Every one of F2-239's residual never-firing null-guards was defended by nothing but the shape of one page's payload, so the whole population was swept and the work list became an invariant — and the gate's own create-path leg turned out to have been a whole-file substring check for two slices |
| **Severity** | 🟠 P3 (latent-by-caller throughout: all 6 live callers echo back every initialised field, and 4 of the 11 routes have no frontend write client at all — but 4 of the 19 resets are flattering on live data, dev = prod) |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · server-owned state |
| **Modules** | 11 entities across `bcm`, `sust` (×5), `platform/controls` (×2), `ndi` (×2), `tprm`; 4 create paths (2 services, 2 request records); 1 gate widened + 1 leg corrected; 2 new test classes |

### The population was re-derived, and reach found nothing left to rank

F2-239 filed 19 residual sites, all `PUT`, and said to order them by reach. Re-derived per F2-221:
**11 routes resolved from their controllers, all binding the ENTITY, none carrying `@Valid`**, 7 with
a frontend write client, and **every update method having exactly one Java caller — its own
controller**, so there is no second producer (F2-238's question, asked and answered).

Then the ordering itself came up empty: **all six live callers explicitly send every initialised
field they could omit.** `NdiPage` builds one 25-key body for both create and edit;
`EsgClimateTab`, `EsgCapaTab`, `EsgGhgInventoryTab` and `EsgSgiTab` each name every axis. So no site
was live, and reach had nothing to sort.

🔑 **That is an argument for sweeping the population, not for closing the file.** F2-237's own
headline is that *a defence in one client is not a defence*; here the defence was the shape of one
object literal, and for six of the nineteen there was no client at all — F2-214's
invitation-to-build shape. Removing the initialisers makes the hazard **absent rather than latent**
(F2-213), and takes the gate from *"19 known"* to *"none representable"*.

### Sorted by what the initialiser ASSERTS, four are flattering — measured dev = prod

| entry | reset to | rows it would change | what the reset asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `VendorAssessment#riskRating` | `MEDIUM` | **13 of 19** are HIGH | downgrades a third-party risk rating |
| `GhgEmissionRecord#coveragePercent` | `100.00` | 8 of 18 sit at 48–89% | **manufactures** ISAE 3410 assurance coverage |
| `NdiFrameworkItem#mandatory` | `false` | **13 of 20** are mandatory | makes a mandatory NDMO requirement optional |
| `ControlMapping#coverage` | `FULL` | 1 of 5 is PARTIAL | reports partial control coverage as full |
| `NdiComplianceAssessment#complianceStatus` | `UNDER_REVIEW` | 12 of 14 | re-opens a settled NCA/NDI assessment |
| `CorrectiveAction#priority` | `MEDIUM` | 14 of 25 | |
| `ClimateRiskOpportunity#impact` / `#likelihood` / `#timeHorizon` | `3` / `3` / `MEDIUM` | 12, 10, 7 of 17 | flattens a TCFD / IFRS S2 assessment |
| `BcmCommunicationContact#escalationLevel` | `1` | 12 of 19 | resets a crisis call-tree tier to the first rung |
| the other 6 | | 0 | latent on today's data |

🔑 **A reset that manufactures an assurance does not lose a fact, it asserts one** — F2-238's rule,
and two of the four sharpest are of that kind rather than the losing kind.

### The fix needed a fifth writer kind, and the gate would have failed on the correct fix without it

Two of the nineteen defaults belong in a purpose-built request record's `toEntity()`, not in a
service: `POST /api/sustainability/climate-risks` and `POST /api/sustainability/ghg` bind
`ClimateRiskCreateRequest` / `GhgCreateRequest` and hand the service an entity they built —
F2-233's fourth wire-closing mechanism, arriving on the **writer** side. The gate's `Moved` leg
resolved writers through `liveServices()` (files named `*Service.java`), so it would have reported
both as *"no such writer"* on a correct fix. `liveWriters()` widens it, and
`theWriterScopeReallyIncludesNonServiceWriters` asserts the widening is load-bearing rather than
decorative — mutation M8 confirms narrowing it back goes red.

### ⚠⚠ THE GATE'S CREATE-PATH LEG HAD BEEN A WHOLE-FILE SUBSTRING CHECK SINCE F2-238

The mutation harness found M7 surviving: deleting `NdiFrameworkItemService#create`'s
`if (req.getMandatory() == null) req.setMandatory(false);` left the build **green**, because
`everyRemovedInitialiserHasAWriterOnTheCreatePath` asked whether the writer *file* contains
`setMandatory(` anywhere — and `importJson` and `update` both do. **F2-194's
substring-satisfied-by-something-else, in the leg that has been certifying this fix shape for two
slices.** Every `Moved` entry now names the **method**, which is self-verifying (a method that does
not exist, or does not hold the setter, fails), scoped by a brace-balanced `methodBody()` with its
own synthetic positive control. 8/8 killed after.

⚠ A name-shape classifier could **not** have derived those methods: `CloudServiceService` puts all
nine of F2-238's defaults in a helper called `applyCreateDefaults`, which matches no
`create|add|import` pattern. They were read, not guessed.

### ⚠⚠ MY OWN GATE REFUTED MY OWN FIX ON ITS FIRST RUN

Closing the separate defect below meant adding `if (req.getStatus() != null)` to
`updateAssessment` — over a field `VendorAssessment` also initialised, i.e. **a brand-new
never-firing guard**. The gate named it immediately. Roughly two in ten of a slice's own claims fall
on first run (F2-188, F2-192, F2-204, F2-211); this one fell to the instrument the same slice was
extending. `status` joined the sweep as the 55th `Moved` entry, its default owned by
`createAssessment`.

⚠ `tprm.vendor_assessments.status` carries a **database DEFAULT of `'PLANNED'`**, and that does not
rescue it: the entity maps the column insertable, so Hibernate names it in the INSERT and sends an
explicit null. F2-215's fourth filling mechanism looks like it applies here and does not.

### A separate defect the probe walked into — F2-213's family, in the file F2-213 half-fixed

`TprmService#updateAssessment` wrote `assessmentDate`, `assessor`, `status`, `findings` and
`nextReviewDate` **unconditionally**. Because `assessment_date` and `status` are NOT NULL, the route
answered **400 "A required field was not supplied"** to every partial body — and a body that did
supply those two nulled the other three, populated on **18 of 19** live rows in dev and **19 of 19**
in prod. F2-213 fixed exactly this shape in `updateVendor` **sixty lines above** and left this one
(F2-215: two of N, and the mechanism a reader finds present makes the rest look covered). No
frontend client calls the route, so guarding it cannot break a working request — it converts a 400
into a partial update that behaves as its verb reads.

🔑 **Found by the probe, not by a gate**, and recorded that way: `FullReplaceUpdateContractTest`
passes over it because the method persists the loaded row rather than its own parameter.

### An existing test's FIXTURE depended on the initialiser

`CorrectiveActionServiceTest.aggregate_countsByType` went 1 → 0 on `CORRECTIVE`: its helper built
`new CorrectiveAction()` and leaned on the entity's `actionType = "CORRECTIVE"` to make one of two
rows corrective, while explicitly setting `PREVENTIVE` on the other. 🔑 **A fixture where one value
comes from the entity and the other from the test cannot tell you which half is load-bearing**
(F2-179) — and here the silent half was the defect. The fixture now says CORRECTIVE out loud.

### Four detector errors while deriving this, in both directions

F2-228's rule — two errors in opposite directions produce an answer neither earns:

1. the body-type regex demanded `@Valid @RequestBody` (a literal `@` before an optional group) and
   reported `body=None` on **all 11** routes;
2. the frontend path match was a literal while the house idiom is `const BASE = '/api/…'` plus a
   template, so it reported **0 frontend clients** — the flattering direction here;
3. the omit check read only the call ARGUMENT, so the opaque `updateFrameworkItem(id, body)` read as
   sending nothing and reported 4 false omissions;
4. with locals resolved it still missed `weight,` — an **ES6 shorthand property** does not match
   `field\s*:`.

⚠ Two self-inflicted edit errors as well, both caught by reading the diff: `([ \t]*)` captured the
spaces between a same-line `@Column(...)` and the field (this codebase column-aligns them), so a
`//` comment landed mid-line and commented out the declaration; and `([^\r\n]*)$` **cannot match in
a CRLF file** — with `(?m)`, `$` sits immediately before `\n`, after the `\r` the class forbids —
so the corrected script reported **0 of 19** until the anchor became `(?=\r?\n|\Z)`. The CRLF trap
for the fourth time in this lineage, in the script where I had just added CRLF handling for the
output.

## F2-239 · The register is the boundary, and `@Valid` on a bound entity was refusing every partial body

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-239 |
| **Title** | Editing a transcribed NCA ECC requirement moved it to the top of the regulation, marked it a placeholder and recorded it English-only — and on the change checklist the same family met `@Valid`, so neither "Add task" nor the status toggle had ever worked |
| **Severity** | 🔴 P2 (live, dev = prod: 207 of 214 citations are not placeholders, 212 of 214 are ordered, 207 of 214 are past EN_ONLY — the edit form omits all three; both change-task write routes answered 400 to every body the UI sends) |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · server-owned state |
| **Modules** | `platform/regulatory` (2 entities, 1 service), `change_mgmt` (entity, service, controller, repository), FE (3 files), 1 gate, 2 new test classes |

### The ordering that finds the live sites is WHICH FIELD THE CALLER OMITS

F2-238 filed a 28-entry work list, all `PUT`, and ranked it by **what the initialiser asserts** —
naming `GhgEmissionRecord#coveragePercent` (resets to 100.00, an ISAE 3410 assurance input) and
`AuthorityDocument#isPlaceholder` (resets to true) as the two sharpest.

Re-derived (F2-221), the population is 14 routes across 12 services, **all binding the ENTITY**
(resolved from the controllers, not guessed). 10 have a frontend write client. But neither body
width nor initialiser severity decides reachability: **what decides it is whether the live caller's
object literal contains that field's key.** Measured that way, of 28 entries **4 are live**:

| entry | initialiser | the live caller |
|---|---|---|
| `AuthorityDocumentCitation#sequenceOrder` | `0` | omitted by `RegulatoryLibraryPage`'s citation form |
| `AuthorityDocumentCitation#isPlaceholder` | `true` | omitted |
| `AuthorityDocumentCitation#translationStatus` | `"EN_ONLY"` | omitted |
| `ChangeTask#sortOrder` | `0` | omitted by `ChangeDetailPanel`'s `{ status: next }` |

🔑 **F2-238's ranking picked one field that is not reachable and the wrong half of the other.**
`coveragePercent` IS sent by its only caller. The live `isPlaceholder` is the **citation's** — a
different entity, edited by a second form on the same page which has inputs for three fewer fields.
**Harm-if-reached and reach are two orderings and they disagree; a work list has to carry both.**

### The regulatory half, probed against rows the probe plants itself (F2-206)

```
planted:  seq=300  placeholder=False  translation=AR_OFFICIAL  mandatory=False  weight=2.50  req_ar=yes
PUT /api/v1/regulatory/citations/{id}   the page's exact 6-key body   ->  HTTP 200
after:    seq=0    placeholder=True   translation=EN_ONLY
```

`sequence_order` is what orders a regulation: the repository finder ends `OrderBySequenceOrderAsc`
and `citationsToTree` sorts by it. **Document 9 holds 167 citations spanning 100..4360 with 159
distinct values**, so editing any one requirement paragraph moved it above section 1-1-1.
`is_placeholder` renders as a warning badge on the citation tree, so a transcribed NCA ECC
sub-control started reading as a stub.

🔑 **And `translation_status` → `EN_ONLY` is the sharpest, because the reset contradicts the request
that produced it.** The citation form has Arabic inputs and sends them; 214 of 214 rows carry
`title_ar` and 196 of 214 carry `requirement_text_ar`. So a human translating a requirement into
Arabic and pressing Save recorded the citation as English-only. Arabic is the platform's primary
language (house rule 7). F2-213's *a reset is worse than a null* one step further: this reset
asserts the absence of the exact data the caller just supplied.

🔑 **The correct artefact was 20 lines above the wrong one in the same file.** `createCitation`
already defaults all five of these fields and *inherits* `isPlaceholder` from the parent document — a
citation transcribed into a placeholder document is a placeholder. That reasoning predates this
finding; `updateCitation` discarded it on every edit.

### ⚠⚠ The change-task half was not a reset. Both its write routes REFUSED

`ChangeTask.titleAr` is `@NotBlank` (F2-30, enforcing house rule 7) and both routes bound the entity
with `@Valid`. Probed live with the exact bodies the UI sends:

```
POST /api/v1/changes/{id}/tasks   { titleEn, status, ownerName, dueAt }   ->  400  titleAr: Field must not be blank
PUT  /api/v1/changes/tasks/{id}   { status: next }                        ->  400  titleAr: Field must not be blank
PUT  /api/v1/changes/tasks/{id}   { status, titleAr }                     ->  200  sort_order 300 -> 0
```

So **neither the "Add task" button nor the status toggle on the change implementation checklist had
ever worked**, and the third line is the reset sitting behind the 400. 🔑 **A reachability derivation
that stops at the caller's body cannot see that the route refuses it** — F2-238's
*the-throw-was-holding-the-write-shut*, from the other side and in a mechanism with no hand-written
guard in it: bean validation runs before the service is entered and cannot tell an OMITTED mandatory
field from a BLANK one.

🔑 **F2-105 diagnosed this exact mechanism, wrote eleven lines explaining it, and fixed it in the
FRONTEND** — the PIR card resends `{...change}`, with a comment noting the card "400'd on every save
from the day F2-30 landed". That closes one caller. It is not a defence (F2-237), and **the write-up
is what made the two siblings in the same controller look covered** (F2-215): a reader who finds the
mechanism explained does not then ask which other routes share it.

### The fix

* **Remove the initialiser, own the default on the create path** — 9 initialisers across 3 entities.
  Every column is NOT NULL, so `everyRemovedInitialiserHasAWriterOnTheCreatePath` asserts all 35
  `(entity, field, writer)` triples in both directions: a writer that stops setting one turns a
  silent reset into a **500 on create**, and `ddl-auto=none` means nothing else would notice. There
  are **no other Java producers** of these three entities (0 `new X()` sites; the other five classes
  touching their repositories only read), so the service creates are the whole population.
* **Drop `@Valid` from the two partial-update PUT routes** and put the invariant on the ROW:
  `requireNotBlank` refuses a BLANK mandatory title with a 400 naming the field, while an OMITTED one
  leaves the stored value alone. Kept on the two CREATE routes, where a full entity genuinely
  arrives — and the add-task form now has the Arabic input house rule 7 requires, which is why the
  create's 400 is correct rather than the defect.
* **`ClosedVocabulary` for the translation status, per column.** `updateCitation` validated nothing,
  so a caller could store any string in a CHECK-constrained column and get the CHECK's 409 rather
  than a 400; and because the column collates case-INSENSITIVELY (F2-179), `'ar_official'` was
  ACCEPTED and stored verbatim while every reader compares case-sensitively — probed both, pre-fix.
  `require`, not `coerce`, per F2-182's test: the CHECK already refuses everything outside the
  vocabulary, so no working request can start failing. This also retires a **seventh hand-rolled
  vocabulary** that `HandRolledVocabularyMirrorTest` never listed.
* **`OrderBySortOrderAscIdAsc`** on the task finder, matching the sibling `ChangeConditionRepository`
  which has always had the tie-break. Every UI-created task carries `sort_order = 0`, so ties are the
  normal case and without a second key their order is whatever the database returns (F2-197).

### The new gate leg, and its pre-fix control

`noPartialUpdateRouteBindsAnEntityWithValid` is a **hard zero with an EMPTY exemption map**: the
better fix is always available (bind a purpose-built request record, which puts the route outside the
population by construction — F2-213's structural direction), so there is no correct code for it to
fail on. Measured: **172 PUT/PATCH routes take a body, 94 bind an entity, 9 of 411 entities declare a
bean-validated mandatory field, and exactly 2 routes were in the intersection.** Both fixed → 0.

⚠ **The leg passed on its first run, which is also what a rotted regex looks like.** Restoring
master's controller into the tree makes it fail naming both routes and nothing else, and a synthetic
self-test drives both patterns against the literal pre-fix and post-fix shapes. The one that matters
is the annotation ORDER: the house idiom is `@Valid @RequestBody T x`, and a pattern anchored on
`@RequestBody` looking only forwards reported **0 of 2** — indistinguishable from a clean tree.

`CitationPartialUpdateTest` **7/7** and `ChangeTaskPartialUpdateTest` **5/5** · full suite

against a backend restarted on the fixed tree (F2-217), with the pre-fix control reproducing all

**0 residual** `[REVIEW-TEST]` (hard-deleted with `CHARINDEX`).

  (`BcmCommunicationContact` ×3, `RiskControlLink#linkType`, `SustainabilityEvidence

## F2-238 · A PATCH whose omitted fields are written is a contract violation, and the throw was holding the write shut

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-238 |
| **Title** | The only write the cloud-service register offers reset eight columns including five NCA CSCC security flags, and on three sibling registers the same shape refused the request instead — every row broken one way or the other |
| **Severity** | 🔴 P2 (live, dev = prod: a status-only PATCH rewrote 8 of 8 planted security-posture fields; 5 of 5 crisis events, 4 of 7 BIA assessments and 6 of 13 issues could not be PATCHed at all) |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · server-owned state |
| **Modules** | `cyber`, `bcm/cycle` (×3), `platform` (×2), FE (1 file), 1 gate |

### The slice boundary is the HTTP verb, and it is derived rather than chosen

F2-237 filed a 46-site work list with no verdicts. Executing it, the population was ordered by
**reachability** rather than by field count — a never-firing null-guard is a defect on paper
wherever it appears, and what makes one live is a caller that sends a body narrower than the entity.
Re-derived: all 20 routes bind the ENTITY (re-checked, not assumed), 14 of 20 have a frontend write
client, and **10 narrow-literal call sites across 9 services** send a partial body.

Of the 20, **six are `@PatchMapping`**. That is the boundary this slice took, because a `PUT` has
full-replace semantics as a defensible reading — a caller who omits a field there arguably asked for
the default — while **a PATCH's entire contract is that omitted fields are left alone**. Writing the
entity's initialiser over a stored value there is a contract violation, not merely a defect.

### ⚠⚠ Two consequences of one shape, and which you get depends only on whether the guard's body is a WRITE or a THROW

| register | verb | consequence | measured, dev = prod |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CloudService` | PATCH | **WRITE** — silent reset of 9 fields | SSO/MFA/encryption-at-rest true on **14 of 15**, kingdom-residency on **10 of 15**, deployment model on 4 of 15 |
| `CrisisEvent` | PATCH | **THROW** — the route refuses | **5 of 5** live crisis events cannot be PATCHed at all |
| `BcmBiaAssessment` | PATCH | **THROW** | **4 of 7** |
| `Issue` | PATCH | **THROW** + 2 resets | **6 of 13**; severity differs on 8 of 13, priority on 12 of 13 |
| `BcmComplianceMapping` | PATCH | **WRITE** | `is_placeholder` differs on **392 of 412** |
| `Department` | PATCH | **WRITE** | 0 of 34 (latent) |

The three THROW cases all carry
`if (patch.getStatus() != null && !patch.getStatus().equals(existing.getStatus())) throw` — the
"use `transition()` to change status" guard — over a status the entity initialises. The null test
can never be false, so the **comparison** fires for every row not in the initial state.

🔑 **And in those three the THROW was holding the WRITE shut.** A row past the initial state got a
400 and was therefore *safe* from the resets; a row still in the initial state was reset. **Fixing
only the throw would have converted a broken route into a data-destroying one** — F2-203's rule
(fixing one defect is what detonates the next), and the reason the fix is "remove the initialiser"
rather than "rewrite the guard": removing it closes both halves in one move.

### The live half, probed against rows the probe plants itself (F2-206)

`CyberCloudServicesPage` has **no edit form at all** — `formOpen` is only ever opened by "New
service" — so the register's only write is `cyberCloudServicesApi.update(svc.id, { status })`.
Unlike F2-237, **the frontend carried no workaround**. Pre-fix control, live as `so_officer`:

```
planted:  IAAS · PRIVATE · ksa=True · CRITICAL · sso=True · mfa=True · atRest=True · inTransit=False
PATCH {"status": "UNDER_REVIEW"}  ->  HTTP 200
after:    SAAS · PUBLIC  · ksa=False · MEDIUM   · sso=False · mfa=False · atRest=False · inTransit=True
8 of 8 fields silently rewritten
```

🔑 **`encryptionInTransit` resets to `true` — the one flag whose initialiser is not `false`.** Every
other reset LOST an assurance; that one MANUFACTURES one, turning a service recorded as not
encrypting in transit into one that does. F2-213's *a reset is worse than a null* at its sharpest,
and it is the latent half (0 of 15 rows hold `false` today).

Three rows are `GOV_PRIVATE` — the National Government Cloud, the SDAIA/NDMO national data
platform and the sanctioned analytics platform — so a status change reclassified the tenant's most
sensitive services as **PUBLIC cloud** while clearing residency, SSO, MFA and encryption at rest.

**Post-fix 25/25**; pre-fix control fired on 3 of 3 reachable legs. ⚠ The crisis/issue WRITE half
**cannot be demonstrated pre-fix at all, and that is the finding rather than a gap in the probe**:
the throw refuses the request before any setter runs.

### ⚠⚠ Fixing the reset detonated the next defect, exactly as predicted — and the vocabulary was masking it

`update()` ends with `validate(existing)`, and `DEPLOYMENT_MODELS` was
`{PUBLIC, PRIVATE, HYBRID, COMMUNITY}` while `cyber.cloud_services` carries **no CHECK constraint of
any kind** and stores `GOV_PRIVATE` on 3 live rows in both databases. Pre-fix the reset overwrote
`deploymentModel` with `"PUBLIC"` *before* `validate()` saw it, so the mismatch was invisible.
Preserving the stored value — the correct behaviour — is what makes `validate()` reachable for it:
**omit the token and the fix turns a silent reset into a 400 on the National Government Cloud.** So
declaring `GOV_PRIVATE` in the server's Set and in `CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT_MODELS` is not a separate
tidy-up, it is part of the same fix. F2-180's lesson inverted — the only narrowing was wrong about
what the register holds.

### The fix, and its one real hazard

Per entity: **remove the initialiser, own the default on the create path.** That makes the
null-guard mean what it reads, and it is the design F2-237 established. 24 initialisers removed
across 6 entities.

⚠ **No entity has a `@PrePersist`**, so the initialisers were the only default mechanism for three
Java producers that bypass the service create. `CcmService` (the third-consecutive-CRITICAL-failure
issue F2-228 fixed) and `KriBreachService` set severity/priority explicitly and route through
`issueService.create`, so a create-path default covers them; **`BcmAuditCompletionService` saves
straight to the repository** and set only 3 of `CrisisEvent`'s 5, so its two flags are now stated
there — honestly, since a SIEM auto-escalation does not know either fact at detection time.

`everyRemovedInitialiserHasAWriterOnTheCreatePath` asserts all 26 (entity, field, writer) triples in
**both** directions: the entity must not initialise the field, and the writer must set it. Every one
of these columns is NOT NULL, so a writer that stops setting it turns a silent reset into a **500 on
create** — the one way this fix shape can go wrong, and `ddl-auto=none` means nothing else in the
tree would notice.

### ⚠⚠ A phantom in my own gate: 18 entries were fixed and one was never real

The gate reported `CloudService#status` as still open after the cyber initialiser was removed.
`initialisedFields` keyed entities by their **simple name** and merged with `computeIfAbsent`, and
there are two live `CloudService` classes — `module/cyber/entity` and `module/outsourcing/entity`,
the latter declaring `status = "ONBOARDING"`. So the outsourcing twin's initialiser was attributed
to the cyber service. **F2-233's keying-ambiguity lesson, in an instrument written one slice before
it.** It OVER-reports, so it fails loudly rather than hiding a site — but **a phantom entry in a
hard-asserted list is worse than a missing one, because it looks measured.** Re-keyed to the
fully-qualified name, with the pairing resolved by longest shared package prefix and both twins
pinned by name in both directions. Work list **46 → 28**: 17 fixed, 1 phantom.

⚠ My own anti-vacuity leg caught the re-keying (it looked up `inits.get("MaterialTopic")` by simple
name and went null) — which is the leg doing its job.

### Verification

`NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` **5/5** · full suite **4,100 / 0 / 0** on a forced
`target/test-classes` rebuild (F2-223) · live probe **25/25 post-fix**, pre-fix control 3 of 3
reachable legs firing plus the 8-of-8 CloudService reset reproduced on a planted row · FE `tsc`
clean, **72 files / 797 tests** · registers restored to 15 / 5 / 13 live rows with **0 residual**
`[REVIEW-TEST]` (hard-deleted with `CHARINDEX`, because the API's DELETE is a soft delete —
F2-237 left three rows behind that way).

⚠ Two probe corrections, both from running it: `compliance` is **403** on `/cyber/cloud-services`
(needs `CYBER:WRITE` → `so_officer`), and `/api/v1/issues` is reachable **only by `admin`** —
`PLATFORM:WRITE` is held by one role with zero active users, which is F2-220's own open filing
confirming itself. Stated because *admin proves nothing about authorization*; that leg tests data
semantics, and the guard is the filing.

### Filed

- **The remaining 28-site work list**, all `PUT` routes. The sharpest by consequence are
  `GhgEmissionRecord#coveragePercent` (resets to **100.00**, an ISAE 3410 assurance input) and
  `AuthorityDocument#isPlaceholder` / `AuthorityDocumentCitation#isPlaceholder` (reset to **true**,
  marking a real regulatory instrument a placeholder). Read the route and probe it; do not write 28
  reasons (F2-188).
- **`cyber.cloud_services` has no CHECK constraint on any of its four vocabulary columns** — now
  cheap to add, since this slice closed the only open writer and declared the missing token
  (F2-183's rule: the constraint and its writer land in the same commit).
- **The structural root, unchanged from F2-213**: 83 entity-bound `PUT` handlers. A purpose-built
  request record per endpoint would make this whole family unrepresentable, because a field the
  bound type does not declare can never arrive. Bigger than one slice, and an owner decision.
- `platform.issues` and `bcm.crisis_events` still have **no CHECK on `status`** (F2-220's filing).

## F2-237 · A null-guard on a field whose entity declares an initialiser can never fire

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-237 |
| **Title** | `if (req.getX() != null)` reads as a partial update and behaves as a full replace — an edit to a topic's title took a CRITICAL double-materiality score to 0.0 / LOW, and the frontend was carrying the workaround |
| **Severity** | 🔴 P2 (live: silent destruction of a CMA Article 92(a) / CSRD-ESRS double-materiality input on every edit that omitted the axes) |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · server-owned state |
| **Modules** | `sust/materiality`, `db/migration` (V379), FE (1 file), 2 gates |

### What was measured — F2-220's filed population, re-derived first (F2-221)

F2-220 filed *"the population of transition-by-parameter registers is unmeasured"*. Re-derived in
Java over the same tree as the shipped detector (F2-213: a Python locator with a narrower resolver
reports *absent* where the gate reports *classified*):

| | |
|---|---|
| machines `ServerStampedFieldContractTest.machineOwned` sees | **28** |
| machines a permissive scan that also walks NON-PUBLIC methods sees | **30** |
| delta the shipped detector can never see | **15 sites / 13 keys** |
| create-side hits in that delta | **6**, all delta-only |
| confirmed live | **1** |

🔑 **The nine registers named in `MEASURED_MACHINES` are an anti-vacuity guard, not a census** — the
detector already saw 28. That is now asserted with the real figure beside it, so the next reader
cannot mistake one for the other.

**The four genuine machines the gate is blind to, for three distinct structural reasons** — all four
closed on the create side today by their own mechanism, which is a fact about today and not a
property of the control (F2-182), and therefore asserted rather than assumed:

- **a different exception family** — `RecertificationService#decide` (IAM access recertification,
  four-eyes: *"reviewers cannot certify their own access"*) and `SodService#disposition` both refuse
  with `ResponseStatusException`, which the detector's inline
  `IllegalState|IllegalArgument|IllegalTransition` test cannot match. F2-231's headline, on the
  machine side this time.
- **a refusal in a shared helper, plus a write-verb name** — `EvidenceRequestService#updateStatus`
  fails two clauses at once.
- **a PRIVATE machine** — `EvidenceItemService#transitionStatus`, called by five public wrappers.
  This gate's population is `publicMethods`, so it is invisible *by construction*. Two more are
  private and otherwise fully visible: `PlanDistributionService#transition` and
  `ChangeManagementService#closeCondition`, which is exactly the 30 − 28. **F2-198's shape at an
  ACCESS MODIFIER** — the eleventh narrowing this programme has met, after a filename, a three-entry
  allow-list, a module name, a controller-bearing table, an `extends` clause and a field-name list.

⚠ **9 of the 15 delta sites are my own detector over-matching.** The relaxation that let a helper
satisfy *"reads F on that row"* pulled in `CorrectiveAction#titleEn`, `EvidenceReview#notesEn`,
`BcpPlan#planType` and `NdiComplianceAssessment#evidenceRef` — none of them state. It pointed at a
real defect anyway, of an **adjacent shape**: not a state machine but a **validated range**.

### The adjacent shape, measured as its own population

*A method that refuses a numeric parameter outside a range and writes field F from it, in a service
whose create/update writes F from the request with no such refusal.* **13 range-guarded fields, 11
bypassed pairs, 3 services** — and 2 of the 3 refuted by reading:

- `NdiAssessmentCycle#reportingYear` — **REFUTED**: `validate()` already throws *"reportingYear must
  be 2020..2100"* and both write paths call it. F2-182's recorded lesson exactly (a guard sits in a
  shared `validate()` a setter-site regex cannot see).
- `ProcessorAssessment#assessedBy` — **REFUTED**: an actor id, not a range.
- `MaterialTopic` — **CONFIRMED**, 8 of the 11 pairs.

🔑 **The pattern was already in the tree, in the sibling artefact.**
`NdiAssessmentCycleService.validate()` carries its range rule so no write path can miss it;
`MaterialTopicService.validate()` checked the topic name, the category, the reporting year and the
status — and not the two axes the whole register exists to record.

### 🔑 The live defect, and it is not the range

The unit test written for the range failed on a fixture built the way Jackson builds a request
(`new MaterialTopic()`), and **that failure was the finding**. `MaterialTopic` declares
`= BigDecimal.ZERO` on all four score columns because they are NOT NULL, so a PUT that omits the key
deserialises to ZERO rather than to null: **`if (req.getImpactMateriality() != null)` was true on
every single request.** The line read as a partial update and behaved as a full replace.

Probed live as `compliance` (SUST:WRITE, not PLATFORM_ADMIN) against a topic the probe plants itself
(F2-206) — **pre-fix control 5 legs firing, post-fix 11/11**:

```
PUT /api/sustainability/materiality/{id}  {"topicEn": "...", "category": "GOVERNANCE"}
  pre-fix   HTTP 200   impact=0  financial=0  score=0.0  tier=LOW      ← was 3.5 / 2.0 / 3.5 / HIGH
  post-fix  HTTP 200   impact=3.5 financial=2.0 score=3.5 tier=HIGH
```

**An edit that changed only the title took a scored topic to LOW.** `recomputeScore` runs on every
save, so `materiality_score` and `priority_tier` followed it down.

🔑 **The frontend was carrying the workaround.** `EsgMaterialityTab`'s edit handler echoed both axes
back with a comment explaining that *"an omitted value would zero out the score + tier"*. **A defence
in one client is not a defence** — the next caller does not have it, and this whole family is
reachable exactly where machine callers live (F2-179). The echo is now deleted along with the reason
for it.

⚠ **And the create was worse than latent.** The pre-fix probe stored `impact=4.6` with
`stakeholderImportance=0`: the create never mirrored the legacy pair, so **the two spellings of one
fact disagreed from birth**. Measured 0 disagreeing rows in dev and prod only because every seeded
row was written by `seed_real_data.py` and not through the API.

### Why no gate in this tree could already see it

| gate | why it was green |
|---|---|
| `FullReplaceUpdateContractTest` structural leg | asks whether a method persists its own request parameter; this one persists the loaded row |
| its coverage leg | asks whether a written field is *declarable* by the frontend type — with a `Partial<MaterialTopic>` client every field is (F2-214's recorded reason) |
| `ServerStampedFieldContractTest` | subtracts anything a null-guard protects — **the exact subtraction this defect defeats**, because the guard is decorative |
| `WireContractTest` | the types agree; the payload builder is free to omit |

### The fix

One private `applyAxes()` is the only writer of all four score columns: it calls `requireAxis()`
(0..5, naming the field), mirrors the legacy pair **from** the canonical axis, and recomputes. The
range also goes into `validate()`, so a future write path that forgets the writer still cannot store
an out-of-range score — the shape `NdiAssessmentCycleService` already had.

**The edit route writes none of the four.** The axes belong to `create()` and to the dedicated Score
action, which is what the register already said out loud (*"Scoring is owned by the dedicated Score
action"*). A route that cannot write them cannot zero them, and the mirror cannot be driven apart.

`require`, not `coerce` (F2-182's test — what already refuses this?): the frontend gates 0..5 in the
create form and the score dialog, so no request a human can make starts failing, and clamping would
silently record a materiality score nobody chose.

⚠ **The audit line now names the derived move.** `recomputeScore` runs on every save, so an edit to
an owner name can move a CMA disclosure input; the old line read `"Material topic updated"` whatever
changed (F2-188: a duplicated derivation agrees on the row and differs on the trail, which is the
part nothing asserts).

### V379 — the two CHECKs, and *which* two were missing

`sust.material_topic` already carried **five** CHECK constraints, two of them bounding
`stakeholder_importance` and `business_impact` to 0..5 — the **legacy** mirror pair — while the
canonical `impact_materiality` / `financial_materiality` had none. **F2-215's two-of-N shape, at the
schema.** Scope tied to the writers the same commit closed (F2-183); measured in both databases first
(26 live rows each, 0 outside range, 0 disagreeing mirrors), so no `WITH NOCHECK`; applied twice to
dev, both constraints trusted, all four columns proven to refuse against a planted `[REVIEW-TEST]`
row that a legal value still updates.

⚠ The pre-fix probe shows the migration and the writer are two halves: with V379 applied and the
service reverted, an out-of-range create answered **409 with a diagnostic naming no field**; the
service fix is what makes it a **400 naming `impactMateriality`**.

### The general shape — 46 sites, shipped as a work list with NO verdicts

`NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` derives every entity-bound update that guards
`if (req.getX() != null)` on a field the entity initialises: **46 sites across 20 services** (50
before this slice), exactly asserted in both directions, **no reasons attached** (F2-188: five reasons
written for code nobody had read were five false claims, and fluency read as verification). Whether
each is live depends on what its callers omit — a fact to establish per site.

Two things are clear from the initialisers alone:

- **a reset is worse than a null** (F2-213) — `false`, `0`, `"MEDIUM"` and `new BigDecimal("100.00")`
  all read as facts rather than as missing data;
- **several are flattering in the direction that matters** —
  `GhgEmissionRecord#coveragePercent` resets to **100.00** (an ISAE 3410 assurance input),
  `CloudService#encryptionInTransit` to **true**, while `CrisisEvent#severity` resets to **1** and
  `AuthorityDocument#isPlaceholder` to **true**, marking a real regulatory instrument a placeholder.

- Live probe **11/11 post-fix**, and a **pre-fix control** run against the stashed service on the same
  live stack — 5 legs fire, including the zeroing.
- `MaterialTopicServiceTest` **11/11** (6 new: the range per route, the omitted-axis case with the
  initialiser asserted, the mirror, the audit both ways, and a structural leg that each of the four
  setters has exactly one writer).
- `NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` **4/4**, including a synthetic self-test driving the detector
  against the literal pre-fix shape and three shapes it must NOT flag (F2-195).
- `ServerStampedFieldContractTest` **21/21** with the four blind-spot machines named.
- Full suite **4,099** tests; the only two failures were `MeasuredBaselineFreshnessTest` demanding the
  migration count and pending set be updated for V379 — the gate doing its job.
- FE `tsc` clean. 26 live rows before and after; 3 soft-deleted probe rows hard-deleted with
  `CHARINDEX`, 0 residual.

### 🔑 My own claim, refuted by my own gate on its first run

The first draft asserted that `EvidenceItemCreateRequest` declares no `status` — *"the strongest
closure there is, because a field the bound type does not declare can never arrive"*. **It declares
one.** The closure is the weaker kind: the client may send a status and `applyRequest` silently drops
it. Roughly two in ten of a new instrument's own claims fall on first run (F2-188, F2-192, F2-204,
F2-211), and the reverse-facing assertion is what found this one. Recorded in the gate so nobody
re-derives the stronger claim from the SEC-EVD-002 comment, which only says the service must not read
it.

### Filed

- **The 46-site work list** — read the route, probe it, record the verdict, lower the figure in the
  same commit. Do NOT write 46 reasons.
- **`sust.material_topic`'s stored derived values, and this one is larger than F2-230's**: 20 of 26
  live rows hold a `materiality_score` LOWER than `MAX(impact, financial)` and **0 higher**, so the
  register under-states materiality; **14 priority tiers would move on the next save, 12 to
  CRITICAL**; **8 rows' tier contradicts their own stored score** (id 14 stores 4.5 with tier HIGH
  where the bucket says CRITICAL, which proves the stored tier was never computed by this code).
  Identical in dev and prod. `recomputeScore` runs on every save, so each self-repairs the first time
  an operator edits it — which is why the audit line now names the move. Re-deriving 26 live rows in
  two real databases is an **owner decision** (F2-183, F2-196, F2-230).
- **`MaterialTopicCreateRequest` has no Arabic topic field on the create form's required set** while
  `topic_ar` is offered — house rule 7 territory, unchanged by this slice.

## F2-235 · The corpus an instrument cannot read scores exactly like a clean one

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-235 |
| **Title** | Three source files held raw control bytes; a NUL makes ripgrep read the file as binary, so every content sweep silently skipped the KB XSS guard |
| **Severity** | 🟠 P3 (no runtime defect — measurement integrity, and the file affected carries a stored-XSS guard) + instrument closure |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · instrument integrity |
| **Modules** | `config` (new gate), `security` (F2-234's own gate file), `intake` (test fixture), FE `knowledge-base` |

### What was measured

Not a filed item. Found while grepping `SplitAttributionContractTest` to re-read F2-234's work
list: the Grep tool answered **`binary file matches (found "\0" byte around offset 27186)`** and
returned **no lines**, for a pattern that occurs many times in that file.

Census across the trees every instrument in this repo scans (`tss-grc-backend/src/main`,
`.../src/test`, `tss-grc-ui-v2/src` — **3,557 files**):

| file | bytes | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| `security/SplitAttributionContractTest.java` | 3 × NUL | invisible to ripgrep — written by **F2-234's own** escape collapse, one slice earlier |
| `pages/knowledge-base/KbArticlePage.tsx` | NUL + 0x1F | invisible to ripgrep **since `957b679e`**, the commit that ADDED the URL-scheme XSS guard |
| `module/intake/service/IntakeSystemSubmissionTest.java` | 0x01 | greppable, but **deliberate** (F2-175's C0-control payload fixture) and illegible to a reader |

**All three were behaviour-preserving, which is exactly why they survived a 4,073-test green
build.** A raw 0x00 in a Java string literal is legal — the JLS says a `StringCharacter` is any
`InputCharacter` but `"` and `\` — so `"\0"` and a raw NUL compile to the same string. In a JS
regex literal `[\s<NUL>-<0x1F>]` and `[\s\x00-\x1f]` denote the same range. Nothing failed,
nothing behaved oddly, and no test could have noticed.

### Why it matters: the harm is to every measurement, not to a request

🔑 **Every finding in this programme is a scan over those two trees.** ripgrep classifies a file
containing a NUL as binary: a content-mode search prints `binary file matches` and **no lines**,
and a search whose pattern does not match prints **nothing at all** — indistinguishable from a
clean file. So the file contributes nothing to any sweep, and **the absence reads exactly like
nothing being wrong**. That is the under-reporting direction this register keeps recording
(F2-198's comment stripper, F2-208's heredoc `\b`, F2-217's lower-case-only shape, F2-229's
schema-less key).

The sharpest instance is `KbArticlePage.tsx`. It holds `sanitiseUrl`, the strict URL-scheme
allowlist for markdown links rendered through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` — the guard that stops
`[click me](javascript:alert(1))` executing with the reader's session. **So the one frontend file
most worth reading in a security sweep is the file no security sweep could read, since the day
the guard was written.** And `git diff --stat` reports it as `Bin 6962 -> 8366 bytes`: **git will
not show a textual diff for it either**, so the collapse was invisible in code review as well.

### The guard was sound, and had no test of any kind

Read rather than assumed, then pinned. `renderMarkdown` escapes `&`/`<`/`>` across the whole
document in step 1 and rewrites links in step 3, so the ordering closes the vector the allowlist
cannot see: written with real entities, `&#106;avascript&#58;alert(1)` contains **no colon at
all**, so `!trimmed.includes(':')` — the relative-path fallback — **accepts it**, and a browser
decoding the attribute would get `javascript:` back. What makes it inert is that step 1 has
already turned `&` into `&amp;`. 🔑 **Move step 1 below step 3 and the guard opens with no other
change**, and nothing asserted the ordering.

The comment sitting on that very line asserted the opposite: *"The HTML-escape pass above already
handled &lt;, &gt;, &amp;, **but the raw URL never passed through it**."* False, and false in the
one direction that matters — F2-184's shape, on the sentence a reader consults before touching the
pipeline.

`kbMarkdownSanitiser.test.ts` — **26 assertions, the file's first** — drives the renderer rather
than the private predicate, because the pipeline is the attack surface: 11 blocked schemes
(including tab-, NUL- and 0x1F-prefixed `javascript:`, `data:`, `vbscript:`, `file:`), 9 legitimate
URLs, the entity vector, the ordering asserted structurally, and the body escape.

### Two things only the mutation harness could show

⚠ **The obvious blocked-vector assertions did not depend on the mechanisms they appear to test.**
Deleting the leading-control strip leaves every `<TAB>javascript:` case **still blocked** — the
colon rule does that work — and deleting `.toLowerCase()` leaves `JavaScript:` blocked for the same
reason. Both mutations SURVIVED. The strip's and the case-fold's only observable effect is on a
**legitimate** URL (`<TAB>https://sama.gov.sa`, `HTTPS://SAMA.GOV.SA`), so two positive vectors had
to be added before either could be killed. 🔑 **A test that blocks the right things can still be
blind to why**, and the code comment naming the tab as *"a real XSS bypass in older WebKit"* points
at the strip, which is not the defence.

⚠ **My own gate file contained two raw control bytes and would have failed its own invariant** —
I wrote the self-test's NUL and 0x1F literally and they landed on disk faithfully. Fixed by
rewriting them as the octal escapes `\0` and `\037`, which is the claim the gate makes. The new
test builds its control characters with `String.fromCharCode` for the same reason: **a test that
pins this defect must not be able to contain it.**

### The gate

`config/ScannableSourceContractTest` — **a hard zero with no exemption map**, and that is safe
rather than strict (F2-214): Java and TypeScript both offer an escape for every control character,
so a raw one is never the only way to express an intent. The deliberate `intake` fixture is the
proof — it kept its behaviour and gained a reader.

Four legs: the invariant over a **derived** population (walk, don't list); a **per-root** floor
rather than one total, because the wrong answers are *a root that stops resolving* and *a scan that
reaches one tree* (2,000 / 400 / 700 against measured 2,286 / 446 / 825 — F2-215: a floor must sit
above the largest WRONG answer); a **synthetic self-test** that the detector fires on 0x00 and 0x1F
and not on tab/CR/LF (F2-195); and a leg naming **the three files by path**, because a count can be
satisfied by the wrong files while a walk that resolves the backend but not the frontend passes.

### Verification

- Pre-fix control: the detector **fires on `master` for all three files** (3 / 1 / 2 bytes) and is
  clean on the fixed tree. F2-229's rule — a green scan on the fixed tree cannot tell you the
  detector works.
- Mutation harness: **6 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss**, after two positive vectors were
  added. A 7th was **withdrawn as invalid** rather than counted: it weakened one of my own
  assertions, and you can always delete an assertion (F2-206).
- Full backend suite green; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; **72 vitest files / 797 tests** (from 71/771).
- No live probe: nothing about a request path changed. The claim is about what an instrument can
  read, and it is proved by the Grep tool's own output, quoted above.

### Filed

- `DB-11072026.sql` at the repo root is a **13 MB UTF-16LE** SQL dump (13.4 M NUL bytes),
  **untracked** — so it is not in the repo, but it does make local `*.sql` sweeps skip it. Excluded
  from the gate by root scoping rather than by name.
- The `//evil.com` protocol-relative case is **REFUTED as a finding**: `/` admits it, and the
  comment says *"same-origin relative paths"*, but a KB author who can write a link can already
  write `https://evil.com` — the allowlist permits http(s) by design — so it grants nothing. Noted
  because the comment overstates what `/` means, not because there is a defect behind it.

## F2-234 · One question, asked of a parameter, answered on one side of the wire

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-234 |
| **Title** | The four BCM services named their own state; a parameter-borne actor half was invisible to the split gate |
| **Severity** | 🔴 P2 (live: BCM CAPA evidence requirement, ISO 22301/SAMA OPRES compliance assessment, legacy ISO 22301 plan lifecycle) + instrument widening |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · instrument integrity + server-owned state |
| **Modules** | `bcm` (4 services), `security` (two gates) |

### What was measured

Executing F2-233's filed **4 BCM services**. The population was re-derived from the gate's own
printed output first (F2-221), not from the filing's prose: `BcmComplianceMappingService`,
`BcmRemediationService`, `BcmService`, `BcpPlanService` — **7 reported sites**. All four controllers
bind the ENTITY, checked rather than assumed, so all four were genuinely open.

Measured in **both databases, byte-identical**: `bcm.bcm_plans` 10 rows (DRAFT 7 / APPROVED 3,
**zero CHECK constraints** on a NOT NULL `status`), `bcm.bcp_plans` 10, `bcm.bcp_sections` 120
(`last_edited_at` 93), `bcm.corrective_actions` 10 (`closure_date` 0, `evidence_id` 0 — **no CAPA
has ever been closed**), `bcm.compliance_mappings` **412, every one `NOT_ASSESSED`, `assessed_at`
and `assessed_by` null on all 412** — so the assessment route had never once been exercised.

### The live half — eleven defects, probed 11/22 pre-fix and 22/22 post-fix

Probed as **`compliance`** (GRC_ADMINISTRATOR, one of only three principals holding `BCM:WRITE`)
against **planted `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows** (F2-206), pre-fix via a stash of the four main sources so
the "before" claim is measured rather than asserted.

**`BcmRemediationService#createCapa` — the sharpest, because it skipped an EVIDENCE REQUIREMENT.**
`if (status == null) setStatus("OPEN")` followed by a MEMBERSHIP test, so `CLOSED` was accepted:
`POST /api/v1/bcm/capas {"status":"CLOSED"}` answered **200**, while the very next probe leg shows
`POST /capas/{id}/transition {"to":"CLOSED"}` answering **400 — "Cannot CLOSE without evidence,
attach evidence first"** for the identical edge. A caller-chosen `closureDate: 2001-01-01` was
stored on a corrective action that had never been closed. The row was then unmovable: `updateCapa`
refuses to edit a CLOSED CAPA and `transitionCapa` has `case "CLOSED" -> false`, so a `BCM:WRITE`
holder could manufacture a record only a `BCM:APPROVE` holder can touch.

🔑 **F2-220 fixed `createGap` in THIS FILE, with THIS primitive, under a comment naming this exact
defect — and left the identical two lines in `createCapa` eighty lines below.** Not a sibling file
and not a sibling module: the same file. F2-215's headline at its sharpest — fixing the instance you
noticed leaves the remainder looking covered, because the mechanism that covers it is visibly
present.

**`BcmService` — the legacy ISO 22301 plan register**, still routed at `/api/v1/bcm/legacy-plans`
and still rendered by `/bcm/legacy`. `createPlan` was a bare `save(req)` with no state guard and
**no vocabulary test of any kind**: `status=APPROVED` answered **201**, and so did
`status=TOTALLY_MADE_UP` — and because the table has zero CHECKs and every transition guard is an
equality test against a named state, such a row is **permanently untransitionable by every route**
(F2-220's `platform.issues` shape, creatable on demand). `updatePlan` wrote the status
unconditionally, so `PUT` performed DRAFT → APPROVED at **200** — exactly what `approvePlan` guards,
under the same `BCM:WRITE` permission. No escalation: the object-level machine was the only control
and the update sat beside it without one (F2-219's shape). The page already offers all four
lifecycle buttons, row-conditional on state, so the form's status select was a second unguarded way
to do what they do properly.

**`BcmComplianceMappingService#create` — a fabricated ISO 22301 / SAMA OPRES / NCEMA assessment.**
`validate()` tested only MEMBERSHIP, so a mapping could be created **COMPLIANT** (200) carrying
`assessedAt: 2001-01-01` and `assessedBy: "Nobody Who Assessed This"` — a requirement recorded as
met with no assessor, no clock and no "Compliance assessed" audit row.

**`BcpPlanService`.** `create` left `currentVersion` as a DEFAULT one line below the four fields
F2-220 had just closed, so a brand-new continuity plan could claim **v7** with no `BcpVersion` row
behind it — and `snapshot()` derives the next number from the versions table, so the first approval
would silently reduce 7 → 1. `addSection` stored caller-supplied `lastEditedAt`/`lastEditedBy`, an
edit history for a section that had never been edited.

### The instrument half — a second finding, and it is F2-233's shape one slice later

Reading `assessCompliance` found a **split attribution**: the server stamps `assessedAt` from its own
clock and copied `assessedBy` out of the request. That is F2-223's defect on a regulator-facing BCM
register, and the UI's half was `window.prompt('Reviewer name')` with **`?? ''` on Cancel** — so the
recorded assessor could be anybody, or the empty string. F2-223 fixed six such surfaces and nineteen
request fields and **this one survived**.

🔑 **Why it was invisible: the actor half reaches its setter as a BARE SCALAR PARAMETER.**
`SplitAttributionContractTest`'s `REQUEST_VALUE` requires a named receiver (`req.`/`body.`/…), and
`m.setAssessedBy(assessedBy)` names none — the wire-ness lives at the **call site**, where
`BcmComplianceMappingController` passes `body.assessedBy()`. **F2-222 established exactly that rule**
("whether a scalar parameter is caller data is a fact about its call sites") **and taught it to the
STAMPING side of this question only.** One question, asked of a parameter, answered on one side of
the wire — the same structural asymmetry F2-233 found for fallbacks one slice earlier, where the
accepting side had carried the mirror since F2-219 and the stamping side never did. **Assume a third
instance exists.**

**GAP 10** resolves it: parameter-borne actor halves are collected per method, then resolved against
the controllers' call sites. Measured: **92 candidates paired with a server clock, 13 resolve FROM
THE WIRE**; the classifier removes 2 as ASSIGNMENT (`NdiSubmissionPackageService`'s
`preparerName`/`preparerEmail`), `REFERENCE_TAIL` removes 1 as a document reference, and this slice
fixed the BCM one — leaving **9 on a decrease-only work list with NO verdicts** (F2-188). The other
**79 correctly take the actor from `actor(auth)` / `userIdOf(auth)` / `currentPrincipalName()`**,
which is why the gate's green was mostly earned.

⚠ **My own measurement repeated F2-187's recorded mistake and I nearly believed it.** The first
resolver matched `.<method>(` in **any** controller without resolving the receiver's type, so
`approve` picked up every unrelated `approve(` in the tree and reported ~20 sites "from the wire"
that were almost entirely cross-contamination. F2-187's words are *"a method-NAME fallback silently
clears the methods most likely to be duplicated elsewhere — resolve per owner type."* With the
receiver resolved to a field declared of the service's own type, the honest answer is 13 of 92.

⚠ **`appointedByReso` is a demonstrated false positive, and it is the negative control.** The wide
`By[A-Z]\w*` branch exists so `approvedByLegalName` pairs, and it also matches
`CommitteeMemberTerm#appointedByReso`, whose javadoc reads *"Board-resolution code that appointed
this member — links back to the resolution register for traceability."* A board-resolution CODE is
not a person. `REFERENCE_TAIL` narrows it, pinned in **both** directions — six must-pair fields, four
must-not-pair — because a narrowing that is too wide silently SHRINKS the population, which reads
exactly like a clean tree.

### Verdicts

**Fixed (11 live defects):** CAPA `status` + `closureDate`; legacy plan `status` on create and
update; compliance `complianceStatus` + `assessedAt` + `assessedBy` on create; the `assessCompliance`
split; BCP `currentVersion`; section `lastEditedAt` + `lastEditedBy`.

**BY_DESIGN, with the narrowing that keeps the gate off correct code (F2-214):** `progressPercent` on
both CAPA write paths. `transitionCapa` stamps it to 100 on CLOSE, but that is a COMPLETION side
effect, not ownership — the rest of the time it is the action owner's own progress report, validated
0..100 and defaulted to 0. Refusing it would break a working request.

`BASELINE_CONTRADICTED_SERVICES` **4 → 0**, re-derived from the gate's own printed figure (F2-207).
⚠ The work list is now EMPTY, and **an empty work list is exactly what a rotted detector produces**
(F2-219). What carries the weight is not the number but the three reverse legs — every `BY_DESIGN`,
`CLOSED_ELSEWHERE` and `FILED_OWNER_DECISION` entry must still name something the scan finds, so a
detector that stops matching fails 15 assertions rather than reporting success.

`SplitAttributionContractTest`'s `WORK_LIST` moves **0 → 9**, and the direction is deliberate: the
question was right and the ANSWER was under-measured, so the figure moves and says why (F2-205),
rather than the question being re-scoped (F2-204).

### Verification

- Full backend suite **4,073 / 0 / 0** (from 4,058 — 15 new tests across four classes).
- `ServerStampedFieldContractTest` **20/20** at the new hard zero;
  `SplitAttributionContractTest` **18/18** with GAP 10 and its both-directions pin.
- Frontend `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npx vitest run` **771 / 71 files**, all passing.
- Live probe as `compliance`: **11/22 pre-fix, 22/22 post-fix**, against planted rows, cleaned with
  CHARINDEX — 47 rows removed, 0 tagged rows left, all five registers back to their measured sizes
  (10 / 10 / 120 / 10 / 412).
- Mutation harness **18 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss**.

⚠ Two of my own errors, both caught by running things. **(a)** The first harness run reported one
**ANCHOR-MISS**: my M1 anchor spanned two lines with `\n` against a CRLF file, so it could never
match — the CRLF trap for the **fourth** time in this lineage (F2-212, F2-219, F2-229), in a harness
whose own docstring states the rule. Anchor-miss being a distinct non-zero outcome is the only reason
it was visible. **(b)** My new gate leg failed on a correct tree, because the javadoc explaining the
removal of `assessedBy` NAMES the field it removed — so the detector read the epitaph as the corpse
(F2-193). Comments are stripped first now.

⚠ Two probe bugs, both mine: a guessed field name (`planTitleEn`; it is `titleEn`, resolved from the
entity) produced a 400 that reads exactly like the fix having broken, and asserting `200` where the
controller returns `201` made a leg fail on a correct server.

### Filed

- **Nine parameter-borne split-attribution sites**, no verdicts (F2-188), decrease-only. Read
  `SupplierResilienceTestService#approve` first: its controller passes
  `body.getOrDefault("approverName", "admin")`, so an omitted approver is recorded as the literal
  **`admin`**. Two are plausibly BY_DESIGN — a data-sharing agreement's counterparty signer is by

  (canonical, 10 rows), F2-196's disjoint-register shape, carved out at audit T1.1 and still both live.
- **`bcm.bcp_sections.last_edited_by` holds an invented officer name on 72 of 120 rows**
  (`Khalid Al-Mutairi`) plus two provenance markers (`template:…`, `BIA generator`) — F2-207's
  measured cast of 65 invented names, in a *server* register. Owner decision: rewriting live rows.
- The remaining **45** `MassAssignmentRatchetTest` NEEDS-VERDICT rows.

## F2-233 · Roughly a third of what a work list reports is the instrument

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-233 |
| **Title** | Four detector holes inflated the server-stamped-field work list; two creates named a state |
| **Severity** | 🔴 P2 (live: PDPL Article 25 DPIA + SAMA/NCA regulatory-change register) + instrument correction |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-18 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · instrument integrity + server-owned state |
| **Modules** | `privacy` (DPIA), `compliance` (regulatory change), `security` (the gate) |

### What was measured

Executing F2-231's filed **11-service work list**. Every one of the eleven was read. The population
then split almost evenly between *the code was wrong* and *the instrument was wrong*:

| | |
|---|---|
| Narrowed away (detector holes) | `NdiGapService`, `ProcessorAssessmentService`, and 8 fields across 5 others |
| Fixed and probed live | `DpiaService#create`, `RegulatoryChangeService#create` |
| Verdicts in two new buckets | `SustainabilityReportService`, `PolicyService`, `PrivacyService` |
| Still a work list, no verdicts | the 4 BCM services |

`BASELINE_CONTRADICTED_SERVICES` **11 → 4**, re-derived from the gate's own printed figure (F2-207).

🔑 **Roughly a third of what an instrument like this reports is the instrument.** The corrected
headline is *not* "seven services were fixed", and saying so would have been the more flattering and
less true story — F2-228's lesson about two detector errors producing a green neither earned.

### The four detector holes

**(a) A comma in a character class, wrong in BOTH directions at once.**
`readOnlyOnTheWire()` parsed field names out of entity source with
`\b\w[\w<>,.\[\]]*\s+(\w+)\s*[;=]` — "type token, then field name". That class contains a **comma**, so

```java
@JsonProperty(access = JsonProperty.Access.READ_ONLY)
@Column(name = "risk_score", precision = 4, scale = 1) private BigDecimal riskScore;
```

parsed the token `4,` as the type and **`scale` as the field name.** Measured tree-wide: **4 phantom
names** (`scale` ×3, `length` ×1) and **4 genuinely closed fields never subtracted** —
`ProcessorAssessment#riskScore`, `NdiAssessmentCycle#complianceScore`,
`VendorAssessment#workflowStatus`, `VendorAssessment#computedScorePct`.

🔑 **One regex, two opposite errors.** Losing the real field **over**-reports — a field the wire already
refuses is published as an open contradiction. Inventing `scale` **under**-reports — a phantom entry in
the closed set would silently subtract any real field of that name, the quiet direction. The second half
is latent only because none of those three entities declares a field called `scale` or `length`, which
is precisely why it was invisible: **a phantom exclusion that matches nothing scores exactly like a
correct one.**

⚠ **My reading of that regex said `riskScore`, twice.** Only running it against the entity gave `scale`.
The gate now carries the self-check the derivation never had —
`everyDerivedReadOnlyNameIsARealField` — which resolves every captured name against the entity's own
declarations.

**(b) `instanceof` pattern variables, and the house idiom is TWO hops.** Every `/{id}/action` route whose
payload is a `Map<String, Object> body` writes its fields as
`Object lvl = body.get("impactLevel"); if (lvl instanceof String s) e.setImpactLevel(s);` — so the value
at the setter is `s`, bound **by a pattern, not an assignment**, to a local that is itself an alias of the
request. The old resolver looked for `s = …`, found nothing, and read the caller's own value as a server
stamp. **12 setter sites across 6 services**, including `Dpia#conclusion`/`#rejectionReason` (the
substance of an Article 25 assessment) and `RegulatoryChange#impactLevel`/`#impactSummary`.

**(c) Lambda parameters.** `controls.forEach((k, v) -> … a.setC1WrittenInstructions(v))` —
`allParamNames` parses the *method's* parameters and never a lambda's, so all eight PDPL Article 28
control answers read as stamps. **8 sites in exactly 1 service**, which is the argument for fixing the
detector rather than writing eight near-identical `BY_DESIGN` reasons: 🔑 **a verdict says the code is
right; a narrowing says the instrument was wrong, and eight fluent reasons for one detector bug is the
artefact F2-188 measured at five claims, five false.**

**(d) A fallback is not an ownership claim.** `if (p.getEffectiveFrom() == null) p.setEffectiveFrom(now())`
supplies a value only when the caller did not; and a field the same method **also writes from the
caller** at another site is not owned by it however many literals appear elsewhere.
🔑 **F2-218's headline — `if (x == null) x = INITIAL` is a default, not a guard — read on the STAMPING
side.** The accepting side has carried the mirror of this since F2-219
(`settled.removeAll(defaults(...))`); the stamping side never did, and **that asymmetry is the
finding**: one question, asked of the request on one side and of the loaded row on the other, answered on
only one. The fields it hit are exactly the ones a professional is supposed to fill in —
`Dpia#nextReviewDate` (the Article 25 review cadence), `Policy#effectiveFrom`,
`NdiCorrectiveAction#completionDate` — so every one was a gate failing on correct code (F2-214).

⚠⚠ **The narrowing's own limit was found by my own gate's REVERSE leg.** Following every identifier
reached `c` in `SgiCommitment c = get(id);`, and `callerSupplied` answers TRUE for `get(id)` because
`id` is a parameter — so a row **loaded from the database** read as caller data and
`refreshValue`'s `c.setCurrentValue(sv.value())` stopped counting as a stamp.
`everyByDesignEntryStillDescribesSomethingTheScanFinds` failed, naming `SgiCommitment#currentValue`.
🔑 **The id is the caller's; the row it names is the server's** — and the error direction is the
opposite of the bug the widening fixes (a real stamp read as caller data HIDES a contradiction), which
is why the leg that caught it is the one nobody writes first (F2-199).

### The live half

**`DpiaService#create` — PDPL Article 25.** `DpiaController` binds the `Dpia` ENTITY and the create did
nothing but `setId(null)`, `setOrganisationId(…)`, `save(req)`. Probed live as `compliance`, **19/19
pre-fix**: `POST /api/v1/privacy/dpias` with `status=APPROVED` answered **201** storing APPROVED,
skipping DRAFT → IN_REVIEW → APPROVED entirely, plus a caller-chosen `rejectedAt` of 2001 and an
invented rejection reason. `PRIVACY:WRITE` guards the create **and** `/approve`, so there is no
escalation to find: the state machine was the only control and the create sat beside it without one.
The audit row said `DPIA_DRAFTED` whatever status was stored.

🔑 **`approvedAt` was already refused, because `Dpia` annotates that ONE field
`@JsonProperty(READ_ONLY)` and not `status`, `rejectedAt`, `rejectionReason` or `conclusion`** —
F2-215's two-of-N shape at one of five. Its side effect is the interesting part: the probe confirmed
`approved_at = NULL` on the forged APPROVED row, so **the single annotation left the dangerous forgery
internally detectable and the REJECTED one seamless** (both of those columns are writable) — and
nothing reads either.

**`RegulatoryChangeService#create`.** Same shape on the register that records how a SAMA/NCA/SDAIA
change was assessed: filed **CLOSED** with a caller-chosen `closedAt`, having passed through none of
NEW → APPLICABILITY_ASSESSED → IMPACT_ASSESSED → CONTROLS_UPDATED → CLOSED, each of which demands
something on the way through (F2-220). 🔑 **F2-213 fixed the UPDATE and wrote the reasoning onto it;
the create two methods above was not touched** — F2-215's headline for the fourth time in this lineage.

Both refusals are `require`, not `coerce`, and neither can break a working request (F2-182):
`dpiaApi.create` is dark (`apiClientMethodReachability` records it as a HOLE — *"a DPIA can be approved,
rejected and expired but never created"*, which reads as an invitation to build the screen that would
have fired this), and `RegulatoryChangeRequest` declares neither `status` nor `closedAt`.

### Two new verdict buckets

**`CLOSED_ELSEWHERE`** — a **fourth wire-closing mechanism, and the strongest of the four.** The gate
subtracts `BaseEntity`'s nine (F2-218) and per-field `READ_ONLY` (F2-219); neither knows about a create
whose ENDPOINT binds a purpose-built record and hands the service an entity it built itself.
`SustainabilityAnnexController` binds `ReportingYearCreateRequest` and calls
`service.createYear(req.toEntity())`, and that record's own javadoc states the rule: *"a year can never
be born APPROVED/PUBLISHED"*. A field the bound type does not declare can never arrive. Also holds
`PolicyService`'s four stamps, closed by a **retired route** (CH-6 / PM-C1 removed the `/policies`
write mappings; `DarkServiceMethodTest` holds all nine legacy methods; the service exits at CH-9) —
recorded as a verdict rather than "fixed", because adding a guard to a class scheduled for deletion is
code on a corpse. Every entry is resolved **mechanically** — reflection over the record's components,
absence of a write mapping — because an exclusion nobody can audit is an assumption wearing a citation.

**`FILED_OWNER_DECISION`** — because filing these under `BY_DESIGN` would **assert they are correct.**
`PrivacyService`'s `DataBreach#status` and `DataSubjectRequest#status` are live holes deliberately left
open: no CHECK, no declared machine, and `DsrRequestLifecycle` declares only a TERMINAL set, so
`requireInitial` has no initial state and would refuse the NEW/OPEN/PENDING creates the register already
holds. 🔑 **F2-197's rule one level up: an invented figure invites a question, an invented all-clear
closes one.** A verdict vocabulary limited to *"the caller legitimately owns this"* cannot express
*"the caller must not own this and closing it rewrites live rows"*, so the defect would have been
recorded as a design — F2-224's lesson, which landed on this gate's verdict vocabulary once already.

⚠ Note what left the gate's output silently: `DataSubjectRequest#dueDate`, the **PDPL Article 4
statutory deadline** and the sharper half of F2-231's filing. `startDsr()` only supplies it as a
FALLBACK, so under (d) it is correctly not a stamp. **The filing stands on F2-202's rule — only the
server may issue a statutory deadline — and does not depend on this instrument.** Recorded in the
verdict so it cannot vanish with the detector change.

### Verification

- Backend suite **4,058 / 0 / 0** (was 4,047; 11 new tests).
- Gate **20/20**, including 5 new legs: the derivation self-check, the three binding forms + the
  fallback rule pinned in both directions over literal source, the reverse leg for both new buckets,
  and mechanical resolution of every `CLOSED_ELSEWHERE` claim.
- Live probe **19/19 pre-fix** and **16/16 post-fix** as `compliance`, against rows the probe plants
  itself and removes with `CHARINDEX` (house rule 5 / F2-206). Post-fix asserts **both** directions:
  the forgeries are refused with a message naming the owning route, the honest payloads still return
  201 at the machine's root, the assessor's own fields survive, and the guarded routes still reach
  APPROVED / APPLICABILITY_ASSESSED and still stamp `approved_at`.
- Mutation **9 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss** — one per narrowing and one per fix, each naming
  the test that must die. Every narrowing is load-bearing rather than decorative, and the two create
  guards are each asserted by a behaviour test rather than only by the gate.
- Two in-flight catches by the gate's own legs, both recorded above: the `SgiCommitment` over-widening,
  and `VendorAssessment` being declared in **two** packages (F2-222's filed hazard) so a merged derived
  set was compared against one file's fields — 🔑 **a keying ambiguity is harmless until two things key
  on it differently.**

### Filed

- The **4 BCM services** (`BcmService`, `BcmRemediationService`, `BcmComplianceMappingService`,
  `BcpPlanService`) with per-site evidence in `target/server-stamped-fields.txt` and deliberately **no
  verdicts** (F2-188). All four controllers bind the **entity** — checked, not assumed — so they are
  genuinely open. `BcmService#createPlan` has two internal callers (`BcmBiaAssessmentController`'s
  BCP/DRP generation), both of which explicitly pass `DRAFT`, so the fix is safe but needs its own probe.
- `BcmRemediationService#createCapa` is the sharpest: `if (status == null) "OPEN"` followed by a
  **membership** check, so a BCM CAPA can be created `CLOSED` — and `transitionCapa` refuses CLOSE
  without evidence, so the create skips an evidence requirement (F2-217's `audit_lc` shape).
- `SustainabilityReportService`'s `ReportingYear#status` is stamped through a **scalar parameter**, so
  it is invisible to this gate either way — F2-220's filed transition-by-parameter blind spot, still
  unmeasured as a population.
- `PrivacyService`'s two `status` columns and `data_subject_requests.due_date` (carried from F2-231).
- The remaining **45** `MassAssignmentRatchetTest` NEEDS-VERDICT rows.

## F2-232 · Reading the one unread lead refuted it, and that is the argument for the rejection

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-232 |
| **Title** | Both net-new findings from F2-231's rejected stamp-half widening are false positives — 2 of 2 |
| **Severity** | Instrument correction (no defect; no code change) |
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-17 |
| **Programme** | Platform Bible F2 · instrument integrity |
| **Modules** | `admin/committee` (read), `security` (the gate's own record) |

### What was measured

F2-231 built the mirror of its own write-half widening — following private helpers on the **stamp**
half — measured it at **11 → 15 services**, narrowed it twice back to 13, and rejected it because one
of the two net-new findings was a demonstrated false positive (`ChangeManagementService#addLink`
reported as accepting a `ChangeLink`'s own data fields *"stamped by transition"*). It named the other
as the one lead worth reading, **with no verdict** (F2-188).

Read, it is **BY DESIGN with provenance, and F2-40 built the mechanism.**
`CommitteeResolutionService#create` accepts `voteFor`/`voteAgainst`/`voteAbstain` because the
secretariat form posts the tally straight from the minutes for a committee that votes in the room —
the normal path — and the row records *which kind of tally it is*:

- `ASSERTED`, with the recorder taken from `Authentication` and **never** from the body (the DF-3 rule;
  `tallyRecordedByUserId`/`Name` are explicitly nulled before being set), versus
- `COMPUTED` for a resolution created empty and decided through `recordVote`.

Measured 2026-08-17: **22 live rows in dev, 20 in prod.** `ASSERTED_LEGACY` **20 / 20** — F2-40's
honest label for rows that predate the mechanism, carrying no recorder because none was ever recorded
through the API — and **0** rows carrying `ASSERTED` with a recorder, so the provenance path is
**latent and correct** rather than bypassed.

### Why this is worth its own entry

🔑 **A population produced by a detector already judged unsafe refuted at 2 of 2**, where this
programme's usual rate against a predecessor's claims is about 2 in 10 (F2-188, F2-192, F2-204,
F2-211, F2-228). That takes the stamp-half widening from *"needs care"* to *measurably wrong as
formulated*, and it is the argument for the rejection rather than a footnote to it.

**Do not re-enable the stamp half expecting a defect behind either name.** If it is ever revisited,
the missing distinction is between a helper implementing a **guarded route's** stamp and one
implementing an **invariant every path shares** — and neither refuted site turned on that distinction,
which is exactly why two narrowings did not rescue it.

### What shipped

No code change. The correction lands in three places so it cannot be read past: the gate's own
blind-spot javadoc (which quotes the sentence it replaces), F2-231's register spec, and CLAUDE.md.
Gate 16/16 after the correction.

### The instrument findings

⚠ **Two probe errors of mine, both loud, and both the recurring guessed-name error.**
`admin.committee_resolutions` has **no `is_deleted` column**, so a `WHERE is_deleted = 0` scoped query
answered *"Invalid column name"* — which F2-199 records as reading exactly like *"the data isn't
there"* — and the tally columns had to be resolved from `sys.columns` rather than assumed. **Resolve
from `sys.columns`; never guess.** Recurring since F2-198.

⚠⚠ **The docs gate caught this entry's own absence, which is the third instance of F2-219's lesson in
this lineage.** Referencing `F2-232` in the plan pushed `specsOwedOnlyEverDecreases` from 29 to 30
before this spec existed. 🔑 **A docs commit is precisely what a docs gate breaks, and a correction
recorded only inside the finding it corrects is a correction an auditor reading the register's index
will not find.**
