## F2-223 · The server stamps WHEN, the caller says WHO — one attribution split across two owners

**Found** 2026-08-16, re-deriving F2-222's filed denominator. **P2** — eleven governance and
regulatory registers recorded a person who did not perform the act. **Closed** the same day. No
migration; 11 backend services, 6 frontend surfaces, 19 request-DTO fields deleted.

### Re-deriving the filing, and why the number was the wrong question

F2-222 filed *"the remaining 31 authority fields written from the request with no guarded route
stamping them anywhere"*. That 31 came from a **name-shape** test — the same instrument class
F2-217 had just proved measures its own vocabulary rather than the codebase. Per F2-221, the
denominator was re-derived, and the better question turned out to be structural:

🔑 **When one method writes `set<verb>At(<the server's own clock>)` and, for the SAME verb, writes
`set<verb>By…` / `set<verb>erUserId(…)` FROM THE REQUEST, it has split one attribution across two
owners. The clock half is the proof: by stamping the time itself the server has already declared
that it — not the caller — is the recorder of this act.**

Nothing in that pairing depends on which spellings anyone thought of; the verb root comes from the
code. Population, **after the pre-fix control forced a seventh detector correction**: **23 split
sites**, plus **2** the split detector is structurally blind to = **25**. Of those, **11 CONFIRMED
and fixed · 2 FILED · 1 REFUTED · 10 UNADJUDICATED** on a decrease-only work list.

🔑 **The 10 are the argument for running the control at all.** The shipped detector was run over
`git show master:` and reported `CrisisCommsTemplateService` SILENT — a file this slice had already
fixed by hand. There the clock reaches the setter through a **local variable**
(`LocalDateTime now = LocalDateTime.now(); … setApprovedByLegalAt(now)`), which an argument-only
test for `now(` cannot see. Teaching the detector that shape immediately surfaced ten more sites
across ERM, BCM invocation, MTPD inheritance, obligation attestation, regulatory change and vendor
BCP attestation. **A green scan on the fixed tree cannot tell you the detector works; only running
it against the defect can.**

⚠ They ship **unadjudicated, as a work list and NOT as reasons**. F2-188 measured what happens when
a slice writes a reason for something it has not read: five claims, five false, and the fluency of
the prose is what made them look verified. At least one is probably BY DESIGN —
`VendorBcpAttestationService#doSubmit` takes `submittedByContactName/Email` on a **vendor portal**
submission, where the submitter is an external contact and may not be an authenticated principal at
all — and that is a guess, which is exactly why it is on the list rather than in `BY_DESIGN`.

### The complementary question, and why both are needed

A second, independent scan asked: *which routes are guarded by a permission whose ACTION NAMES AN
ACT (`MODULE:APPROVE` — 17 catalogued permissions in dev, 11 in prod) and let the body say who
performed it?* That found `CptyService#assignRating` and `#upsertLimit`, which the split detector
**cannot see** — because there the client supplied `approvedAt` too, minting a SAMA large-exposure
approval date in the browser. 🔑 **A detector keyed on an asymmetry cannot see the case where both
halves fell the same way.**

### The live defect, probed 14/14 pre-fix and 18/18 post-fix against PLANTED rows (F2-206)

As `compliance` (user id 3), which holds `AML:APPROVE`, `AUDIT:WRITE`, `ETHICS:APPROVE`,
`BCM:APPROVE` and `PRIVACY:WRITE`:

| leg | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| IIA Std 2010 annual audit plan → APPROVED with `approverUserId: 4` | **stored 4** (actor is 3) | stored 3, forgery ignored |
| the same, **omitting** the approver | **400 — required** | 200, records the principal |
| PDPL Art.18 disposal certificate `verify` + `complete` | **`verifierName` = `executorName` = `"Nobody Who Approved This"`** | both `"compliance"`, `verifiedBy` id agrees |
| AML sanctions hit review with `reviewerUserId: 4` | **stored 4** | stored 3, and the audit row reads `by user=3` |

🔑 **The sharpest is the annual plan: the server did not merely ACCEPT an approver, it REQUIRED
one and threw if absent** — insisting on an attribution it never verified while stamping the time
itself on the next line. And **F2-217 closed the CREATE path on that same register**, which
funnelled every approval through this method.

🔑 **The audit row quoted the caller's claim.** `SanctionsHitService` logged
`" by user=" + req.reviewerUserId()`, so a forged attribution was invisible to the trail an
auditor reads. Every audit line in the population now reads off the SAVED ROW.

### The fix already existed in the tree, one file away

`KycService#disposition` resolves the decider from `CurrentActor` and refuses to proceed without
one — *"An AML disposition with no decider is not a disposition."* It is in the **same package** as
`AmlAlertService`, over the **same concept** (`decidedByName` on a screening hit), and was never
copied. Seventh instance in this lineage of the correct artefact sitting beside the wrong one.
F2-222's filing said the CPTY fix was blocked on *"a principal→user-id resolution this slice did
not build"* — the resolution is `currentUserId()`, **one line above the defect**.

### The visible half: the UI asked the operator to type it

`EthicsPage` opened `window.prompt(t('amlDecidedByPrompt'))` and sent the answer as the decider of
an AML alert — including `STR_FILED`, a Suspicious Transaction Report to the Saudi FIU — with
`?? ''` on Cancel, so the attribution could be the empty string. `StrategyRoiPage` and
`QuantitativeBiaPage` used `dialog.prompt` with the placeholder *"e.g. Faisal Al-Subaie — Group
CFO"*, and `CrisisCommsDispatchWizard` had a free-text *"Dispatched by (name)"* input. 🔑 **An
invented officer in a placeholder is how a free-text attribution field teaches an operator to type
somebody else's name.** All six removed; 19 request-DTO fields deleted on both sides of the wire
so no client can offer them again (F2-184).

### Six detector corrections, five of them shrinking the population

| # | bug | direction |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `@PreAuthorize(CONSTANT)` invisible — the house idiom in `CptyController` | under |
| 2 | nested DTO types (`CptyDtos.UpsertLimitRequest`) unresolvable by `<Name>.java` lookup | under |
| 3 | fields declared `@NotBlank @Size(…) private String x;` — the regex anchored on the modifier | under |
| 4 | the `-or` agent noun: `executorName` reduced to root `name` | under |
| 5 | a qualifier BETWEEN verb and tail: `approvedByLegalName` matched no tail | under |
| 6 | *(the same, in `ACTOR_TAIL`)* — found only when the gate's own vacuity fixture failed | under |

🔑 **Every one shrank the population, which reads exactly like a clean tree.** Bug 4 was found only
because the fix for `DisposalCertificateService#verify` sat one method below `#complete`, an
identical site the scan had never reported — **the class looked measured**. Bug 5/6 cost a real
site: `CrisisCommsTemplateService#transition`, found by a residual grep rather than by the
instrument, and it is the CISO sign-off `CrisisCommsDispatchService` refuses to send a crisis
cascade without (*"only APPROVED_BY_CISO templates may be dispatched"*). Its own comment called the
result *"an honest governance trail"*.

### Refuted and filed

- **REFUTED** — `ObService#revokeConsent::revokedBy` is a **party** (`CUSTOMER`/`BANK`/`TPP`), not a
  person; `ObConsentsPage` declares `useState<RevokedBy>('BANK')`.
- **FILED** — `CrossBorderTransferService#assess::residencyCheckBy`. 🔑 **Where a method lets the
  caller supply the clock TOO, the act may not be this call, so its performer need not be the
  caller.** Whether the PDPL Art.29 register wants an external assessor's name is an owner call.
- **FILED** — `ControlLibraryService#updateMapping::reviewerUserId`, ambiguous between attribution
  and assignment, and blocked on a second defect: `setLastReviewedAt(now())` fires on **every**
  update, so editing a rationale already records the mapping as reviewed.

### The gate

`SplitAttributionContractTest` (hermetic, source-only) derives the population and holds it at a
**hard zero** outside a 3-entry `BY_DESIGN` map enforced in both directions, plus:
a **vacuity fixture** replaying all five shapes this slice fixed (at zero, a rotted detector and a
finished sweep look identical — F2-219); a **negative fixture** proving it does not fire on a
server-stamped actor, on an unpaired actor, or on two different verbs in one method (a gate that
fails on correct code is the one failure a gate must never have — F2-214); and the ACT-guarded half
asserted against `CptyService` and `SanctionsHitService` by call shape.

**Verification** — backend suite, FE `tsc --noEmit` clean, FE **756/756**, gate **7/7**, live probe
**14/14 pre-fix · 18/18 post-fix**, 17 planted rows deleted with CHARINDEX (0 remaining; registers
back to `screening_hit` 3, `credit_rating` 108, `large_exposure_limit` 74).

| Field | Value |

No migration. |

## F2-222 · A scalar parameter is caller data at the declaration and the principal at the call site — the C-6 approval control, its input and its attribution

**Found** 2026-08-16, asking what F2-218's derived gate cannot see. **P2** — a segregation-of-duty
control defeated in three calls with one permission. **Closed** the same day. No migration, no
endpoint change, no frontend change.

### The blind spot

`ServerStampedFieldContractTest` asks: *does a create ACCEPT a field that a guarded route on the
same service STAMPS?* That question needs a control to exist and needs the gate to recognise the
stamp. Its **fourth detector correction** — *"a scalar method parameter is still caller data"* — was
added in F2-218 because `markUnderReview(Long id, String reviewerName)` is filled from a body field
and was reading as a server stamp.

🔑 **That correction is right at the DECLARATION and wrong at the CALL SITE.**
`PolicyManagementService#transition(Long id, String to, String actor)` is called exactly once, as
`service.transition(id, body.get("to"), actor(auth), isComplianceAdmin(auth))`. `actor` is the
authenticated principal, so `p.setApproverName(actor)` **is** a server stamp — and because the gate
decided otherwise, `PolicyDocument#approverName` never entered the stamped set and `update()`
writing it from the request was not a contradiction by that gate's stated question.

### What it hid: leg 1, the attribution

`transition()` enforces C-6 segregation of duty — *"the policy author/owner cannot approve their own
policy"* — the S5 committee-referral resolution check, and CH-10 document control, then stamps
`approverName` from the acting principal. `update()` is guarded by the **same** permission
(`COMPLIANCE:WRITE`, **13 roles, 5 of them with an active holder**, identical in dev and prod) and
copied `approverName`/`approverEmail` straight out of the body.

Probed live as `auditor` and `compliance` against policies the probe **planted** (F2-206):

```
POST /documents/{id}/transition {to: APPROVED}   as the author  -> 403  C-6 fires
POST /documents/{id}/transition {to: APPROVED}   as another     -> 200  approverName="auditor"
PUT  /documents/{id} {approverName:"Nobody Who Approved This"}  -> 200  STORED, still APPROVED
PUT  /documents/{id} {approverName:"compliance"}  as the author -> 200  the act C-6 refused
```

🔑 **The freeze was already there and was written for the wrong state.** The top of `update()` says
*"Once PUBLISHED, only metadata fields are editable"* and excludes the approver — but the stamp
happens at **APPROVED**, so the attribution was frozen **one state too late**.

### Leg 2, sharper: the control's own input

C-6 compares the actor against `createdBy`, `ownerName` and `ownerEmail`. `createdBy` is immutable
(`READ_ONLY` at the wire, F2-215). `ownerName` was editable through `update()` in REVIEW:

```
POST /documents/{id}/transition {to: APPROVED}  as the owner   -> 403
PUT  /documents/{id} {ownerName: "somebody else"} as the owner -> 200
POST /documents/{id}/transition {to: APPROVED}  as the owner   -> 200
```

🔑 **The party a control constrains could edit the control's own input through an adjacent route
with the same permission.** Leg 1 defeats the *record* of the control; leg 2 defeats the *control*.
Note the detail: in leg 2 `approverName` is stamped correctly, so the audit trail tells the truth
about who acted while the control that should have stopped them did not run.

### The fix, and what it deliberately does not break

- `approverName`/`approverEmail` stay editable in **DRAFT/REVIEW**: of the **24 of 41** live dev
  rows (**23 of 37** in prod) that name an approver, most name an **office** — `'رئيس الهيئة'` ×12,
  `'Board Risk Committee'`, `'Audit Committee Chair'`. Refusing those is breaking a working request,
  the one thing a fix must not do (F2-182). ⚠ So the column carries **two meanings** — a principal
  from the stamp, an office from the form — which is F2-196's shape inside one column. **Filed**, not
  collapsed: separating them is a column and a product decision.
- `ownerName`/`ownerEmail` freeze at **REVIEW**. Reassignment is not removed: the machine's
  `REVIEW → DRAFT` edge is the route, so the window narrows rather than the capability disappearing.
- `BEFORE_APPROVAL` is **derived**, not typed: the test drives the real machine for every value of
  `ck_policy_status` and asserts membership is exactly *"APPROVED is still reachable from here"*
  (F2-196). An **inclusion** list is the safe direction — an unrecognised status protects the
  attribution rather than exposing it.

### The gate

`PrincipalStampedFieldContractTest` resolves the parameter where the answer lives: a field written
from a scalar that **every** controller call site fills from the principal is an attribution, and no
write path on that service may then write it from the request. Hard zero. Its narrowings are
self-tested in both directions — *any* call site filled from the body makes the field caller data
(F2-218's correction, kept), and **unresolved is never an attribution**, because *"no call site"* and
*"a principal at every call site"* are the two answers this programme keeps confusing.

⚠ An anti-vacuity leg asserts the gate still **resolves** `PolicyDocument#approverName`: at zero, a
rotted detector and a finished sweep are indistinguishable (F2-219).

### What was refuted on the way

The scan that found this raised 32 candidates; reading them killed most.

- **`DpiaService#addMitigation`** — the value is
  `"VERIFIED".equals(req.getStatus()) ? LocalDateTime.now() : null`. 🔑 **A ternary whose CONDITION
  reads the request but whose BRANCHES are both server values is a server stamp**, not a caller
  write — a sixth shape after F2-219's five detector corrections.
- **`RegReportFiling#preparerUserId/reviewerUserId/approverUserId`** — set as a trio: that is stage
  **assignment**, not attribution.
- **`next*ReviewDate` across seven services** — a plan, not a record of an act.
- **19 "cross-class" candidates, all spurious.** A first scan keyed `Type#field` on the **simple**
  type name and reported creates in one class contradicting stamps in another. All four pairs are
  **duplicate simple names in different packages** (`Vulnerability`, `CapaTask`, `ScreeningHit`,
  `RegulatoryChange`). 🔑 **A type name in scope is not the type that governs** — F2-221's constant
  lesson, one level out.

⚙ **Filed, and latent rather than live: 15 of 433 entity simple names are declared in two packages**
(30 classes, 30 distinct tables), and three shipped gates key on `Type#field` by simple name.
Measured: **no key collapses two registers today**, because only one twin of each pair has a machine
or a guarded route. Nobody is maintaining that — F2-177's *"close a harmless drift anyway"*.

### My own errors

- ⚠ **The first `authorityish` shape matched a stem anywhere in the name, so `clos` matched inside
  `linkedCmaDisclosureId`** — a link, not an authority act. Scoped to camelCase word starts.
- ⚠⚠ **The population measurement ran AFTER the first probe and counted its own row.** It reported
  *"42 live, 25 with an approver, **1 whose approver equals its own createdBy**"* — and that 1 was
  the probe's own forgery. 🔑 **A measurement taken after the probe counts the probe's rows, and the
  artefact it invents looks exactly like a finding about the platform.** Real: 41 / 24 / 21 / **0**.
- ⚠ A guard-resolution scan keyed on the method name `update` matched every controller in the tree
  — the unscoped-scan mistake this register keeps recording.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-16.** Backend **3,960/0/0** · mutation **12 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss** · live probe **13/13 pre-fix, 13/13 post-fix** · pre-fix control fires 5 of 10 behaviour legs and the gate's hard zero. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **Whether a scalar parameter is caller data or a server value is a fact about its CALL SITES, and the gate that had to decide it only had the declaration.** A narrowing added to stop a gate firing on correct code is itself a claim about the codebase, and it inherits a population — here, every attribution that reaches its service as a parameter. 🔑 And: **a control's INPUT deserves the same protection as its VERDICT.** Freezing the attribution alone would have left the owner editing themselves out of the check. |

## F2-221 · A state machine and its column are two artefacts, and nothing compared them — 28 machines, not the nine the previous slice happened to visit

**Found** 2026-08-16, taking F2-220's filed item (`platform.issues` and `bcm.crisis_events` have no
CHECK on `status`). **P3** for the two constraints; **P2** for what measuring the population found.
**Closed** the same day. V376; no Java main-source change, no endpoint change, no frontend change.

### The population was a previous slice's itinerary

F2-220 filed those two because they were among *the nine registers it happened to visit*. Run the
same structural discriminator over the whole tree —
`ServerStampedFieldContractTest#machineOwned`, which F2-220 already ships — and there are **28**
declared machines. The nine were the subset whose create *also* accepted the field.

🔑 **The invariant was real; the population it was drawn from was an itinerary.** Ninth appearance of
F2-198's shape in this lineage, after a filename, a three-entry allow-list, a module name, a
controller-bearing table, an `extends` clause, a field-name list inside a fix, a name list in a
census, and a claim shape in a gate.

Measured across all 28, joining each machine to its entity's `@Table`/`@Column` and then to the
column's CHECK:

| verdict | n | |
|---|---|---|
| **AGREE** | 12 | the constant and the CHECK name the same tokens |
| **NO CHECK** | 7 → **5** | the vocabulary lives only in the heads of its readers (F2-196) |
| **no named constant** | 6 | the column is constrained; the machine is a switch with nothing to mirror |
| **not a vocabulary** | 5 | the transition writes a person, an id or a location |
| **DISAGREE** | **0** | — |

The whole-database denominator, for the next slice: **324** state-ish text columns in dev, **201**
with no CHECK, **177** of those populated.

### The live finding: 11 of 30 ethics cases cannot be advanced by any route

`EthicsCaseService.transition` opens `TRANSITIONS.getOrDefault(c.getStatus(), Set.of())`. The map's
keys are INTAKE, TRIAGE, INVESTIGATION, SUBSTANTIATED, UNSUBSTANTIATED, NO_VIOLATION, REMEDIATION,
ESCALATED, DISMISSED, CLOSED. `ethics.cases` stores **INVESTIGATING (8)** and **TRIAGED (3)** —
identical in dev and prod — and neither is a key, so `allowed` is empty and every target throws.

🔑 **Both are near-synonyms of real keys**, which is exactly why nobody noticed: a reader skimming the
register sees "INVESTIGATING" and reads it as the investigation state. F2-203's `audit_lc` shape
(19 of 46 rows) in a module nobody had checked, and the consequence is a whistleblowing or
misconduct case that cannot be substantiated, dismissed, escalated to a regulator, or closed.

Proved live 2026-08-16 against a **planted** case (F2-206), not a seeded governance record: all five
declared targets refused; the same case moved to `INVESTIGATION` then advanced to `SUBSTANTIATED`
with a 200. **It is the token, not the route.**

⚠ **Not fixed here, and that is the F2-183/F2-196/F2-203 rule, not reticence.** The writers are
already closed — F2-22b(v) made `create` and `update` refuse a body-set status, thoroughly — so
these 11 rows came from `seed_gov_ethics.py`. Adding a CHECK would fail Flyway on them; collapsing
the synonyms rewrites live rows in two real databases. **Owner decision, filed, with the
measurement done so the next slice does not repeat it.**

### V376: the two F2-220 filed, and only those two

F2-183 ties a constraint's scope to the writers you close, so the precondition was measured rather
than assumed: `IssueRepository` has exactly **one** user; each service holds exactly **two**
`setStatus` sites (a `ServerOwnedState.requireInitial` create and the machine); both `update()`
paths refuse a status change; seven other classes hold `CrisisEventRepository` and none writes
status; no native `@Modifying` touches either table. Both databases: 13 issues / 7 crisis events,
**0 violations**, so no `WITH NOCHECK`.

⚠ **No casing normalisation, unlike V375 — and that was checked, not assumed.** The collation is
case-insensitive, so a CHECK alone would accept `'open'`; here both writers compare case-*exactly*,
so a variant is refused at the boundary rather than stored, and the migration's pre-flight THROWs if
a historical row ever proves otherwise.

### Three refuted, and the refutations are the instrument lessons

- **`ChangeRequest#status` DISAGREE — refuted.** The scan matched `OUTCOMES.contains(...)`, the
  vocabulary of a *different field* in the same method. 🔑 **A constant that is in scope is not the
  constant that governs.** Same for `NdiAssessmentCycle`, where `JUMP_STATUSES = Set.of("ARCHIVED")`
  is one jump target, not a vocabulary. The shipped gate resolves the constant by **reflection**, which
  cannot make that mistake.
- **`ControlAssessment#workflowStatus` "17 rows untransitionable" — refuted.** It is
  `switch (from) { … default -> false }` and `APPROVED` simply has no case. 🔑 **For a switch machine an
  omitted case IS the terminal declaration, so "the row is stuck" and "the row is finished" are the
  same observation.** Only a machine with explicit terminal keys (`"CLOSED", Set.of()`) can tell them
  apart — which is why ethics stands and this does not.
- **`ApprovalRequest#decidedBy` "9 of 9 untransitionable" — refuted.** It was comparing four analysts'
  names against a status vocabulary.

### My own errors, all caught by running things

- ⚠⚠ **House rule 5 landed in my own detector.** The first CHECK lookup was
  `cc.definition LIKE '%[status]%'` — and in T-SQL `[status]` is a **character class**, so it matched
  any definition containing s/t/a/u, i.e. every CHECK on the table. Five registers that AGREE were
  reported DISAGREE. The rule is written down for test data; it applies to any `LIKE`. **CHARINDEX.**
- ⚠⚠ **And the gate's own claim-verifier had the same shape.** `migrationDeclaresCheckOn` was
  `CONSTRAINT \w+ CHECK\([^;]{0,4000}?\bcolumn\b` over any file mentioning the table, and it
  reported CHECKs on three columns that have none. 🔑 **Scope a scan to the shape of its claim** —
  third instance in one slice. Both over-reported, which is the direction that fails loudly.
- **Two guessed packages of eleven** (`sust.climate.service`, `sust.annex.service`) and **three guessed
  columns/tables** (`control_assessments.status` is `workflow_status`; `ethics.cases` has no
  `case_number` or `reported_at`). Recurring since F2-198 — resolve from `sys.columns`, never guess.
- **A control fixture that failed on correct code**: I wrote the two set-difference directions the
  wrong way round in the gate's own positive control.

### Mutation: 11 killed, 1 equivalent, 0 anchor-miss

Two survivors on the first run, and **neither was a hole in the gate**:

- **The un-scoping mutation survived because `ethics.cases` has zero CHECK constraints**, so an
  un-scoped detector had nothing to falsely match and answered correctly by accident. 🔑 **A negative
  control has to reach the code it controls** — F2-220's headline, one slice later, in my own harness.
  Re-fixtured on `bcm.gaps`, which carries three vocabulary CHECKs and is not a table V376 touches.
- **The unresolvable-constraint branch survived because on a green tree every constraint resolves.**
  Only the pre-fix control reached it. Extracted as `mirrorDrift` and asserted directly.

Recorded rather than patched: **first-vs-last declaration is an equivalent mutant**, because every
mirrored constraint is declared exactly once — now enforced by its own leg rather than assumed. And
raising the decrease-only ceiling was dropped as an **invalid** mutation: you can always weaken an
assertion (F2-206), and a decrease-only ceiling cannot be mutation-tested by editing the ceiling.

⚠ One anchor miss on the first run: **V376 is LF and the services are CRLF**, so a `\r\n` anchor
could never match. F2-218's lesson, third slice running.

|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-16.** V376 adds `CK_issues_status` and `CK_crisis_events_status`, applied twice to dev, both enabled and **trusted**. `StateMachineColumnMirrorTest` (6) classifies all 28 machines from the derived population and mirrors 12 of them by reflection against the migration SQL. Backend **3,945/0/0** · mutation 11 killed / 1 equivalent / 0 anchor-miss · live probe **13/13** · pre-fix control fires on both constraints. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A filed item inherits the population of the slice that filed it.** F2-220's two unconstrained columns were true and were two of *seven*, out of *twenty-eight* machines, in a database with *201* unconstrained state columns. Before executing a filing, re-derive its denominator. 🔑 And **"the row is stuck" and "the row is finished" are the same observation unless the machine declares its terminal states explicitly** — which is the difference between the finding this slice keeps and the two it threw away. |

## F2-220 · A create that names the state skips the machine's EVIDENCE requirements — nine registers, and the gate could not see any of them by construction

**Found** 2026-08-16, taking F2-219's filed item (the transition-by-parameter blind spot, population
unmeasured). **P2.** **Closed** the same day. No migration, no endpoint change, no frontend change.

### The shape, and why no instrument could see it

`ServerStampedFieldContractTest` asks: *does a create accept a field a guarded route **stamps** with
a server-derived value?* A transition written as `transition(Long id, String to)` writes
`cur.setStatus(to)` — and **a scalar method parameter is caller data** (F2-218's fourth detector bug,
the only one that pushed its population onto correct code). So `status` never enters the STAMPED set,
and a create accepting `status` is not a contradiction by that question.

F2-219 met this as a **surviving mutant** and recorded the right verdict — *a surviving mutant the
gate legitimately cannot see is an unasserted behaviour, not a loose instrument* — answered it with
one test, and filed the population as unmeasured. This slice measured it.

The discriminator carries **no list of field names** (F2-217: a census keyed on a list of names
measures the list). A method is a transition route for field F when it **(1)** loads a row,
**(2)** READS F on that row, **(3)** throws conditionally, and **(4)** writes F on that row from a
scalar parameter. (2) and (4) together are what make it a machine rather than a setter with a longer
name: *the value it will accept depends on the value already there.*

**Nine registers. Every field a `status`. 0 of 9 refuted by reading** — unusual for this programme,
and attributable to the structural discriminator being tight rather than to luck.

### 🔑 The headline: the create did not merely bypass the machine, it bypassed the machine's evidence requirements

Each transition demands something *on the way through*, and a create landing straight in the end
state supplies none of it. All nine probed live 2026-08-16 (**36/36 pre-fix legs**), each as a
persona that holds the module's WRITE:

| register | create reached | what the transition demands that the create skipped |
|---|---|---|
| `platform.authority_documents` | `SUPERSEDED` | a successor document, resolved and verified not to be itself |
| `bcm.gaps` | `CLOSED` on a **CRITICAL** gap | at least one linked corrective action |
| `bcm.bcm_risks` | `CLOSED` | the TRANSITION audit row; the AR-T1 ERM fan-out |
| `bcm.bcp_plans` | `PUBLISHED` | review, approval, and the `BcpVersion` **snapshot of what was approved** |
| `bcm.continuity_strategies` | `APPROVED` | an RTO **or** an RPO — its guard's own comment says a strategy with no recovery target should not be approved |
| `platform.control_assessments` | `APPROVED` | the DRAFT → UNDER_REVIEW → APPROVED walk |
| `bcm.crisis_events` | `CLOSED` | **spec §J.13** — a root cause AND a lessons-learned record |
| `platform.issues` | `CLOSED` | a validated resolution code, `resolved_at`, `closed_at` |
| `tprm.questionnaire_templates` | `ACTIVE` | **at least one question** — then sent to vendors as an assessment |

In every case the `/transition` route answered **400 or 409 for the identical edge**, so the control
exists and the create walked around it.

### Authorization: this is F2-219's shape, not F2-218's

**No privilege escalation.** All nine carry the *same* permission on the create and on the
transition, so the object-level machine is the **only** control — and it sat one method away with
nothing consulting it. Worth saying plainly, because F2-218's instance *was* an escalation and the
two read alike in a summary.

⚙ Measured in passing: **`PLATFORM:WRITE` is held by one role with zero active users**, so the Issue
register's write routes are reachable in dev only by `admin` (which proves nothing about
authorization — CLAUDE.md's rule — but the finding here is object-level, not permission-level).

### Four of the nine had no vocabulary check at all, and two have no CHECK constraint either

`BcpPlanService`, `ControlLibraryService`, `CrisisEventService` and `IssueService` tested nothing.
`platform.issues` has **no CHECK constraints at all** and `bcm.crisis_events` none on `status`, so
for those two **an arbitrary string was storable** — and `transition()`'s `default -> false` then
makes the row **permanently untransitionable by any route**. That is F2-203's `audit_lc` shape (19
of 46 rows stuck in states no route can leave), creatable on demand through the API.

### 🔑 One register needed a different primitive, and measuring is what showed it

`platform.authority_documents` defaults to **ACTIVE** while its machine's root is **DRAFT**, and both
are accepted today. Forcing one initial state would have **refused a working create** — the one
failure F2-182's test exists to prevent. So `ServerOwnedState` gained a second overload,
`requireCreatable(supplied, creatable, initial, register, route)`, used by exactly this register with
the reason recorded, and it **self-checks that the default is in its own creatable set** so the value
the server picks and the values it accepts cannot disagree. Deliberately *not* the general form: a
per-register list of allowed states is precisely the artefact F2-217 found measuring its own list.

### Verification

- **Pre-fix live probe 36/36** and **post-fix 45/45**, run twice. Every row planted by the probe
  (F2-206), tagged `[REVIEW-TEST] F2-220`, removed with `CHARINDEX`, children first — resolved from
  `sys.foreign_keys`, because the first draft invented `bcp_plan_sections` and a 547 on cleanup reads
  exactly like the probe having gone wrong.
- **Backend 3,939/0/0** (from 3,914: +14 behaviour, +4 gate, +7 primitive).
- **Mutation 20/20 killed, 0 survived, 0 anchor-miss.**
- **The pre-fix control**: the new gate run against `git stash`-reverted main sources reports
  **exactly the nine**, so the hard zero is a measurement and not an empty population.

### 🔑 The Java gate and the scratch census agreed 9/9 — the first exact agreement in this lineage

F2-213's locator found 5 where its gate found 9; F2-214's found 3 where its gate found 11. Both
recorded the rule *write the sweep as the gate, over the same tree, in the same language*, and both
kept the scratch measurement until the shipped gate reproduced it (F2-217). Doing both here cost one
extra hour and bought the only evidence that the hard zero means anything.

### My own errors, all caught by running things

- **Three probe payload bugs**: two guessed vocabulary tokens (`CYBER` for `CYBERATTACK`,
  `ALTERNATE_SITE` for `BACKUP_SITE`) and a **guessed column name** (`notes` on
  `control_assessments`, really `notes_en`). Recurring since F2-198 — **resolve from `sys.columns`,
  never guess** — and each one failed in the direction that reads like a refutation.
- **A CRLF anchor miss** in the import script: `^import .*?;$` under `re.M` cannot match, because
  `$` sits before the `\n` and there is a `\r` after the `;`. Third slice running.
- ⚠⚠ **One mutation SURVIVED and the control was wrong, not the gate.** M18 deletes the narrowing
  that stops the caller's own payload counting as a loaded row — and my negative control read the
  field on the loaded row (`e.getNote()`) rather than on the payload, so the *read-the-same-field*
  clause already excluded the fixture and the narrowing was never exercised. 🔑 **A negative control
  that does not reach the code it controls proves nothing, and its passing reads exactly like the
  narrowing being sound** (F2-197's rule). Fixed, and M18 is killed.

### ⚙ One inert construct removed rather than left

`TEMPLATE_STATUSES` in `QuestionnaireService` had exactly one reader — the create's membership test,
the very check that admitted ACTIVE — and `transitionTemplate`'s switch is exhaustive, so an
unrecognised target already throws. Deleting it beat leaving it unread (F2-184: an inert construct is
worse than none, because it answers the question a reader was about to ask). The vocabulary is stated
by the machine and by `ck_qt_status`.

### ⚙ F2-215's headline, one more time, found in passing

`BcpPlan` marks `approvedBy` and `approvedAt` `@JsonProperty(READ_ONLY)` and **leaves `publishedAt`** —
two of three, sibling forgotten, exactly as `TcfdItem` did in F2-219. The create scrubs all three so
the answer does not depend on which were annotated.

|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-16.** Nine creates routed through the refusal primitive; hard zero in `ServerStampedFieldContractTest#noCreateMayNameAStateATransitionRouteAdjudicates` with the nine machines named so the population cannot silently empty; `CreateMayNotNameATransitionStateTest` (14) and `ServerOwnedStateTest` (7) pin the behaviour. Backend 3,939/0/0 · mutation 20/20 · probe 36/36 pre, 45/45 post. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A create that names the state does not merely skip the machine — it skips the machine's evidence requirements**, and those are the whole reason the machine exists: a successor document, a linked corrective action, a recovery objective, one question, a resolution code, a root cause. 🔑 And **a gate cannot see a defect whose value arrives by a route the gate classifies as caller data** — F2-219 named that blind spot rather than papering over it, which is the only reason this was findable. |

## F2-219 · A default is not a settlement — the gate F2-218 built to catch that counted one as a settlement, and hid a forged policy attestation

**Found** 2026-08-16, taking F2-218's derived work list (the 8 services). **P2.**
**Closed** the same day. No migration, no endpoint change, no frontend change.

### The instrument was wrong first

F2-218's headline is that **`if (x == null) x = INITIAL` is a DEFAULT, not a guard**, and its gate
then computed the create-side answer as *"did anything overwrite the field before the save?"* — for
which a default answers **yes**. So a defaulted field dropped out of the ACCEPTED set entirely.

🔑 **F2-218's own headline, inside the gate F2-218 built to enforce it.** Worse, the positive
control asserted the behaviour as correct, in those words: *"crucially it does NOT read as a caller
write, which is why the create-side check must be 'did anything overwrite it before the save'"*.
F2-159's shape — **a test can lock in a defect, and it is hardest to spot when it describes the
code accurately.**

Correcting it moved the population **8 → 9 services**, and every field it added was a **`status`**:
the decisions.

### Five detector corrections, and the direction of each

| # | correction | direction | what it hid or invented |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `readsRequest` was line-blind (`String#matches` with no `(?s)`) | **under**-reported | Every setter whose argument WRAPS. The house idiom `setStatus(ServerOwnedState.requireInitial(\n body.getStatus(), …))` wraps by width, so the four services F2-218 closed were passing the hard zero **for the wrong reason**. |
| 2 | the refusal primitive was not recognised | would have **over**-reported | Fixing (1) alone reports `requireInitial(...)` as an acceptance — i.e. the fix F2-217/F2-218 introduced, reported as the defect it prevents. |
| 3 | a DEFAULT counted as a settlement | **under**-reported | The finding itself: 3 registers, all `status`. |
| 4 | a bare-identifier local aliasing caller data | **over**-reported | `NdiComplianceAssessmentService`'s correct, null-guarded update read as a contradiction. |
| 5 | per-field `@JsonProperty(READ_ONLY)` was invisible | **over**-reported | `DataSharingAgreement#signedAt`, on F2-218's list as open, has carried the annotation all along. |

🔑 **Two of them cancelled out.** (1) and (2) were both live, in opposite directions, so the CLOSED
services passed a hard zero that neither error earned. **Two errors agreeing produce a green.**

🔑 **On (5): `CLOSED_AT_THE_WIRE` names `BaseEntity`'s nine and no per-field annotations, and a
reader who finds that subtraction present does not then ask which OTHER fields are closed the same
way.** F2-215's headline, one level up, on the gate rather than on a fix. It is now DERIVED from the
entity source.

### The live defect it hid, probed as `ranalyst` (holds `COMPLIANCE:READ`, held by **32 roles**)

| request | result |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/policy/attestations` `{policyId: 1, userUsername: "compliance", status: "ATTESTED", attestedAt: "2001-01-01"}` | **200**, all three stored |
| `POST /api/policy/attestations/{id}/attest` on a record assigned to someone else | **403** |

`PolicyManagementService.attest()` carries **SEC-CMP-004** — in its own words, *"only the assignee
(or an admin override) may complete an attestation-of-record"* — plus a PENDING gate, `attestedAt`
from the clock, the acting principal recorded in `updatedBy` *"for non-repudiation"*, an ATTEST
audit row and a `POLICY_ATTESTED` event. **None of it ran**, and no ATTEST audit row was written, so
the forgery is invisible to the trail an auditor reads.

A policy attestation is the artefact produced to show that a **named individual** personally
acknowledged a policy. Both endpoints are guarded by `COMPLIANCE:READ` — deliberately, because
attesting is a duty, like the ADR-010 intake exception — so the object-level check is the *only*
control, and the create route sat two lines away from it without one.

⚠ **No permission escalation, and that is worth stating plainly.** Unlike F2-218 there is no
403-vs-200 asymmetry: the same permission opens both routes. What is bypassed is the object-level
authorization, the state gate, the clock, the attribution and the audit row.

### Two more confirmed live, same shape

- **`DataSharingAgreementService#create`** — `POST /api/privacy/data-sharing` with
  `{status: "ACTIVE", signerName: "Nobody Who Signed This"}` → **201**, stored: a third-party
  data-sharing agreement live and signed without `submit()` or `activate()` (which stamps
  `signed_at` from the clock). ⚠ Its `if (status == null) DRAFT` was followed by
  `if (!STATUSES.contains(status)) throw` — 🔑 **checking a value is IN the vocabulary is not
  checking it is one a record may START in** (F2-217's sentence about `audit_lc`). A detector
  cannot infer "settled" from the presence of a throw, which is exactly why the DEFAULT test is
  scoped to the guard's own `if/else` chain.
- **`CommitteeActionItemService#create`** — a governance action item created `COMPLETED`, never
  passing `complete()`, which stamps `completed_at`, records the notes, writes the
  `ACTION_COMPLETE` audit row and publishes the transition the committee pack reads.

### Two refuted, both for the same reason

- **`TcfdItem#approvalStatus,approvedAt,approvedBy`** — INERT. `TcfdItemCreateRequest` declares
  none of them, and `update()`'s whitelist does not copy them. ⚠ But `approvedBy` and `approvedAt`
  carry `@JsonProperty(READ_ONLY)` **and `approvalStatus` did not** — two of three marked, the
  sibling left, F2-215's shape again. Closed with the annotation (F2-182: close a refuted site when
  it gates a control), so the protection is a mechanism rather than two accidents.
- **`ProcessorAssessment#approvedAt`** — **all seven** of the fields that create appears to accept
  already carry `@JsonProperty(READ_ONLY)`. A scrub would be decoration, and an inert construct is
  worse than none because it answers the question a reader was about to ask (F2-184) — so the fix
  was **reverted** and replaced by the measurement as a comment. `ProcessorAssessmentService` is
  deliberately NOT in `CLOSED`: listing a service that was never open makes it indistinguishable
  from one that was read and fixed.

**2 of 6 refuted** — the ~2-in-10 rate F2-188/F2-192/F2-204 each measured, and both refutations have
one cause: **the gate measures the service layer while the closure lives at the wire.**

### The shape the gate still cannot see, named rather than papered over

`ClimateRiskOpportunityService#transition(Long id, String to)` enforces the linear machine and then
writes `cur.setStatus(to)` — from a **parameter**. A scalar parameter is caller data (F2-218's third
detector bug), so `status` never enters the STAMPED set and a create accepting it is not a
contradiction by this gate's stated question. The mutation restoring that default **SURVIVED the
whole build**. 🔑 **A surviving mutant the gate legitimately cannot see is an unasserted behaviour,
not a loose instrument** — widening the gate would mean treating a caller-supplied parameter as a
server stamp again, reinstating the correction that stopped it failing on correct code. The answer
was a test. **Filed: every register whose transition route takes its target state as an argument is
outside this instrument by construction.**

### The figure

`BASELINE_CONTRADICTED_SERVICES` **8 → 0**, with `CLOSED` at 10 and a **three-entry `BY_DESIGN` map**
(`NdiSettingService`, `SgiCommitmentService`, `NdiComplianceAssessmentService`), each read in this
slice and enforced in **both** directions so an entry cannot outlive its subject.

⚠ **The anti-vacuity floor had to change shape with the number.** It was `>= BASELINE - 3`; at zero
that reads `>= -3` and can never fail. 🔑 **A floor is only worth having if it sits above the largest
WRONG answer (F2-215) — and here the wrong answer IS zero**, because a rotted detector reports an
empty population and that is indistinguishable from a finished sweep. The floor is now the reverse
leg over `BY_DESIGN`, which a bare count could not be.

### Verification

Backend **3,914/0/0** · mutation **16/16 killed, 0 survived, 0 anchor-miss** · live probe **30/30**
post-fix (**18/22** pre-fix, where the four failures were the probe's own and are recorded below).
Half the post-fix legs assert the guarded routes still work — SEC-CMP-004 still answers 403 to a
non-assignee, the assignee still attests with a clock stamp and an audit row, `submit()`/`activate()`
still run and stamp `signed_at`, `complete()` still records its notes, `approve()` still stamps the
principal — because a slice that closed a bypass by breaking the control it protects would score
identically. Probe run twice, identical (F2-203: a probe that writes rows must be re-runnable).
`[REVIEW-TEST]` rows removed with `CHARINDEX`. **No frontend file changed**, so no FE run is claimed.

WARNING: **four of the pre-fix probe's failures were mine, not refutations** — TCFD answers **201**
where I asserted 200; a caller-chosen `2001-01-01` stores as `2000-12-31 21:00` because the box is
**UTC+3** and the server is UTC; and two payloads were missing NOT NULL columns, one of them
`title_ar` (house rule 7). ⚠ I also guessed a column (`permissions.module_code`, really `module`)
and two tables (`policy.policy_documents` → `policy.documents`, `sust.tcfd_items` → `sust.tcfd_item`)
— **resolve from `sys.columns`/`sys.tables`, never guess** (F2-198/F2-199, recurring).

WARNING: **my own new test failed on the unmutated tree and the harness did not notice.**
`validateAxes()` runs before the status guard in the climate create, so an incomplete fixture threw
for the wrong reason — and the assertion passed on a message unrelated to its claim. 🔑 **A test
that fails on the unmutated tree makes every mutation routed through it read as KILLED.** Found by
the full suite, not by the harness; the harness was re-run against a green tree afterwards.

WARNING: **ANCHOR-MISS on the one multi-line anchor, in a harness whose own docstring says the
services are CRLF.** Second instance of F2-212 in two slices. 🔑 **Naming a trap does not exempt you
from it** (F2-192's rule, now three-for-three).

### Also

F2-218's register row had **no `**Status**` cell**, so `FindingsRegisterConsistencyTest` was red on
master for a day. That slice's final re-run named five gate classes — including the two it had just
written — and not this one. 🔑 **A targeted re-run after a docs commit is not the suite, and the docs
gate is precisely the gate a docs commit can break.** Corrected here.

  `ClimateRiskOpportunityService#transition` and `TcfdItemService#transition`. The population is

- `TcfdItem#approvalStatus` is **NULL** on a fresh row, not `PENDING`, although `APPROVAL_STATUSES`

| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-16.** Five detector corrections, three live defects fixed, two refuted and one reverted as dead code. `BASELINE_CONTRADICTED_SERVICES` 8 → 0; `CLOSED` 10 services; `BY_DESIGN` 3, verified by reading and enforced both ways. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **F2-218's headline inside the gate F2-218 built: a default and a guard are indistinguishable to any scan that only asks whether the setter is present — including one written to answer that very finding.** And **two detector errors in opposite directions produce a green that neither one earns.** |

## F2-218 · A caller holding only NDI:WRITE could approve NDI evidence, and the comment removing the reviewer's name sat one line above the decision itself

**Found** 2026-08-15, taking F2-217's filed work list (the 55 NEEDS-VERDICT rows). **P2.**
**Closed** the same day. No migration, no endpoint change.

### The defect, probed live as `ranalyst` (holds `NDI:WRITE`, **not** `NDI:APPROVE`)

| request | result |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/ndi/evidence/1/approve` | **403** |
| `POST /api/ndi/evidence` `{status: ACTIVE, reviewerName: "Nobody Who Reviewed This", reviewedAt: 2001-01-01, ownerName: "ranalyst"}` | **200**, all three stored |
| `PUT /api/ndi/evidence/{id}` `{status: ACTIVE}` on a PENDING row | **200**, transition performed |

`NdiEvidenceItemService.approve()` carries the SEC-NDI-003 maker/checker control: `NDI:APPROVE`
at the controller, a segregation-of-duties check in the service (*the evidence owner may not
approve their own item*), the reviewer resolved from the authenticated principal, and an audit
transition row. **Both write paths reached the same end state with none of it**, and neither
wrote an audit row. 12/12 probe legs pre-fix.

KEY: **the comment was right about one of the three fields the same control owns.** The update
carried, verbatim: *"reviewerName is the attribution field for the maker/checker SoD control - it
is stamped server-side from the authenticated principal at approve/reject, never bound from the
request body."* Directly beneath it sat `if (body.getReviewedAt() != null) e.setReviewedAt(...)`
and `if (body.getStatus() != null) e.setStatus(...)`. `reviewerName` is the *attribution*,
`status` is the **decision**, `reviewedAt` is *when*. **Removing the name while leaving the
decision meant a WRITE-only caller could approve evidence; the record simply did not say who.**
F2-215's headline one level down, and the fourth instance in this lineage of the correct artefact
sitting beside the wrong one (F2-209's reader 200 lines below, F2-213's `CyberEvidenceService`,
F2-214's `PrivacyBreachRequest` eight lines below).

Two sibling registers, same shape: an improvement plan created `COMPLETED` with
`approverName="Nobody Who Approved This"` (skipping `DRAFT -> APPROVED` and the whole machine
under it), and an assessment cycle whose `if (status == null) status = "DRAFT"` let any declared
status through.

### KEY: a default and a guard are indistinguishable to any scan that only asks whether the setter is present

`body.setStatus("DRAFT")` **discards** what the caller sent. `if (body.getStatus() == null)
body.setStatus("DRAFT")` **keeps** it. My scratch census reported both as `sets:status` - a scrub
- because its guard regex used `[^)]*`, which cannot cross the `)` in `getStatus()`. **The
discriminator is not the guard, it is the VALUE**: a literal, a clock or the principal means the
server owns the field; an expression reading the request means the caller does.

### The instrument: the verdict is DERIVED, not another name list

F2-217 established that a census keyed on a list of field names measures the list. The lesson
generalises past widening the list: **the authority a field carries is a fact about the service
that owns it, and the service already states it** - in the methods that stamp the field after
checking a state and recording who acted. `ServerStampedFieldContractTest` intersects, per
service and **per entity type**, the fields its guarded routes stamp with the fields its
create/update paths take from the request. Four services are a **hard zero**; the remaining
**8** ride a decrease-only figure with the evidence printed per site into
`target/server-stamped-fields.txt` - a work list, **not** a set of manufactured reasons
(F2-188's failure mode, avoided deliberately).

KEY: **this is what makes `MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s verdict column derivable rather than 55
pieces of plausible prose.**

### Three detector bugs, and the direction each failed in

| # | bug | direction |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | a DEFAULT read as a guard (`[^)]*` cannot cross `getStatus()`'s paren) | **shrank** the population - reads as a clean tree |
| 2 | an inverted null test (`!= null`) read as an unconditional server write | **shrank** it - cleared 7 wide-open sites |
| 3 | a **scalar method parameter** read as a server value (`markUnderReview(String reviewerName)`) | **grew** it - a false positive on correct code |

The third is the worse one. **A gate that fails on correct code trains the next reader to edit
the assertion rather than the code** (F2-214). 11 raw sites -> 8, three refuted by the gate's own
corrections. And a fourth, caught on the gate's first run: both halves were keyed by **service**,
so `NdiImprovementPlanService#addItem` - which persists an *item* - was charged with accepting
three fields of the *plan*. KEY: **a service that owns two entities has two field vocabularies**;
F2-191 recorded the same shape one level up (*a same-package proxy is not same-entity*).

### KEY: a gate measuring the service layer cannot see a fix made at the wire layer

7 of the gate's first 24 findings were `isDeleted` and `updatedAt` - already closed by
F2-206/F2-215's `ServerOwnedFieldsModule`, an introspector that marks `BaseEntity`'s nine fields
READ_ONLY on every entity Jackson binds. Subtracted explicitly, with the exclusion list checked
against the introspector's own source in both directions rather than restated.

### What was NOT done

Server-**derived** state still differs from the initial state, asserted in both directions: Rule 6
still flips an item to `EXPIRED` at `approve()`, and a CAPA still lands `OVERDUE` from its target
date. *"A create always lands in the initial state"* is an equally passing and wrong reading of
this change. The cycle's initial state is `FORWARD_FLOW.get(0)` - **derived, never typed**
(F2-196's rule).

`ServerOwnedState` **refuses** rather than coercing, per F2-182's test (*what is already refusing
this?*): the create already rejected anything outside the register's vocabulary, so every value
that succeeds today is a declared state, and the only requests newly refused are ones performing
an unguarded transition. **A request that performs an unguarded transition is not a working
request.** The create form sends no status at all, and the entity's own `@PrePersist` already
defaults to `PENDING`, which is what made this safe to enforce.

### Verification

Backend **3,897/0/0** - frontend **756/0/0** + `tsc` clean - mutation **11/11 killed, 0 survived,
0 anchor-miss** - pre-fix control fires on all three services - live probe **17/17** post-fix
(12/12 pre-fix demonstrating the bypass). The post-fix probe deliberately spends half its legs on
the guarded routes still working - approve reaches ACTIVE, the reviewer is `compliance` from the
principal, the audit row is written, SoD answers **409** - because a slice that closed the bypass
by breaking the approval workflow would otherwise score identically. `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows removed
with `CHARINDEX`.

WARNING: two mutations survived the first run and **neither was a gate hole**: the gate
legitimately cannot see them (the plan's approver is caller-supplied on *both* routes; the cycle's
derivation is one line). KEY: **a surviving mutant the gate cannot see is an unasserted behaviour,
not a loose instrument** - the answer was `NdiCreateInitialStateTest`, not a wider gate. Widening
it would have meant treating a caller-supplied parameter as a server stamp again, i.e.
reinstating detector bug 3.

WARNING: two anchor misses, from multi-line anchors - **the services are CRLF and the files this
slice wrote are LF**, so either separator misses on half the tree. ANCHOR-MISS is a distinct
non-zero outcome precisely so it does not read as a pass (F2-212).

### Also

`ndiEvidence.ts`'s `approveEvidence`/`rejectEvidence` dropped their inert `reviewerName`
parameter; the single call site passed the literal `'admin'`. The server has always ignored it
(SEC-NDI-003) - **a parameter the server discards is a claim about where the attribution comes
from.**

### Filed

- **8 services** on the derived work list, with evidence:
  `TcfdItem#approvalStatus,approvedAt,approvedBy` on create; `ProcessorAssessment#approvedAt,
  approverName`; `PolicyDocument#approverName,publishedAt` (create and update);
  `DataSharingAgreement#counterpartySigner,signedAt,signerName`;
  `ClimateRiskOpportunity#assessedAt,closedAt,treatedAt`; `SgiCommitment#currentValue*`;
  `NdiComplianceAssessment` (5 fields); `NdiSetting#valueText`;
  `SustainabilityEvidence#supersedesId`. Some will be BY DESIGN - an M&A letter-of-intent signing
  date is genuinely the caller's - which is why they are a work list and not a verdict.

| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-15.** Fix `bbdbd1c1`, docs `279a3f08`, tracker `953969f0`. The three NDI registers refuse a create that names a non-initial state; `ServerStampedFieldContractTest` holds four services at a hard zero and the remainder on a derived work list. F2-219 then took that list — and found this entry's own numbers under-measured, because the gate counted a DEFAULT as a settlement. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **Removing the attribution while leaving the decision means a WRITE-only caller can approve, and the record just does not say who** — the comment naming `reviewerName` as server-stamped sat one line above the two lines copying `status` and `reviewedAt`. And **`if (x == null) x = INITIAL` is a default, not a guard: the discriminator is not the guard, it is the VALUE.** |

⚠ **This row had no `**Status**` cell until F2-219 added it, and the suite says so.**
`FindingsRegisterConsistencyTest.everyRowExposesAState` was red on master for a day. The slice's
final re-run covered five gate classes by name — including the two it had just written — and not
this one. 🔑 **A targeted re-run after a docs commit is not the suite, and the docs gate is
precisely the gate a docs commit can break.** Run the suite after the last commit, not the last
code commit.
- `MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s remaining **48** NEEDS-VERDICT rows (was 55; 7 adjudicated here:
  5 CLOSED, 1 INERT, 1 BY DESIGN).
- The **83 entity-bound PUT handlers** (F2-22) remain the structural root.

## F2-217 · An internal-audit plan could be created already approved by the Audit Committee, and the ratchet built for forged authority spelled the columns differently

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-217 |
| **Severity** | **P2 — live, not latent.** Three governance registers accepted a create that both named a terminal state and forged the attribution for it. Reachable by any holder of `AUDIT:WRITE`; probed live and reproduced on all three. Not P1 only because the affected registers are internal-audit artefacts rather than a statutory filing, and no evidence of use exists in dev or prod. |
| **Status** | **CLOSED 2026-08-15** (`3e0fcd7c`). Backend refuses a non-initial status and clears the transition-stamped columns; the ranking instrument is corrected; 6 of the surfaced endpoints adjudicated, 55 filed as a measured work list. |
| **Where** | `module/audit_lc/service/AuditLifecycleService` (3 creates), `security/MassAssignmentRatchetTest`, `tss-grc-ui-v2/src/lib/auditLifecycle.ts` |

**What was asked.** [[F2-216]] left one item on its Status row: *"`MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s **184 TENANT-tier
rows have an EMPTY adjudication column**, and its own header says the adjudication column is the authority, not
the tier."* This is that population, read.

**The instrument was ranking a field it had already closed, and hiding one it had not.** The tier ladder read
`tenant && (authority||outcome) ? CRIT : (authority||outcome) ? HIGH : tenant ? TENANT : state ? STATE : LOW`.
Two problems, and they reinforced each other:

- **`tenant` outranked `state`.** 145 of the 214 endpoints bind `organisationId` **and** a state field, so they
  ranked TENANT and the state binding never appeared in the tier at all. The STATE tier read **4**.
- **`tenant` was also required to reach CRIT**, on the premise that a bindable `organisationId` is an
  unmitigated cross-tenant write. [[F2-216]] measured that premise one slice earlier and it no longer holds:
  202 entity-bound writes all stamp the tenant, and the interceptor is wired and enabled in dev *and* prod.

🔑 **A ranking whose top discriminator has been CLOSED no longer ranks risk — and while it stays on top it
MASKS whatever it outranks.**

**And the authority vocabulary was a literal list of field names.** `AUTHORITY` held `approvedBy`,
`reviewedBy`, `closedBy` — written from the four bypasses this class was built after (DF-3, DF-4, [[F2-25]],
the roster link), i.e. **from those four instances' spellings**. Measured from the regenerated profile:
**24 distinct authority-shaped names on 64 of the 214 endpoints** the list did not spell — `acApprovedBy`,
`reviewer`, `reviewedAt`, `closedAt`, `approverName` (13 endpoints), `reviewerName` (14), `publishedAt`,
`ratifiedAt`, `integrityVerifiedAt`, `loiSignedAt`, `pirReviewedBy`…
🔑 **A census keyed on a list of names measures the list, not the codebase** — the eighth appearance of
[[F2-198]]'s shape here (*the invariant is real, its POPULATION is narrower than it looks*), and the sharpest,
because this instrument's own javadoc says it exists **because** *"ranking 214 endpoints by hand is how the
first four were found — one at a time, over months."*

**The live defect underneath.** All three `audit_lc` creates persist the request entity and validated `status`
only for **membership of the vocabulary**, never for being a state a record may *start* in. Probed live as
`compliance` (not `admin` — the guard is `AUDIT:WRITE` and the defect is post-guard):

| create | sent | stored | the guarded route, same transition |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /annual-plans` | `status=AC_APPROVED`, `acApprovedBy="Nobody Who Approved This"`, `acApprovedAt=2001-01-01` | **200**, all three | `DRAFT → AC_APPROVED` → **409** |
| `POST /working-papers` | `status=APPROVED`, `reviewer="Nobody Who Reviewed This"`, `reviewedAt=2001-01-01` | **200**, all three | machine requires `PEER_REVIEW` first |
| `POST /capas` | `status=CLOSED`, `closedAt=2001-01-01` | **200**, both | `CLOSED` only from `AWAITING_VERIFICATION` |

So: an internal-audit annual plan filed as **approved by the Audit Committee** with no approval; an **IIA
Standard 2330 working paper** created already peer-reviewed, attributed to a name of the caller's choosing; a
corrective action **closed without ever being verified**, backdated. That is DF-3/DF-4's defect — forged
authority — sitting in the tier the instrument mis-ranked.

⚠⚠ **The fix that preceded it names the field it left open.** [[F2-203]] closed `author` on
`createWorkingPaper` — *"an invented auditor was PERSISTED as the author of an IIA Standard 2330 working
paper"* — and its comment says *"the same rule `transitionWorkingPaper` below already applies to `reviewer`."*
True of the transition; **false of the create it is written on.** The live probe returned
`author=compliance`, correctly stamped, **beside a `reviewer` the caller had chosen**. 🔑 [[F2-215]]'s headline
one level down: **fixing the field you noticed leaves the remainder looking covered, because the mechanism
that covers them is visibly present** — and here a comment explicitly cites the sibling protection as
evidence.

**Fix — two rules, and the second is what makes them checkable.** Each register declares its **initial state**
once, read by *both* the default applied when the caller says nothing *and* the new guard, so the value the
server picks and the value it accepts cannot drift ([[F2-178]]'s one-predicate shape). The transition-stamped
columns are cleared on create. ⚠ Refusing rather than coercing follows [[F2-182]]'s rule — *ask what is
already refusing*: the create already rejected anything outside the vocabulary, so the only requests this
newly refuses are ones performing an unguarded transition, and **a request that performs an unguarded
transition is not a working request**. The 400 names the field and the route that can record who decided.
⚠ Server-**derived** state still runs — `applyOverdue` may still move a new CAPA to `OVERDUE` from its target
date, and a test asserts it, because *"a create always lands in the initial state"* would be an equally
passing and wrong reading of the change.

**Instrument fix.** The authority vocabulary becomes a **shape** — an act (`verb` + `By`/`At`, matched as a
suffix so `acApprovedBy` is caught with the bare form) or an actor (agent noun + optional `Id`/`Name`) — with
the literal list retained **only** to split the CRIT population in two. Tiers move **CRIT 18 → 79, HIGH 3 →
merged, TENANT 184 → 29, STATE 4 → 101.**

⚠⚠ **The number the assertion holds went UP, and that is the finding, not a regression.** The pre-F2-217 CRIT
set keeps its **hard zero** — every endpoint the old ladder ranked CRIT is still adjudicated. The 55 the
widening surfaced ride a separate decrease-only figure, printed **NEEDS-VERDICT** into
`target/mass-assignment-risk.txt` with the fields that put each there, so it is a work list rather than a
count. 🔑 [[F2-205]]'s rule, not [[F2-204]]'s: **there a ratchet's QUESTION was wrong so it was re-scoped;
here the question was right and the ANSWER was under-measured, so the figure moves and says so. A hard zero
over a population the instrument cannot see is the most reassuring possible artefact.** 6 adjudicated in this
slice (3 creates CLOSED, 3 updates INERT — all three updates are field whitelists that never mention status or
the authority columns); 55 remain, deliberately **not** given manufactured reasons ([[F2-188]]'s failure mode,
[[F2-194]]'s ratified alternative).

⚠⚠ **My detector under-reported and only a second measurement caught it.** `AUTHORITY_SHAPE`'s first draft was
lower-case-only, so it did not match `acApprovedBy` — **the two `AnnualPlan` endpoints whose live probe
motivated the whole slice ranked STATE, and the build was green.** Found by diffing against the throwaway
census that had used `CASE_INSENSITIVE`. 🔑 **A detector that cannot match reads exactly like a clean tree, and
it UNDER-reports** — the argument for keeping the scratch measurement until the shipped gate reproduces it.

⚠⚠ **The mutation harness found a hole two shape assertions had left between them.** Restoring only the
`tenant &&` half of the old ladder **SURVIVED**: it lowers the CRIT count, which a `<=` ceiling reads as
progress; it leaves no TENANT row binding a state field, so the masking leg is satisfied; and it quietly
demotes the three endpoints binding an approval field on a body with no `organisationId`. 🔑 **Two shape
assertions that each look complete can still leave the predicate between them free to move.** Closed with
`anEndpointBindingAnAuthorityOrOutcomeFieldIsAlwaysRankedCrit`.

⚠ **A gate leg of mine failed on correct code and was narrowed, not exempted.** The frontend gate asserted
`to:` on every transition payload; `transitionFinding` posts `{ status, mgmtResponseEn, … }` while the
plan/paper/CAPA routes post `{ to }`. **A gate that fails on correct code is worse than no gate — it trains
the next reader to edit the assertion rather than the code** ([[F2-214]]).

⚠ **Probe-harness landmine, and it is [[F2-215]]'s defect seen from the other side.** `DELETE` here is a
**soft** delete while the UNIQUE index on `(organisation_id, external_id)` still sees the row, so a re-run with
a fixed `externalId` fails on the index — **which reads exactly like the fix having broken**. Every run now
mints a fresh suffix ([[F2-203]]: a probe that writes rows must be re-runnable).

⚠⚠ **Correction to [[F2-216]]'s environment note.** That entry recorded *":8084 MAY NOT BE YOUR BACKEND"* and
concluded the listener belonged to another session, from its log timestamp. It did not: the process's own
`-Djava.io.tmpdir` names **this** session's scratchpad. 🔑 **A log timestamp is not process identity — the
JVM's own arguments are.** The practical consequence was the opposite of the one recorded: the listener was
mine to restart, and it needed restarting, because `mvn -o test` had rewritten `target/classes` **without**
DevTools reloading the context — the post-fix probe scored 7/14 against code the running process had never
loaded. 🔑 **A stale listener answers `/actuator/health` 200 and serves the OLD behaviour, which is the most
misleading possible result for a fix-verification probe.**

**Verification.** Backend **3,878/0/0**; frontend **756/0/0** across 69 files + `tsc` clean. Mutation
**13/13 killed, 0 survived, 0 anchor-miss**. Pre-fix control: both changed files restored from `master` and
the gates **fail**, as they must. Live probe **14/14 post-fix** on a restarted backend (**7/14 pre-fix**, same
script). 15 `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows removed with `CHARINDEX`. **No migration, no endpoint change, no schema
change.**

**Filed.** The **55 NEEDS-VERDICT rows** are the next slice of F2-22b, already sorted by the fields that put
them there — `approverName` (13), `reviewerName` (14), `closedAt` (12), `reviewedAt` (11), `publishedAt` (7),
`lastReviewedAt` (8) — and the largest clusters are `PolicyController`, `CyberController`, `NdiEvidenceItem`,
`SustainabilityEvidence` and `ControlLibraryController`. Each needs its service read; the verdict is CLOSED /
INERT / BY DESIGN, and lowering `BASELINE_UNADJUDICATED_NEW_CRIT` belongs in the same commit.

**Lesson.** 🔑 **A risk ranking built from a literal name list finds exactly the spellings its author had
already seen — so the instrument built to stop a defect recurring reproduces the blind spot that let it
happen.** And its corollary, which is what made this one findable: **when a ranking's top discriminator gets
closed, re-read the ladder, because a closed field at the top is not neutral — it hides everything beneath
it.**

## F2-216 · The platform-wide tenant backstop exempts the one value that means "every tenant", and the reason it gives is false

| | |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-216 |
| **Severity** | **P3 — latent.** No caller can reach it today. Recorded because what makes it unreachable is a property nobody had written down, and because two neighbouring classes described the control as not running at all. |
| **Status** | **CLOSED 2026-08-15** (`666d8526`). Reason corrected, invariant gated, wiring claims fixed. Behaviour deliberately unchanged. |
| **Where** | `common/tenant/TenantWriteGuardInterceptor#decideInsert`, `common/tenant/TenantContext`, `config/TenantWriteGuardConfig` |

**What was asked.** F2-215 filed `organisationId` as the last unclosed field of `MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s
TENANT tier — *"services assign it explicitly from `TenantContext`, so closing it at the wire needs its own
measurement."* This is that measurement, and it went the other way: **`organisationId` is defended at every
reachable point.** 202 entity-bound write endpoints, every one with a tenant stamp on its create path; the
`TenantWriteGuardInterceptor` wired and enabled in dev **and** prod with both legs (F2-22b added the insert
leg). Probed live: `POST /api/v1/controls` with `organisationId: 2` from an org-1 caller stores org 1.
🔑 **A filed item that measures as already-defended is a result, not a dead end — the value is in what the
measurement passes on the way.**

**What the measurement found.** `decideInsert` waves through a row whose `organisationId` is null, and says
why: *"not a cross-tenant write. It is a NOT NULL violation about to happen, and the database says so far
more clearly than a SecurityException would."* Read from `sys.columns` in both databases: of the **427
org-bearing tables** (421 in prod), **11 declare the column NULLABLE** — so for those the database says
nothing, and the sentence predicting what it would say was the only analysis anybody had done.

**And on eight of the eleven, NULL is not an absence — it is a value meaning PLATFORM-GLOBAL.**
`aml.sanctions_list`, `aml.sanctions_list_entry`, `fraud.fraud_typology`, `iam.roles`, `iam.sod_rules`,
`opres.opres_pillar`, `platform.help_topic`, `platform.three_lines_role_mapping` are each read by a repository
asking `organisationId IS NULL OR organisationId = :orgId`, and `SanctionsListRepository`'s own javadoc states
it. **169 of their 177 rows in dev, 158 of 166 in prod, are stored that way.** Verified with the repositories'
own predicate as SQL: org 1 reads back **5 sanctions lists, 8 SoD rules and 69 roles that no tenant owns**.

🔑 **So the value the platform-wide cross-tenant backstop declines to judge is precisely the value that
publishes a row to every tenant.** Not the NOT NULL violation the comment predicted — an entry added to every
other tenant's sanctions screening, or a role added to every other tenant's IAM catalogue, with the backstop
watching and returning `false` without logging a line.

⚠⚠ **The internal inconsistency is the tell, and it was visible the whole time.** The UPDATE leg treats the
same value as protected: `decide` compares old against new, so a global row pulled into one tenant
(`null → 5`) throws, and `blocksWhenOrganisationIdGoesFromNullToValue` has asserted that since the leg was
written. **One value: guarded on update, unjudged on insert.**

**REFUTED, and the refutation is why nothing was changed.** None of the eight globally-visible entities is
bound by any write endpoint (authority: `MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s reflection scan, 202 entity-bound
writes), and all four services that write those tables stamp from `TenantContext` on create. Making
`decideInsert` throw would be **F2-183's defect** — a constraint added while its writers are open: 169
legitimate global rows, tenant onboarding creating them off-request, and "null now, stamped a moment later"
is the ordinary shape of a service that builds an entity before stamping it. ⚠ **F2-182's rule is the whole
point: reachability is a fact about today, not a property of a control.** So the reason was corrected and the
property that makes it safe became a build failure.

⚠⚠ **THE BRANCH WAS TESTED, WHICH IS WORSE THAN UNTESTED — and my first draft of this finding claimed it had
no test.** `TenantWriteGuardInterceptorTest` covered it from the beginning (15 methods, not the 12 my
truncated `head -25` showed). But the test was **named for the false premise** —
`allowsAnInsertWithNoTenantOnTheRowAndLetsTheColumnComplain` — and its javadoc repeated the claim word for
word. Its assertion was correct; everything a reader uses to judge whether the branch is *right* was wrong.
🔑 **A green test whose NAME asserts the behaviour under review is the strongest possible reason not to look
further.** An untested branch at least reads as untested. F2-159's decoy and F2-175's rule in one artefact: a
test written by reading the implementation can only agree with it, and the agreement is hardest to see when
the description is accurate about the code and false about the world.

⚠⚠ **Two neighbouring classes described the control as not running.** `TenantContext`: *"The Hibernate
interceptor is not yet wired in — these are the building blocks…"*. `TenantWriteGuardConfig`: *"intentionally
not connected to the SessionFactory"*, a heading reading *"Feature flag — default OFF"*, and *"operators
should activate first in staging, watch the audit log … for a sprint, then flip to true in prod."* All three
stopped being true when F2-22b added `onSave` and enabled the flag; the dev log has printed
`[TenantWriteGuard] interceptor WIRED` on every boot since. 🔑 **A stale claim about whether a security
control RUNS is not a documentation nit — it is the input to somebody's next threat model**, and read
together the pair told a reader the backstop was unbuilt while it adjudicated every insert and update in both
environments.

**Gate — `TenantGuardNullExemptionContractTest` (4 legs).** The load-bearing one is a hard zero: **no write
endpoint may bind an entity whose rows can be platform-global**, with the population **derived from the
repositories** (an entity is global if some repository queries it with `organisationId IS NULL`) rather than
listed, so a ninth is covered the day its repository is written. Asserted **exactly**, not as a floor
(F2-204). Plus: the banned reason and the required one, and the wiring status checked against the profiles in
**both** directions — turn dev's flag off and the comments claiming it runs become false, and the build says so.

⚠ **My hand-written population was wrong and the gate corrected it on its first run** — I listed seven and
`HelpTopic` is the eighth. F2-213/F2-214's rule for the third time: **write the sweep as the gate, in the same
language, over the same tree.** A Python locator had already told me all 202 sites carry a stamp, which was
true but is not the same question.

⚠⚠ **Three instrument bugs of mine, each caught by running something.** (a) `unquoted()` applied to a whole
Java file **pairs a javadoc citation's quotes with a string literal's quotes** elsewhere in the file, leaving
the citation exposed — fixed by isolating `commentsOnly()` first. (b) A **phrase ban cannot tell an assertion
from a denial**: my own sentence *"would not be committing the NOT NULL violation the comment predicted"*
tripped the detector. F2-193's convention extends to denial — **cite the retired wording in quotes even when
you are refuting it**, because the alternative is a detector that has to parse negation. (c) A prose claim
**wraps across lines**, so a raw `contains` can only anchor on whichever fragment you picked, and the mutation
gutting the consequence survived *twice* before I asserted **flowed** javadoc text. A multi-line expected
string is not the fix either — this tree is CRLF and an embedded `\n` can never match (F2-212).

**Verification.** Backend **3,865/0/0**. Mutation **10/10 as expected, 0 anchor-miss** — 7 killed, **3
recorded as EQUIVALENT with measured reasons** rather than counted as holes (F2-206/F2-211: a surviving
mutant is a hole only if the mutated code is *wrong*; two of my first-round "survivors" were a mis-targeted
anchor and a 1-of-2-sites replacement, and one was an invalid mutation — **weakening an assertion always
passes**). Pre-fix control: both claim legs fire on master's text. **No migration, no endpoint change.**

⚠ **The live half is partial and says so.** The body-is-ignored leg was probed live (`controls` → org 1,
`departments` → 403); the NULL-is-global leg was verified at **SQL level with the repositories' own
predicate**, not through the API, because :8084 entered a state where every token it issues is rejected
(`WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`, curl agrees). That process is **not this session's** — my backend log stops at
13:04 and the listener was still serving at 16:47 — which is the recorded F2-74 hazard: **another session's
DevTools backend loads THIS tree's `target/classes`, so twelve `mvn -o test` runs hot-restarted it into my
working tree.** Not killed, deliberately.
⚙ **A probe-harness landmine worth carrying:** Python 3.14's `http.client` rejects this server's chunk
terminator and raises `IncompleteRead` **after buffering the whole payload** — `e.partial` held all 5,305
bytes curl reported. Reading the body inside the `with` and letting that escape discarded a healthy 200 and
reported the backend down for 180 s. 🔑 **A probe that cannot read a reply looks exactly like a server that
never sent one.**

**Filed.** The `organisationId` item F2-215 left open is **closed as measured-and-defended**, not as a fix.
Still open and untouched: the **83 entity-bound PUT handlers** (F2-22) that make this whole family
representable, and `MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s **184 TENANT-tier rows with an empty adjudication column** —
the 18 CRIT ones were F2-22b's work and the profile's own header says the adjudication column is the
authority, not the tier.

## F2-215 · An invariant generalised one field at a time covers exactly that field — eight of BaseEntity's nine were never widened

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-215 *(measured 2026-08-15. Lineage: [[F2-206]] → this, crossing the [[F2-198]]…[[F2-214]] line rather than continuing it. Chosen by asking what [[F2-206]]'s own artefact does NOT say: it is named `ServerOwnedIdentityModule`, it sits under a superclass that protects nine fields, and nothing anywhere states which of the nine it covers.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2, live and platform-wide.** Not P1: the three proven effects are forgery and namespace denial rather than destruction of existing data, and the sharpest destructive claim was **refuted**. But it is reachable on **170 of the 214 entity-bound write endpoints** across **102 entities**, and one of the three is the DF-3/DF-4 defect the platform has twice treated as an authority bypass. |
