All historical incidents are closed **and notifications dispatched**."* The empty state is reached by there being no OPEN breach; it knows nothing about whether SDAIA was ever notified, and for all 17 live breaches in both databases the answer is `NOT_REPORTED`. 🔑 **An empty state may report what it measured and must not vouch for what it did not look at.** Then the browser found two more: the clause citation rendered **`25(A)`** because the enclosing label is `text-transform: uppercase` — the Implementing Regulations cite sub-paragraphs in lower case, so a CSS rule was silently altering a regulatory reference — and the awareness timestamp rendered as the raw **`2026-08-14T12:21:45`** while every other date on the same screen was localised, on an Arabic-primary surface (house rule 7), in the field that starts the statutory clock. Plus a stale comment in `PrivacyPage` still describing *"the auto-generated SDAIA notification packet"*. **Fourth consecutive slice** where the browser finds a text- or presentation-level claim no code-scoped gate can see. |
| **⚠ Authorization: two gate mechanisms whose holder sets are disjoint** | Reading a breach is `hasPermission('PRIVACY','READ')`; recording the SDAIA submission is `hasAnyRole('DPO','CISO','PLATFORM_ADMIN')`. Measured in dev: `compliance` holds PRIVACY READ/WRITE/DELETE/EXPORT and is **403** on the record (verified live); `so_officer` **is** CISO and holds **no PRIVACY grant at all**, so it cannot read the breach. **No non-admin persona can both read a breach and record its notification**, and `DPO` — the role the guard names first — exists in `iam.roles` with **0 active holders**. CLAUDE.md's standing warning, on a statutory control. The probe's success leg is therefore `admin` and is **labelled as mechanism-only**, since PLATFORM_ADMIN bypasses in code. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-14** — `bad3df62`. `lib/pdplBreach.ts` rewritten (the generator, the packet type, `DEFAULT_CONTROLLER` and `addHours` gone; `ARTICLE_25_FIELDS`, `isSdaiaReported`, `isSdaiaSubmitted`, `severityIsProvisional`, `dataSubjectsDeadline` added); `PdplBreachConsole` loses `PacketPreview`, `downloadPacket`, the dispatch button and the `onDispatch` prop, gains `Article25Inventory` and the SDAIA status badge. Gates: `sdaiaNotificationProvenance.test.ts` (**15**) and `Article25FieldBackingContractTest` (**5**, the cross-codebase half per [[F2-193]]). **Backend 3842/0/0 · FE 729/729 + typecheck clean · mutation 17/17 killed with SHA-256-verified restore · 16/16 detectors fire on the pre-fix tree, 0 silent · live probe 27/27** as `compliance` and `viewer` (403 on the role-gated record, ACKNOWLEDGED terminal → 409, unknown state → 400, breach lifecycle status untouched by a SDAIA record), planting its own victim per [[F2-206]] and cleaning up — **17 live rows and 0 non-default SDAIA statuses afterwards, so no seeded row was touched.** Browser: the inventory, the `· provisional` band, the `NOT_REPORTED` badge, `25(a)`–`25(d)`, the localised timestamp, and a recorded row correctly **leaving** the urgent pool so a genuinely overdue real breach (+1675h, 999% of budget) took its place. **No migration.** |
| **Filed by this slice** | **(a) `privacy.data_breaches` has no `title_ar` and no `description_ar`** — a PDPL statutory register cannot be described in Arabic, the platform's primary language (house rule 7), and the console renders `titleEn` unconditionally. Needs a migration + entity + DTO. **(b) The breach `status` vocabulary is open**: 7 distinct values stored (CLOSED 4 / ESCALATED 2 / INVESTIGATED 2 / INVESTIGATING 2 / NOTIFIED 4 / OPEN 2 / REMEDIATED 1), **no CHECK on the table at all**, no declared machine, and two readers use *exclusion* lists over it — [[F2-196]]'s rule (open must be the complement of a declared terminal set) unapplied. `REMEDIATED` and `INVESTIGATED` are treated as open. **(c) `PrivacyBreachDto` declares `severity`, `occurredAt`, `reportedAt` and `affectedRecords`, and the wire carries a non-null value for NONE of them** (probed) — so `PrivacyPage`'s breach **Severity column** renders `—` for every row and its advanced **severity filter** can never match anything. [[F2-198]]'s `crossBorderTransfer` shape inverted: the client declares fields no column produces. **(d) `notifyDataOffice` sets `pdpcNotificationRequired = true` unconditionally**, overwriting the controller's own Article 25 determination of whether notification was required (8 of 17 rows currently say it was not). Defensible but undocumented. **(e) `DPO` has 0 holders** while guarding the statutory record path. **(f) The remaining minter population: 49 prefix sites in 24 files, 41 with browser entropy** — of which the **authority-owned** ones are the sharp bucket (`NCA-ACK-`, `NCA-AD-`, `SAMA-CTI-` in `lib/cyberLifecycle.ts`; `NCEMA-` in `CrisisManagementPage`; `SAMA-OPRES-` in `BcmLifecyclePage`), all on surfaces [[F2-205]] already filed as unbacked authority-packet emitters. 🔑 **A reference only an outside authority can issue is not a reference the server may mint either — it is received and recorded, or it is absent.** |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **Ask what an emitted document ASSERTS that no column records — per field, not per file.** A provenance rule that asks whether a page talks to a server ([[F2-198]]), whether it emits a document ([[F2-199]]), or which of its data reaches what it emits ([[F2-203]]) all pass a **hybrid** artefact, where real server fields sit beside invented ones and lend them credibility. And the second, independent lesson: **when a screen asks a statutory question, check it is reading the column the server keeps the answer in** — here the right column, the right predicate and the right comment were all present in the same file, 200 lines from the code that ignored them, and the consequence was that the four breaches furthest past a 72-hour deadline were the four the console would never show.

## F2-208 · The CAPA register merged twenty invented rows into fourteen real ones, and advanced them — including the independent sign-off — in localStorage

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-208 *(measured 2026-08-13. Lineage: [[F2-194]] → [[F2-198]] → [[F2-201]] → [[F2-202]] → [[F2-204]] → [[F2-205]] → [[F2-207]] → this. Chosen by re-measuring [[F2-207]]'s filed item (b), the 14 browser-side reference minters, which pointed at `CapaPage`'s `CAPA-<year>-PA-<Math.random>` and from there at the register behind it.)* |
| **Severity** | **P1 for the trail, P2 for the register.** No row is lost — the fourteen real CAPAs are read on every render — but an operator advancing a corrective action through owner test, independent test and **audit sign-off** wrote nothing to the server, while the screen and a reload both said the sign-off had happened. An ISO 9001 §10.2 / IIA IPPF 2500 reviewer asks *"was the fix verified, by whom, and when?"*; for any CAPA advanced through this screen the register's answer was blank and the screen's answer was invented. |
| **The three sources `useCapas()` merged** | `GET /api/capa/tasks` (**14 live rows, identical in dev and prod**, probed as `compliance`); `CAPAS`, a **507-line corpus of twenty invented CAPAs** in `lib/capa.ts` with eleven invented owner mailboxes at the real company domain; and a `localStorage` overlay (`grc.capas`) of `added` rows and per-row `patches`. The register therefore showed **34 rows where 14 exist**, with nothing on the row distinguishing them. Two of the corpus rows carry `auditSignedOffBy: 'audit.lead@tss.sa'` — an invented auditor recorded as having signed off remediation. **Eighth, ninth and tenth invented officers** in this programme after [[F2-201]]'s 16-deep registry, [[F2-203]]'s three, [[F2-204]]'s CRO and [[F2-207]]'s five; and part of the 65-name cast [[F2-207]] filed. |
| **⚠⚠ The patches were applied on top of the SERVER's rows** | `items` was assembled as `[...apiRows, ...seedNotInApi].map(c => overlay.patches[c.id] ? { ...c, ...overlay.patches[c.id] } : c)`. So `advance()` on a **real** CAPA wrote a patch keyed on its real `external_id`, and every subsequent render showed the patched status for a record the server had never been told about. This is the inverse of [[F2-201]]: there the fabricated page had no server data at all, so the two never met; here they are interleaved in one list and the operator cannot tell which rows a regulator would see. |
| **🔑 Why it outlived [[F2-201]]: a localStorage overlay is DURABLE** | [[F2-201]]'s fabricated approvals reverted on refresh, which is part of what eventually gave it away. Here the reload that should expose the fabrication **confirms** it. The reusable form: **when a fake write survives a reload, the cheapest test a user knows becomes evidence for the defect.** |
| **⚠⚠ The vocabulary was the tell, and nothing compared the two** | The client declared **eight** states (IDENTIFIED / IMPLEMENTING / OWNER_TESTED / INDEPENDENT_TESTED / AUDIT_SIGNED_OFF / CLOSED / VERIFICATION_FAILED / CANCELLED) against `CapaTaskService.ALLOWED`'s **five** (OPEN / IN_PROGRESS / AWAITING_VERIFICATION / CLOSED / CANCELLED). `fromCapaTaskDto`'s `STATUS_MAP` had **no source status** for three of them, so OWNER_TESTED, AUDIT_SIGNED_OFF and VERIFICATION_FAILED were producible **only by a local write**. 🔑 **A state only the browser can reach is a state only the browser knows about** — and two of those three are the owner test and the independent sign-off, i.e. exactly the gates the module exists to evidence. ([[F2-193]] had already noted `VERIFICATION_FAILED` appears in no Java source, as a connector-catalogue detail; nobody had asked what that implied about the register.) |
| **⚠⚠ REWIRE, not retire — and the server side was already HARDENED** | `POST /api/capa/tasks/{id}/transition` existed the whole time, refuses an illegal edge with **409**, and stamps `verified_by` **from the authenticated principal**: `TransitionRequest` had `verifiedBy` **removed** at F2-22b(vi) with a comment saying a caller-supplied verifier is the defect. So this is [[F2-201]]'s shape — a finished, hardened control with a client that shadowed it — and the **second** member of that population to be rewired rather than retired. `capaTaskApi` had only `counts` and `list`. |
| **⚠ Deliberately SIMPLER than what it replaced, and gated to stay so** | Eight states collapse to five; eight fields go. [[F2-207]]'s question — *diff the client's tokens against the column before choosing rewire over retire* — has the opposite answer here: the tokens are not **refused**, the server's machine is **coarser**. So the honest move is to drive the five and stop advertising eight, which is the judgement [[F2-201]] made when a fabricated approver chain met a server carrying one assignee. 🔑 **[[F2-199]]'s rule twice more: a fabrication more granular than the platform's own model is what makes it look more finished.** |
| **⚠ The eight deleted fields have no column ANYWHERE — read from `sys.columns`, not inferred** | `capa.tasks` has **26 columns** and none for `rcaMethod` / `rcaSteps` / `rootCause` / `rootCauseCategory` (the RCA tab and the Pareto tab), `effectivenessDueDate` / `effectivenessVerified*` (the 90-day re-test), `parentCapaId` (recurrence chains), `customerDisclosureRequired` / `customerDisclosureDate` (21 CFR §820.100), `frameworkRefs`, `ownerTest*` / `independentTest*` / `auditSignedOffBy`, or the local event `history`. Capturing any of them needs a migration and a product decision; keeping them as client state was the defect, and inventing values to fill the gaps would have been [[F2-196]]'s. |
| **⚠⚠ Deleting the invented figures would have ASSERTED HEALTH — four digest figures removed rather than zeroed** | `audCommitteeDigest` reported `verificationFailed`, `recurrent`, `customerDisclosures` and `topRootCauses`, all derived from columnless fields, each rendered `tone={x > 0 ? 'danger' : 'success'}`. Keeping them after the corpus was gone would have shown an audit committee **"verification failures: 0 · recurrent: 0 · top root causes: none"** in green — [[F2-197]]'s rule exactly: *an invented figure invites a question, an invented all-clear closes one.* They are gone; the seven that remain are counts over real columns, plus an `undatedRows` disclosure so a short denominator cannot hide. Also deleted: `RECIPIENT_FOR_KIND`, which mapped each signal to an invented mailbox under the field name *"suggested recipient"* while nothing in the platform delivers a CAPA notification ([[F2-38]](d)) — a recipient nothing sends to is a claim with no source ([[F2-193]]). |
| **⚠⚠ `lib/paTriggers.ts` DELETED, because wiring the register would have made it dangerous** | It derived *"a KRI has breached — file a preventive action"* from `pages/risk/mockRisks` (`KRIS`, `KRI_TRENDS_BY_ID`, `MOCK_RISKS`) and offered a one-click **"Open PA"** that called `create`. With `create` wired that becomes a **real row in `capa.tasks`** whose `originId` points at a mock KRI and whose description quotes an invented breach. 🔑 **A real write driven by a fabricated signal is worse than a fake write driven by one** — so the trigger engine went, and the capability (PA suggestions over the real KRI register) is filed. |
| **⚠ No `create` wrapper was added, on purpose** | The nearly-shipped version had one, whose **only** caller was that modal. `POST /api/capa/tasks` stays clientless: this register is filled by the intake substrate (DD-76 — a `CONTROL_OBSERVATION` submission triages into a **finding**) and by other modules' automation — the four non-seeded rows carry `origin_type` `rca` and `processor_assessment`. [[F2-207]]'s rule: **an unused client method should not ship.** ⚙ `BASELINE_CLIENTLESS_GUARDED_WRITES` therefore drops by exactly **1** (199 → 198), and the comment at that constant now records that wiring the create would be the *wrong* kind of progress. |
| **⚠ THREE real columns the client never read — [[F2-198]]'s `crossBorderTransfer` shape** | `progress_notes_en` (7/14 rows), `progress_notes_ar` (7/14) and `evidence_refs` (10/14) were populated and on the wire, and the client's own type never mentioned them. Restored. And a fourth the **server** never declared: `created_at` is NOT NULL and populated on all 14 rows, but `CapaTaskDto` did not expose it, so a CAPA's age was computed from `startedAt ?? targetDate` — i.e. from when work began or, failing that, from its own deadline, meaning an unstarted CAPA could never be old. Now on the wire and read-only in effect. |
| **⚠ `CapaTaskService.TERMINAL` was a second hand-written list** | `List.of("CLOSED", "CANCELLED")` beside an `ALLOWED` table that did not contain those keys — and it feeds the `open` and `overdue` queries, so a drift would have silently dropped a state from the overdue sweep. [[F2-196]]'s defect on the CAPA clock; [[F2-205]] made the identical conversion in `VulnerabilityService`. `ALLOWED` now carries all five states (terminals with empty edge sets) and `TERMINAL` is derived from it, which is also what makes the FE↔BE parity a straight key-set comparison. |
| **⚠ F2-172(d)'s EIGHTH through THIRTEENTH instances, swept rather than drip-fed** | Grepping `req.getId() != null ?` — which CLAUDE.md instructs and which was four-for-four — returned **six live sites**: `bcm_lc/InvocationService` (a BCP invocation raised *during* a crisis), `board_pack/BoardPackService` (the papers a board resolution was taken on), `capa/CapaTaskService`, `knowledge/KbArticleService`, **`nca_ecc/NcaEccFilingService`** (the NCA ECC self-assessment return) and `regchange/RegulatoryChangeService`. 🔑 **Six survivors after seven one-at-a-time fixes is not bad luck, it is what fixing instances of a shape produces** — so all six are closed in one commit and `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest` holds the shape at zero. |
| **⚠⚠ And the grep everyone has been running cannot see the whole family** | `req.getId() != null ?` is one **spelling**. Across all **48** `setExternalId(`/`setRefNumber(` sites the caller's value also reaches a column as `req.externalId()` (a record accessor — no `get`, no null test) and `in.getExternalId()` (an entity bound straight from the body). [[F2-192]]'s headline turned on CLAUDE.md's own instruction. The gate is therefore written on the **defect's signature** — a null-coalesce on a reference setter inside a `create*` method — not on a spelling. ⚙ Having widened the net, **all five caller-derived sites outside create paths were refuted by reading**: each carries an upstream system's identifier (a SIEM event id used as the dedup key one line above, a Splunk alert id from an inbound webhook, a scanner finding id, a threat-intel advisory id). They are named in `UPSTREAM_OWNED` with a reason each, asserted in both directions. |
| **⚠ `NcaEccFilingService`'s constant `-001` suffix was left alone, deliberately** | `String.format("NCA-%d-001", fiscalYear)` would be [[F2-48]]'s collision bug on any other table. It is correct there **only** because `uk_ncaecc_year` is UNIQUE on `(organisation_id, fiscal_year)`, so a tenant can hold at most one filing per year. Checked against `sys.indexes` rather than assumed, and recorded at the call site because the gate is hermetic and cannot see an index. ⚙ Separately worth knowing: all four stored filing references read `NCA-ECC-<year>`, a format the generator does not produce — they come from `seed_real_data.py` and V122, so the API path was **latent** on that register rather than exercised. |
| **⚠⚠ MY OWN DETECTOR WAS SILENT ON THE DEFECT IT WAS WRITTEN FOR, and only the pre-fix control said so** | The load-bearing leg's first draft banned `{ ...c, status: to }`. The real code built `{ ...existingPatch, ...stampField, ...(extra ?? {}), status: to, history: [...] }` — **three spreads between the brace and the property** — so a pattern demanding them adjacent could not see it. 🔑 **A detector written for the shape you imagine rather than the shape that existed reads exactly like a passing gate.** Rewritten as *no status value may reach a React state setter*, walking each setter's brace-balanced argument. ⚠⚠ **And banning a word was still not enough**: the mutation harness showed `setItems(prev => prev.map(c => c.id === id ? { ...c, ...body } : c))` **SURVIVING** it, because a spread carries the status without naming it. The final leg asserts the **positive** — every write to register state must be the server's row (`saved` / `fromCapaTaskDto`) or an explicit clear. There is no third legitimate source. |
| **⚠⚠ A `\b` written into a bash heredoc becomes a literal BACKSPACE (0x08), and the regex can then never match** | The pre-fix control reported 12/13 with the state-setter detector SILENT; the same regex run standalone found the defect immediately. The bytes were `r'\x08set[A-Z]…'`. 🔑 **A regex that cannot match reads exactly like "the code is clean", and this failure mode is invisible in the source listing** — the escape looks right on screen. Direction: it **under**-reports, the dangerous way. Author scan scripts with a file write, never a heredoc; and this is the reason the control exists at all. |
| **⚠ Two of sixteen mutations "survived", and both were the harness's fault** | Those two legs are asserted by the **backend** cross-codebase gate (`CapaMachineParityTest` reads `lib/capa.ts`), and I had classified the mutations by the **file they touch** rather than by the gate that asserts them, so the frontend runner was asked a question only the backend runner can answer. 🔑 **Classify a mutation by the assertion that should catch it, not by the file it edits** — a cross-codebase gate breaks the usual correspondence. Re-run correctly: **16/16 killed.** |
| **⚠⚠ FOUND IN THE BROWSER, AFTER EVERY GATE WAS GREEN — twice** | (a) `capaPageSub` still promised *"Every action with a documented root cause, verification gates, and effectiveness check"*: two of those three have no column. [[F2-205]]/[[F2-207]]'s lesson, **third consecutive instance** — a claim about what a surface does lives wherever a user reads text. Caught by a new gate leg over the `capa*` keys, which fired on **three** strings I had not fixed (`capaPageSub`, `capaSearchPh`, `capaFilterModalHint`). (b) Three **Arabic** digest labels named a STATE where the predicate counts a PERIOD — `capaCommitteeOpened` rendered *"مفتوحة"* (open) for `createdAt ∈ quarter`, and `capaCommitteePreventive` *"وقائية مفتوحة"* for preventive actions **raised** in the quarter. The English carried the past tense and the Arabic did not; in an Arabic-primary UI (house rule 7) that is the primary reading. 🔑 **[[F2-196]]'s label-versus-predicate question applies per language, not per key.** |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-13** — backend sweep + gate `7ff7c810`, the rewire `e75d50bf`. `lib/paTriggers.ts` deleted (215 lines); `lib/capa.ts` 1,008 → 386; `CapaPage` 921 → 566; `CapaDetailPage` 367 → 283; `capaNotifications` 239 → 195; **net −1,320 lines**, 70 dead translation keys removed and 24 added in both languages. Gates: `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest` (4 legs incl. a synthetic positive control), `CapaMachineParityTest` (5), `capaRegisterServerBacked.test.ts` (10). **Backend 3837/0/0, FE 714/714 + typecheck clean, mutation 16/16 with SHA-256-verified restore, 13/13 detectors fire on the pre-fix tree as a control, live probe 23/23 as `compliance` and `viewer`** — and a transition driven from the **browser** landed in SQL Server with two `platform.audit_log` rows and `verified_by = 'compliance'`. Two `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows planted by the probe remain (house rule 6). **No migration.** |
| **Filed by this slice** | **(a) FIVE CAPA-ish registers, 78 rows, five disjoint status vocabularies**, identical dev/prod: `capa.tasks` 14 (OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/AWAITING_VERIFICATION/CLOSED/CANCELLED), `audit_lc.capa_tasks` 12 (IN_PROGRESS/OPEN/**VERIFIED**), `bcm.corrective_actions` 10 (OPEN/ASSIGNED/IN_PROGRESS/UNDER_REVIEW), `ndi.corrective_action` 17 (IN_PROGRESS/NOT_STARTED), `sust.corrective_action` 25 (OPEN/IN_PROGRESS/COMPLETED/VERIFIED). [[F2-196]]'s shape at five tables for one concept, and [[F2-203]] already filed the `audit_lc` half. Which is canonical is an owner decision. **(b) The whole `capa` schema has ZERO CHECK constraints**, so `status` and `severity` are narrowed only by the DTO's `@Pattern` (status) and by nothing at all (severity) — [[F2-183]]'s rule applies: a CHECK and its writer land together. **(c) `/capa`'s primary button opened the intake form for a control observation, which lands in a DIFFERENT register** — the label now says what it does, but the register still has no create path from any screen. **(d) PA suggestions over the real KRI register**, the capability the deleted trigger engine faked; the KRI API exists, `mockRisks` is the blocker. **(e)** The remaining members of [[F2-207]]'s two populations: 13 browser-side reference minters (one closed here) and the 65-name invented cast (three mailboxes closed here). |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **When a browser store and a real register are MERGED rather than alternatives, the fabrication is not a shadow — it is camouflage, and the reload test recruits the user into confirming it.** The corollary for choosing rewire over retire: [[F2-207]] asks whether the client's tokens are *refused* by the column, and this adds the other case — when the server's machine is merely **coarser**, rewire and delete the extra granularity, because the granularity is what made the fabrication look more finished than the real thing. And the sharpest instrument lesson: **a detector written for the shape you imagine rather than the shape that existed is silent, and silence is indistinguishable from clean** — which is why every detector here was run against `git show master:` before being trusted.

## F2-207 · Three PDPL statutory registers are kept in localStorage beside three complete server-backed surfaces that already exist

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-207 *(filed by [[F2-206]] 2026-08-13, which found it while measuring the privacy module; spec written the same day because the register is what an external auditor is handed and a finding recorded only in the plan disappears when the plan is superseded — [[F2-200]]'s precedent.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2.** No governance decision is silently discarded the way [[F2-201]]'s and [[F2-204]]'s were — but the platform shows a Data Protection Officer an editable ROPA, DPIA and cross-border register that the register a regulator would be shown knows nothing about, and it attributes signed statutory assessments to people who do not exist. |
| **The three stores** | `lib/privacyLifecycle.ts` keeps `SEED_ROPA` / `SEED_DPIA` / `SEED_CBT` in `localStorage` (`grc.privacy.ropa.v1`, `…dpia.v1`, `…cbt.v1`) and `PrivacyLifecyclePage` renders and mutates them. Real registers, measured 2026-08-13 in dev and prod: `privacy.processing_activities` **11 rows** (PDPL Art. 31), `privacy.dpia` **6 dev / 5 prod** (Art. 25), `privacy.cross_border_transfers` **9 rows** (Art. 29). The `privacy_lc` twins hold **0 rows** in both databases, so wiring to `privacy_lc` would show an empty register. |
| **⚠⚠ Retire, do NOT rewire — all three real surfaces already exist and are complete** | `/privacy?tab=ropa` renders `privacyApi.ropa()` and `RopaWizard` creates through `privacyApi.createRopa`; `/privacy?tab=dpia` renders `dpiaApi.list()` and drives **all four** workflow transitions (`submit-for-review` / `approve` / `reject` / `expire`); `/pdpl-extensions?tab=cbt` renders `listCrossBorderTransfers()` with `cbtAssess`/`cbtApprove`/`cbtReject` and **already declares the server's vocabulary correctly**. So this is ADR-017 §D-5, the answer [[F2-42]], [[F2-198]] and [[F2-199]] each reached — a second *real* surface for one statutory object would be [[F2-196]]'s own defect. |
| **⚠⚠ `lib/privacyLifecycle.ts` and `lib/pdplExtensions.ts` declare `CrossBorderTransfer` and `CbtStatus` under the SAME TYPE NAMES** | One is the real API client, one is invented, and the invented one has `adequacy`/`safeguard`/`preRiskScore` where the real one has `transferMechanism`/`residencyCheckOutcome`. A reader importing `CrossBorderTransfer` gets whichever file they happened to import from and **TypeScript cannot warn, because both are valid types.** [[F2-201]] recorded this shape ("the browser copy used the same type name as the server entity"); this is a second instance, in the same statutory module. |
| **The measured vocabulary divergence** | `CbtStatus` = `DRAFT\|ASSESSING\|APPROVED\|BLOCKED\|PERIODIC_REVIEW`, and **`CK_cbt_status` admits only `REQUESTED\|ASSESSED\|APPROVED\|REJECTED\|EXPIRED`** — so **4 of the 5 browser tokens are refused by a CHECK constraint**, and 6 of the 9 live rows carry a status no browser artefact can name. `SafeguardMechanism` = `NONE_NEEDED\|STANDARD_CLAUSES\|BINDING_CORPORATE_RULES\|CERTIFICATION\|EXPLICIT_CONSENT` against `CK_cbt_mechanism`'s `PUBLIC_INTEREST\|VITAL_INTEREST\|CONTRACT_NECESSITY\|EXPLICIT_CONSENT\|BCR\|SCC\|ADEQUACY` — again **4 of 5 refused, and three of those are the same concept under a different spelling** (`STANDARD_CLAUSES`/`SCC`, `BINDING_CORPORATE_RULES`/`BCR`, `NONE_NEEDED`/`ADEQUACY`), which is [[F2-180]]'s *"being right about what a state means is not evidence about what the column stores it in"*. `RopaStatus`'s four tokens match **none** of the 11 stored rows (`ACTIVE` 10, `UNDER_REVIEW` 1). `DpiaStatus` invents `RISK_ASSESSMENT` and `CONSULTATION` (0 rows) and lacks the server's `IN_REVIEW` and `EXPIRED`. 🔑 **A naive rewire would therefore convert today's silently-local writes into CHECK violations** — [[F2-183]]'s rule, and the reason this is a retirement. |
| **⚠ Five invented officers, one of them signing a statutory assessment** | `'Layla Al-Ghamdi (DPO)'` appears as the organisation's Data Protection Officer on two ROPA records **and as `dpoSignedBy` on the Article 25 DPIA**; `'Salman Al-Dossari (CHRO)'` and `'Hessa Al-Rasheed (Head of Marketing)'` own records; `'Khalid Al-Falih (Audit Committee Chair) + DPO'` approved one; and the ROPA approve handler passes the literal **`'DPO + CRO'`**. Fifth, sixth and seventh invented officers in this programme after [[F2-201]]'s 16-deep registry, [[F2-203]]'s three and [[F2-204]]'s CRO. The `SEED_CBT` row also names **Mixpanel**, a real company, as receiving Saudi personal data under standard contractual clauses. |
| **⚠ Client-side minters to delete, not move** | `createDpia` mints `DPIA-<year>-<4 base-36 chars of Math.random()>` as the reference for an Article 25 assessment — [[F2-172]](d)'s shape, and [[F2-202]]'s DSR minter had three digits of entropy. `upgradeCbtSafeguard` **invents the residual-risk arithmetic** (`BCR → −4`, `CERTIFICATION → −3`, `SCC → −2`, floor of 2), i.e. a PDPL Article 29 risk score computed from a hard-coded table in a browser. `ADEQUACY_BY_COUNTRY` classifies Iran and Syria as `PROHIBITED` and the US/Singapore/India/Canada/Australia as `NOT_ADEQUATE` under a comment that calls itself *"illustrative — actual list maintained by SDAIA"*: a regulatory determination presented as platform data. Note the server's `destination_country` is `@Size(max = 3)` and holds ISO alpha-3 (`USA`, `GBR`, `IRL`, `NLD`, `DEU`, `IND`), so the browser's full country names would be refused anyway. |
| **⚠ What the real CBT register contains, for scale** | 9 transfers naming AWS, Workday (Dublin), Stripe Payments Europe, HubSpot Germany, OpenAI (azure-eastus), TCS payroll BPO and Dow Jones — with a real rejection reason on the OpenAI row explaining that its sub-processor list chains a second cross-border hop without subject re-consent. The browser shows **one** transfer, to Mixpanel, approved by an invented DPO. 🔑 **The fabrication is smaller and less useful than the register it hides**, which is the opposite of [[F2-199]]'s pattern and worth noting when judging what "looks finished" means. |
| **⚠ One real row cannot be advanced by any route** | `privacy.dpia` holds a row with `status = 'UNDER_REVIEW'`, which `DpiaService`'s machine does not declare: `submitForReview` requires `DRAFT`, `approve` requires `IN_REVIEW`, `expire` requires `APPROVED` — so all three throw. Identical in dev and prod. [[F2-203]]'s `audit_lc` shape on a PDPL register. It is a **synonym** of `IN_REVIEW`, so collapsing it rewrites a live row in two databases and is an owner decision ([[F2-183]]/[[F2-196]]'s rule), not a side effect of a display fix. |
| **What must NOT happen** | Wiring `saveRopa`/`transitionDpia`/`transitionCbt` to the real endpoints as they stand. The invented `dpoSignedBy` and `'DPO + CRO'` would be **persisted** as a real officer's sign-off on a statutory assessment — exactly the trap [[F2-204]] caught one commit before shipping — and the out-of-vocabulary status tokens would become CHECK violations. Retire the three tabs, delete the corpora and the minters, and point at the surfaces that exist. |
| **⚠ CORRECTION to this filing's own measurement** | The spec above said the real cross-border surface is `/pdpl-extensions?tab=cbt`. **It is `/data-lifecycle?tab=cbt`** — `/pdpl-extensions` is a `<Navigate to="/data-lifecycle" replace />`, and React Router does **not** carry the search string across a redirect, so a link written that way arrives with no `?tab` at all. It *looked* correct only because that page's default tab happens to be `cbt`. Caught by the new tab-link gate on the link **this slice itself had just written**, which is [[F2-202]]'s rule one layer out: **a plausible path string is worth nothing until something resolves it.** Fifth guessed-path error in this lineage. |
| **⚠⚠ FOUND IN THE BROWSER, AFTER EVERY GATE WAS GREEN: the page header still advertised the three registers it no longer had** | `prcEyebrow` read *"Privacy · PDPL Article 22 / 25 / 29 / 4"* and `prcPageSub` described *"ROPA Article 22 register, DPIA Article 25 high-risk assessment, Article 29 cross-border transfer adequacy"*. 🔑 **[[F2-205]]'s lesson, second instance: a claim about what a surface DOES can live anywhere a user reads text, and a gate scoped to code cannot see the place written specifically to be read.** Retiring a tab means retiring the sentence that advertised it. ⚠ It also carried a wrong citation — **four places said ROPA was PDPL "Article 22"** while every other citation in the tree says **Article 31**, including `lib/moduleAnchors.ts`, the regulator-citation catalogue W2-1a-i deliberately keeps, whose row reads `PDPL / Article 31 / "Records of processing activities."` So the correction follows the codebase's settled convention rather than adjudicating Saudi law. Gated, scoped to the `prc*` keys. |
| **⚠⚠ AN ADJACENT DEFECT CLASS CLOSED WITH IT: a `?tab=` link that lands on a page ignoring `?tab`** | Three KPI tiles here linked `to="?tab=dsr"` while the page held its tab in `useState` and never read the query string — so each tile navigated, re-mounted the page on the PIPELINE tab, and read to an operator as a control that does nothing. This is [[F2-197]]'s rule one step earlier: there a tile's **figure** disagreed with the list it opened, here the **navigation itself** is the false claim, and it is worse in one respect — a wrong figure invites a question, a link that silently lands elsewhere reads as the reader's own mistake. ⚠⚠ **My first detector reported a population of 1 and that was wrong**: it only matched RELATIVE (`to="?tab=x"`) links, the shape I had just found. Resolving every link to its **target page** instead gave **5 links across 3 pages, of 22 total** — `AuditWorkspacePage` links its own absolute path, and `SocOpsEventsPage` links `/cyber?tab=incidents` to a `CyberPage` that also ignored it. 🔑 **Scoping a detector to the shape that produced the finding reports a smaller population, which reads exactly like "the rest are fine."** All three fixed, so `tabLinkTargets.test.ts` ships as a **hard zero with no exemption map**. ⚙ `AuditWorkspacePage`'s link was **deleted, not honoured**: `WsTabId` never had an `engagements` member, so there was no tab to open, and the list behind it is the fabricated `AUDIT_ENGAGEMENTS` corpus [[F2-203]] filed — building a tab over invented rows is the defect, not the fix. |
| **⚠⚠ TWO OF MY OWN GATE LEGS FIRED ON CORRECT, PRE-EXISTING CODE, and measuring what they caught produced two populations far larger than this slice** | Both are **filed**, and both are why those legs are scoped to the privacy surface rather than app-wide ([[F2-192]]'s rule). **(a) 65 distinct invented person-names across 39 product files.** The five officers on the retired PDPL tabs are not this page's invention — they are a SHARED CAST, deepest in `lib/userDirectory.ts` (18) and `lib/crisis.ts` (16), and also in `lib/assets.ts`, `lib/bcmLifecycle.ts`, `lib/regulatoryChange.ts`, `lib/monitoring.ts`, `lib/approvalChains.ts`, `lib/auditCommittee.ts`, `lib/cyberLifecycle.ts`, `lib/policyLifecycle.ts`, `lib/auditors.ts`, `lib/vendorPortal.ts`. ⚠ **Most of those files are NOT named `mock*`**, so the population sits largely outside the de-mocking boundary [[F2-194]] measured — the same blind spot one level up. **(b) 14 client-side business-reference minters in 12 files**, entropy from `Math.random`: `NCA-ACK-…` and `SAMA-CTI-…` (regulator-facing acknowledgements), `WP-…` (IIA working papers), `CAPA-…`, `ACC-…` (risk acceptances), `INV-…`, `IR-…`, `SOC-…`, `KRI-BR-…`. [[F2-172]](d)'s rule — only the server may issue a business reference — has been applied one instance at a time ([[F2-202]]'s DSR minter, [[F2-203]]'s finding refs) with nobody measuring the frontend population. 🔑 **A gate that fails on code the slice did not touch is a gate nobody can keep green** — so the honest move is to scope the assertion and file the measurement. |
| **⚠ A THIRD leg I wrote, ran and DELETED, because the deletion is the finding** | It asserted *"every page that reads `?tab` narrows it to a declared tab"* — which is TRUE; I checked all 12 by reading them. The detector flagged `ChangesPage`, `CompliancePage` and `EsgPage`, **3 for 3 false positives**, because each narrows it differently (`TAB_IDS.includes(…)`, `isTabId(…)`, `isEsgTab(…)`, `VALID_TABS.includes(…)`). "Is this value narrowed before use?" is a dataflow question a regex cannot answer ([[F2-182]]). 🔑 **A gate that fails on correct code is worse than no gate: it trains the next reader to edit the assertion rather than the code.** The claim is recorded in prose instead. |
| **⚠ Two more of my own detector bugs, both already named in CLAUDE.md** | (a) The dead-translation-key scan **did not strip comments**, and the page's new header comment EXPLAINS the retirement by naming the four KPI keys it deleted — so `prcKpiRopa`/`prcKpiCbt`/`prcKpiCbtBlocked`/`prcKpiDpiaHighRisk` were reported as still in use. [[F2-202]]/[[F2-205]]'s *"prose about code, stored as data, invents callers in a token scan"* — the 9th instance here. ⚙ Note the direction: comment-blind **under**-reports dead keys, so it fails safe for a delete. (b) The key regex missed QUOTED keys, so `'prcCbtTrigger Review'` — declared with a literal space in **both** dictionaries — read as never declared, which would have looked like *"a button labelled with a raw key."* It was not; both dictionaries agree on that odd name. Final count: **52 dead keys removed, 8 added, 0 undeclared references** — and `prcKpiAvgDays` was already dead before this slice. |
| **⚠ Both ratchets were ALREADY ONE ABOVE THE TRUTH before this slice touched them** | [[F2-204]] set `BASELINE_BROWSER_LOCAL_STORES` and `BASELINE_ENDPOINT_BEARING_NOT_WIRED` to 6 correctly; [[F2-205]] then wired `cyber-vulnerabilities` (BROWSER_LOCAL → SERVER_BACKED) and **lowered neither**, so each ceiling silently tolerated one store that no longer existed. 🔑 **CLAUDE.md house rule 3's warning arriving from the inside: a ceiling left in place after a sweep makes a tolerated member indistinguishable from a reviewed one.** Now **2 / 2**, each the number its own detector returns, with `DECLARED_CORPORA` **18 → 15** asserted exactly. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-13** — `81eeee93`, merged to master and pushed. `lib/privacyLifecycle.ts` deleted (511 lines); the ROPA/DPIA/CBT tabs, their four KPI tiles, 28 CSS rules and 52 translation keys removed; a count-free pointer card links the three real surfaces; `CyberPage` and this page derive `tab` from the URL; `AuditWorkspacePage`'s dead link deleted. Gates: `privacyRegisterRetirement.test.ts` (11 legs), `tabLinkTargets.test.ts` (6, hard zero), `LifecycleStoreBackingContractTest` server-side. **FE 704/704 + typecheck clean, backend 3828/0/0, mutation 15/15 with byte-verified restore, 13/13 detectors fire on the pre-fix tree, live probe 20/20 as `compliance`, browser-verified on all five affected surfaces. No migration, no backend behaviour change.** |
| **Filed by this slice** | (a) the 65-name invented-officer cast across 39 files; (b) the 14 browser-side reference minters; (c) `privacy.processing_activities.transfer_mechanism` holds `DATA_OFFICE_APPROVAL` under **no CHECK at all**, a token `CK_cbt_mechanism` on the sibling table would refuse — [[F2-196]]'s disjoint-vocabulary shape across two tables for one concept; (d) `privacy.dpia` still holds one `UNDER_REVIEW` row that no route can advance ([[F2-206]]'s filing, re-confirmed live). |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **When a browser-local store shadows a real register, ask whether a real SURFACE for it already exists before writing a client — the answer here was yes three times out of three**, and each of those surfaces was more complete than the fabrication. And a corollary for type safety: **two files declaring the same type name, one real and one invented, is a divergence the compiler cannot see** — the second recorded instance after [[F2-201]].

## F2-206 · A create endpoint answered 201 Created while overwriting a PDPL Article 31 record, and the ratchet built for that defect had been green for a year

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-206 *(measured 2026-08-13. Lineage: [[F2-22a]] → [[F2-172]] → [[F2-202]] → [[F2-203]] → [[F2-204]] → [[F2-205]] → this. Found while measuring the privacy module for the ROPA/DPIA/cross-border rewire, which is now filed as F2-207.)* |
| **Severity** | **P1.** Any caller holding `PRIVACY:WRITE` could silently destroy any processing-activity, DSR or breach record in their own tenant through the endpoint that creates them — and be told the record had been *created*. It is a data-integrity defect on three PDPL statutory registers, not a display defect. |
| **The defect, probed live** | `POST /api/v1/privacy/ropa` with `{"id": <n>, …}` answers **HTTP 201 Created** and **overwrites** processing activity `n`. `CrudRepository#save` calls `merge()` rather than `persist()` when the id is non-null, so the "create" retargets the row the body names, and every column the body omits is written as **NULL**. Measured on a planted record: `activity_name_ar` → NULL, `purpose_en` → NULL, `retention_period_months` 84 → NULL, `data_categories_json` `'["HEALTH","BIOMETRIC"]'` → NULL, PDPL Article 5 lawful basis `LEGAL_OBLIGATION` → `CONSENT`, and `special_category_flag` TRUE → FALSE — **the flag that makes the activity Article 25 high-risk in the first place.** On `POST /dsrs` the same shape turned an `ERASURE` request into `ACCESS` and nulled the data subject's email: a PDPL Article 4 erasure request silently reclassified. Probed as `compliance` (GRC_ADMINISTRATOR), never `admin`. |
| **⚠ Cross-tenant reach: REFUTED** | Naming another organisation's row id answers **500** and changes nothing — the tenant boundary holds. This matters because `DpiaService.create`'s own comment warns about `merge()` "into a potentially cross-tenant row", and that is the half that is *not* reachable. 🔑 **The comment recording the risk named the wrong half of it**, and the half that was live — destruction of your own tenant's records, reported as 201 Created — is not what it warns about, which is a plausible reason a reader of `createRopa` never saw the need to copy the mitigation. |
| **⚠⚠ THE REUSABLE FINDING: the gate for this exact defect existed and was green** | `MassAssignmentRatchetTest` has asserted `id must not bind — a create could retarget an existing row` since F2-22a, in those words. It is not wrong. It proves the claim through **`class Probe extends BaseEntity`**, and `BaseEntity` does carry `@JsonProperty(access = READ_ONLY)` on `id`. Measured by reflection: **174 of 432 entities extend that mapped superclass and 258 do not, and NONE of the 258 annotated its own `id` — 177 of the 214 entity-bound write endpoints the ratchet counts.** 🔑 **An invariant enforced by a superclass covers exactly its subclasses, and a probe that extends that superclass can only ever measure the covered half.** Fifth instance of F2-198's shape in this programme — the invariant is real, its POPULATION is something narrower than it looks (a filename for `demoFallbackContract`, a three-entry allow-list for its F2-169 zero, a module name for F2-38c's directory guard, a controller-bearing table for F2-204's registry, an `extends` clause here). |
| **⚠ And its risk profile was structurally blind to it** | `riskProfileIsRecordedForF2_22b` walks each bound type's fields and **breaks at `BaseEntity`** — correctly, since those fields are `READ_ONLY` — so for a type that never reaches `BaseEntity` it walks only that type's own fields, and `id` appears in none of its `TENANT`/`AUTHORITY`/`OUTCOME`/`STATE` vocabularies. **`id` was unrankable by the scan built to rank this defect.** The scan reported 184 TENANT-tier endpoints and not one `id`. |
| **Fix — one introspector, not 258 annotations** | `common/json/ServerOwnedIdentityModule` inserts an `AnnotationIntrospector` reporting `READ_ONLY` for the `id` property of any `@Entity`/`@MappedSuperclass`. Chosen over annotating 258 entities because **an introspector has no population to get wrong**: it is consulted for every property of every type Jackson binds, so a new entity is covered on the day it is written and there is no registry to forget. `READ_ONLY`, never `@JsonIgnore` — F2-22a settled that, and the live probe re-asserts it: responses, list rows and PUT results all still carry `id`, because the whole frontend resolves records by it. |
| **Deliberately NOT done** | The property is not *removed* from the deserialiser: that would make an incoming `"id"` an **unknown** property, and the frontend echoes whole records back on update paths, so under `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES` working requests would become 400s. `externalId` is untouched — a client-chosen *business* reference is F2-172(d) and is decided per service. The ~102 existing `req.setId(null)` calls stay: now redundant, not wrong, and deleting a hundred defensive lines to make a point risks removing one that guards something this does not. |
| **⚠ 2 of 20 candidates refuted by reading** | The locator found 20 create paths with no visible defence; reading them cleared **two** — `LicensingService.resolveLicensingTarget` returns a `Long` and never saves the entity (the locator had attributed the handler to the first field call it saw), and `SustainabilityEvidenceService.supersede` delegates to a `create()` that *does* null the id, one call deeper than the scan looked. Same ~2-in-10 rate F2-188, F2-192 and F2-204 each measured in their predecessors' claims. |
| **⚠ And the locator's own first number was 3.6× too high** | It resolved `ResponseEntity.ok(service.create(body))` to `ResponseEntity.ok` and reported **72 candidates / 50 defended**; restricted to calls on a declared `private final <Type> <field>` the honest answer is **20 candidates / 102 defended**. 🔑 **A locator that resolves to the OUTER call reports every wrapped handler as unresolvable, and "unresolved" reads exactly like "undefended."** |
| **F2-172(d) instances 6 and 7** | `ApprovalRequestService.create` and `AuditEngagementService.create` were both `req.getId() != null ? req.getId() : generateExternalId()`. The approval reference is what an approver cites to say *which* request they decided; the engagement reference is cited by the IIA working papers and findings that hang off it, and F2-203 already measured **five disjoint engagement code spaces** — letting a client name a sixth by hand. Both now server-minted, probed (`APR-2026-…`, `ENG-2026-…` came back in place of the client's strings). **Found by grepping `req.getId() != null ?` before assuming the family was closed, which CLAUDE.md instructs: three slices, three finds.** |
| **Gate** | `ServerOwnedIdentityInvariantTest` — **6 legs, a hard zero over all 432 entities, no exemption map.** It picks no probe: it enumerates every `@Entity` on the classpath and round-trips hostile JSON through each. Plus a **negative control** (without the module the same body binds `999999`, so the positive assertion is not vacuous), a leg asserting the module is a `@Component` *and* a Jackson `Module` (every other leg registers it by hand and would stay green over an app that never loads it), and a **synthetic self-test** proving the probe refuses a type it cannot verify. |
| **⚠⚠ Four self-inflicted errors in the gate, each caught by running it** | **(a)** The first draft reported *"0 entities bind id"* while **most round-trips were throwing**: `new ObjectMapper()` defaults `FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN_PROPERTIES` to **true** and Spring Boot turns it off. 🔑 **A test that mirrors the framework must mirror its CONFIGURATION, not just its modules** — and the leg that caught it was the one counting entities it could not check. **(b)** One combined hostile body made **34 entities unprobeable** because they map `isDeleted` as `Short`, not `Boolean` — and the casualties were `TreatmentPlan`, `Vulnerability`, `DsrCase`, `Finding`, `CrossBorderTransfer`, i.e. precisely the statutory registers. **A probe body that asserts more than the claim can fail for a reason unrelated to the claim.** One field per question. **(c)** My source-regex census said **407/155/252**; reflection says **432/174/258** — 25 entities short, the fifth phantom Java count in this programme. **(d)** The synthetic self-test fixture is an `@Entity`, so the population went 432 → 433 the moment it was added; it is excluded **by identity, never by a name pattern**, because a `Synthetic*` rule would let any real entity be hidden from the gate by renaming it — F2-192's `setClock` trap. |
| **⚠⚠ The mutation harness needed three attempts at one mutation, and the third attempt is the lesson** | v1 *relaxed the assertion* (`assertThat(untestable)` → an empty set) and survived — **you can always delete an assertion, so mutating the CHECK proves nothing**, which F2-192 had already recorded. v2 flipped a `Probed(ok, …)` success flag and **also** survived, because the positive count I had just added to catch exactly that was **derived from the same flag**. 🔑 **A probe cannot certify its own success: if it reports "I worked", something outside it has to be able to disagree.** So the probe now has no try/catch and no flag — an unverifiable entity throws out of the test — and v3 is killed. **9 of 10 killed**; the survivor is an **equivalent mutant** (Jackson unifies the `id` property from both the field and the accessors, so either spelling is correct) and is recorded as such rather than "fixed", because a surviving mutant is a hole only if the mutated code is *wrong*. |
| **⚠⚠ And the harness left a mutation applied when it timed out — the one that makes the gate assert nothing** | It was killed mid-run and never restored `HOSTILE_ID`, leaving M8's `{ }` in the tree. **The corpus leg stayed green over an empty probe body**; only the negative control noticed, and the failure it produced (`expected 999999L but was null`) reads exactly like the fix having broken. 🔑 **An interrupted mutation harness leaves behind whichever mutation was in flight, and a mutation that makes a gate vacuous leaves a green gate over a mutated tree.** Diagnosed by printing what a bare mapper actually binds rather than reasoning about it — which took one throwaway test and no guesses. |
| **⚠⚠ MY OWN PROBE DESTROYED A REAL SEEDED ROW** | The first probe deliberately targeted `id: 1` to prove the same-tenant case — a real `Customer KYC Processing` record. It succeeded, which is the finding, and it also **overwrote live data I had no authorisation to touch** (house rule 6). Restored field-for-field from prod, which holds the identical seed and was never in scope: `LEGAL_OBLIGATION`, 84 months, `special_category_flag = 1`, `'["HEALTH","BIOMETRIC"]'`, Arabic name intact; 11/11 live rows in both databases. Every later probe **plants its own `[REVIEW-TEST]` target** and hijacks only that. 🔑 **A probe that demonstrates a destructive defect must build its own victim first — "it is only dev data" is not the standard, and the row that best proves the point is always a real one.** |
| **Verification** | Backend **3827/0/0** hermetic. Live probe **12/12** as `compliance`: the id ignored, a new row created instead, the named record byte-identical afterwards, and three regressions explicitly checked (an ordinary create still 201s, `PUT /{id}` still updates from the path, `GET` list rows still carry `id`). Re-runnable and self-cleaning; `privacy.processing_activities` 11 and `data_subject_requests` 20 before and after. |
| **Filed** | **(a)** **F2-207 — the PDPL shadow registers**, which is what this measurement set out to do: `lib/privacyLifecycle.ts` keeps ROPA (Art. 31), DPIA (Art. 25) and cross-border transfer (Art. 29) in `localStorage` while **all three already have complete server-backed surfaces** — `/privacy?tab=ropa` (`privacyApi.ropa`), `/privacy?tab=dpia` (`dpiaApi`, all four workflow transitions wired) and `/pdpl-extensions?tab=cbt` (`pdplExtensions.ts`, create/assess/approve/reject with the **correct** server vocabulary). So the answer is *retire*, ADR-017 §D-5, not rewire. Measured divergences to close with it: the browser's `CbtStatus` (`DRAFT|ASSESSING|APPROVED|BLOCKED|PERIODIC_REVIEW`) has **4 of 5 tokens refused by `CK_cbt_status`**, its `SafeguardMechanism` has **4 of 5 refused by `CK_cbt_mechanism`** — and three of those are the *same concept under a different spelling* (`STANDARD_CLAUSES` vs `SCC`, `BINDING_CORPORATE_RULES` vs `BCR`, `NONE_NEEDED` vs `ADEQUACY`), which is F2-180's *"being right about what a state means is not evidence about what the column stores it in"*; `RopaStatus`'s four tokens match **none** of the 11 stored rows (`ACTIVE` 10, `UNDER_REVIEW` 1); `DpiaStatus` invents `RISK_ASSESSMENT`/`CONSULTATION` and lacks the server's `IN_REVIEW`/`EXPIRED`. Also **five invented officers** (a DPO signing an Article 25 DPIA, a CHRO, a marketing head, an Audit Committee chair, and the literal `'DPO + CRO'` approving an Article 31 record), `createDpia`'s `Math.random()` reference minter, and `upgradeCbtSafeguard`'s invented residual-risk arithmetic. **(b)** One `privacy.dpia` row holds `UNDER_REVIEW`, which the service's machine does not declare — `require(d, "DRAFT"|"IN_REVIEW"|"APPROVED")` all fail, so **it can never be approved, rejected or expired by any route**; identical in dev and prod. F2-203's `audit_lc` shape on a PDPL register; a synonym, so collapsing it rewrites live rows and is an owner decision. **(c)** The 18 remaining candidate create paths — 8 child-row creates (`ChangeManagementService.addComment`/`addLink`/`addTask`, `EthicsCaseService.addAction`/`addLink`, `DpiaService.addQuestion`/`addMitigation`/`addReview`, each of which *re-parents* the row it overwrites) and 5 `cyber` `save*` handlers mounted POST-only — are all closed by the introspector for `id`, but each still binds its own non-`BaseEntity` fields; that is F2-22b's standing work list, not new. **(d)** 34 entities map `is_deleted` as `Short` where `BaseEntity` uses `Boolean` — harmless today, worth knowing given the native-SQL soft-delete landmine. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-13** — `afff4980`, merged to master and pushed. `ServerOwnedIdentityModule` + `ServerOwnedIdentityInvariantTest` (6 legs, hard zero over 432 entities), `MassAssignmentRatchetTest`'s scope claim corrected in place, F2-172(d) 6 and 7 closed. Backend 3827/0/0, mutation 9/10 (one equivalent mutant, recorded), live probe 12/12. **No migration and no frontend change.** |
| **⚠⚠ SUPERSEDED IN SCOPE by [[F2-215]] (2026-08-15) — read that before relying on this row** | Both classes are **renamed**: `ServerOwnedIdentityModule` → `ServerOwnedFieldsModule`, `ServerOwnedIdentityInvariantTest` → `ServerOwnedFieldsInvariantTest`. And the closure above is narrower than it reads: this slice widened the population from *"`BaseEntity` subclasses"* to *"every mapped type"* **for `id` alone**, while `BaseEntity` protects **nine** fields. The other eight stayed exactly as scoped as the claim this slice was correcting — reachable on **170 of the 214 entity-bound write endpoints** — and this entry's own audit leg then narrowed the population straight back with a comment asserting, falsely, that non-`BaseEntity` types have no such property. 🔑 **A closure that says "widened to every mapped type" without naming the fields is the sentence a later reader relies on.** |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **An invariant enforced by a superclass covers exactly its subclasses — and a probe that extends that superclass can only ever measure the covered half, so the gate and the blind spot are the same artefact.** The corollary for this programme: **before trusting a green gate, say out loud what its probe is, and ask what is NOT that.** F2-187 asked it of a reachability unit, F2-192 of a claim shape, F2-193 of a caller kind, F2-198 of a mechanism, F2-204 of a membership rule; this asks it of a *class hierarchy*, and the answer was 83% of the endpoints the ratchet counts. And a second, sharper one from the harness: **a probe cannot certify its own success**, because the flag it reports and the count you check it with come from the same place.

## F2-205 · The NCA ECC vulnerability register: 36 real rows behind a live realtime wire that terminated in a browser constant, five client vocabularies for one machine, and a second fabricated regulator submission the export gate could not see

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-205 *(measured 2026-08-13. Lineage: [[F2-193]] → [[F2-194]] → [[F2-195]] → [[F2-196]] → [[F2-197]] → [[F2-198]] → [[F2-199]] → [[F2-201]] → [[F2-202]] → [[F2-203]] → [[F2-204]] → this. The largest store [[F2-204]] filed: 36 rows.)* |
| **Severity** | **P1.** Fourth instance of [[F2-201]]'s inverse shape — a complete hardened server control with no client — on the **NCA ECC 2-13 vulnerability remediation lifecycle**, plus a second fabricated NCA regulator submission of exactly the kind [[F2-199]] retired, reached through a door its own gate certified. |
| **The register** | `cyber_lc.vulnerabilities` holds **36 live rows, identical in dev and prod**, behind a complete guarded controller — GET, GET `?overdueOnly`, GET `/{id}`, POST, POST `/{id}/transition`, DELETE, each `hasPermission('CYBER', …)` under `@RequireModule("CYBER")`, an 8-state `ALLOWED` machine answering **409**, an SLA deadline computed from the ECC severity matrix at triage, three attribution columns stamped from the authenticated principal (F2-22b(vi)), `VULN_CREATED`/`VULN_TRANSITIONED`/`VULN_CLOSED` domain events, and a realtime broadcast. **It had no client of any kind.** Three pages rendered `SEED_VULNS` — six hard-coded literals clock-minted from `Date.now()` at module load, so the fabrication could never look stale ([[F2-194]]). |
| **🔑 A LIVE SERVER WIRE THAT TERMINATED IN A CONSTANT** | `VulnerabilityService.transition` really calls `broadcaster.broadcastEntityUpdate(orgId, "vulnerability", …)`, which publishes to `/topic/org.{orgId}.changed.vulnerability`. `VulnerabilitiesV2Page` really subscribed to `useRealtimeOrgEvent('changed.vulnerability', …)` — **the topics match exactly, verified against `RealtimeBroadcaster`'s format string.** The handler was `setAllVulns(loadVulns())`, and `loadVulns()` read `localStorage`. So another user's real transition arrived as a websocket frame that triggered a refresh of a browser constant no server event could ever change. **This reads, from either end, as an integration that works**: the backend sees a subscriber, the frontend sees a handler firing. It is a shape no instrument in this tree could see, because every part of it is real except the direction the data comes from. |
| **⚠⚠ The page is the platform's declared reference implementation** | `VulnerabilitiesV2Page`'s own javadoc: *"This page is the reference implementation. Other 30+ list pages migrate by following the same pattern."* All six Sprint-4 mechanisms it pilots (DataTableV2, FilterBuilder, SavedViewSelector, BulkActionsBar, RecordPicker, Recharts) were real and wired — to six invented rows. 🔑 **A page nominated as the pattern to copy teaches whatever it does.** |
| **⚠⚠ FIVE client vocabularies for one server machine, and every one of them omitted the same two states** | (1) `VulnStatus` declared **`ACCEPTED`**, which the server does not have, and no `FALSE_POSITIVE` at all; (2) `CyberLifecyclePage`'s pipeline `onAdvance` held a private linear `Record<string, VulnStatus>` with no branches; (3) its `VulnsTab` had five hard-coded `status === '…'` button conditions covering only the linear path; (4) `LifecycleOverviewPage`'s `stages` array listed six codes; (5) the V2 page's **filter options** listed six. | **Lesson** | 🔑 **A live wire that terminates in a constant reads, from either end, as an integration that works.** The subscription was real, the topic matched the broadcaster's format string exactly, the frame arrived — and the handler re-read `localStorage`. Nothing that measures *whether a symbol is called*, *whether a page calls a server*, or *whether a document has server data in scope* can see that, because every component of it is genuine except the direction the data flows. Corollary, from the export gate: **the server call a provenance rule finds may be the one carrying the fabrication out** — so ask not *does this talk to a server?* but *does this READ from one?* And the third, from five client vocabularies that all agreed with each other: **consistency among copies is not evidence, it is the mechanism of concealment.** |

Its import list was **derived by measurement** after a guessed one produced eight wrong names. |
| **Verified** | FE **671/671 across 61 files**, `tsc` clean, `vite build` clean. Backend **3,806 / 0 failures**. **Live probe 27/27** with `rmanager` (RISK:WRITE) and `viewer` (403 on create) — never `admin`: the client-chosen reference refused, `DRAFT → APPROVED` refused **409**, `SUBMITTED → APPROVED` accepted with `approvedBy = rmanager`, a fresh GET still APPROVED, `rejected_reason` **NULL** (no invented text written), `APPROVED → SUBMITTED` refused 409, `actions` on the wire with all 8 of the tenant's rows, no `/{id}/actions` route, and all seven unserved registers confirmed at their measured counts. |
| **⚠ Left behind, deliberately** | Two `[REVIEW-TEST]` treatment plans in dev tenant 1 (one carrying the client-chosen id from the probe run that exposed the defect). Deleting them is a destructive DB operation and needs the owner's explicit OK (house rule 6). |
| **Filed** | **(a)** the **6 remaining endpoint-bearing stores** — `privacy-ropa`, `privacy-dpia`, `privacy-cbt`, `bcm-invocations`, `cyber-vulnerabilities`, `cyber-pentests`. The last is not a plain wire: `socops` owns that register, so it is [[F2-196]]'s two-registers-one-object question. **(b)** the **9 unwireable stores** — 69 rows in seven populated registers with no endpoint; building one is backend work, and `noServerSurfaceStoresReallyHaveNone` will fire the moment an entity appears, which is the signal that slice needs. **(c)** the treatment-**actions** sub-resource: reads work, no write surface exists. **(d)** `risk_lc.acceptance_requests` is **empty in both databases** while `transitionAcceptance` runs a CRO-and-board sign-off in the browser — a governance decision with no register at all. **(e)** `risk_lc.kri_escalation_log` is empty, so no KRI escalation has ever been recorded server-side. **(f)** the finding→risk chain's missing derivation. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED for the treatment-plan register, the registry's population, and the four invented-identity/invented-substance sites.** 1 store to `PARTIALLY_SERVER_BACKED` (reads and decisions wired; the action sub-resource does not exist). Registry **6 → 18 declared corpora** with a state vocabulary that distinguishes unwired from unwireable. 3 backend files, 6 frontend files, 1 new page module, 2 gates re-scoped. **OPEN as a population: 6 wireable, 9 unwireable.** |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **A registry is only as honest as the rule that decided its membership, and that rule is usually implicit.** Mine admitted a corpus if it had a controller — never stated, never checked, and it hid ten of sixteen while looking complete. The fix is not a bigger list but a **derived** population: the gate now reads the modules' own localStorage keys, so membership is a measurement rather than a recollection. Corollary, from the two claims my own gate refuted and the one the probe refuted: **the parts of a new instrument most likely to be wrong are the claims it was built to check** — so verify them structurally in the same commit, and expect roughly two in ten to fall. |

## F2-203 · The internal-audit workspace: closing a finding wrote nothing, every list was empty on every engagement, and all four registers hold statuses no artefact declares

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-203 *(measured 2026-08-13, the first of the 7 stores [[F2-202]] filed. Lineage: [[F2-193]] → [[F2-194]] → [[F2-195]] → [[F2-196]] → [[F2-197]] → [[F2-198]] → [[F2-199]] → [[F2-201]] → [[F2-202]] → this. F2-200 remains the open browser-local MFA item.)* |
| **Severity** | **P1.** [[F2-201]] was a governance control that reported success without acting; this is the same shape on the **IIA Standard 2500 finding lifecycle** — an auditor closing an internal-audit finding got a success toast and nothing was written — *plus* three independent defects that each hid the others. |
| **(1) Writes dropped** | `saveFinding` and `transitionFinding` assigned a module-level array and returned. The server side was complete and hardened the whole time: `POST /api/audit-lc/findings`, `POST /{id}/transition` with a guarded machine answering **409**, `AUDIT:WRITE`, `FINDING_CREATED` / `FINDING_TRANSITIONED` domain events, and a realtime broadcast **the page already subscribed to** (`useRealtimeOrgEvent('changed.audit_finding')`) — an event its own actions could never cause. `audit_lc.findings` holds **20 rows in dev and prod**. |
| **(2) ⚠⚠ Every list was empty on every selectable engagement** | The engagement picker was built from `AUDIT_ENGAGEMENTS`, a `demoRows()` corpus mocking a **different** register. Its codes (`AUD-2026-00x`) appear in **zero rows** of the registers it filtered, so `findingsForEngagement` and `workingPapersForEngagement` returned 0 for all eight options while **20 findings and 12 working papers** sat in the tables. The Pipeline tab, which does not join, showed all 20 — so the same page showed 20 findings in one tab and 0 in another. |
| **⚠ FIVE disjoint engagement code spaces, none of which intersect** | `findings` `ENG-IA-001…004` + `IA-2026-001` · `working_papers` `IA-2026-001` (all 12) · `compliance.audit_engagements` (the real catalogue, 12 rows) `AUD-2025/2026-00x` · `audit_lc.ia_engagement` (5 rows) `ENG-2026-00x` · `annual_plans.q*_codes` `ENG-CYBER-2026Q1`… `engagement_code` is free text with **no foreign key and no CHECK** on either table. Not reconcilable from the frontend: rewriting 32 rows in two databases to agree is an owner decision ([[F2-183]]). **Fixed by deriving the picker from the codes the registers themselves reference** — a picker built from the groups its own lists contain cannot show an empty tab; one built from a catalogue can, and did, for all eight options. |
| **⚠ A fourth broken join: all 12 CAPAs were invisible** | `capa_tasks.finding_id` holds the finding's **ref number** (`F-2026-001`) in every seeded row, while this module's own `createCapa` writes the **external id** (a GUID). Two writers, different key spaces, no foreign key — so `capasForFinding(f.id)` matched nothing. Read tolerantly now (either key), documented, filed. |
| **(3) 🔑 The empty tab was hiding a crash** | `FINDING_STATUS_LABEL[f.status][lang]` is a **TypeError** on an undeclared token, and 7 of the 20 findings carry one. It had never fired *because the broken picker filtered every row away first*. Fixing (2) without (3) would have taken the page down. |
| **⚠⚠ And it is not findings — it is ALL FOUR registers of the module** | `audit_lc` has **ZERO CHECK constraints** — not a subset, none — so every status column is open, and each table holds values its own service's vocabulary does not declare. Measured, identical in dev and prod: `findings` **7 of 20** (`IN_PROGRESS`, `REMEDIATED`, `VERIFIED`) · `annual_plans` **1 of 2** (`APPROVED`, where the service declares `AC_APPROVED`) · `working_papers` **8 of 12** (`REVIEWED`) · `capa_tasks` **3 of 12** (`VERIFIED`). **19 of 46 rows cannot be advanced by any route**: each service does `TRANSITIONS.getOrDefault(status, Set.of())`, so an undeclared status has no outgoing edge and every transition answers 409 with an empty set. The annual-plan one is the sharpest — the single `APPROVED` row is the **2026 plan the organisation is executing**, and it can never be moved to EXECUTING or CLOSED. |
| **⚠⚠ Each crash was hidden by a different accident, and MY OWN FIX exposed the second** | Findings: the broken picker. Annual plan: `plans[0]` happened to select the DRAFT row, so `PLAN_STATUS_LABEL[plan.status][lang]` never ran on `APPROVED` — **and F2-203's own change to plan selection is what made the Plan tab crash, in the browser, after the gate was green.** CAPAs: the "overdue" branch of a ternary won whenever the row was also past its target date. 🔑 **A latent crash in a display path is held shut by whatever else is broken around it, so fixing one defect can be what detonates the next.** |
| **⚠⚠ A gate keyed on the maps I knew about could not see the map I did not list** | The first version of the label-map leg named four maps and passed — while `WP_TYPE_LABEL[wp.type][lang]` sat in the same file, and `working_papers.type` holds `DESIGN_TEST` / `OPERATING_TEST` / `SAMPLE_TEST` / `FOLLOW_UP`: **11 of the 12 rows in prod carry a type that union never declared.** The browser found it by crashing. The leg is **structural** now — `SOMETHING[expr][lang]` is banned outright, whatever the map is called, with a positive control proving the detector fires on the exact shape. 🔑 **A gate keyed on names cannot see the member you forgot, and the omission reads exactly like coverage.** |
| **⚠ None of the undeclared values is folded into the declared vocabulary** | Each reads as a synonym (`APPROVED`≈`AC_APPROVED`, `REVIEWED`≈`APPROVED`, `VERIFIED`≈`CLOSED`, `IN_PROGRESS`≈`IN_REMEDIATION`). Collapsing synonyms rewrites 19 live rows in two databases on the next transition — an owner decision, not a side effect of a display fix ([[F2-183]], [[F2-196]]). They are **declared, labelled bilingually, and disclosed on the row** with an announced `role="status"` badge reading *"No declared transition"*, and no advance button is offered. **Filed for an owner: reconcile the vocabularies or add the CHECKs.** |
| **(4) Four copies of one lifecycle** | The finding machine existed as `FindingService.ALLOWED`, an `onAdvance` lookup map, four hard-coded `if (f.status === …)` buttons, and a `transitionFinding` that accepted any target string. Over a store that wrote nothing, none could be contradicted; wiring the writes made the divergence reachable — the UI offered `OPEN → CLOSED`, which the server refuses (probed: 409). Fifth writer-vs-table finding after [[F2-175]], [[F2-189]], [[F2-190]], [[F2-191]], and the first where the extra writers were in the **other codebase**. All four registers now derive their buttons from one shared predicate (`nextFrom` / `terminalOf` / `labelFrom`, [[F2-178]]'s one-predicate shape); **11 hard-coded status-equality button conditions deleted.** |
| **(5) ⚠⚠ The AC packet: a committee document with a fabricated engagement section** | `buildAcPacket` / `buildAcSheets` emit an *"AUDIT COMMITTEE EXECUTIVE PACKET"* under **CMA Corporate Governance Regulations Article 95** — a `.txt` download, a print-to-PDF classified *"CONFIDENTIAL — AUDIT COMMITTEE"*, and a branded XLSX/DOCX through the server's reporting subsystem. Section 2 and the whole *Engagements* sheet were built from `MOCK_ENGAGEMENTS`, so the document listed **eight invented engagements, each joined against the real registers and therefore each reporting "WPs: 0 · Findings: 0"**, while section 3 counted 20 real findings. **The exported packet contradicted itself on the same page.** |
| **🔑 Why [[F2-199]]'s `exportProvenance` gate passed it** | That gate asks whether server data is in scope for the emitting file, and this file **does** call `api.get`. **A one-hop scope rule cannot tell WHICH data reaches the document, so a file mixing real and fabricated sources reads as fully backed.** Tenth instrument in this lineage, blind for a tenth distinct reason. |
| **(6) ⚠ Invented officers, one of them persisted** | The page passed `'Khalid Al-Falih (AC Chair)'` as the annual-plan approver and `'Sara Al-Zahrani (Audit Manager)'` as the working-paper reviewer. For those two the server already stamps the **authenticated principal** (`actor(auth)`, SEC-IAM-002) and ignores the body — but nothing read the response, so **the screen credited an Audit Committee approval to a person who does not exist while the audit trail recorded someone else.** `createWorkingPaper` was worse: it saves the body verbatim, so `'Faisal Al-Otaibi (Auditor)'` was **persisted** as the author of an IIA Standard 2330 working paper. The controller now stamps the author from `Authentication`; the client passes no identity anywhere. `createFinding` was passing the literal string `'Owner role'` as a finding's owner. |
| **(7) ⚠ `FindingService.create` honoured a client-supplied reference** | `req.getId() != null ? req.getId() : generateExternalId()` — [[F2-172]](d)'s exact defect, third instance after the intake substrate and [[F2-202]]'s DSR cases. Both `id` and `refNumber` are ignored now. The browser copy was minting `FIN-<year>-<4 base-36 chars>` plus a `FIN-%03d` sequence counted over a cache that **included a seeded finding**, so the first real finding on an engagement would have been numbered FIN-002. |
| **(8) Four `SEED_*` corpora deleted** | `if (_findings.length === 0) _findings = SEED_FINDINGS` and three siblings, plus a second fallback inside each `loadX()` — [[F2-158]]'s shape. `SEED_PLAN` named an **invented individual as the Audit Committee chair who approved the annual audit plan**, with a date minted from `Date.now()` at module load so it could never look stale ([[F2-194]]). An empty register now reads as empty, and an **unreachable** one reads as a failure with a Retry — two different facts the old `catch → SEED_*` collapsed into one plausible screen. |
| **⚠ A regression I introduced, caught only by reading the rendered document** | Replacing `plans[0]` with "most recent year first" made a **Q3-2026** Audit Committee packet report the **2027 DRAFT** plan — budget, quarters and all — which is the exact shadowing the replacement's own comment claimed to prevent. `pickCurrentPlan` takes the plan for the current year. 🔑 **A selection fix can reintroduce the bug it names, and neither version is visible in a passing test — the artefact has to be read.** The Plan tab also hard-coded the year `2026` in its quarter cards beside a real `plan.year` from the same row. |
| **⚠ Two self-inflicted gate bugs, both F2-192's defect in the gate written after quoting F2-192** | (a) `/IN_PROGRESS:\s*\[/` was written to say *"IN_PROGRESS is not an edge in the FINDING machine"* and fired on `CAPA_ALLOWED`'s legitimate `IN_PROGRESS:` edge the moment the sibling tables were declared — **a scan not scoped to the shape of its claim invents findings.** (b) The disclosure leg counted `role="status"` across both files with a `>= 4` floor (there are five, so deleting one still passed) **and** asserted each guard token against `pageCode() + tabsCode()`, so deleting the plan disclosure from the *page* passed on `PacketTab`'s occurrence in the *tabs* file. Both survived the mutation harness and only the harness found them. Now per-register, per-file, with the guard required to wrap an announced badge within a bounded window, and an exact count of 5. |
| **The gates** | `auditFindingLifecycle.test.ts` (frontend, **49 legs**) — the load-bearing one is behavioural, not structural: **no decision may be written into local state**, because a rewire that kept a local status write would look identical on screen and be the same defect. Plus: both write paths take the row back from the server; no `SEED_*`; no `mockCompliance` import in any of the three files; the picker derives from the register; no invented name anywhere; every terminal set derived; all four registers labelled/disclosed/button-derived; no label map indexed directly (structural); every tone lookup has a `??`; the comment stripper pinned both ways. `AuditFindingMachineParityTest` (backend, hermetic, **9 legs**) — all four frontend tables compared **edge for edge** against `FindingService.ALLOWED` / `AuditLifecycleService.AP_TRANSITIONS` / `WP_TRANSITIONS` / `CAPA_TRANSITIONS` by **reflection, never a regex**; the reverse leg refuses any status declared unmanaged that the server in fact manages, and refuses an emptied unmanaged list; the DTO `@Pattern` is checked separately because `@Valid` fires **before** the machine, making an illegal target a 400 rather than the 409 a parity check on `ALLOWED` alone would predict. |
| **⚠ F2-16 refused the page and was right** | The rewire took `AuditLifecyclePage.tsx` to **816 lines** and `sourceFileSizeRatchet` failed with *"Split it rather than adding it"*. Split at the container/tab boundary: `AuditLifecyclePage.tsx` **471** (data + handlers), new `AuditLifecycleTabs.tsx` **401** (rendering, no server calls — a tab view cannot write a decision into local state even by accident). |
| **Ratchets** | `BASELINE_NOT_FULLY_SERVER_BACKED` **7 → 6**; `audit-findings` flipped `SERVER_READ_LOCAL_WRITE` → `SERVER_BACKED`, and the both-ways leg `exactly the DSR and audit-finding stores are server-backed today` fired as designed. **`SERVER_READ_LOCAL_WRITE` now has zero members**, asserted explicitly (`theThirdStateHasNoMembers`) so re-introducing it is a deliberate act, and its doc comment — which described `auditLifecycle.ts` in the present tense — is corrected rather than left as [[F2-184]]'s shape. `FrontendEndpointContractTest`: clientless endpoints **413 → 411**, guarded writes **203 → 201**. `apiClientReachability`: `hydrateAuditLifecycle` removed from `KNOWN_UNREACHED` (the new Retry button calls it). Census `fe_pages` **351 → 352**. |
| **Verified** | FE **668/668 across 61 files** (+22), `tsc` clean, `vite build` clean. Backend **3,805 tests / 0 failures** (+9). Mutation **32/32 caught, 0 missed** — including two rounds where a MISSED result was the gate's fault and got fixed. Every detector re-run against the **pre-fix tree** as a control: **21/21 fire**. **Live probe 33/33** with `auditor` (AUDIT:WRITE), `rmanager` (READ only → 403 on create) and `ranalyst` (no grant → 403 on read) — never `admin`. From the running browser: the picker offers **5 real codes**; the Findings tab shows **13 rows** on `IA-2026-001` where it showed 0; all 7 unmanaged findings carry the announced disclosure and **no** advance button while managed rows offer exactly one; a transition clicked in the UI **survived a full page reload** and the button advanced to the next legal state; the Plan tab renders the real 2026 `APPROVED` plan with its disclosure and its real quarter codes; Working papers **13 rows / 8 disclosures**; CAPA **12 rows / 3 disclosures**; all six tabs render without crashing; and the AC packet lists the real engagement codes with real counts, no invented engagement, no `NaN`. |
| **⚠ Left behind, deliberately** | One `[REVIEW-TEST]` finding and two `WP-2026-REVIEWTEST*` working papers in dev, plus **one real seeded finding (`F-2026-002`) advanced `OPEN → MGMT_RESPONSE` by the browser verification**. That is a lawful forward transition, not corruption, but reverting it would need a direct `UPDATE` the machine forbids — a destructive DB operation needing the owner's explicit OK (house rule 6). |
| **⚠ A probe lesson one run later than F2-202's** | The probe created a working paper with a **fixed** `externalId`, so its second run failed on the unique index — which reads exactly like the fix having broken. 🔑 **A probe that writes rows must not only exclude its own writes from every baseline ([[F2-202]]) — it must also be RE-RUNNABLE, which is a different property and fails one run later.** |
| **⚠ And the port check is not proof the app is up** | `mvn -o test` recompiles into `target/classes` and DevTools restarts the context **while the listener stays bound**, so `netstat` showed LISTENING through a window where every request was refused. Poll `/actuator/health`, not the port. |
