| **⚠ Two more self-inflicted errors, both caught only by running things** | The FE-parity leg parsed `DSR_REQUEST_TERMINAL` with `\[([^\]]*)\]` and matched the **type annotation** `readonly string[]` first — an empty group, which reads exactly like *"the frontend declares no terminal statuses"*. **Sixth** instance in this programme of a pattern satisfied by something other than its claim. And the PrivacyPage scan fired on **my own correction comment** quoting the code it replaced — [[F2-193]]'s quotation-vs-claim trap, three methods below the `stripComments` helper written for precisely that reason. 🔑 **A warning you wrote yourself is the one you are least likely to apply.** |
| **Verification** | Backend **3,790/0/0**. FE **522/522 across 55 files** (+5). `tsc` clean. Mutation **19/19 as declared** (18 caught, 1 declared SURVIVES with a reason). Live probe **11/11** through :8084: `stats.openDsrs` **12** (complement) vs **10** (old list); `POST /api/v1/privacy/dsr/sla/sweep` → **`{openOverdue: 9, firedEvents: 2}`** where the as-shipped predicate saw **7**, stamping exactly the two EXTENDED cases and writing **2 `SLA_BREACH` audit rows** for entity ids 5 and 12; `fulfil`/`start` on a `RESOLVED` request now **400 "already terminal"** (was 200), including stored lower-case `'resolved'`. `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows removed with a `CHARINDEX` delete; 20 rows and all 12 case statuses unchanged. **0 migrations** — the three columns still have no CHECK, deliberately (see below). |
| **⚠ Why no CHECK constraint** | [[F2-183]]'s rule: a CHECK and its writer land in the same commit, and the migration's scope is the writers you close. Here the vocabularies contain **synonyms** (`FULFILLED`/`RESOLVED`/`COMPLETED` all mean finished; `NEW`/`OPEN`/`PENDING` all mean not started). A CHECK admitting all of them would **bless the synonyms**; collapsing them rewrites live rows in two databases. That is a data decision for the owner, not a side effect of a display fix. |
| **Status** | ✔ **CLOSED.** `DsrLifecycleContractTest` (8 tests) holds: terminal derived from the machine; open as the complement in both registers (an invented status is open); CI-insensitive comparison; no class outside the two lifecycle classes restating either vocabulary in any of **three** shapes; FE↔BE parity in both directions; and `PrivacyPage` calling the shared predicate by **call shape**, not by an import. Plus `PrivacyGapServiceTest`'s selection leg and `PrivacyServiceTest`'s two complement legs. |
| **⬜ Filed, not fixed** | **(a)** the **fourth** DSR register — `privacyLifecycle.ts` drives a `localStorage` DSR store with a `SEED_DSR` corpus behind `PrivacyLifecyclePage` and `LifecycleOverviewPage`, while `privacy_lc.dsr_cases` has 12 real rows and a real API (`/api/privacy-lc/dsr-cases`); the [[F2-172]] shape, and in [[F2-194]]'s 105-corpus population. **(b)** **three registers is the root cause** and consolidating them is an owner decision. **(c)** all four Privacy KPI tiles count `module/privacy` rows and link to `/data-officer/*` screens over **different tables**, so no tile's number can be verified by clicking it — systemic and pre-existing, so not changed unilaterally. **(d)** `DsrCaseService.overdue()` has **no route** — a [[F2-187]] dark method the named map does not yet hold. **(e)** [[F2-195]]'s own filed item, `moduleLifecycles`' 56 hard-coded counts, is still open; two of its numbers need correcting — the red `role="status"` badges are **25 tiles** (29 is the sum of items they assert) and the pages rendering them are **11**, not 12. |
| **Lesson** | 🔑 **When a column has no CHECK, its vocabulary lives only in the heads of its readers — so count the readers before trusting any one of them.** [[F2-189]]/[[F2-190]]/[[F2-191]] asked *"how many things write this status, and how many of them ask?"*; this asks the mirror question about **readers**, and found that seven readers of three tables had produced four vocabularies and two wrong answers. The remedy is the same one-predicate shape, plus the complement rule: make "open" mean *not finished*, so the cost of a forgotten token is a false positive that gets chased rather than a statutory breach that is never reported. |

## F2-195 · The module KPI strip asserted metrics no server computed, and every one was flattering

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-195 *(measured 2026-08-12, immediately after [[F2-194]]. Found by asking F2-194's census question one level up: not "which corpora are fabricated?" but "which record fields ASSERT live operational state?" — a `status`, a metric, a timestamp, a `configured` flag. Ranking the 105 corpora by that shape put `moduleLifecycles`' `activeCount`/`overdueCount` at the top, and reading the pages that render them found a sharper defect in the KPI strip directly above.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2** — same class as [[F2-42]] / [[F2-193]] / [[F2-194]]: a fabricated claim rendered beside real subsystem data. Not P1 (nothing is mis-stored, no control is bypassed). Not P3, and this is the strongest P2 in the lineage: the tiles asserted a **Saudi regulator compliance score**, a **PDPL Article 31 register size** and an **incident-response SLA**, in the one screen region every user reads first. |
| **What was wrong** | Of **1,069 `<Kpi>` tags** across the app, **9 on 5 module pages** displayed a figure no server produced. Measured live against dev, side by side: <br>• **Cyber · "NCA ECC Score" `"87%"`** — all **29** NCA ECC controls in the register are `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`, so the real score is **0%**. An 87-point overstatement of an NCA compliance score, rendered in `success` green. <br>• **Incidents · "Mean TTR" `"4.2h"`** — `/incidents/stats` already returned `avgDays: 4.5`. Not merely 26× low: **the wrong unit**. <br>• **Compliance · "Evidence Items" `"1,283"`** — 78 real items (**16×**). <br>• **Compliance · "Compliance Score" `"87%"`** — 66% by the page's own coverage formula, 70 by the server's `complianceScore`. Rendered **fifteen lines above** a real `RadialGauge` fed by `frameworkApi.coverage()`. <br>• **BCM · "Exercise Pass Rate" `"92%"`** — exactly exercise #1's `score`, presented as an aggregate (real mean: 84). <br>• **BCM · "RTO Compliance" `"76%"`** — nothing computes RTO attainment on this page at all. <br>• **BCM · Critical Processes `procs.data.length \|\| 38`** and **Privacy · Activities `ropa.data.length \|\| 142`**. <br>• **Privacy · "Consent Coverage" `"98%"`** — the same number for every tenant. |
| **🔑 Every one was in the flattering direction** | 0%→87%, 4.5 days→4.2 hours, 78→1,283, 66%→87%, 84→92, 11→142, 8→38. Not one erred low. Second instance of this exact pattern after [[F2-193]], where the two connectors with real pollers had *"the wrong cadence in the flattering direction"* — 900 s shown as "Daily". A fabrication drifts toward the number someone wanted to see. |
| **🔑 The `\|\| N` shape, and why it is the sharp one** | `0 \|\| 142` is 142, so the fallback fires on **exactly** the tenant whose register is empty — a PDPL Article 31 record-of-processing-activities tile reading **142** for an organisation that has recorded none. It is a mock fallback that activates precisely when the truth is "nothing". Third occurrence of a load-bearing client-side fallback after [[F2-158]] and [[F2-42]]. |
| **⚠⚠ And [[F2-52]] had already fixed this shape once, in this codebase, with the rule written down** | `AdminPage.tsx:249` carries the comment: *"F2-52: `roles.length \|\| 7` reported the hardcoded dropdown's length when the server returned nothing — a role count that could not be zero, four of whose roles did not exist. **The real count is the real count, including 0.**"* Its two siblings — on the PDPL and BCM registers — survived untouched. 🔑 **Fixing the instance you noticed is not closing the shape, and the codebase can hold the correct rule, stated in prose, three lines from where nobody applied it.** Same failure as [[F2-185]]'s `CalendarEventDto`, where four inert constraints sat above the comment explaining why the fifth was deleted. |
| **⚠ The trend prop is a second, independent claim** | Four of the nine carried `trend={{ dir: 'up', value: '+4%' }}` — which asserts a **prior-period figure**. Nothing in the platform stores a KPI time series. Wiring a value while keeping its literal trend would have left in place the half of the fabrication that implies history exists, and it would have looked like a completed fix. All four are deleted; the gate refuses a literal trend even on a tile whose value is real. |
| **The fix** | Eight of nine wired to sources that were **already fetched or already on the client**: `incidentApi.stats().avgDays` (a method that had **no caller** — the F2-165 gate confirmed it by demanding its removal from `KNOWN_DARK`, so the dark FE population drops 189 → **188**), `evidenceApi.items().totalElements`, `consentApi.stats()`, the control register's own `status` / `implementationStatus`, and `mean(exercise.score)`. The ECC score is **scoped by `frameworkName`** because the register holds four NCA frameworks plus ISO 27001, and its tone is now **computed** — a 0% score in `success` green is a claim of its own. `bcmKpiExercises` ("Exercise Pass Rate") is retired in favour of `bcmKpiExerciseScore`: the register stores a per-exercise score and **no pass/fail outcome**, so a pass rate needs a threshold that exists nowhere in the schema. |
| **The one not wired, and why that is a measurement not an excuse** | BCM · RTO Compliance renders `value={null}` with an `emptyHint` naming what is missing. ⚠ **My first draft of this row said "no source exists" and that was false** — `bcm_lc.Invocation.actualRtoHours` is real, populated on **2 of 3** dev invocations (4.5 h each), joinable to the BIA target via `affectedBiaIds`, and served by `GET /api/bcm-lc/invocations`, which **has no api-client method**. Wiring it is a feature (a new client method, a join, and a product definition of "attainment"), not a de-fabrication. 🔑 *One file short is the whole error* — third instance, and the only reason it is not in this row as a false claim is that I checked before writing it. `DrTestTrendService` is the near-miss trap: it exposes a real **DR-plan-test** pass rate (67% in dev, `GET /api/v1/bcm/dr-test-trend`) and its own javadoc says *"the per-test measured RTO/RPO is not yet on the entity"* — rendering it on a BCM exercise tile would trade one wrong number for another. |
| **The gate** | `kpiProvenance.test.ts` (8 tests) over all 1,069 tags, refusing three shapes — **LITERAL** (`value={87}` / `"87%"` / `"1,283"` / `"4.2h"`), **FALLBACK** (`\|\| N` where N ≥ 2; `\|\| 0` is honest, since zero is the true answer for a missing count), and **LITERAL_TREND**. Exceptions are a named map with a reason each, enforced **in both directions**, and the reason must argue build-time-ness rather than assert a label. Population after the fix: **1 of 1,069** — `rcKpiLanguages value={2}`, a property of the bundled font set, not of any tenant. |
| **⚠ A scan reporting a small number may be reporting it because the scan is broken** | Three findings in this lineage produced phantom counts over source regexes ([[F2-187]]'s 1,763 endpoints from a javadoc sentence, [[F2-184]]'s phantom 75 types, [[F2-193]]'s 0-of-389). So the scan was **run against the pre-fix tree as a control**: it found **10** there and **1** here, same 1,069 tags. That control is now permanent — `theDetectorActuallyDetects` runs the predicates over **synthetic** tags of each shape, and a negative-control test asserts the five honest shapes are *not* flagged. 🔑 **The corpus assertions pass both when the app is clean and when the regexes have rotted; only a synthetic self-test distinguishes those.** |
| **⚠⚠ My own first draft of one assertion fired on 16 innocent tiles** | *"A nullable KPI must offer an `emptyHint`"* tested `/\bnull\b/` anywhere in the value expression, and matched the `null` inside `x == null ? '—' : …` on tiles that pass a **string**. **Fifth instance in this lineage of a check satisfied by something other than its claim** — [[F2-192]]'s reason citing `list`, [[F2-193]]'s reason quoting the sentence it corrected, [[F2-194]]'s type name `CcmDashboardSnapshot` and its import standing in for a call. Rewritten positionally (`? null :`, `: null`, `?? null`, `value={null}`). |
| **⚠⚠ And the baseline I then wrote was lifted from the buggy detector's output** | Having corrected the detector, I set the hand-rolled-em-dash ratchet to **16** — the count the *broken* assertion had printed, which answered a different question. The real population is **71 across 32 files**. The failing test run is the only reason that number is right. 🔑 **A baseline taken from a measurement of something else is worse than no baseline, because it looks measured.** Held as decrease-only and filed rather than swept: these tiles pass the em-dash as a *string*, so they bypass the component's `emptyHint` tooltip and give a dash with no explanation — a strictly weaker defect than a false number, and closing it means 71 bilingual reasons, which is [[F2-188]]'s failure mode. |
| **⚙ The primitive already existed** | `Kpi` has carried a first-class not-measured treatment since UX-008 — `value == null` renders `.empty-inline-compact` with `emptyHint` as both `title` and `aria-label`, documented *"so 'not yet measured' never reads as a real 0"*. Nothing had to be built for the three unmeasurable tiles. Fourth time in this programme that a recorded blocker was already solved ([[F2-178]]'s three prerequisites, [[F2-179]]'s `ExerciseObserverService`, [[F2-174]]'s seated roles). **Re-measure a recorded blocker before believing its estimate.** `Kpi.test.tsx` (5 tests) now pins the contract, including that a **genuine zero renders as `0`** — because `isNoData` is `value == null` and if it were `!value` the real 0% ECC score would render as an em-dash, and the finding would be re-hidden by the fix meant to expose it. |

That SURVIVES is declared, so a later reader can tell "not caught" from "not checked". |

Every replacement resolves and every value differs from the fabrication it replaces: `4.5d`, `66%` (14 impl + 18 partial of 35), `78`, **`0%` (0 of 29 ECC → tone `danger`)**, `84` (mean of 12 scored), `8`, `11`, `100%` (10 active of 10), and for the unwired tile, proof the source exists and answers. ## F2-194 · A fabricated CCM panel sat directly beneath the real monitoring engine, and the de-mocking boundary could not see it

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-194 *(measured 2026-08-12, immediately after [[F2-193]]. Its question — "what else on this page asserts capability nothing provides?" — was asked of the page I had just edited, and the answer was in the component mounted six lines below the one I fixed.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2** — the same class as [[F2-42]]: a façade beside a working subsystem, on one screen, making framework-coverage claims. Not P1 (nothing is mis-stored, no control is bypassed). Two "Continuous Control Monitoring" panels, one real and one invented, stacked on one screen. |

| **⚠⚠ The measurement that makes this more than one component** | The de-mocking programme's boundary is drawn by **filename**. [[F2-15]] counts 15 files named `mock*` (3,550 lines); its own row already records that *"'15 files' is the wrong boundary — it was drawn by filename"* and extends it by 7 modules found with a **second** rule (modules defining records with **numeric** ids). That second rule has its own blind spot, and this is it: `lib/ccm.ts` keys its rows `cn-tenable.s3-encryption`, so it is in **neither** count. 🔑 **A boundary correction made by a second rule inherits a second blind spot.** |
| **And W2-1b's ratchet cannot see any of them** | `demoFallbackContract.test.ts` ratchets **`/mock/i` imports** — imports *from files named* `mock*` — at 33 imports across 27 files. A corpus in a file called `ccm.ts` or `assets.ts` is invisible to it by construction, so the one enforced instrument in this area could never have counted this. |
| **The census, by shape rather than by name** | Scanning `src/` for an exported `const` initialised to an array of **≥3 object literals** that another product file imports: **52 files declare 105 such corpora, and exactly 1 of those files is named `mock*`.** The scan LOCATES; classification needs reading, and the list is genuinely mixed — `moduleAnchors.ts` / `moduleLifecycles.ts` are navigation and lifecycle **configuration**, `AUTHORITIES` is the Saudi regulator catalogue that W2-1a-i deliberately kept as product reference data, and `moc.ts`'s three arrays are regulatory requirement text. | **The gate** | `connectorsProvenance.test.ts` (7 tests), modelled on `boardPackProvenance.test.ts` and copying its two load-bearing ideas: assertions run over **comment-stripped** source, and the check asserts a **pairing** — the fabrication absent **and** the real engine's calls present, because a page that simply deleted its monitoring panel would pass the absence half alone. |
| **⚠⚠ Two of my own assertions were satisfied by something that was not the claim** | The mutation harness caught both. (1) *"the prose explaining the removal is still there"* asserted the bare word `CcmDashboard` in the raw source — which passed because the page imports the **type** `CcmDashboardSnapshot` from the real engine's client; now it asserts the retired **path** (`components/compliance/CcmDashboard`) present in prose and absent in code, the same string in both directions. (2) *"the page drives the real engine"* used `toContain('getCcmDashboard')`, which an **import statement** satisfies — a mutation replacing the call with `Promise.resolve(null)` SURVIVED; now it requires call syntax. 🔑 **Third and fourth instances in one lineage of a substring check satisfied by something other than the claim** — [[F2-192]]'s reason citing `list`, [[F2-193]]'s reason quoting the sentence it corrected, and now a type name and an import. |

## F2-193 · The connector page told an operator that five connectors with no backend were actively ingesting

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-193 *(measured 2026-08-12, by following [[F2-192]]'s closing instruction — "assume a third shape exists" — into the one bucket of `DarkServiceMethodTest.TOLERATED` it had left intact: the **trigger** claims. Fifth consecutive finding produced by interrogating the previous slice's own instrument.)* |
| **Severity** | **P2** — an operator-facing screen asserting capability the platform does not have, under NCA ECC 2.6 / 6.1, ISO 27001 §A.8.8, PDPL and SAMA Outsourcing §5.4 references. Not P1: nothing is mis-stored and no control is bypassed. Not P3: the reader is a CISO or ORG_ADMIN deciding whether their SIEM and scanner feeds work, and the screen answered yes for connectors that do not exist. |
| **Where the audit started** | Six entries in `TOLERATED` say a capability is absent not because no route exists but because **nothing fires it** — *"NO PRODUCTION TRIGGER … the integration reads as working while no domain event reaches it"*. That is a claim about the **kind** of caller a class has, and neither of the map's gates measures kinds. [[F2-192]]'s citation rule made it worse rather than better: it forced each of those reasons to name a live sibling, and **a named routed sibling reads as evidence the integration is exercised**. |
| **The backend half — one false claim** | The Splunk entry said *"Splunk differs from ServiceNow: `#pushSecurityEvent` is live from SplunkController's `POST /security-event/{id}`, so that module **has one real trigger**"*. That route exists. Its own `@Operation` summary reads **"Manually push a known SOC security event into Splunk"**. 🔑 **A route is not a trigger.** Measured across the module: no `@Scheduled` class and no event listener calls the service, so Splunk egress has no production trigger either — what it has that ServiceNow lacks is a typed *manual* route beside the smoke test. Same failure mode as [[F2-188]]'s five: the truth was one line away, in a doc annotation nobody had opened. |
| **⚠⚠ And then the same question, asked of the frontend, found the real defect** | `tss-grc-ui-v2/src/lib/connectors.ts` is the catalogue behind the Connectors screen. Twelve entries, each with a hand-set `status`, a `cadence`, a `lastRunAt` and an `intake30d` count — *"records auto-ingested in the last 30 days"*. **Eight read `ACTIVE`.** Measured against the backend: **five of the eight have no implementation of any kind** — the SDAIA, NCA and SAMA regulator watches (no RSS client, no poller, no regulator-watch service anywhere), the vendor SOC 2 / ISO 27001 expiry watcher (`tprm` has no scheduler), and the CAPA effectiveness re-test, whose description promises to flag `VERIFICATION_FAILED` — **a token that appears in no Java source** — from a `capa` module with no scheduler. A sixth (Splunk) is webhook-only, not the `EVERY_5MIN` poll shown. |
| **The two that are real were wrong in the flattering direction** | `cn-tenable` is a real `@Scheduled` loop at **fixedDelay 900 s** — shown as *"Daily"*. `cn-kri-monitor` is a real `@Scheduled(cron = "0 0 6 * * *")`, daily at 06:00 — shown as *"Hourly"*. Both are **off by configuration**: `grc.integrations.tenable.polling-enabled` is `false` in `application-dev.yml` and in the base profile (prod declares no `integrations` block at all), and `grc.kri.scheduler-enabled` defaults to `false` in code and is set in **no profile in the repo**. |
| **⚠ The inversion that shows the list was never compared with the code** | **CrowdStrike — the connector with the shortest real interval of any, `@Scheduled` at 60 s — was not in the catalogue at all.** Five connectors with no code were listed as ACTIVE; the one with the most aggressive real poller was absent. |
| **The sharpest single number** | The `intake30d` values summed to **292** in a KPI captioned *"Auto-intake (30 days)"* that **linked to `/intake-inbox`**, where `intake.intake_records` holds **0 rows in dev and prod**. For `cn-tenable` specifically the page claimed **247** findings ingested in the last 30 days; `platform.tenable_finding_log` has held **5 rows in total**, every one written by somebody pressing *Poll*. 🔑 **[[F2-172]] deleted the fabricated intake records and left the fabricated COUNT of them** — a de-mocking that stops at the store and not at the aggregates that summarise it. |
| **⚠ Two dead controls beside it** | The `Pause` / `Activate` buttons wrote to a React `useState` map and toasted *"Connector activated — first run scheduled within the next cadence window"*. The page's own comment said the backend *"is not yet wired up"*, and a `connectorsPauseHint` string admitted *"in demo mode the action surfaces here"* — an honest note nobody could see, under a button that reported success. The card's blurb made three claims: connectors *"push records into the platform on the cadence shown"*, *"pause to disable; activate to enable"*, and *"configuration credentials are stored encrypted in the secrets vault"*. There is no vault; credentials come from environment variables and `external.properties`. |
| **🔑 Lesson** | **The fabrication did not live in the data, it lived in the type.** A field called `lastRunAt` on a catalogue no server feeds can only ever be invented, and a field called `status` that a human sets is a claim with no source. So the fix is structural rather than editorial: `status`, `lastRunAt`, `intake30d` and the per-connector `owner` email are **deleted from the interface**, and each entry now declares the `trigger` that runs it (`SCHEDULED_POLL` / `INBOUND_WEBHOOK` / `OPERATOR_INITIATED` / `NOT_IMPLEMENTED`), the `backing` symbol that provides it, and the `gate` property that must be set for it to fire. |
| **The gates — and why it takes two** | `ConnectorBackingContractTest` (backend, hermetic, 7 tests) reads `connectors.ts` and resolves every `backing` against this codebase: a claimed poll must carry **`@Scheduled` on the named method**, a claimed webhook must be a **mapped route**, an unimplemented connector must name **nothing**, and every `gate` must be a property the application actually binds. `connectorTriggerHonesty.test.ts` (frontend, 10 tests) checks what only the catalogue can answer: the retired fields have not returned, `cadence` appears **iff** `SCHEDULED_POLL`, and an unimplemented connector describes itself in the **planned voice in both languages** — because the badge is not what a reader reads. Mutation 3 is the pair's proof: a fabricated Qualys poller with a perfect shape and a nonexistent backing class **passes the frontend gate and fails the backend one**. |
| **⚠ The trigger-claim gate failed on its own correction** | `everyTriggerClaimMatchesItsOwnerClassCallerKinds` classifies each owner class's cross-class callers as container-driven (`@Scheduled` / `@EventListener`) or not, and requires a trigger claim to match. Its first run flagged **my corrected Splunk reason** — because a correction **quotes the sentence it replaces**, which is the register's convention and the only reason the corrections are auditable at all. 🔑 **A detector that reads a quotation as an assertion forces every correction to paraphrase away its own evidence.** Fixed with `unquoted()`, pinned in both directions. |
| **⚠ The census is what makes the gate non-vacuous, and it is small** | **2 of 36** `TOLERATED` owner classes have a container-driven caller: `CcmService` (via `CcmSchedulerService`) and `SanctionsHitService` (via `SanctionsScreeningSchedulerService`) — **exactly the two whose reasons already claim a scheduler drives them**, which is independent corroboration rather than a coincidence. Both legs are asserted by measurement, not by example: [[F2-192]]'s fourth surviving mutation was a negative assertion naming methods that were never in the population. |
| **Mutation** | **14/14 as declared**, including one deliberate **SURVIVES**: stripping quotations before matching the *denial* changes nothing, because no reason quotes a denial. Saying so is more honest than implying both halves of `unquoted()` are load-bearing — only the claim side is. |
| **Live probe** | **15/15.** All four adapter status routes answer (`enabled: true, mode: STUB, healthy: true`); both scanners report `pollingEnabled: false`, which is the fact the new `gate` field exists to expose; the Splunk webhook answers **401** (mapped, shared-secret — a 404 would have meant the catalogue names a route that does not exist); the manual egress route answers 200; `intake.intake_records` is **0**. Splunk's `lastSuccessfulPushAt` is **real**, read from `platform.splunk_hec_outbound_log` — which is precisely why live state belongs to the adapter panel and capability to the catalogue. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-12.** Backend suite **3,779/0/0** (+9), frontend **497/497 across 51 files** (+10), `tsc --noEmit` clean, mutation **14/14**, probe **15/15**, **0 migrations, 0 production Java lines**. The probe left one row in `platform.splunk_hec_outbound_log` (a stub-mode egress log, indistinguishable from an operator smoke test) and deleted the one `platform.integration_external_link` row it created, with `CHARINDEX`. |
| **⬜ Filed, not fixed — the product decision this exposes** | Four vendor connectors ship and **none has a domain trigger**: nothing in the platform pushes an incident to ServiceNow or an event to Splunk when one happens. The catalogue now says so and the six `TOLERATED` reasons say so, but *wiring* one is a product decision with real consequences — an outbound push transmits tenant data to a third party, so it needs a per-tenant configuration surface and an owner's call on which events qualify. The same applies to building the seven `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` connectors. **Recording the absence honestly is this slice; deciding what to build is not.** |

## F2-192 · The gate F2-188 built to verify reasons verified the one claim shape F2-188 had audited

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-192 *(measured 2026-08-11 by asking what [[F2-188]]'s new gate could **not** see. Fourth consecutive finding produced by interrogating the previous slice's own instrument — [[F2-165]]→[[F2-166]], [[F2-184]]→[[F2-185]], [[F2-187]]→[[F2-188]], this.)* |
| **Severity** | **P3** — a governance-artefact defect, not a runtime one: 0 production lines changed. It is filed because the artefact in question is the platform's own record of *what a user cannot do*, and **7 of its 18 capability claims were false**. |
| **What was wrong** | [[F2-188]] proved a named-map gate cannot prove a reason **true**, and added `noReasonAssertsUnreachabilityWithoutAScanThatVerifiesIt`. Its `UNREACHABILITY_CLAIM` pattern is scoped — deliberately and correctly — to **state-transition verbs**, because that was the claim shape it had just found false five times. But the map's **larger** bucket makes a different claim: *"no endpoint does X"*, *"only the list is wired"*, *"cannot be resolved by any route"*. A state-verb pattern is blind to it, so it was never scrutinised. |
| **The measurement** | Every one of the **18 owner classes has a live cross-class surface**, measured from the constant pool. Of the reasons resting on a capability claim: **7 outright false** — `ThreeLinesService#bandForUser` (*"the independence model is recorded and never enforced or displayed per user"*), `ChangeGovernanceHealthService#isGateConfigured` (*"an answer the platform only ever logs"*), `CommitteeCatalogService#findTemplate` (*"cannot be resolved by any route"*), `ChangeModelService#usageFor`, `ChangeManagementService#isConditional` (*"conditions attached at CAB are invisible downstream"*), `AuthorityDocumentService#citationCount`, `MlModelDriftService#listUnacknowledged`; **4 overstated** (`dispatchToUserIds`, `sendToUser`, `getTarget`, `buildAarSection`); **5 stand**, the sharpest being `EmissionFactorService#resolveActive`, where the live siblings genuinely answer a different question (`GhgEmissionRecordService` resolves a factor by stored FK, never by code + `isActive`, so the ISAE 3410 lineage question this method answers is not the one the numbers were produced with). |
| **🔑 Lesson** | **A gate that verifies claims verifies the claim shape it was written for.** That is [[F2-187]]'s own headline — *a reachability gate certifies the granularity it resolves* — arriving one level up, at the gate built to answer it. In every one of the seven cases a **routed sibling on the same class** already did the thing the reason called impossible, and the reason had been written from the dark method alone. |
| **The gate** | `everyReasonIsWrittenAgainstItsOwnerClassLiveSurface` — a reason must **cite, in method notation (`#name`), at least one live method of its own owner class**. Notation rather than a bare word because half the siblings are called `list` or `get`, and *"no endpoint **lists** unacknowledged drift"* would satisfy a substring check for `list` **while asserting its opposite**. This makes [[F2-185]](a)'s *"one file short is the whole error"* a build failure: you cannot write the entry without having read what the class already exposes. |
| **⚠ It fired on its first run, on a claim shape I had not even counted** | `SanctionsScreeningSchedulerService#setClock` was listed as a **"DECLARED TEST SEAM … reached by tests only, which is the point"**. The new seam check looks for the call site in `target/test-classes` and found **none** — not in main sources either. `SanctionsHitServiceTest` calls the identically-named setter on the **sibling** class. So the entry had been classified a seam **because the method is called `setClock`** — and the comment **three lines above it** warns, in [[F2-187]]'s own words, that *"a `setClock`-shaped exemption would let any dark method be hidden by renaming it"*. 🔑 **Naming a trap does not exempt you from it, and a warning you wrote yourself is the one you are least likely to re-read.** |
| **⚙ And that failure was the slice's only real gap** | `SanctionsScreeningSchedulerService#runSlaSweep` is a **cross-tenant sweep that flips `sla_breach = 1` and fires `SANCTIONS_HIT_SLA_BREACHED`** on an AML control, with its cutoff from `LocalDateTime.now(clock)` — and it had **no test of any kind**. The seam had been built for tests nobody wrote. Deleting the unused setter was the other option and it is the wrong one: the sweep cannot be tested deterministically without it. `SanctionsSchedulerSweepTest` (7 tests) now drives both ticks through it — cutoff arithmetic, one call per **distinct** tenant under that tenant's `TenantContext`, no tenant leak, skip-and-log on a failing tenant ([[F2-191]]'s `flipToOverdue` rule), the `DAILY` filter's `equalsIgnoreCase`, the NULL-org fallback, and the `scheduler-enabled` gate. |
| **⚠⚠ Four of my seventeen mutations survived, and all four were the mutation's fault** | (1) stripped **one** of two citations in the same reason; (2) replaced only the first of **six** concatenated string literals, leaving `#list is live` in the tail; (3) expected a **relaxed** check to fail, which it cannot do on a corpus that already satisfies the strict one; (5) asserted the cross-class narrowing against two method names it never touched — one is private (skipped on visibility), the other an entry point nothing calls. 🔑 **A negative assertion naming something that was never in the population passes for a reason unrelated to the property being tested.** Rebuilt: the narrowing is now pinned by **measurement** (34 public `@Service` methods are reached only from inside their own class, and that count drops to 0 if the narrowing is deleted), and 2/3 became a **pair** — a citation-free reason is CAUGHT under the strict check and SURVIVES under a bare-word one, which is what proves the notation requirement is load-bearing. **17/17** after the rebuild. |
| **⚠ A probe with `admin` alone would have CONFIRMED the false claim** | The live probe (**18/18**) exists because the corrections came from bytecode, and *a controller calling a service method is not proof the endpoint answers* — [[F2-158]]'s `RoleController#list` had a controller, a call site and a frontend caller and returned **500 to every request since it was written**. Probing `/three-lines/user/{id}/role-band` as `admin` returns `allBands: []` and `lod_band: []`, because PLATFORM_ADMIN maps to no line of defence — which reads exactly like *"never displayed per user"*. As `rmanager` it returns `effectiveBand: "LINE_2"` and the **JWT carries `lod_band: ["LINE_2"]`**. 🔑 **CLAUDE.md's "admin proves nothing about authorization" has a second edge: admin also proves nothing about a role-DERIVED value, and there it fails in the direction of agreeing with you.** |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-12** (measured 2026-08-11; the slice crossed local midnight, and CLAUDE.md's own F2-178 landmine is about exactly that boundary being where a date-relative claim goes wrong — so the two dates are recorded separately rather than rounded to one). Suite **3,770/0/0**, mutation **17/17**, live probe **18/18**, **0 migrations, 0 production lines, 0 frontend change**. |
| **⬜ Filed, not fixed** | `ThreeLinesService#bandForUser` is a redundant third variant (scalar / list / DTO) of one computation whose other two are routed — the [[F2-185]](a) precedent says delete. It is **left in place** because four `ThreeLinesServiceTest` cases assert the band-ranking semantics through it, so deleting it is a product decision about a tested accessor, not a fix. Same for `findTemplate`/`citationCount`/`usageFor`/`isConditional`/`isGateConfigured`, which are now correctly described as redundant variants of routed methods. |

## F2-191 · The attestation guard declared OVERDUE unreachable, and three writers reached it daily

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-191 *(measured 2026-08-11 by asking the question [[F2-190]] ended on — "how many things write this status, and how many of them ask?" — module by module)* |
| **Module** | `module/compliance/obligation` — `ObligationAttestationService` (×2) and `ObligationCampaignService`, against the per-cycle state machine in the service's own javadoc |
| **Category** | a declared lifecycle contradicted by every writer of it — the [[F2-189]]/[[F2-190]] family, fifth instance, first found deliberately rather than in passing |
| **Severity** | **P3.** No illegal state was reachable, but an F8 event carried the **wrong previous status** on a real path, and the campaign-driven escalation emitted no row-level event at all |
| **What was wrong** | `guardAttest` was a `switch` whose arms lumped `DUE`, `OVERDUE` and `IN_PROGRESS` together and allowed **none** of them to become `OVERDUE`. Three writers set it directly, none calling the guard: `markOverdueForCampaign`, `sweepOverdueForOrg` (daily, via `ComplianceDeadlineScheduler`) and `ObligationCampaignService#escalateOverdue`. **Three artefacts, three answers** — and the one that was right was the class javadoc, whose state machine says `DUE → … \| OVERDUE` and `IN_PROGRESS → … \| OVERDUE`. |
| **The two consequences reading one file could not show** | ① **The event lied about the previous status.** Both sweeps called `emit("OBLIGATION_OVERDUE", a, "DUE")` with the literal `"DUE"`, while their own candidate query selects `DUE` **or** `IN_PROGRESS` — so a cycle an officer had already started was reported to the rule engine as never begun. ② **The campaign path was silent.** Its copy of the loop emitted no per-attestation event at all, only the campaign-level `OBLIGATION_CAMPAIGN_ESCALATED`, so an F8 rule keyed on the row-level trigger saw nothing for campaign-driven escalation — the [[F2-188]] payload-divergence shape, in its most extreme form: not a different key, no event. |
| **✅ What shipped** | `ATTEST_TRANSITIONS` replaces the `switch`, saying exactly what the javadoc says; `mayAttest` is the shared predicate; `guardAttest` reads it; both sweeps share one `flipToOverdue(candidates)` that consults the guard, **skips and logs** a row the table forbids rather than aborting a daily batch half-way, and passes each row's **real** previous status to `emit`; and `ObligationCampaignService#escalateOverdue` calls `markOverdueForCampaign` instead of keeping a third loop, taking its roll-up from what was actually flipped. |
| **⚙ The gate noticed the fix was incomplete, for the second time** | `markOverdueForCampaign` was in [[F2-187]]'s dark-method map with the reason *"the two must not diverge"* — they already had. Giving it a caller made `aToleratedEntryThatGainedACallerMustLoseItsEntry` fail, which is the both-directions half of that map doing its job (the first time was `markOverdue` in F2-188). |
| **⚠ The prose is now the specification, and the build enforces it** | `AttestationOverdueGuardTest.theProseAndTheTableAgree` parses the javadoc's arrow lines and compares them edge for edge with `ATTEST_TRANSITIONS`. Deliberate: F2-190 found a lifecycle described in a comment and implemented as something else, and here the comment was the only correct artefact — so the cheapest defence is to make the prose fail the build when it drifts. |
| **⚠ Two of my own errors in this slice, both caught by a test** | ① I wrote in `ATTEST_TRANSITIONS`' comment that the campaign escalation could flip a `NOT_APPLICABLE` cycle to OVERDUE. It cannot — `escalateOverdue`'s query filters to `DUE`/`IN_PROGRESS`; I had read a status filter belonging to a **different method** of that class. The claim is left in the file as a correction rather than deleted, because [[F2-188]]'s lesson is that fluent prose in an authoritative place reads as verification, *including when it is mine and wrong*. ② The structural assertion first read `doesNotContain("setAttestationStatus(")`, which fails on the campaign's legitimate `setAttestationStatus("DUE")` when it materialises cycles — **entity creation is not a transition**, the same distinction that made `setStatus("DRAFT")` F2-189's 52-writer false positive. |
| **⚠ And an existing test had pinned the campaign's own copy of the loop as correct** | `escalateOverdue_flipsOverdueRowsAndAdvancesCampaign` stubbed the attestation *repository* and counted saves — so it asserted the unguarded, event-less loop as the expected behaviour. Fifth instance in this programme of a test that agreed with the implementation it was written from. |
| **⚙ The measurement, and its honest limit** | The sweep asked: per module package, which (setter, state) pairs have more than one writing class where at least one holds a transition table? **13 groups from 55 table-holding classes** — and **12 were false positives**, because a package is not an entity: `[bcm] setStatus("DRAFT")` lists nine services that each create a different entity. Only the obligation-attestation group was a genuine same-entity case, and confirming even that needed opening the file (`ObligationCampaignService`'s table governs the *campaign's* status, not the attestation's). 🔑 **A same-package proxy for same-entity is 1-in-13 precise here; it is a locator, and the reading is the measurement.** |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-11.** Suite **3,761/0/0**, 0 migrations, 0 frontend change. |
| **Lesson** | ⚙ **Five instances now** ([[F2-175]], [[F2-188]], [[F2-189]], [[F2-190]], this) of one shape: a status a service owns, written by something that never asks. Four were found by accident from different angles; this one by asking the question directly — and the yield was **one real defect out of thirteen candidates**, which is the honest cost of asking. ⚙ The recurring detail worth internalising: **each duplicate agreed with the original on the part that is easy to check and differed on the audit trail.** The row always ended up in the right state. What differed was the event, the previous status, or nothing being emitted at all — and none of those is visible from the row. |

## F2-190 · The evidence bridge was the third writer of workflow status, and its "drive through the state machine" comment drove around it

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-190 *(measured 2026-08-11 by following the lead [[F2-189]] recorded and deferred — "a third copy of a status vocabulary in one module, compared to neither of the other two")* |
| **Module** | `module/workflow/requests` — `WorkflowEvidenceBridge` vs `WorkflowRequestService.TRANSITIONS`. Third writer, after the interactive service and the SLA sweep |
| **Category** | a control described in a comment and implemented as something else — the [[F2-189]] family, one file over |
| **Severity** | **P3, latent** — measured before grading: **0** evidence requests anchored to `WORKFLOW_REQUEST` in dev or prod, **0** events authored by `evidence-bridge`, 0 requests in DRAFT or RETURNED. The bridge has never run |
| **What was wrong** | Its comment said *"Drive through the WF-1 machine: pre-submit states hop via SUBMITTED first"*, and it wrote `setStatus` directly. Two hard-coded sets — `TERMINAL` (4) and `PRE_SUBMIT` (7) — covered **11 of the table's 16** states. For the five in neither (`DRAFT`, `SUBMITTED`, `UNDER_REVIEW`, `RETURNED`, `RESUBMITTED`) it wrote the outcome straight in, and the table forbids two of those moves: **`DRAFT → APPROVED`** — a request nobody ever sent, marked approved by an evidence event, when DRAFT's only legal continuations are `SENT` and `CLOSED` — and **`RETURNED → APPROVED`**, which must pass through `RESUBMITTED` because that is what "returned for changes" means (plus `RETURNED → RETURNED`, an undeclared self-loop, on a rejection). |
| **🔑 And the hop was decorative** | `setStatus("SUBMITTED")` immediately followed by `setStatus(target)` collapses: the row never rested in SUBMITTED, no event recorded it, and nothing downstream could tell the hop had happened. 🔑 **A control described in a comment and implemented as two consecutive writes runs as neither** — it neither satisfies the state machine (which was never consulted) nor leaves the trail it implies. |
| **✅ What shipped** | `WorkflowRequestService.hopVia(from, to)` beside [[F2-189]]'s `mayTransition` — the single intermediate that makes a move legal in two hops, **capped at depth 2 on purpose**: `DRAFT → SENT → SUBMITTED → APPROVED` exists in the table, and walking it would have an evidence approval *send* the request on the requester's behalf. The bridge now asks direct-then-hop-then-refuse, records the hop as its own event so the trail matches the machine, and leaves the row untouched when there is no route. `PRE_SUBMIT` is **deleted**, not left unread — an unread second opinion is how the next reader decides it is the authority. `TERMINAL` stays, documented as a product decision: `APPROVED`/`REJECTED` are not graph-terminal, but an already-decided request must not be re-decided by a late evidence event. |
| **⚠ The candidate order is declared, not incidental** | `SUBMITTED` first (the original intent), then `RESUBMITTED`, then alphabetical. [[F2-186]] is a live finding about a regulator-facing answer that depended on `HashMap` iteration order; a hop chosen by whichever state a `Set` happened to yield first is the same defect in a lifecycle. |
| **⚠⚠ An existing test had pinned the collapsed behaviour as correct** | `WorkflowEvidenceBridgeTest.approvedEvidence_drivesOpenRequestToApproved` asserted `verify(eventRepo).save(any())` — Mockito's *exactly once* — which is only true while the hop is invisible. `IN_PROGRESS → APPROVED` is not in the table, so the correct behaviour is two events. Fourth instance in this programme of a test that agreed with the implementation it was written from ([[F2-159]], [[F2-175]], [[F2-174]], this). |
| **⚠ And my own new test asserted an API I expected rather than the one I wrote** | The first draft of `hopViaAnswersOnlyItsOwnQuestion` asserted that `hopVia("SUBMITTED","APPROVED")` is empty *because a direct move exists* — the convenience the implementation deliberately refuses, with the reason in its javadoc two lines above. It failed, returning `UNDER_REVIEW`. 🔑 **A test written from a method's name instead of its contract asserts the API you expected**, and it happened to fail safe only by luck. The contract stands: merging "no hop needed" and "no hop exists" into one empty `Optional` is how a caller writes a bypass by accident. |
| **Gates** | `WorkflowEvidenceBridgeLegalityTest` (9): DRAFT refused with no write, no event and no notification; RETURNED reaching APPROVED via RESUBMITTED with **both** hops recorded and the deciding event starting where the hop left the row; the rejection path not self-looping; SENT still hopping via SUBMITTED (now visibly); UNDER_REVIEW decided directly with exactly one event; terminal ignored; `hopVia`'s contract; the structural leg that `PRE_SUBMIT` is gone; and the invariant — for every non-terminal state, both outcomes are reachable in ≤1 hop **or** the state is named in the expected-refusal set, which is `containsExactly("DRAFT -> APPROVED", "DRAFT -> RETURNED")` so a state joining or leaving it fails the build. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-11.** Suite **3,755/0/0**, 0 migrations, 0 frontend change. All three writers of workflow-request status now consult one table. |
| **Lesson** | ⚙ **Three writers, three slices, one shape.** [[F2-175]] (a peer module constructing the entity), [[F2-188]] (a sweep duplicating a transition), [[F2-189]] (a scheduler ignoring the table), this (a bridge with its own hop list). Each was found from a different angle and none of the earlier fixes would have caught the later ones. 🔑 **When a module has a declared state machine, the question worth asking is not "is it correct?" but "how many things write this status, and how many of them ask?"** |

## F2-189 · The workflow engine's SLA sweep performed a transition its own lifecycle table forbids

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-189 *(measured 2026-08-11 by generalising [[F2-188]]'s shape — a scheduler writing a state a service owns)* |
| **Module** | `module/workflow/requests` — `WorkflowRequestSlaScheduler` vs `WorkflowRequestService.TRANSITIONS`. The engine `CLAUDE.md` records as **adopted by 14 modules** |
| **Category** | two lists that had to agree with nothing comparing them — the [[F2-156]] class, with a **declared state machine** on one side and a **scheduler's scan list** on the other |
| **Severity** | **P3, and latent** — measured before grading: **0** events recording the illegal transition in dev, **0** in prod, **0** candidate rows today. What is wrong is that the engine's declared contract was not the authority on its own lifecycle |
| **What was wrong** | `WorkflowRequestService.TRANSITIONS` is the declared lifecycle: `transition()` answers `IllegalTransitionException` → **409** outside it, and it is what a reader, the frontend and `WorkflowEvidenceBridge` consult to know which states are reachable. It declared `REOPENED → {IN_PROGRESS, SUBMITTED, ESCALATED, CLOSED}` — **no OVERDUE**. `WorkflowRequestSlaScheduler` kept its own `OVERDUE_SCAN_STATUSES`, which **includes `REOPENED`**, and wrote `r.setStatus("OVERDUE")` directly. So a reopened request past its due date would be flipped **on a schedule** into a state the table says it cannot reach, while the identical move through the API was refused. |
| **The second, quieter half** | When a WF-10 multi-tier ladder climbed a rung on a request already in OVERDUE, the code re-set `OVERDUE`. The table declares no `OVERDUE → OVERDUE` self-loop, so every tier climb was also an undeclared transition. ⚠ **Unobservable in the data by construction** — it writes the same value, so "did it happen" cannot be answered from the database, and this row does not claim it was seen. Advancing the tier never needed a status write. |
| **⚠ Which side was wrong, and why that is not obvious** | The **sweep** was right about the product: a reopened request with a due date in the past *is* overdue, and refusing to escalate it would be the worse bug. So the table was **completed** (one edge added) rather than the behaviour changed — and the sweep now asks `WorkflowRequestService.mayTransition` instead of holding a second opinion. That is [[F2-178]]'s shape: **one predicate, read by both**. The wrong instinct here would be to "fix" the sweep to skip REOPENED, which would silently stop escalating a class of overdue request. |
| **✅ Gates** | `WorkflowSlaTransitionLegalityTest` (8). The load-bearing one is `everyStatusTheSweepScansMayBecomeOverdue` — it compares the two lists that diverged, which is the thing nobody was doing. Completing the table makes the runtime skip branch unreachable through the scan list, so per [[F2-183]]'s rule it is exercised directly with a state the lifecycle genuinely forbids (`APPROVED`) rather than assumed. Plus: REOPENED still escalates and its event records `from = REOPENED`; a tier climb advances `escalationLevel` **without** a status write; the table has no dangling targets; and two anti-vacuity legs (the table resolved ≥15 states, the scan list still contains REOPENED and OVERDUE). |
| **⚠ Two measurement mistakes worth recording, both caught by looking** | ① The first sweep grouped `set*Status("LITERAL")` by **setter name** across the tree and reported `setStatus("DRAFT")` with **52 writers** at the top of the work list — 52 *different entity types* each getting a creation default, collapsed into one row because the grouping key was not the thing being measured. Sixth instance of that in this repository, and it presented as the highest-priority finding. Re-scoped to the question F2-188 actually proved — *does a `@Scheduled` class write a state a service owns?* — the answer is a readable **8 of 31 schedulers**, of which most are the owner of the state they write. ② The database probe first reported **1** `OVERDUE → OVERDUE` event as the self-write having fired; reading the row showed it is an **`ESCALATED`** event whose from/to are both OVERDUE *because the status correctly did not change*. 🔑 **An event whose from and to are equal is not evidence of a write.** |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-11.** Suite **3,746/0/0**, 0 migrations, 0 frontend change. |
| **Lesson** | ⚙ **A declared state machine is only a control if the code that changes state consults it.** `TRANSITIONS` was a good artefact — explicit, complete-looking, 409 on violation — and one of its two writers had never read it. ⚙ And the generalisation from [[F2-188]] held but was narrower than hoped: of 31 `@Scheduled` classes, **8** write a state literal and most of those *are* the owning service with a scheduled method, which is legitimate. The population worth reading was two. **A shape that produced one real defect does not imply a population.** |
| **⚙ Noted, not fixed** | `WorkflowEvidenceBridge` holds a **third** list of "open" statuses (`SENT, ASSIGNED, IN_PROGRESS, WAITING_RESPONSE, REOPENED, ESCALATED, OVERDUE`). It answers a different question — which statuses are open for evidence bridging, not which transitions are legal — so it is not the same defect, but it is a third copy of a status vocabulary in one module and nothing compares it to either of the other two. |

## F2-188 · A named-map gate proved its reasons existed, not that they were true — and all five of the strongest were false

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-188 *(measured 2026-08-11, the day after [[F2-187]] shipped, by starting to work its highest-graded members)* |
| **Module** | the instrument (`DarkServiceMethodTest`) · `module/admin/committee` (`CommitteeScheduledSweep`, `CommitteeActionItemService`) |
| **Category** | a measurement whose *population* was right and whose *reasons* were unverified — and one real duplicated state transition found by auditing them |
| **Severity** | **P2 for the instrument** (it published five false severity claims into the register, which is what a register is for), **P3 for the code defect** (a governance register's overdue transition never reaching the audit ledger) |
| **What was wrong with the instrument** | [[F2-187]] holds 38 dark methods as a named map with a reason each, and grouped five under *"A state nothing can ever move to: the sharpest bucket, because the row just sits."* Working them found **all five false**: `CcmService#recordRun` is a *third* entry point to `recordRunInternal` (`CcmSchedulerService#tick` is `@Scheduled(fixedDelay = 60_000)` and `POST /ccm/tests/{id}/run-now` exists); `ObligationAttestationService#markOverdueForCampaign` was **superseded** by `sweepOverdueForOrg`, and `ComplianceDeadlineScheduler`'s javadoc *names the method it replaced*; `IrPlaybookService#recordInvocation` was superseded by `IrPlaybookRunService`, whose comment says it preserves *"the legacy invocation semantics the dashboard + F8 rules rely on"*; `ThreatIntelService#markActioned` carries *"Legacy shim — the old 'mark done' path … now records a REVIEWED action"* **one line above the signature I read**. |
| **🔑 The lesson, and why the existing gate could not help** | `everyToleratedEntryCarriesARealReason` enforces that a reason is **substantial**. Nothing enforced that it was **true**. 🔑 **A named-map gate proves a reason exists; it cannot prove the reason is true — so the reasons are the least-verified part of the most authoritative-looking artefact.** Worse: the substantiality check *caused* this. It rejected six of my first-draft labels, so I rewrote them as fluent prose naming a consequence, and **fluency reads as verification.** |
| **⚠ Fourth consecutive instance of one error** | Four of the five truths were in a comment I had not opened — the scheduler's, the replacement's, or the method's own javadoc. [[F2-179]] (*"`ExerciseObserverService` is open"*), [[F2-185]](a) (*"the retaliation lifecycle cannot be closed"*), [[F2-174]] (a test comment arguing the defect was correct) and now this. 🔑 **One file short is the whole error**, and the file is almost always the neighbour — the caller, the replacement, or the line above. |
| **The one real defect the audit found, and it is narrower than the claim** | `CommitteeScheduledSweep` flipped an action item to OVERDUE **in place** — `a.setStatus("OVERDUE"); actions.save(a);` — while `CommitteeActionItemService#markOverdue` existed, owned the transition, and said in its javadoc *"Called by the scheduled sweep."* Because the sweep is the **only** producer of OVERDUE in production, two things followed that neither file showed alone: **(a)** no `ACTION_OVERDUE` row had ever been written for any tenant — the only audit trace is the dedup marker `COM_FIRE:COMMITTEE_ACTION_OVERDUE · "Sweep fired …"`, which records that a *trigger* fired, not that a status changed and from what, on a register V158's own rule text calls *"the primary evidence that committees follow through"*; **(b)** the two emitters sent the same trigger name with **different payload keys** — `ownerName` against `owner`, and no `fromStatus`/`toStatus` — so the service's shape never occurred, and a rule keyed on `owner` would match nothing. Latent, because AR-148 carries `condition_json = '{}'`; `AutomationRuleEngine`'s javadoc already records one condition that compared `"" == "HIGH"` and so could never match for any payload. |
| **🔑 Why a duplicated transition hides so well** | It agrees with the original on the part that is easy to check — the row ends up OVERDUE — and differs on the parts nothing asserts: the audit sentence and the payload keys. Any test reading `status` passes over it. This is the [[F2-175]] single-writer family with a *scheduler* as the second writer instead of a peer module. |
| **✅ What shipped** | ① The sweep calls `markOverdue`, and `publishTransition` emits the **union** of the two payloads — both `owner` and `ownerName` deliberately, because four triggers have only ever sent the first and one only the second, and silently retiring either is a behaviour change to a notification path dressed as a refactor. ② The five reasons rewritten to what the methods are (redundant entry point / superseded / legacy shim), each **naming its live twin**. ③ `markOverdue` left the map — it has a caller, which the both-directions assertion required. ④ The new gate: a reason may make an unreachability claim only if the entry declares the (entity, state) in `CLAIMS_NO_OTHER_WRITER`, which the test then verifies by scanning for other writers. **Empty today, and that is the finding rather than a gap.** ⑤ `CommitteeOverdueTransitionTest` (6) pins the audit sentence, the union payload, *exactly one* event (the obvious wrong fix — call the service **and** keep the publish — double-escalates to the owner's line manager), that the service's guard still decides, and a structural leg that the sweep contains no `setStatus(`. |
| **⚠ The new gate's own first draft invented three findings** | It matched bare `is NEVER` and `nothing routes`, and flagged three reasons that were **already correct and already method-level** — `hideHost` (*"containment IS reachable; #hideHost is a second containment verb nothing routes to"*), `pushCyberIncident`, `hasRecentApprovedAssessment`. "Nothing calls this method" is what the bytecode measurement establishes; "no path anywhere moves a row into this state" is the stronger claim that sets severity. 🔑 **A scan not scoped to the shape of the claim invents findings** — the fifth instance in this repository, after the javadoc-as-code endpoint count, the 0-of-389 sweep, the phantom 75 types and the `VALID_NDI_TABS`/`ck_change_risk` pairing. |
| **⚙ A strengthening worth knowing about** | Routing through the service makes the transition **tenant-scoped** (`findByIdAndOrganisationId(id, TenantContext…)`) where the in-place flip trusted the candidate query alone. `tick()` sets the tenant per organisation before calling, so it holds in production; the test has to set it by hand, which is how the change surfaced. |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-11.** Suite **3,738/0/0**, 0 migrations, 0 frontend change. [[F2-187]]'s population is now **37** and its severity claim is corrected in place rather than quietly dropped. |
| **Lesson** | ⚙ **The first act of working a finding should be re-reading its own strongest sentence.** Five of five here, three of ten in [[F2-184]]'s hand-off, the urgency claim in [[F2-174]], the P2 in [[F2-185]](a), the "why it matters" in [[F2-183]]. That is now consistent enough to be a rule rather than an observation: **a filing's measurements are more reliable than its reasons, and its reasons are more reliable than its recommendations** — and severity lives in the reasons. |

## F2-182 · Five open writers, not ten — and the two "control bypasses" this row claimed were unreachable

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-182 *(filed 2026-08-11 as the residual population of [[F2-179]]'s scoped sweep; **worked the same day, and the first act of working it was refuting its own headline**)* |
| **Module** | `ai/governance`, `cyber/asm`, `sust/sgi`, `platform/calendar` (genuinely open) · `ndi/compliance`, `risk/kri` (closed anyway, see below) · `bcm/cycle`, `sust/cma`, `sust/tcfd` (already closed, left alone and pinned) |
| **Category** | [[F2-179]]'s casing family — but the finding's own defect is a different and more useful one: **a static scan answering a dataflow question it cannot answer** |
| **Severity** | **P3 Medium.** The row said P3 "but read the two control bypasses first". There are no control bypasses; the worst real site is an ASM risk score. |
| **⚠⚠ Read this first: 6 of the 10 sites were already closed, including both the row called control bypasses** | The filing classified a writer as *open* whenever the setter's argument came from the request. Measured by reading the code, a guard can sit in at least **four** places a setter-call-site regex cannot see: ① a conjunction in the **same `if`** (`NdiComplianceAssessmentService.update` — `COMPLIANCE_STATUSES.contains(...) && `); ② a **shared `validate()`** called by every mutation path (`KriDefinitionService.validateEnums`, `CmaDisclosureService.validate`, `TcfdItemService.validate`); ③ an **`if` block wrapping** the setter (`BcmRiskService`); ④ a **bean-validation annotation on the DTO** (`SgiCreateRequest`). 🔑 **"Is this writer closed?" is a dataflow question, and a regex over setter call sites cannot answer it** — it can only tell you where to go and read. |
| **The corrected per-site verdict** | **OPEN (5 columns, 4 sites):** `ai_governance.ml_model_audit.audit_type` + `.status` (`@NotBlank @Size(max=40)` only, no vocabulary check anywhere) · `cyber.attack_surface_finding.severity` (`@NotBlank @Size(max=20)` only) · `sust.sgi_commitment.value_source` (**update only** — `PUT /{id}` binds the entity with **no `@Valid` at all**, so the DTO's `@Pattern` never ran on that path) · `platform.calendar_events.recurrence`. **CLOSED, claim refuted:** `ndi.compliance_assessment.compliance_status` · `risk.kri_definition.value_direction` · `.source_query_type` · `bcm.bcm_risks.control_effectiveness` · `sust.cma_disclosure.disclosure_status` · `sust.tcfd_item.disclosure_status`. |
| **⚠ The worst real site was the one described as "a dashboard KPI undercounts"** | `cyber.attack_surface_finding.severity`. `AttackSurfaceAssetService.SEVERITY_WEIGHT.getOrDefault(severity, …get("LOW"))` scored an asset carrying a lower-case `critical` finding at **15 instead of 100**; `pickHighestOpenSeverity` skipped the row and returned `"LOW"`; and the critical-findings KPI omitted it. An internet-facing asset with an open critical finding read as the platform's **lowest** risk band. This is the inverted-indicator harm the row attributed to the KRI column, and it fails **open** — the number that exists to raise an alarm is the number that goes quiet. Probed live: `risk_score` **100.00**, `severity` byte-exact `CRITICAL` under `Latin1_General_100_BIN2`. |
| **⚙ Two consequences the row overstated, corrected rather than quietly dropped** | **(a) `sgi_commitment.value_source`** was described as guarding "a refresh that should not run". It could not run: `computeSourcedValue` switches on the *same* string, also case-sensitively, and returns empty for `'manual'` — so the background sweep no-ops and the endpoint still refuses, just with the wrong message ("no source data available" instead of "has no linked source"). 🔑 **A second case-sensitive comparison downstream had accidentally neutralised the first one's defect.** That is luck, not design, and it evaporates the moment anyone gives that switch a `default` branch. **(b) `calendar_events.recurrence`** was described as "picking the wrong RRULE". `rruleFor` has `default -> null` and the caller emits nothing when null, so the `.ics` carried **no recurrence rule at all** — a quarterly audit day or DR test subscribed once and never again. |
| **⚠⚠ The calendar site carried a sub-finding worth more than the casing fix** | `CalendarEventDto` declared `@Pattern(regexp = "NONE\|DAILY\|WEEKLY\|MONTHLY\|QUARTERLY\|ANNUAL")` on `recurrence` — and **that class is the outbound payload**, assembled by `fromEntity()`. Both endpoints bind the nested `CalendarEventDto.CreateRequest`, whose `recurrence` had no annotation. Bean validation runs only against a parameter marked `@Valid`, so the constraint protected nothing. 🔑 **A validation constraint on a response DTO is worse than none, because it answers the question a reader was about to ask.** Same family as the `safeRole(role){return role;}` decoy ([[F2-175]], [[F2-179]]) — but the tell is *structural*, not lexical: the class is never a `@RequestBody`. Deleted rather than relocated: an `@Pattern` **refuses** `'monthly'` where the vocabulary **normalises** it, and a regex inside an annotation can never be checked against `chk_calendar_recurrence`. ⚙ A general sweep for this shape was attempted and **abandoned**: the scan attributed nested records to their container class and reported 75 "dead" types, of which the first one checked (`AsmDtos.FindingRequest`) is bound and validated. Not shipped, not counted — filed as **[[F2-184]]** to do properly by reflection. |
| **The two closed sites that were closed anyway, and why that is not gold-plating** | `ndi.compliance_assessment.compliance_status` and `risk.kri_definition.value_direction` had **no reachable defect** — but both gate a control, and in both the *read* was case-sensitive. A row carrying that casing from any other origin (a data fix, a restore, a future importer) would have walked through an NCA/NDI approval gate, or inverted a KRI's bands. 🔑 **Reachability was the only thing protecting them, and reachability is a fact about today rather than a property of a control.** The KRI failure mode is the sharper of the two: the column holds exactly **two** tokens, so a mismatch does not degrade to a default — it silently selects the opposite branch. An LCR of 95% against a 130/120 ladder is a serious breach and reads GREEN inverted. |
| **⚙ One deliberate behaviour change, stated rather than slipped in** | `NdiComplianceAssessmentService.update` used to **silently ignore** an unrecognised `complianceStatus`: the caller supplied the field, got **200**, and the status had not moved. It is now a 400 naming the value, consistent with `setStatus`. No request the register screen can send is affected (the status is a fixed dropdown); an integration whose casing differs now **succeeds** where it previously received a 400 from `setStatus` or a silent no-op from `update`. |
| **🔑 The new decision rule, which retires F2-179's per-field agonising for this whole family** | F2-179 established that `require` vs `coerce` is a product decision, and cited `CyberInputValidation`'s line — *no request that succeeds today can start failing*. The decisive test turns out to be mechanical: **ask whether a coercion already exists upstream.** Where one does (the whistleblower portal's `safeSeverity` returned `MEDIUM` and *the report arrived*), out-of-vocabulary values succeed today and `coerce` is mandatory. Where none does, the **CHECK constraint is already refusing** everything outside the vocabulary — so every value that succeeds today is a case-variant of a legal token, and `require` **cannot break a working request**. It only converts a CHECK violation into a 400 that names the field, and normalises the casing that currently slips through. All five sites here are the second kind, hence `require` (and `orDefault` for `recurrence`, where `NONE` is a real member rather than a null stand-in). |
| **What shipped** | Five vocabularies on the open sites (`CK_ml_audit_type`, `CK_ml_audit_status`, `CK_asm_finding_severity`, `ck_sgi_value_source`, `chk_calendar_recurrence`) plus three on the closed-anyway ones (`ck_ndi_comp_status`, `CK_kri_def_direction`, `CK_kri_def_source`) — eight new `ClosedVocabulary` declarations, all picked up automatically by `ClosedVocabularyPinTest` and all agreeing with the migration SQL on the first run. Named constants for every literal a side effect or gate compares against. `SgiCreateRequest`'s `@Pattern` and `CalendarEventDto`'s misplaced one both **deleted**, so each column has exactly one authority. `CalendarService.applyCreate` made package-private static — visible for testing, see the mutation row. **0 migrations, 0 frontend change.** |
| **Gates** | `HandRolledVocabularyMirrorTest` (2) — **the durable half**: the six hand-rolled `Set<String>` mirrors this slice deliberately did *not* convert, read by reflection and compared against their `CHECK` constraints. Directional on purpose (a Java set **wider** than its column is a latent 409; **narrower** is policy, printed not failed), with an anti-vacuity floor on the comparison count. All six were exactly equal. · `NdiComplianceStatusVocabularyTest` (9) — the approve gate holds against a row **no writer could have produced**, plus the negative control that a compliant item still approves and the SoD refusal still fires. · `KriDefinitionVocabularyTest` (5) — a class that did not exist; see below. · `CalendarRecurrenceVocabularyTest` (5) — including the reflective leg that the outbound DTO declares no constraint, with an anti-vacuity check that the same walk *does* see `eventType`'s real one. · `MlModelAuditServiceTest` +6, `AttackSurfaceFindingServiceTest` +4 (one of them states the 100-vs-15 arithmetic against the real weight map), `SgiCommitmentServiceTest` +4, `KriMeasurementServiceTest` +4. |
| **Mutation** | **26/27 caught**, and the two survivors it started with are worth more than the score. **(a)** The mutation removing normalisation from `KriDefinitionService.applyFields` survived — not because a test was weak but because `KriDefinitionService` **had never been tested directly**; the KRI module had measurement and breach tests and the register half was covered only incidentally. 🔑 **A mutation harness reports "this class has no tests" as a survivor, which is how the gap became visible to a green suite and to a coverage figure nobody reads per-class.** `KriDefinitionVocabularyTest` exists because of it. **(b)** Two calendar mutations survived because the test was calling `RECURRENCE.orDefault(...)` **itself** rather than the writer that uses it. 🔑 **A test that reaches around the code under test measures the library, which was never in doubt** — the same mistake twice in one class, the second time letting an `orDefault → coerce` swap through, which would silently record a typo'd recurrence as `NONE`. Fixed by driving the real `applyCreate` (made package-private static for exactly this). **The one remaining survivor is genuinely unkillable without changing behaviour**: restoring `"MANUAL".equals(…)` in the SGI *quiet sweep* changes no observable outcome, because `computeSourcedValue` switches on the same string case-sensitively and returns empty either way. Reported as a survivor with the reason rather than as 27/27 with a contrived test. |
| **⚠⚠ Two ways the harness itself lied, both fixed, both the class of bug it exists to find** | **(a)** Mutation 17 edits one file twice. Backups were keyed per *edit*, so the second edit wrote the `.mutbak` from the **already-mutated** text, then the restore loop read a path it had already unlinked — crashing, and **leaving edit 1 in the tree**. Caught by `git status`, not by the harness. 🔑 **A second write to the thing that is meant to be the record of the original** is the double-save shape from [[F2-175]] in a tool rather than a service — and a tool that silently corrupts the tree it measures is worse than no tool. **(b)** A wrong assertion of mine left the baseline **red**, and the harness then reported mutation 08 — an SGI change — as *"CAUGHT by CalendarRecurrenceVocabularyTest"*, which is not causally possible. 🔑 **A mutation harness run against a red suite reports every mutation as caught.** It now runs the unmutated suite first and aborts if it is not green. ⚙ The wrong assertion is itself worth a line: `assertThat(e.getRecurrence()).isNull()` on the refusal path fails against *correct* code, because `CalendarEvent` initialises the field to `NONE` — the assertion is "still the entity default", not "null". |
| **Live probe (43/43)** | Backend on :8084 from a freshly built jar; prod :8090 untouched throughout. Real personas, not `admin`, wherever a guard allowed: `rmanager` (ROLE_RISK_MANAGER) for the ML-audit and KRI legs, `so_officer` (ROLE_CISO + SUSTAINABILITY_OFFICER) for ASM and SGI. **A (13):** a `fairness`/`passed` audit → 201, both columns byte-exact under `Latin1_General_100_BIN2`, `has_fairness_audit` **flipped** (asserted false first, not assumed), `last_fairness_audit_date` stamped, and `GET …/audits/latest/FAIRNESS` returning the row the casing also hid from it; unknown tokens 400 naming field *and* value; and a lower-case `explainability`/`failed` audit as the negative control, with `has_explainability_doc` asserted **still false**. **B (6) — the arithmetic, on one asset:** a fresh PUBLIC/CRITICAL asset scores **15.00** (the LOW fallback — exactly where a lower-case critical finding used to leave it), and after the `severity: "critical"` finding it scores **100.00**. **C (5):** `create` now accepts `'manual'` (the deleted `@Pattern` used to 400 it) and `PUT` stores `GHG_TOTAL` byte-exact. **D (4):** `recurrence: "quarterly"` stored `QUARTERLY`, and the `.ics` carries `RRULE:FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=3;UNTIL=20270901T235959Z` where it previously carried no RRULE line at all. **E (5):** `higher_is_better` accepted and normalised, and a measurement of **95 against green 130 evaluates RED** through the real evaluator. **F (5):** the NDI row — a lower-case status now succeeds, an impossible one still refused naming the value, and `update` refuses instead of accepting-then-ignoring. **G (3):** cleanup by id captured at creation plus a `CHARINDEX` belt, the borrowed NDI row restored field by field (it happened to be sitting in `EVIDENCE_REQUIRED`), every table back to baseline as a **failing** leg, and an anti-vacuity leg asserting the probe created rows at all — 8 of them. |
| **⚙ Six probe bugs, every one of them mine, and two named by the platform's own diagnostics** | `@Valid` fires before the service, so an omitted `@NotNull auditDate` made the 400 name the wrong field and the vocabulary check never ran — the F2-179 owner-ids trap again · the "latest" route is `/audits/latest/{auditType}`, a path variable, not a query parameter · `finding_type: "RCE"` is not one of the ten `CK_asm_finding_type` allows, and **the 409 named the column** (F2-180's diagnostic fix earning its keep — the old wording would have sent me hunting a foreign key) · `UQ_ml_audit_model_type_date` refuses a second audit of the same type on the same date · `attack_surface_asset` has no `severity` column, which turned out better: scoring the same asset before and after is a stronger claim than reading a stored label · and the probe **crashed on its own output**, because the Windows console is cp1252 and the leg labels carry `⚠`. 🔑 **A probe whose output crashes it reports nothing** — `sys.stdout.reconfigure` rather than dropping the characters. |
| **Effort** | M (8 vocabularies across 7 services, 2 DTO annotations deleted, 3 new test classes + 4 extended, ~60 assertions, 27 mutations, 43 probe legs, **0 migrations, 0 frontend change**) |
| **Status** | ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-11.** Backend suite **3,671/0/0**, FE **487/487** in 50 files + `tsc` clean (**0 frontend files touched** — run because "no FE change" is a claim, not an exemption), mutation **26/27** (the survivor explained; the confirming full sweep re-ran all 27 against a green baseline and agreed — 1 survived, **0 false kills, 0 skipped, 0 `.mutbak` residue**), live probe **43/43**, `mvn -o clean package` hermetic, census `--check` clean. The last two mutations are the ones worth naming, because they are the durable instruments proving themselves rather than the fixes: widening a hand-rolled mirror past its column was caught by `HandRolledVocabularyMirrorTest`, and re-adding the misplaced `@Pattern` to the outbound DTO was caught by `CalendarRecurrenceVocabularyTest.theOutboundDtoDoesNotPretendToValidate`. Filed on the way out: **[[F2-184]]** (bean-validation constraints on types never bound as a request body — do it by reflection, not the regex that failed here). |
| **Lesson** | ⚙ **A static scan cannot answer a dataflow question**, and a finding that gets reachability wrong makes correctness look urgent: this row named two control bypasses that no caller could reach, and under-described the one site where a risk score actually inverted. ⚙ **Reachability is a fact about today, not a property of a control** — which is why the two refuted sites were closed anyway. ⚙ **`require` is free wherever no upstream coercion exists**, because the CHECK is already refusing; that retires the per-field argument for this whole family. ⚙ **A mutation survivor can mean "this class has no tests"** rather than "this assertion is weak" — the most useful thing the harness found was a missing test class. ⚙ **A test that reaches around the code under test proves the library works.** ⚙ And the recurring one, third instance: **read the code before believing a register row's claim about it, including your own — written yesterday.** |

## F2-179 · A lowercase severity passes the CHECK constraint and silently skips the auto-escalation

|  |  |
|---|---|
| **ID** | F2-179 *(filed 2026-08-10 while working [[F2-175]] — found by asking what validates the trigger, after noticing the request DTO constrains severity only by length)* |
| **Module** | `module/ai/governance` (`MlModelDriftService#record`, `AiGovernanceDtos.DriftObservationRequest`) — and the shape is not local to it |
| **Category** | Two artefacts that must agree where one **cannot** enforce the agreement — the [[F2-94]] recipient-key class, in a third disguise: a case-insensitive database constraint behind a case-sensitive Java comparison |
| **Severity** | **P3 Medium** — the CRITICAL-drift escalation (auto-file a `RISK_ISSUE`, flip the model to `REVISION`) does not happen, and nothing anywhere reports a problem |
| **What is wrong** | The escalation trigger is `if ("CRITICAL".equals(req.severity()))`. `severity` is validated only by `@NotBlank @Size(max = 20)`, and the column's CHECK (`CK_ml_drift_sev`) restricts it to `{CRITICAL, MAJOR, MODERATE, MINOR, INFO}` — **under collation `Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_SC_UTF8`, which is case-insensitive.** So `"critical"` satisfies the bean validation, satisfies the CHECK, is stored verbatim in lower case, and then fails the Java comparison. The observation is recorded and looks entirely valid; the issue is never filed and the model is never flipped. |
| **Measured live, not inferred** | Probed on the running stack during F2-175's verification (leg 9): `POST …/drift-observations` with `severity: "critical"` → **201**, row stored with `severity = 'critical'`, `triggered_issue_id` NULL, `intake.intake_records` count unchanged, and the parent model **still `IN_PRODUCTION`** rather than `REVISION`.
