## F2-286 · A column the mapping refuses must not be accepted at the wire — and `insertable = false` on a column nobody else can fill means the fact can never be recorded at all

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-22 (`f8baca8b`) |
| **Severity** | **P3** — `ethics.screening_hits.screened_at` was `insertable = false`, so no API caller and no Hibernate write could ever state **when a sanctions screening ran**: the column could only hold the instant its row was inserted. Meanwhile the create accepted a `screenedAt`, discarded it, and echoed it back. Measured live: all 12 rows in both databases are microsecond-precision instants in three seed-insert batches on one day, while `decided_at` beside them holds round business times — so **2 of 12 hits read as decided 370 days before they were screened** |
| **Found by** | asking [[F2-285]]'s question one level up — *how many other entity-bound creates echo a field the database refuses?* |
| **Fix** | `screened_at` becomes **insertable** (still `updatable = false`) and `KycService#recordHit` supplies the clock when the caller does not, and refuses a future screening · the remaining **13** refused columns are closed at the wire with `@JsonProperty(access = READ_ONLY)` — 8 newly, and [[F2-285]]'s own five strengthened · new `RefusedColumnWireContractTest` (hard zero, derived population, no exemption map) and `KycScreeningTimeTest` |
| **Verified** | live probe **6/6 pre-fix, 13/13 post-fix** as `auditor` / `compliance` against planted `[REVIEW-TEST]` rows, the **columns** checked and not just the response · pre-fix control **5 of 11** legs fire, `javap` verified in both directions · backend **4510/0/0** |

### F2-215's two-of-N, on the slice that had just shipped

[[F2-285]] fixed five columns on `privacy.data_breaches` that the database refused and the
create response echoed. Measured the next morning, those were five members of a
**fourteen**-member shape: `insertable = false` fields, outside `ServerOwnedFieldsModule`'s
nine, on an entity a `@PostMapping @RequestBody` binds.

🔑🔑 **The discriminator is not "does the endpoint bind the entity" — it is "does the handler
return the instance Jackson bound".** `AmlAlertService#create` does
`AmlAlert a = new AmlAlert(); applyEditable(a, req); return repo.save(a)`, so the caller's
instance is never saved and never returned. **Eight of the nine survivors are immune for
exactly that reason** — the shape [[F2-213]] drove this platform toward, paying a second
dividend. The one that was not immune was `KycService#recordHit`: `return hitRepo.save(body)`.

### The sharper half: a column nobody could fill

`insertable = false` does not merely refuse *the caller* — it refuses **Hibernate**, so the
column can only ever take its database default. For `screened_at` that default is
`sysutcdatetime()`, i.e. *the moment the row was inserted*, which is not when the screening
ran.

🔑 **The precision is the tell.** A column whose every value is a microsecond instant
clustered into insert-shaped batches was filled by a default; one holding round business
times was stated by somebody:

```
ethics.screening_hits.screened_at     2026-05-03 12:04:17.880489  x2
                                      2026-05-03 13:42:37.160240  x8
                                      2026-05-03 13:43:21.435985  x2
   id=1  screened=2026-05-03 12:04:17.880489   decided=2025-04-29 04:00:00
   id=2  screened=2026-05-03 12:04:17.880489   decided=2025-04-29 04:30:00
```

⚠ And the one route that could have corrected it is the one that appeared to work: `recordHit`
accepted `screenedAt`, the column discarded it, and the response echoed it — so a caller who
supplied the real screening time was told it had been recorded.

### The rule, and what it deliberately does not assert

**If the mapping refuses the value, the wire must not accept it. If the caller should be able
to state it, make the column insertable.** That reading settles both halves without presuming
who owns a fact — and the same measurement has *opposite* correct answers depending on the
owner: F2-285's five are read-only because **the bridge** owns them, and `screened_at` is
insertable because **the screening run** does ([[F2-268]]'s third kind — an outside party's
date is received and recorded, or absent).

⚠ The default is not tidiness. The column is NOT NULL, so once insertable an omitted value
would reach the INSERT as **null** — `recordHit` supplying the clock is what stops the widening
breaking the create outright. And a screening cannot have happened in the future: refusing that
is what makes the widening safe, because it is the one value that could only ever be forged.
Nothing sends the field today, so no working request can start failing ([[F2-182]]).

### `@Setter(AccessLevel.NONE)` does not stop Jackson writing a field

⚠⚠ The gate's first run reported [[F2-285]]'s own five as **open at the wire**, and it was
right. `MapperFeature.INFER_PROPERTY_MUTATORS` is on by default, so a visible getter pulls in
the private field even with no setter. F2-285's `@PrePersist` fixes the **echo** — the response
is honest — and the value still *arrives*. 🔑 **A reader who sees "no setter" reads "not
bindable".** All thirteen now carry one mechanism.

### Instrument errors, four of mine

- ⚠⚠ **A detector keyed on annotation POSITION cannot see a claim.** The census read the
  annotation block *between* `@Column` and the field, and the fix puts `@JsonProperty` one line
  *above* `@Column` — so it reported eight already-closed fields as open. Annotation order is
  meaningless to Java. The gate asks **Jackson** instead, which is immune to position, to which
  annotation was used, and to a mixin.
- ⚠⚠ **A patch script that re-reads each file from disk per target and writes once at the end
  keeps only the LAST edit per file — and reports every one as done**, because it verifies
  against a buffer it then discards. `AmlAlert` has two targets; one was silently dropped. Only
  re-measuring from disk caught it. A script may not certify its own write.
- ⚠ **A route regex anchored on `@PostMapping` looking *forward* returned 0 on a tree holding
  47**, because the house style puts a multi-line `@Operation`/`@PreAuthorize` block in between.
  Anchor on `@RequestBody` and walk **back** to the enclosing signature. A smaller population
  reads exactly like a clean tree.
- ⚠ **A first pass paired the `Optional` external-id finder from one twin with the table from
  the other.** `AuditEngagement` and `AuditEngagementRepository` each exist in two packages
  ([[F2-222]]'s 15 duplicate simple names), so a "live" hit was a mis-pairing — [[F2-278]]'s
  landmine, caught before it shipped. Resolved: **9 of 10 registers with such a finder carry a
  unique index, and the tenth's finder belongs to the other twin**, so that whole hypothesis is
  refuted at 10 of 10.

### Which legs discriminate

5 of 11 fire on the pre-fix tree. 🔑 **The three unit legs about a *stated* value cannot
discriminate, and the reason is worth stating: a mocked repository has no schema, so no unit
test can see an `insertable = false` column** — `hitRepo.save(body)` returns the body with the
caller's value intact whatever the mapping says. Only the live probe could see this, which is
house rule 4 earning its place again. F2-285's gate stayed green throughout, which is what
proves the control reverted exactly what it meant to.

### Filed

- **`ethics.aml_alerts.first_detected_at` is still `insertable = false`**, so the API can never
  state when suspicious activity was first detected — the start of the FIU reporting clock. Not
  the same defect: the column holds **8 distinct real business dates** across 10 rows, because
  the seed wrote them by direct SQL, bypassing Hibernate. Enabling it means widening
  `applyEditable`, which is a product call about whether an alert's detection time is the
  caller's to state.
- **The 12 seeded `screened_at` insert-instants, and the 2 hits decided before they were
  screened.** Identical in dev and prod. Rewriting live AML rows in two databases is an **owner
  decision** ([[F2-183]]/[[F2-196]]), and there is no source for the real screening times.
- **`LocalDateTime` columns are stored in UTC and rendered in the JVM's local zone** (UTC+3
  here), so a stated `09:15` reads `06:15` in the column. Round-trips are lossless and the two
  are never comparable directly — [[F2-178]]'s mirror, and it cost one probe iteration.
- **`GuardExpressions.stripComments` removes comment LINES rather than blanking them** (76 → 59
  on one file measured here), so any offset taken from its output does not refer to the file.
  Every assertion in the new gate is a `contains`, which is why that is safe.
- `ethics.screening_hits` has **no CHECK constraint** on `list_source` or `disposition`, and
  `ethics.kyc_subjects.full_name` has an `*_ar` sibling the create does not require (house rule
  7).

## F2-287 · A gate's population can be scoped by the HTTP VERB — and the slice that discovers a rule is the worst-placed slice to apply it to its own leftovers

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | 🟢 CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`78def62f`) |
| **Severity** | **P3** — `ethics.aml_alerts.first_detected_at` is *when the TM engine detected the suspicious activity*, the start of the FIU reporting clock. It was `insertable = false`, which refuses **Hibernate** as well as the caller, so the column could only ever hold `sysutcdatetime()` at the instant the row was inserted — while `AmlAlertRepository` orders the whole register by it. Probed live: a stated detection time was discarded in silence and the create's response reported `null` |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-286]]'s own filing and disbelieving it ([[F2-221]]) — and finding that the gate F2-286 shipped is scoped to `@PostMapping` |
| **Fix** | `first_detected_at` becomes **insertable** (still `updatable = false`), `AmlAlertService.create` supplies the clock when the caller does not and refuses a future detection time, and `update` **echo-guards** it — the mapping refuses a change, so the wire must not appear to accept one · new `UpdateRefusedColumnWireContractTest` (the verb mirror, census asserted) and `AmlDetectionTimeTest` |
| **Verified** | live probe **14/14 post-fix**, pre-fix control **6/6 fire**, `javap`-verified in both directions · **9 of 13** test legs discriminate · backend **4523/0/0** |

### The instrument finding

`RefusedColumnWireContractTest.population()` — shipped by F2-286 the day before — reads:

```java
if (col == null || col.insertable()) continue;
```

…over entities bound by a `@PostMapping @RequestBody`. So its claim, *"a column the mapping
refuses must not be accepted at the wire"*, is scoped to the **INSERT half**. The mirror is
`updatable = false` on an entity bound by a `@PutMapping`/`@PatchMapping`: the caller sends
the field, Hibernate omits the column from the UPDATE, and nothing happens.

🔑 **F2-198's shape again — the invariant is real and its population is a mechanism. Here the
narrowing is neither a filename, an allow-list, a module name nor an `extends` clause: it is
which VERB the slice was looking at.** Measured: **40** `updatable = false` fields on
update-bound entities outside `ServerOwnedFieldsModule`'s nine, **28** of which Jackson
accepts and silently discards.

### F2-286 filed its own remaining member on a premise that was wrong twice

Its filing read: *"`ethics.aml_alerts.first_detected_at` is still `insertable = false` … **not**
the same defect, because the column holds **8 distinct real business dates** across 10 rows …
and enabling it means widening `applyEditable`, a product call."*

The measurement was **right** — confirmed in both databases: 8 distinct values, **0 of 10** with
sub-second precision, **0** equal to `created_at`, and the seed derived every `sla_due_at` from
it at exactly +30 days. 🔑 **That is F2-286's own tell running the other way: a column of round
business times was STATED by somebody, and one of microsecond insert-instants was DEFAULTED.**

Both halves of the *blocker* were wrong.

- ⚠⚠ **The mechanism.** `applyEditable` is called by `create` **and** `update`, and the column
  is `updatable = false` — so a write there would compile, run on the update path and change
  nothing. Measured over the whole tree: **no service writes an `updatable = false` column on a
  row it loaded**, so the filed fix would have created the **first instance** of that shape.
- ⚠⚠ **The ownership.** The entity's own javadoc says the alert *"surfaces from the bank's TM
  engine"*, so the detection time is **received from outside** — [[F2-268]]'s third kind, which
  [[F2-209]] already settles: received and recorded, or absent. Not a product decision.

🔑🔑 **The slice that discovers a rule is the worst-placed slice to apply it to its own
leftovers, because the leftover gets filed with the reasoning that was current while the rule
was still forming.**

### The pre-fix control refuted my own description of the defect, and the correction is sharper

I predicted the control would show the create's response **echoing** the caller's value
(F2-285's shape). It reports **`null`** — because F2-286 had already closed the echo with
`@JsonProperty(access = READ_ONLY)` while leaving the field unstatable.

🔑 **An HONEST response over a DEFAULTED column is what makes this defect invisible: nothing
contradicts anything.** F2-285's version at least left a discrepancy a re-fetch would expose.
Here the wire truthfully said *"I am not telling you"* about a value the caller had just
supplied and the column had silently replaced.

### 0 of 4, and the cause was my own instrument twice over

The `updatable = false`-written-on-a-loaded-row census reported **4 candidates and all 4 were
creates**:

- ⚠⚠ **A per-FILE map keyed on a variable name keeps only the last assignment.** A service
  reuses `e` / `c` in every method, so `create`'s `new AuditEngagement()` was overwritten by
  `transition`'s `repo.findBy…`. **This is [[F2-286]]'s patch-script bug one artefact over** —
  *a map keyed on a name keeps only the LAST entry* — and it manufactures a fully-formed
  finding on a create path. Resolve origins inside the enclosing method.
- ⚠⚠ **A fallback for an unresolved type reintroduces exactly the ambiguity the resolution
  removed.** After keying the entity off the file's **imports**, an
  `if (fqcn not in population) fall back to the simple name` branch put `audit_eng`'s service
  against `compliance.entity.AuditEngagement` again — and `audit_eng`'s own twin declares
  `externalId` as a plain `String(64)`, so it was never in the population at all. Third
  instance of [[F2-222]]/[[F2-278]]'s twin trap in two slices, and the first caused by the fix
  for it. **It fails in the confident direction: a finding naming the wrong table.**

### Three more instrument errors, all of mine

- ⚠⚠ **A member regex that CONSUMES its leading `;` cannot match two consecutive single-line
  members, so it skips every other one.** It reported **210** `updatable = false` fields on a
  tree holding **424** — almost exactly half — and this codebase's house style puts `@Column`
  and the field on one line, several in a row. 🔑 **A smaller population reads exactly like a
  clean tree.** Use a lookbehind. The residual after fixing it was **420 + 2 on `BaseEntity`**,
  which accounts for all 422 in entity files (the other 2 are in **comments** in two services).
- ⚠ **A method-signature regex of the obvious shape backtracks catastrophically** — modifiers,
  then a lazy type class that also matches whitespace, then the name — and hung a whole-tree
  scan past 120 s. Anchor it to the line.
- ⚠ **The CRLF trap, and the heredoc trap, in one slice.** A patch script's anchors were written
  with `\n` against a CRLF tree and matched **0**; then a `<<'PY'` heredoc collapsed `\\n` into a
  real newline inside a Python string literal and produced a `SyntaxError`. Both are recorded in
  CLAUDE.md and I hit both anyway. **Use the Write/Edit tools for file content; normalise an
  anchor to the target file's own line endings.**

### Which legs discriminate

**9 of 13**, measured against the reverted tree rather than argued. The four that do not are
the two census/anti-vacuity **measurements** (correctly — they are not claims about this fix)
and the two update-path **tolerance** legs, which cannot fail before the echo guard exists:
before it, an echo is trivially accepted and an omission trivially leaves the value alone.

### Filed

- ⚠⚠ **`externalId` is NOT one of `ServerOwnedFieldsModule`'s nine**, so on an entity-bound
  POST a caller can send it and Jackson binds it. Census: **75** entities with an `externalId`
  bound by a `@PostMapping @RequestBody`, **68 OPEN** (7 refused by the mapping). Most are
  immune because the service mints over the top — but **`ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest`
  cannot see any of them either way**: its key is a `setExternalId(...)` call inside a `create*`
  method, and an entity-bound POST has no setter call at all, because Jackson writes the field.
  F2-198's shape on the reference ratchet, and [[F2-172]](d)'s family. **No verdicts** — the
  narrowing is *does the create overwrite it*, which is a reading job ([[F2-188]]).
- The **28**-member update-verb census, dominated 27-to-1 by `externalId`, is a decrease-only
  figure in the new gate rather than a work list: a field the caller may send on a PUT and the
  server discards is [[F2-214]]'s shape, i.e. mild.
- `ethics.aml_alerts` has **zero CHECK constraints**, so `severity`, `alert_type`,
  `disposition` and `status` are narrowed only by Java — and `status` by `ServerOwnedState`
  alone. Cheap now that this slice touched the register's writers ([[F2-183]]).
- `amlApi.create` and `amlApi.update` have **no call sites**, so this register has no create or
  edit screen; the fix is live for an integration and latent for the UI, which is where this
  family lives ([[F2-179]]). Note [[F2-214]]'s warning: a dark client reads as an invitation to
  build the screen.
- `first_detected_at` is rendered by **no page**, and `AmlAlertDto` declares it — so the wire
  carries a value nothing shows ([[F2-198]]'s shape). `sla_due_at` likewise, with **no server
  computation anywhere** ([[F2-268]]'s standing filing).
- `subject_name_ar` is **absent from the production table**: V391 is one of the 47 pending
  migrations, so that is the deployment gap and not a defect.

## F2-288 — the escalation that makes a screening match matter was on the RECORD path and absent from the REVIEWER's

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`a4eec5b9`) |
| **Severity** | P1 — a KYC subject with a confirmed OFAC sanctions match could be approved for business |
| **Register** | `ethics.screening_hits` (12 rows), `ethics.kyc_subjects` (16 rows) — byte-identical in dev and prod |
| **Standards** | FATF R.12 (PEP enhanced due diligence), SAMA AML/CFT Rules, Saudi FIU STR filing |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-287]]'s top filing, disbelieving it ([[F2-221]]), and asking [[F2-196]]'s question of the register the refutation landed in |
| **Verification** | live probe **8/18 pre-fix · 18/18 post-fix** on a freshly restarted listener; unit control **15 of 21 legs fire**; backend **4523 → 4544 / 0 / 0** |

### The defect

`KycService` reacted to a **confirmed** sanctions/PEP match by flagging its subject —
`isSanctioned` + `riskRating = PROHIBITED` for the four sanctions lists, `isPep` +
`eddRequired` + a STANDARD/LOW → HIGH raise for `PEP_GLOBAL`. That reaction lived inline in
**`recordHit` only**. `disposition()` — the route a reviewer uses to *adjudicate* a hit — wrote
the decision, the decider and the timestamp, and applied **none** of the consequences.

Probed live as `compliance` (GRC_ADMINISTRATOR; *admin proves nothing about authorization*)
against a `[REVIEW-TEST]` subject the probe plants itself ([[F2-206]]):

| leg | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| confirm an `OFAC_SDN` match on review | 200, `isSanctioned = false` | 200, `isSanctioned = true` |
| the resulting risk rating | `STANDARD` | `PROHIBITED` |
| **`POST /kyc/{id}/approve` afterwards** | **HTTP 200** | HTTP 400 |
| confirm a `PEP_GLOBAL` match on review | `isPep = false`, `eddRequired = false` | both true, rating `HIGH` |

🔑 **The third row is the finding.** `approve()` has always refused a sanctioned subject —
*"Cannot approve a sanctioned subject"* — so the gate existed and could never fire, because
nothing on the reviewer's path ever set the flag it reads. A control that cannot fire is
[[F2-112]]'s shape; here it was one method away from the thing that would have armed it.

### 🔑 The comment in `recordHit` is why nobody asked

It documents the reaction mechanism at length and warns a future reader *not* to refuse the
caller's disposition, because *"the service **reacts** to it below by flagging the subject
sanctioned or PEP — refusing it would break the mechanism, which is the F2-40 trap."* Every
word true, and every word about `recordHit`. [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N in the comment whose entire
subject is this mechanism: **a reader who finds a mechanism explained does not then ask which
sibling route is missing it.** That same comment lists **three** of the vocabulary's four
tokens, which is what made it a fourth uncounted copy.

### 🔑 The CHECK constraint is not the fix, and the probe proved it

`ethics.screening_hits` had **zero** CHECK constraints of any kind, so `disposition` was
narrowed by nothing and `disposition()` stored whatever string arrived. The vocabulary lived in
**four** places and was enforced in none: the frontend's `HIT_DISPOSITIONS` dropdown (4 tokens),
`recordHit`'s case-sensitive `"TRUE_MATCH".equals(...)`, the badge's tone ternary, and the
comment above (3 tokens).

⚠⚠ **V392 was applied to dev BEFORE the writer fix, so the pre-fix probe ran with the CHECK in
place — and `disposition: "true_match"` was ACCEPTED, stored verbatim, and escalated nothing.**
The collation is `Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_SC_UTF8`, so the constraint cannot see case
([[F2-179]]). **A migration that adds the CHECK and stops leaves the defect intact while
appearing to guard it** — which is [[F2-183]]'s rule demonstrated rather than asserted, and the
reason the writer change and V392 are one commit.

⚙ The same run showed the other half of that pair: with only the CHECK, an unrecognised
disposition surfaced as **HTTP 409** and an unrecognised list source as a 409 **naming no
field**. With `ClosedVocabulary.require()` both are **400 naming the field**. [[F2-230]]'s
observation, live: the migration and the writer are two halves of one diagnostic.

### What shipped

- **One `applyConfirmedMatch`**, the single writer of all four consequences, reached by both
  routes ([[F2-190]]; [[F2-245]]'s rule that the claim which prevents drift is about *where* the
  writes live). It reads the **normalised** values, so it must run after the vocabulary calls.
- **Three `ClosedVocabulary` declarations** naming V392's constraints:
  `CK_screening_hits_disposition`, `CK_screening_hits_list_source`,
  `CK_kyc_subjects_risk_rating`. `require`, not `coerce` — [[F2-182]]'s test says no coercion
  exists upstream so out-of-vocabulary values do succeed today, but every value stored in either
  database is already a member, and an unrecognised AML disposition does not degrade gracefully,
  it **silently skips the sanctions escalation**. This is not the public whistleblower portal
  where a lost report is worse than a mis-graded one.
- **`risk_rating` closed in the same commit** because it is both an *input* to the PEP branch
  (which raises STANDARD/LOW) and its *output* — a non-canonical value there does not render
  oddly, it decides whether a confirmed PEP match raises the rating at all.
- **V392**, with four THROWing self-checks including one asserting that every token
  `applyConfirmedMatch` dispatches on is still admitted, so a later narrowing cannot make a
  sanctions escalation unreachable in silence.

### The gates

`ScreeningEscalationContractTest` (9 legs, hermetic):
- the four consequence setters appear in `applyConfirmedMatch` and in **neither** write route
- both routes contain an `applyConfirmedMatch(` call
- no bare `"TOKEN".equals(...)` comparison survives, scoped to the **shape** of the claim rather
  than the token (which legitimately appears in the vocabulary declaration — [[F2-192]])
- the operator's dropdowns and the vocabularies agree **in both directions**: a dropdown offering
  a refused token is [[F2-180]]'s defect, a vocabulary admitting a token no operator can pick is
  the mirror and reads as coverage
- `RISK_RATING_TONE` covers every member ([[F2-197]]: an unmapped value renders neutral, so a
  PROHIBITED subject could look unremarkable)
- the hit badge's ternary names only real members
- the comment stripper's own self-test, with the **two-pass** form as the negative control (never
  a reordered alternation, which is an equivalent mutant — [[F2-211]])

`KycScreeningEscalationTest` (12 legs) is paired deliberately: the `recordHit` half passed
before this slice and the `disposition` half did not, **so a fix that moved the code without
wiring the second caller fails exactly half of them.**

⚠ **My first draft of the one-writer leg failed on correct code.** It counted `setIsSanctioned(`
and `setIsPep(` at 1 and the tree has 2 — `apply()` legitimately copies all four flags, because
the subject form lets an operator flag a PEP or a sanctioned party **by hand**, which is a
different question from reacting to a hit, and `completeEdd` legitimately clears `eddRequired`.
**A gate that fails on working code trains the next reader to edit the assertion** ([[F2-214]]),
so it is scoped to the shape of the claim: the two hit-writing routes must not write a
consequence themselves. Only `setIsSanctioned(true)` / `setIsPep(true)` /
`setRiskRating("PROHIBITED")` can honestly be pinned at one.

### ⚠ The refutation that produced this, recorded so nobody re-derives it

[[F2-287]] filed: *"`externalId` is not one of `ServerOwnedFieldsModule`'s nine — 75 entities
bind one on an entity-bound POST, 68 OPEN, and `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest` cannot see
any of them because its key is a `setExternalId(...)` call site."* The **census reproduces
exactly** by reflection — 117 entity-bound-POST entities, 75 with an `externalId`, **68 open, 7
refused** — and the ratchet's blindness is real (`REFERENCE_SETTER` is a setter *call*, and an
entity-bound POST has none, because Jackson writes the field).

**Every consequence claim then fell:**

| claim | measured |
|---|---|
| *"most are immune because the service mints over the top"* | **refuted** — 69 of 71 routes never mint. 40 rely on a UUID **field initialiser**, which Jackson overrides because it runs at construction and deserialisation follows; 29 have no filling mechanism at all |
| the 6 NOT NULL sites with no mechanism | 3 are `socops` **ingest** paths carrying an upstream scanner/SIEM/DLP id (the ratchet's own `UPSTREAM_OWNED` bucket, correct); 3 are `audit_lc`, where `createAnnualPlan` **explicitly throws `"externalId is required"`** — caller-named by design, exactly as [[F2-286]] recorded |
| [[F2-286]]'s ambiguity triple, re-paired properly | **HOT = 0.** 57 of 63 `external_id` finders are tenant-scoped, **0** unscoped `@Query`, and none of the 6 unscoped finders belongs to any of the 68 sites |
| the 18 NULLABLE no-mechanism sites | `external_id` null on many live rows (`policy.documents` 22 of 51, `ndi.framework_item` 20 of 20), **no `{externalId}` route, no client, no unique index** — an inert column ([[F2-184]] at a column). Measured and **not** fixed ([[F2-278]]: sometimes the right answer is measure it and do not make it) |

🔑 **A generalisation that returns zero is a result** ([[F2-216]]) — and asking [[F2-196]]'s
question of the register the refutation had walked into is what found the P1.

### ⚠ Instrument errors, all mine

- **A member regex that consumes its leading `;` skips every other single-line member** — it
  reported **210** `updatable = false`-style fields on a tree holding **424**, because the house
  style puts `@Column` and the field on one line, several in a row. Carried over from
  [[F2-287]]'s scratch tooling; a smaller population reads exactly like a clean tree.
- **My pre-fix control script silently converted `KycService.java` from CRLF to LF.**
  `io.open(...).read()` normalises to LF and writing with `newline=""` emits it verbatim. Third
  instance of the line-ending trap in this lineage ([[F2-212]], [[F2-229]], [[F2-234]]) and the
  first caused by a *restore* rather than an anchor. Verify the byte-level line endings after any
  scripted restore, not just the content.
- **`subprocess` resolved `mvn` to a guessed `C:\Sources\...` path** and died with
  `WinError 193` (*not a valid Win32 application*) — the real launcher is on **D:**. The control
  ran from Bash instead, where `mvn` resolves natively. Guessed-path family, at a tool this time.
- **`mvn -o compile` did not trigger a DevTools restart** ([[F2-275]]), so the listener was still
  serving the *fixed* code after the revert. Had the pre-fix probe run then, it would have scored
  the defect as absent — i.e. **as never having been live.** `Started GrcApplication` counted
  1 before and after; the fix is to kill by PID (identified by `-Djava.io.tmpdir`, guarded on
  8090/8091 being the prod jar) and relaunch.

### ⚙ Filed

- **Whether a confirmed `INTERPOL_RED`, `ADVERSE_MEDIA` or `INTERNAL` match should move a
  customer's risk rating.** Those three of the eight list sources escalate nothing, and inventing
  a rule would be [[F2-183]]/[[F2-196]]'s defect. A gate leg asserts the current boundary in both
  directions so it cannot drift silently. **Owner decision.**
- **`kycApi.disposition` has no caller**, so **10 of 12 live hits are permanently
  un-dispositionable through the platform's own screen** — the create form is the only place a
  disposition can be set, and it defaults to `NEEDS_REVIEW`. The fix makes the *route* correct;
  building the review screen is a product change. ⚠ [[F2-214]]'s warning applies squarely: a dark
  client reads as an invitation to build the screen — and until this slice, that screen would
  have fired the un-escalating path.
- **`runScreening` screens nothing.** `POST /kyc/{id}/screening-run` only stamps
  `lastScreenedAt`; it creates no hits and consults no list. The button is labelled "Run
  screening" ([[F2-193]]'s shape: a control whose label describes something the platform cannot
  do).
- **Two screening registers for one concept**, both live and identical in dev and prod:
  `aml.screening_hit` (3 rows, `status`, a **declared 7-token machine** in `SanctionsHitService`,
  a `@Pattern` on its DTO) and `ethics.screening_hits` (12 rows, `disposition`, no machine). The
  vocabularies are **disjoint near-synonyms** — `PENDING_REVIEW`/`TRUE_POSITIVE` against
  `NEEDS_REVIEW`/`TRUE_MATCH` — and **two `@Entity` classes share the simple name
  `ScreeningHit`** ([[F2-222]]'s 15). The UI drives the one with no machine. [[F2-196]]'s shape;
  reconciling them changes what the platform reports to the Saudi FIU. **Owner decision.**
- The `ethics` schema's remaining unconstrained columns: `aml_alerts.alert_type` /
  `.severity` / `.disposition` (whose transition route still takes
  `body.get("disposition").toString()` unvalidated), `cases.status` (11 of 30 rows still
  unadvanceable — [[F2-221]]'s filing, re-confirmed), `kyc_subjects.status` / `.subject_type` /
  `.cdd_level`, `disclosures.status`.
- **The entity's `@Column(length)` disagrees with the column on both hit fields** —
  `disposition` declares 30 against `nvarchar(60)`, `list_source` 60 against `nvarchar(120)`.
  Inert under `ddl-auto=none` ([[F2-276]]'s declaration-versus-column gap), so noted rather than
  changed.
- **The 68-site `externalId` census** stands as measured above, with **no verdicts** and no work
  left that this slice can justify: the finders are scoped, the NOT NULL sites are by design or
  upstream-owned, and the nullable ones are inert.
