The tell was structural: the escalation fires on `>=` while `openConsecutiveFailureIssue` has no dedup, and the Issue title hardcodes "3" while its body renders `d.getConsecutiveFailures()` (the real count) — an internal contradiction that only makes sense if the author believed it fired once. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (Mockito, no Spring/DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `CcmServiceTest.aFailurePastTheThresholdDoesNotOpenADuplicateIssue` (new): a CRITICAL control already AT the threshold (counter 3), next FAIL → 4, asserts `verify(issueService, never()).create(...)` (no duplicate) and that the streak counter still increments to 4. The two existing threshold-crossing legs (`thirdConsecutiveCriticalFailureOpensIssue`, `runTestNow_atTheConsecutiveFailureThreshold_savesTheRunOnceCarryingTheIssueId`) — which set the counter to 2 and cross to 3 — stay green under both `>=` and `==`, so nothing regressed. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): `git checkout a82ae227 -- CcmService.java` (restoring `>=`) makes ONLY the new leg RED (`IssueService.create` IS called on the 4th failure → `verify(never())` fails) while the other 17 stay green (1 of 18 discriminates). |

### Fix

`recordRunInternal`'s escalation guard changes `d.getConsecutiveFailures() >= CONSECUTIVE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD` to `== CONSECUTIVE_FAILURE_THRESHOLD`. The counter only ever increments by 1 (on failure) or resets to 0 (on PASS / create / enable — verified, no other writer), so a streak passes through the threshold **exactly once** — `==` opens exactly one Issue per streak. It also removes the title/body contradiction for free: at the moment it fires, `consecutiveFailures` IS the threshold, so both read "3".

### Note — why `==` and not a dedup ([[F2-188]])

The `>=` was not an intentional retry mechanism (the Issue title hardcodes "3" and the code's own comment declares Issue-open best-effort). A more elaborate alternative — dedup inside `openConsecutiveFailureIssue` against an existing non-terminal Issue for `(sourceModule='ccm', sourceEntityType='ControlTestDefinition', sourceEntityId)` and reuse it — would additionally preserve a best-effort retry if the 3rd-failure open throws and link runs 4,5… to the one open Issue; it was weighed and rejected because it needs a new `IssueRepository` finder and a judgement about whether a `RESOLVED` Issue (non-terminal — [[F2-370]]'s `IssueService.TRANSITIONS` terminal is only `{CLOSED, CANCELLED}`) counts as "reuse-able," which is an owner call. The `==` fix is minimal, provably fires once, and needs no status judgement. Filed: grep for a `count >= threshold` escalation feeding a create/notify with no dedup (the sibling `KriBreachService` sustained-RED-KRI escalation uses a size threshold and is worth checking for the same shape, though it appears keyed on a single breach record rather than fired per-measurement).

## F2-369 — split(",").length counted an empty id list as 1, not 0, on two regulator-facing counts

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — two denormalised counts on regulator/governance-facing registers. `NcaEccFilingService` (the NCA ECC self-assessment return, `capaCount`) and `AuditEngagementService` (an IIA audit engagement, `findingsCount`) each derived the count as `req.getLinkedX().split(",").length`. `"".split(",")` returns `[""]` — a one-element array holding the empty token, not an empty array — so a linked-ids field arriving as `""` made the count read **1 for a list of 0 ids**. Both are written only under `if (req.getLinkedX() != null)`, so it fires when the field is empty rather than null/omitted (F2-283: latent-in-data — a caller sending `""` for "none"). |
| **Registers** | none — one new shared primitive (`common/util/CsvTokens`), two call sites (`.../nca_ecc/service/NcaEccFilingService.java`, `.../audit_eng/service/AuditEngagementService.java`) + a new `CsvTokensTest`. No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-190]] (a shape used in two modules gets one shared primitive, not two hand-rolled copies — `common/util/CsvTokens`, beside `ExternalIds`); [[F2-205]] / [[F2-216]] (a source scan proves both sites call the helper and the `.split(",").length` idiom is gone — wiring + mechanism removal); [[F2-283]] (latent in data / live in code); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — pure string logic + a source scan). |
| **Found by** | Sweeping `nca_ecc` (NCA ECC filing) and `audit_eng` for a bounded defect after the risk/ERM quantitative surface, the capped-aggregate shape, the [[F2-196]] inclusion-list shape and the [[F2-179]] case-sensitivity shape all came up clean or owner-decision in the fresh modules sampled this firing (`RegulatoryHorizonService.ACTIVE_STATUSES` and `EmergingRiskService.ACTIVE` are correct complements; `BoardPackAggregateService.IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES` is a curated board subset, [[F2-290]]'s narrower-question exception). `NcaEccFilingService`'s scoring/attribution and `AuditEngagementService`'s lifecycle are sound; the one clean, unambiguous bug was the shared `.split(",").length` count idiom — grepped platform-wide, exactly these two sites carry it, both feeding a denormalised count a regulator/committee reads. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (no Spring / DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `CsvTokensTest` (3): the count legs are load-bearing — `countNonBlank("")` is 0 (the defect was 1), `null`/blank → 0, `"a,,b"` → 2 (interior blanks do not inflate), `"a,b"` → 2; and a source-scan leg proves both service files call `setCapaCount(CsvTokens.countNonBlank(` / `setFindingsCount(CsvTokens.countNonBlank(` and no longer contain `.split(",").length` ([[F2-205]] wiring / [[F2-216]] removal). Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): a surgical revert of only the two call sites back to `.split(",").length` (keeping the `CsvTokens` symbol so both classes still compile) makes exactly the source-scan leg RED (the file still holds `.split(",").length`, lacks the helper call) while the count legs — which exercise the unchanged helper — stay green ([[F2-225]]: label which legs discriminate). |

### Fix

`common/util/CsvTokens.countNonBlank(String)` (null/blank → 0; counts the non-blank comma-separated tokens) is the one home for the count, and both sites route through it. `"".split(",").length` was 1; `countNonBlank("")` is 0. Strictly more correct on every input — the only behavioural changes are the empty-string case (1 → 0, the fix) and interior blank tokens (`"a,,b"`: 3 → 2), both toward the true id count.

### Note — latent in data ([[F2-283]])

Not re-measured against a running backend (none this slice). The miscount fires only when `linkedCapaIds` / `linkedFindingIds` arrives as an empty (non-null) string; a null or omitted field leaves the count untouched. Whether any live filing/engagement holds an empty linked-ids string was not measured.

## F2-368 — the SAMA quarterly complaints report was computed over all-time, ignoring its period

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P2 — the SAMA Banking Consumer Protection quarterly submission (`POST /api/v1/complaints/reports/quarterly/generate`, `hasPermission('CONSUMER','WRITE')`). `ComplaintService.generateQuarterlyReport(reportPeriod)` fetched every complaint for the tenant (`findByOrganisationIdAndIsDeletedFalse...`, unpaged) and computed all figures — `totalReceived`, `totalResolved`, `totalEscalatedSama`, `avgResolutionDays`, the ack/resolution SLA-breach percentages, `topCategory`/count, `compensationTotalSar` — over that whole set, never filtering by `reportPeriod`. The period string was used only as the storage key on the upserted `ComplaintAggregateReport`. So `generateQuarterlyReport("Q4-2025")` and `("Q1-2026")` produced **identical all-time figures**, each mislabelled by its quarter — on the artefact the entity documents as "one row per (tenant, period)" backing the regulator's quarterly submission. |
| **Registers** | none — one service (`.../consumer/complaints/service/ComplaintService.java`) + three tests added to `ComplaintVocabularyTest`. No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-199]] (a regulator-facing artefact is the highest-stakes surface — the report leaves the platform for SAMA); [[F2-197]] (a figure computed the same way for every period, ignoring the period that is supposed to scope it); [[F2-188]] (reframed as a missing-WHERE-clause bug, not a manufactured cohort decision — the code's own cohort is "received", so the fix applies the filter the report already implies rather than choosing new semantics); [[F2-230]] (the report-period format is `Qn-YYYY` in the stored data it measured, e.g. `Q4-2025`, while the tests use `YYYY-Qn`, e.g. `2026-Q3` — the parser accepts both so no caller breaks); [[F2-178]] (the existing top-category test's fixture is pinned to a fixed in-quarter instant so scoping does not make it quarter-of-run dependent); [[F2-282]] (the parser is the single source of the format — no DTO `@Pattern` to drift from it); [[F2-283]] (latent in data / live in code); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — the aggregation and the parser are pure logic over a mocked repository). |
| **Found by** | Sweeping the `consumer` complaints module (SAMA consumer-protection, regulator-facing) after the risk/ERM quantitative surface, the capped-aggregate shape ([[F2-345]] / [[F2-365]]) and the [[F2-196]] inclusion-list shape in fresh modules all came up clean or correct-complements. `ComplaintService`'s minter is the reference sequential idiom ([[F2-337]]) and its vocabularies are closed ([[F2-183]]); the one substantive defect was `generateQuarterlyReport` reading `all` and never the period. Confirmed the period is used only as the upsert key (never a filter), the entity javadoc mandates per-(tenant, period) `Qn-YYYY`, and the code frames its cohort as "received" (`total_received` is the headline count and the breach-% denominator). |
| **Verification** | hermetic (Mockito over a mocked repository, no Spring / DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `ComplaintVocabularyTest` (+3): `theQuarterlyReportIsScopedToItsQuarter` — the load-bearing leg: five complaints across Q2/Q3/Q4-2026 (including the last instant before the quarter and the first instant of the next) and the Q3-2026 report counts exactly the two received in Q3, proving the half-open `[Jul 1 00:00, Oct 1 00:00)` window; `bothPeriodSpellingsResolveToTheSameWindow` (`Q3-2026` and `2026-Q3` → one window); `aMalformedPeriodIsRefused` (a period naming no quarter is a 400, not a silent all-time report). The pre-existing `aCaseVariantCategoryDoesNotSplitTheSamaReportBucket` was pinned to a fixed in-Q3-2026 instant. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): a surgical revert of only the cohort filter (`cohort = all`, keeping the `QuarterWindow` / `quarterWindow` symbols so the class and tests compile) makes exactly the scoping leg RED (`expected 2` but was 5, the all-time bug) while the parse-tolerance and malformed-period pins and the top-category test stay green ([[F2-225]]: label which legs discriminate). |

### Fix

`generateQuarterlyReport` now resolves `reportPeriod` to a `QuarterWindow` (`[start, endExclusive)` instants) via a tolerant `quarterWindow` parser that accepts `Qn-YYYY` and `YYYY-Qn` (case-insensitive), filters the tenant's complaints to those RECEIVED (`submittedOn`) in that window, and computes every figure over that `cohort`. A period naming no quarter throws `IllegalArgumentException` → 400 naming the expected format. `all` is still the raw tenant fetch; `cohort` is the period-scoped set. No migration, and no `@Pattern` on the DTO — the parser is the single source of the format, so the two cannot drift ([[F2-282]]).

### Note — the cohort reading, and latent in data ([[F2-283]])

The cohort is "complaints RECEIVED in the quarter", which is the code's own framing (`total_received`) and the standard SAMA quarterly complaints cohort — not a manufactured decision. If SAMA's definition were instead "resolved in the quarter", that is an owner refinement — but any period-scoping is strictly correct where the previous all-time behaviour was not. Not re-measured against a running backend (none this slice); the defect is unconditional in code (every period produced all-time figures).

### Filed (deferred)

- Whether the SAMA cohort should be "received in the quarter" (this fix) or "resolved in the quarter" is an owner refinement — recorded so an owner can confirm against the SAMA definition ([[F2-188]]).
- The report-period format is genuinely used two ways across the codebase — `Qn-YYYY` in the stored data ([[F2-230]]) and `YYYY-Qn` in the tests — which the parser tolerates; settling on one documented contract and adding a DTO `@Pattern` is a tightening for an owner.

## F2-367 — the SOC dashboard's "open events" set was a hand-typed inclusion list that dropped ESCALATED

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P2 — the SOC leadership operations dashboard (`GET /api/v1/socops/dashboard`, NCA ECC-2 incident response). `SocOpsDashboardService.get()` built its open-security-event set by concatenating four `findByOrganisationIdAndStatus(...)` calls for a hand-typed list `{NEW, TRIAGED, IN_ANALYSIS, CONTAINED}`. The SecurityEvent statuses actually written are `NEW` (ingest), `TRIAGED` (triage), `ESCALATED` (escalate-to-incident), `RESOLVED` / `FALSE_POSITIVE` (resolve — the two terminal states). So the list **dropped `ESCALATED`** — the state an event enters when it is promoted to a first-class `cyber.incidents` record, i.e. the most serious open events — and named two tokens (`IN_ANALYSIS`, `CONTAINED`) that no writer ever sets. Escalated events therefore vanished from the open counts (`oCritical` / `oHigh` / `oMedium` / `oTotal`) and, because the leadership top-5 (`topEvents`) is filtered from the same list, from the "events to act on" panel — under-reporting open/urgent SOC work in the flattering direction. |
| **Registers** | none — two services (`.../socops/service/SocOpsDashboardService.java`, `.../socops/service/SecurityEventService.java`) + one repository finder + a new `SocOpsDashboardServiceTest` (the dashboard's first). No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-196]] ("open" is the COMPLEMENT of a declared terminal set, never a second hand-typed inclusion list — a list silently drops the state nobody remembered); [[F2-364]] / [[F2-343]] / [[F2-336]] (the same complement rule on the SAMA reg-reporting in-flight set, the fraud open-count and the BCM CAPAs); [[F2-205]] / [[F2-282]] (which reader is authoritative and do they agree — the SLA sweep's `NOT IN ('RESOLVED','FALSE_POSITIVE')` and `SocOpsExportService` both use the complement; the dashboard was the lone outlier); [[F2-299]] / [[F2-343]] (the SLA `@Query`'s excluded set is a necessary second SQL copy of the terminal vocabulary — pinned against the constant so they cannot drift); [[F2-248]] (the dashboard had no test); [[F2-283]] (latent in data / live in code); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — a Mockito test of the extracted selection + source scans; the query's row selection is SQL). |
| **Found by** | The intended vein (risk/ERM quantitative math) was swept and found clean — appetite division guarded (`upper.signum() == 0`), exposure weighting a documented model bounded by a 0.75 clamp, the KRI band logic correct and [[F2-182]] having already fixed its `value_direction` case-sensitivity — so the sweep moved to the `getTotalElements` / capped-aggregate shape platform-wide ([[F2-345]] / [[F2-352]] / [[F2-365]]), which was exhausted (every site is a `PageRequest.of(0, 1)` count-minter or an unpaged read), and then to the [[F2-196]] inclusion-list shape in a fresh, security-critical module. `SocOpsDashboardService`'s `openEvents` list was the lone reader of "open" not using the complement; the SecurityEvent writers (`NEW`/`TRIAGED`/`ESCALATED`/`RESOLVED`/`FALSE_POSITIVE`) confirmed `ESCALATED` is dropped and `IN_ANALYSIS`/`CONTAINED` are dead tokens ([[F2-343]]'s dead-token tell). |
| **Verification** | hermetic (Mockito + source scans, no Spring / DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `SocOpsDashboardServiceTest` (4): `openEventsReadsTheComplementFinder_soEscalatedCounts` — the load-bearing leg: the extracted `openEvents(org)` calls the complement finder with exactly `TERMINAL_STATUSES` and an `ESCALATED` event flows through; `terminalStatusesAreExactlyTheClosedStates` (`{RESOLVED, FALSE_POSITIVE}`, not `ESCALATED`/`NEW`/`TRIAGED`); `theSlaSweepQueryExcludesExactlyTheTerminalSet` — the SLA `@Query`'s `NOT IN (...)` set parsed from source equals the constant ([[F2-299]] / [[F2-343]] drift guard); `getDerivesOpenFromTheComplement_andTheInclusionListIsGone` — a source scan proving `get()` reads `openEvents(org)` via the complement finder and the `IN_ANALYSIS`/`CONTAINED`/`NEW`-inclusion list is gone ([[F2-205]] wiring / [[F2-216]] mechanism removal). Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): a surgical revert of only `openEvents(org)`'s body to the inclusion list (keeping the method extracted so the test compiles) makes exactly the two discriminating legs RED (`openEventsReads…`: `open` empty, no ESCALATED; the source scan) while the two vocabulary/drift pins stay green ([[F2-225]]: label which legs discriminate). |

### Fix

`SecurityEventService.TERMINAL_STATUSES = {RESOLVED, FALSE_POSITIVE}` (the two states `resolve()` writes) is declared as the single authority for "closed"; `SecurityEventRepository` gains a complement finder `findByOrganisationIdAndStatusNotInOrderByEventTimeDesc`; and `SocOpsDashboardService.get()` derives its open set from an extracted `openEvents(org)` that reads the complement — so any non-terminal state, including a future one, counts as open. The dead `openCritical` / `countResolvedAtSeverity` placeholder tied to the old block is removed. There is no declared state machine for SecurityEvent to derive the terminal set from ([[F2-343]]'s ideal), so the terminal set is a declared constant and the SLA `@Query`'s `NOT IN (...)` remains a necessary second SQL copy — pinned equal to the constant by the drift-guard test.

### Note — latent in data, live in code ([[F2-283]])

Not re-measured against a running backend (none this slice). The drop is unconditional in code for any tenant with an `ESCALATED` security event; whether any tenant currently holds one was not measured.

### Filed (deferred)

- `SocOpsDashboardService.scanCritsOpen` sums `findingsCritical` over scanner runs **capped at `PageRequest.of(0, 1000)`** and presents it as a tenant-wide figure — an [[F2-345]] capped-aggregate shape at scale (scanner runs accumulate continuously), compounded by summing a per-run count over many historical runs (a metric-semantics question), so it is an owner decision rather than a mechanical fix ([[F2-188]]).

So the platform truthfully flags the arrangement material while the statutory gate the flag implies is silently skipped. |

| **Standards** | [[F2-179]] (a caller-supplied value stored in a case-insensitive column, compared case-sensitively in Java to fire a control — normalise on write, not `equalsIgnoreCase` at one site, so the gate, the KPI and the automation rule all read one token); [[F2-335]] (the direct precedent — a NO-CHECK case-sensitivity control bypass fixed with a manual `trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)` normalise-on-write, verified with a Mockito capture); [[F2-115]] (the §4 gate this bypass reopens); [[F2-182]] (`require` vs `coerce`: nothing upstream refuses a non-vocabulary value today — no CHECK, no coercion — so a 400 would break a request that succeeds today; canonicalise, don't refuse); [[F2-183]] (no CHECK added — `ClosedVocabulary` needs a CHECK to mirror and adding one needs a both-database measurement, blocked with no backend); [[F2-190]] (extend the module's existing test, don't add a class); [[F2-283]] (latent in data / live in code); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — pure service logic + a Mockito capture; the KPI's row selection is SQL). |
| **Found by** | Fanning out a scout over the financial-crime / regulatory modules for the [[F2-179]] case-sensitivity control-bypass shape (a caller value stored verbatim, then compared case-sensitively to fire a control), then re-deriving its top candidate against the code ([[F2-221]] — the scout terminated early on a spend limit and left the verification unfinished). The scout flagged `OutsourcingService:116` storing `materiality` verbatim and the §4 gate keying on `"MATERIAL".equals(...)`, noting the F2-115 comment proves the gate is load-bearing (7 MATERIAL non-core arrangements measured LIVE, one with no `sama_notified_at`). Confirmed the whole chain: `@NotBlank` with no `@Pattern` (DTO line 30), no CHECK on the column (only a DB DEFAULT, V341:2001), a single writer (`createArrangement`; no update path touches `materiality`), and the two case-insensitive SQL readers plus the V208 automation rule that make the disagreement observable. [[F2-335]]'s own warning ("most of the 389 case-sensitivity candidates are entity-derived or guarded upstream") was checked and does not apply here — the value is genuinely caller-supplied and unguarded. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (Mockito, no Spring / DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `OutsourcingLifecycleTest` (+2): `materialityIsCanonicalisedOnWrite_soTheSamaGateCannotBeBypassedByCasing` — the load-bearing leg: `createArrangement("material")` stores `"MATERIAL"` (captured via `ArgumentCaptor`), and the very same record then hits the §4 gate end-to-end (the LIVE transition throws `SAMA_NOTIFIED` / `MATERIAL`); `anUnrecognisedMaterialityIsUppercasedNotRefused` — `createArrangement("important")` does not throw and stores `"IMPORTANT"` ([[F2-182]]: canonicalise, not a 400). Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): a surgical revert of only the call site (line 116 back to `req.materiality()`, keeping the `normaliseMateriality` helper defined so it still compiles) makes exactly the two F2-366 legs RED (`:308` `expected "MATERIAL"`, `:336` `expected "IMPORTANT"`) while the 11 existing tests — the four state machines and the F2-115 gate suite, which use canonical `"MATERIAL"` — stay green ([[F2-225]]: label which legs discriminate). |

### Fix

`OutsourcingService.createArrangement` — the single writer of `materiality` (there is no update path) — now stores `normaliseMateriality(req.materiality())`, a private null-safe `m.trim().toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT)`. The stored value is always canonical, so the case-sensitive `"MATERIAL".equals` §4 gate, the case-insensitive SQL KPIs (`countActiveMaterial` / `findActiveMaterial`) and the V208 automation rule all read the same token. Deliberately a canonicalise and not a refuse ([[F2-182]]): with no CHECK and no upstream coercion, an out-of-vocabulary value succeeds today, so a `require` would break a working request. No `ClosedVocabulary` ([[F2-183]] — it must name a CHECK to mirror, and adding a CHECK needs a both-database measurement that no backend allows this slice).

### Note — latent in data, live in code ([[F2-283]])

Not re-measured against a running backend (none this slice). The bypass is unconditional in code for any caller sending a non-canonical `materiality`. Whether any live row already holds a non-canonical `materiality` (which a one-time normalising `UPDATE` would fix, needing a both-database measurement and explicit OK to touch customer data) is filed, not measured here.

### Filed (deferred)

- A `CHECK (materiality IN ('MATERIAL','NON_MATERIAL'))` on `outsourcing.outsourcing_arrangement.materiality` ([[F2-183]]) — cheaper now that this slice closed the only open writer, but it needs a both-database measurement first (an out-of-vocabulary or non-canonical live row would fail Flyway on deploy), which no backend allows.
- Whether `materiality` should be server-DERIVED from the risk assessment rather than caller-supplied — it is a SAMA materiality judgement legitimately made by the risk team and recorded on the register, so it is caller-supplied by design, not a defect ([[F2-188]] / [[F2-221]]).

## F2-365 — the ESG dashboard's GHG verification rate divided a capped-page numerator by an all-pages denominator

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — the executive ESG readiness dashboard (`GET /api/sustainability/dashboard`, `hasPermission('SUST','READ')`). `SustainabilityDashboardService.ghgVerificationRate` counted verified GHG records over `page.getContent()` — a result page capped at `PageRequest.of(0, 1000)` — while dividing by `page.getTotalElements()`, Spring Data's separate all-pages COUNT. Numerator and denominator were drawn from two different populations, so a tenant with more than 1000 GHG records in one reporting year (ordered `scope ASC, id ASC`, orthogonal to the `verified` flag, so verified rows spread across every page) had verified rows beyond the first page dropped from the numerator while still counted in the denominator — understating the rate. It is the joint-highest-weighted (0.20) component of the ESG Overall Score and is surfaced verbatim as `scoreBreakdown.ghgVerification`, so the understated rate drags the whole executive readiness score/band down for large tenants. Large-tenant defect (>1000 records/year); the arithmetic inconsistency itself is unconditional. |
| **Registers** | none — two services (`.../sust/ghg/service/GhgEmissionRecordService.java`, `.../sust/dashboard/service/SustainabilityDashboardService.java`) + a test added to `GhgEmissionRecordServiceTest` and a new `SustainabilityDashboardServiceTest` (the dashboard service's first). No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-345]] / [[F2-352]] (a KPI/aggregate over a capped `findRecent` / `PageRequest` presented as an all-tenant figure — the same shape on the NIST MTTR mean and the SAMA counterparty dashboard); [[F2-197]] (the same aggregate exposed `recordCount` but not the verified count, so the rate reached for a second, mis-populated fetch); [[F2-282]] (one reader, many derivations — `aggregate` is the single authority for the year's records and now feeds the rate); [[F2-216]] (the fix makes the mismatch unrepresentable — both terms come from one loop); [[F2-205]] (a leg exercising the primitive says nothing about whether the page CALLS it — the source scan is the wiring proof); [[F2-217]] (a full 11-collaborator `dashboard()` render test was weighed and judged disproportionate for a compiler-typed one-line read); [[F2-248]] (the dashboard service had no test); [[F2-283]] (latent in data / live in code); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — pure arithmetic + source scan; the query's row selection is SQL). |
| **Found by** | Fanning out a scout over the ESG / green-finance calculation surface (`sust` / `finance` / `ghg` / `capa` / `vendor`) for arithmetic-correctness defects, then re-deriving its top candidate against the code ([[F2-221]]). The scout flagged `ghgVerificationRate`'s capped-numerator / full-denominator split as the lone dashboard component reading a paged result — every sibling aggregator (`GhgEmissionRecordService.aggregate`, `CmaDisclosureService.readiness`, `TcfdItemService.readiness`, `SustainabilityEvidenceService.aggregate`, …) reads an unpaged `findByOrganisationIdAndReportingYear`. Confirmed verbatim: `total = page.getTotalElements()` vs `verified` counted over `page.getContent()`; the author's own comment ("the GHG aggregate exposes recordCount but not verification rate — pull a slim count via the service's page helper") records how the mismatch arose. Runners-up read and left: `capaCloseRate` (a javadoc-vs-code definitional oddity) and `GreenPortfolioService.summary` feTotal vs the disclosure roll-up (a which-reader view difference) — both owner decisions ([[F2-188]]). |
| **Verification** | hermetic (pure static helper + a source scan, no Spring / DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `GhgEmissionRecordServiceTest.aggregate_countsVerifiedOverTheFullPopulation` — the load-bearing leg: `verifiedCount` and `recordCount` over the same list. `SustainabilityDashboardServiceTest` (3): `pctOf` arithmetic (900 / 1500 = 60.0, not the 66.7 the capped page yielded; 0-denominator → 0) and a source scan proving the rate reads `ghg.get("verifiedCount")` / `ghg.get("recordCount")` and the capped-page mechanism (`listByYear` / `PageRequest`) is gone ([[F2-205]] wiring / [[F2-216]]). Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): a surgical revert (restore the paged `ghgVerificationRate` + revert the call site + drop `aggregate`'s `verifiedCount`, KEEPING `pctOf` defined so the test class still compiles) makes exactly the two discriminating legs RED (`aggregate…`: `expected 3`; the source scan: found `listByYear` / `PageRequest`, missing `ghg.get("verifiedCount")`), while the `pctOf` arithmetic legs stay green ([[F2-225]]: label which legs discriminate). |

### Fix

`GhgEmissionRecordService.aggregate(year)` — the single unpaged read the dashboard already calls — now counts `verifiedCount` in its existing loop over `all`, so it is over the same full population as `recordCount` by construction. `SustainabilityDashboardService` derives the rate via a pure package-private helper `pctOf(asInt(ghg.get("verifiedCount")), asInt(ghg.get("recordCount")))` over that already-fetched aggregate map, and the paged `ghgVerificationRate` method (and its redundant capped query) is deleted. The two terms of the rate can no longer be drawn from different populations, and the dashboard makes one fewer query per request.

### Note — latent in data, live in code ([[F2-283]])

Not re-measured against a running backend (none this slice). The arithmetic inconsistency is unconditional in code; it only diverges from the true rate once a tenant has more than 1000 GHG records in one reporting year, so it is a large-tenant defect rather than one that mis-computes for every tenant.

### Filed (deferred)

- `SustainabilityDashboardService.capaCloseRate` — its javadoc says "(closed + verified) / total" but the body counts `verified` only, and its population (`CorrectiveActionService.aggregate`) excludes CLOSED/CANCELLED entirely, so an actually-closed CAPA is in neither the numerator nor the denominator. Internally coherent as "fraction of active CAPAs that are verified/ready-to-close," so it is a javadoc-vs-code definitional oddity rather than an unambiguous arithmetic bug — owner decision ([[F2-188]]).
- `GreenPortfolioService.summary`'s `feTotal` sums financed emissions over ALL lifecycle stages while `FinancedEmissionsService.computeTotalForYear` (the disclosure roll-up) sums only APPROVED/PUBLISHED — two readers of "financed-emissions total" that plausibly serve different views (portfolio management vs regulatory disclosure), a [[F2-205]]-shaped which-reader question left for an owner decision.

## F2-364 — the SAMA reg-reporting "in flight" set was a hand-typed subset that dropped ACKNOWLEDGED

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a board/operator-facing SAMA regulatory-reporting dashboard indicator (`regreporting.reg_report_filing`). `RegReportingService.dashboard()` counted `inFlightFilingCount` and built the `inFlightByStatus` / `inFlightByRegulator` breakdowns over `IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES`, a hand-typed 6-status list. The declared machine (`ALLOWED`) has terminal set `{CLOSED, EXEMPTED}`, so the non-terminal complement is 7 states; the hand-typed list was that complement MINUS `ACKNOWLEDGED` (`ACKNOWLEDGED → CLOSED`, a declared non-terminal state). So a filing the regulator has acknowledged but that is not yet CLOSED was absent from the in-flight count and could never appear in the by-status breakdown — under-reporting open regulatory-reporting work in the flattering direction, until the filing was closed. |
| **Registers** | none — a service (`tss-grc-backend/.../regreporting/service/RegReportingService.java`) + a new unit test (`RegReportingInFlightStatusContractTest`, the service's first). No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-196]] ("open / in-flight" is the COMPLEMENT of a declared terminal set, never a second hand-typed list — an inclusion list silently drops the state nobody remembered); [[F2-343]] (derive the terminal set FROM the machine, never type it — the fraud open-count precedent); [[F2-336]] / [[F2-361]] (the same complement rule on BCM CAPAs and the committee overdue sweep); [[F2-205]] / [[F2-282]] (which reader is authoritative and do they agree — `countOverdue`, `countSubmittedSince` and `upcoming` all treat SUBMITTED + ACKNOWLEDGED as peers / use the terminal complement; `IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES` was the lone outlier); [[F2-283]] (latent in data / live in code); [[F2-248]] (the service had no test); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — reflection over the constants; the query's row selection is SQL). |
| **Found by** | Fanning out a scout over the cold modules (knowledge, board_pack, governance, regreporting, sharia, openbanking, aml, fraud, consumer, nca_ecc) for the F2-196 inclusion-list shape, then re-deriving its top candidate ([[F2-221]]). The scout flagged `IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES` dropping ACKNOWLEDGED plus a residual "in flight = not yet acknowledged" reading. Refuted by the set's own contents — it also includes SCHEDULED / IN_PREPARATION / IN_REVIEW / APPROVED / REJECTED, none of which is "in transit to the regulator," so it plainly means "all non-terminal work," and dropping only ACKNOWLEDGED is a drift rather than a narrower question. Confirmed the machine's terminal set is exactly `{CLOSED, EXEMPTED}` and that three sibling readers treat SUBMITTED + ACKNOWLEDGED as peers. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (reflection over the private static constants, no Spring / DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `RegReportingInFlightStatusContractTest` (3 tests): `terminalSetIsExactlyTheMachinesEmptyOutgoingStates`, `inFlightIsExactlyTheComplementOfTheTerminalSet`, `acknowledgedIsInFlight_notDropped`. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): reverting only `IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES` to the hand-typed 6-set (keeping `TERMINAL_STATUSES` derived so it still compiles) makes the complement leg and the ACKNOWLEDGED leg RED (`to contain "ACKNOWLEDGED" but could not find`), while the terminal-set leg stays green — a surgical revert that isolates the finding. |

### Fix

Derive both `TERMINAL_STATUSES` (the declared states with no outgoing edge) and `IN_FLIGHT_STATUSES` (the complement) from the `ALLOWED` machine, so neither can drift and the in-flight view can never again silently drop a non-terminal state. Behaviour-identical for every reader except the in-flight view, which now includes ACKNOWLEDGED. `overdueRecent` re-filters its input by `OVERDUE_APPLICABLE` (which excludes ACKNOWLEDGED), so it is unaffected; `inFlightByStatus` is a dynamically-keyed map, so an ACKNOWLEDGED bucket surfaces automatically — no DTO or FE change.

### Note — latent in data, live in code ([[F2-283]])

Not re-measured against a running backend (none this slice); reachable through ordinary use the moment a filing reaches ACKNOWLEDGED — a real lifecycle step between SUBMITTED and CLOSED (the regulator has acknowledged receipt, the org has not yet closed the filing out).

### Filed (deferred)

- `OVERDUE_APPLICABLE`, `countOverdue`'s `{SUBMITTED, ACKNOWLEDGED, CLOSED, EXEMPTED}` and `countSubmittedSince`'s `{SUBMITTED, ACKNOWLEDGED, CLOSED}` are left as hand-typed sets — each asks a genuinely NARROWER question than "in flight" ([[F2-290]]'s exception: a narrower question is not a dropped-state bug), so they are not complement-of-terminal counts and were read and left.
- (From the same scout sweep, and NOT this shape) `CcmService`: the runner status vocabulary is `{PASS, FAIL, ERROR, SKIPPED, TIMEOUT}` — `LdapGroupMembershipRunner` emits `SKIPPED` when `grc.ccm.ldap.enabled=false` — but the consecutive-failure ladder (`isFailureLike` / `"PASS"`) and the dashboard's four status counts both handle only `{PASS, FAIL, ERROR, TIMEOUT}`, so a SKIPPED run neither increments nor resets the failure counter and is invisible on the dashboard ([[F2-293]]'s produced-token-no-reader-handles). Surfacing SKIPPED needs a `DashboardSnapshot` field + FE, and how a skip should affect the failure ladder is a policy judgment — a product / owner decision ([[F2-188]]), not a hermetic fix.
- `sharia.ShariaService.dashboard()` counts open Sharia findings as `{OPEN, REMEDIATION}`, dropping `VERIFIED` (declared non-terminal, `VERIFIED → CLOSED`) — but there is no declared `TERMINAL_STATUSES` constant and every reader consistently excludes VERIFIED, so "an open finding still needs remediation; VERIFIED is done-pending-closure" is a defensible narrower reading. Owner decision, filed not forced.

## F2-363 — the SAMA Op-Res completeness denominator was hard-coded /5, not the tenant's active-pillar count

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a board-facing SAMA Operational-Resilience self-assessment completeness indicator (`opres.opres_assessment`, SAMA Op-Res 2024). `OpResService.createAssessment` set `completeness = "0/5"` while `upsertCell` recomputes the denominator from `pillarRepo.findActiveForOrg(org).size()` — shared catalog rows (`organisation_id IS NULL`) plus tenant-specific extensions, filtered `isActive = true` (the repository's own javadoc). The active-pillar count is genuinely variable per tenant, so a freshly created assessment on a tenant with ≠ 5 active pillars showed a denominator that contradicted both the real count and the value the first cell edit recomputes — understating (6 shown as 5) or overstating (4 shown as 5) the work the board's Risk Committee sees, until the first cell upsert corrected it. |
| **Registers** | none — a service (`tss-grc-backend/.../opres/service/OpResService.java`) + a new unit test (`OpResServiceTest`, the service's first). No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-197]] (a figure computed one way on create and another on update, disagreeing with reality until touched — F2-197 built the KPI-tile version of this); [[F2-195]] (the correct dynamic rule sat in `upsertCell` beside the create that hard-coded a constant — the `|| N` shape, a codebase holding the right rule next to the place it was not applied); [[F2-282]] (one predicate, N readers — a single `completeness(scored, orgId)` helper computes the denominator for both create and every edit, so they cannot drift); [[F2-283]] (latent in data / live in code — correct at exactly 5 active pillars, wrong the moment a tenant's count differs); [[F2-248]] (the service had no test at all — a path with no test is not a path somebody decided was safe); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — mocked repos; the pillar query's row selection is SQL, only a live probe could count rows). |
| **Found by** | Reading a cold Saudi-module service end-to-end against the battery — `module/opres`, one service, SAMA Op-Res 2024, no prior test. Most was sound (declared machine with an explicit terminal set, DTO-bound create so no mass-assignment, `approvedByUserId` from the principal, a cross-tenant pillar check, an uncapped cell aggregate). The one inconsistency was `createAssessment`'s hard-coded `"0/5"` against `upsertCell`'s dynamic `findActiveForOrg(...).size()`. `OpResPillarRepository`'s own javadoc — "shared catalog rows plus any tenant-specific extensions" — confirmed the count varies per tenant, so the hard-code defeats the very query it sits beside. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (mocked repos, no DB — [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]). `OpResServiceTest` (3 tests, the service's first): `createAssessment_completenessDenominatorIsTheActivePillarCount_notHardcodedFive` (6 active pillars → `"0/6"`), `createAssessment_completenessTracksAThreePillarTenant` (3 → `"0/3"`, so a hard-coded constant of any value fails, not just 5), `createAssessment_numeratorIsZeroBeforeAnyCellIsScored`. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): reverting only the create-site to `"0/5"` (keeping the helper so it still compiles) makes both `isEqualTo` legs RED (`expected "0/6" / "0/3" but was "0/5"`); the third errs on `UnnecessaryStubbingException` because the reverted literal body never consults the pillar query at all — which is itself the defect. |

### Fix

Extract one `completeness(long scored, Long orgId)` returning `scored + "/" + pillarRepo.findActiveForOrg(orgId).size()`. `createAssessment` now calls `completeness(0, orgId)`; `upsertCell` calls `completeness(withCurrent, a.getOrganisationId())` (behaviour-identical — the reader the create is being aligned to). One source of the denominator, so create and every subsequent edit agree ([[F2-282]]).

### Note — latent in data, live in code ([[F2-283]])

Correct today wherever a tenant has exactly the five-pillar SAMA catalog active; wrong the moment a tenant activates a sixth pillar or deactivates one — which `findActiveForOrg` and `upsertCell`'s recompute exist precisely to handle. Not re-measured against a running backend (none this slice); the migration only CREATEs `opres.opres_pillar` (V341), so the catalog is seeded outside Flyway and the current per-tenant count was not read.

### Filed (deferred)

- `submit()` and `close()` stamp `submitted_at` / `closed_at` from the server clock, but `OpResAssessment` declares **no `submitted_by` / `closed_by` column** — so those lifecycle acts record WHEN with no WHO. This is NOT [[F2-256]] (the columns do not exist to be left unwritten); adding attribution is a migration plus a design decision about the Op-Res sign-off model, not a hermetic fix. The SAME shape holds for `data_officer` DPIA / Breach / EthicsReview, which stamp `decided_at` with no `decided_by` column.
- `upsertCell` counts `withCurrent` over cell ROWS while the denominator is the active-PILLAR count, so deactivating a pillar that already has a scored cell can momentarily yield `withCurrent > total` (`"6/5"`). A rare mid-assessment operator action; noted, not fixed (scope).

## F2-362 — the SGI "target met" evidence gate checked FK presence, not the evidence item's state

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P2 — a public governance/assurance control on the Saudi Green Initiative commitment register (`sust.sgi_commitment`, CMA/ESG). `SgiCommitmentService.achieve` (Rule D — "no public 'target met' claim without attached evidence") gated on `cur.getEvidenceItemId() == null`. `evidence_item_id` is `FK_sgi_evidence_item` → `evidence.evidence_items` (V250), so the gate was discharged by ANY non-null id the FK accepts — a REJECTED, EXPIRED, DRAFT or PENDING_REVIEW evidence item, i.e. the evidence module's own rejected/lapsed output. So an SGI commitment could be publicly declared ACHIEVED, with `achieved_by`/`achieved_at` stamped, citing an evidence item its own four-eyes review had rejected or whose validity had lapsed. |
| **Registers** | none — a service guard (`tss-grc-backend/.../sust/sgi/service/SgiCommitmentService.java`) + its unit test. No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-243]] (the EXACT same defect — a four-eyes/evidence gate discharged by id-PRESENCE rather than the referenced record's STATE — fixed for GHG's Rule 2 in the SAME module; this is its untouched sibling, [[F2-215]] two-of-N); [[F2-282]] (one predicate, N readers — reuse `EvidenceItemRepository.findUsableAsEvidence`, never a second copy); [[F2-196]] (a caller cannot invent its own idea of what counts as evidence; the state vocabulary is `module/evidence`'s); [[F2-182]] (the legacy free-text `evidence_ref` branch is deliberately untouched — a request naming an external assurance statement keeps working); [[F2-180]] (the refusal names the item's state); [[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]] (hermetic — the `findUsableAsEvidence` query's row selection is SQL, only a live probe could count rows). |
| **Found by** | Sweeping the coldest ungated vein — F2-243's "a gate consumes a foreign key but checks presence, not the referenced record's state" (≈119 findings back). A grep for `getEvidenceItemId() == null` surfaced GHG (already fixed, carries the F2-243 comment) and `SgiCommitmentService.achieve` — same accessor, same module, same dual-branch (`evidenceItemId` OR legacy `evidenceRef`) — with the presence test still live. V250 confirmed the FK to `evidence.evidence_items`. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (mocked `EvidenceItemRepository`, no DB — [[F2-320]]/[[F2-325]]). `SgiCommitmentServiceTest` (26 tests): `achieve_refusesWhenEvidenceItemIsNotUsable` (a REJECTED item → 400 naming the state), `achieve_acceptsWhenEvidenceItemIsUsable` (an APPROVED, in-date item → ACHIEVED), `achieve_viaLegacyEvidenceRefDoesNotConsultTheItemRepo` (the free-text branch short-circuits — `verify(never()).findUsableAsEvidence`), and the pre-existing `achieve_acceptsWhenDecreaseTargetMet` updated to stub a usable item ([[F2-237]]: an unstubbed mock returns empty, so the gate would otherwise fail). Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): reverting only `requireRuleDEvidence`'s body to the presence test makes `achieve_refusesWhenEvidenceItemIsNotUsable` RED (the achieve succeeds where it must throw). |

### Fix

Extract `requireRuleDEvidence(cur)` mirroring GHG's `requireRule2Evidence`: the legacy `evidence_ref` free-text branch short-circuits first ([[F2-182]] — untouched); an absent `evidenceItemId` throws "requires evidence"; otherwise `evidenceItems.findUsableAsEvidence(itemId, org(), LocalDate.now())` must resolve (APPROVED + not past `validTo`), and the refusal names the item's state so the caller knows whether to chase a review or re-collect ([[F2-180]]). The state is checked at CONSUMPTION, not at attach time, because an item can be APPROVED when linked and EXPIRED by the time the pledge is declared met.

### Note — latent in data, live in code ([[F2-283]])

No dev backend this slice, so the DB population that discharged the gate is not re-measured here — but F2-243 measured it live in the SAME evidence subsystem: **51 of 78 items NOT APPROVED** (31 EXPIRED / 15 PENDING_REVIEW / 4 DRAFT / 1 REJECTED, dev = prod), so the discharging population is real. The gate is reachable through ordinary use (attach an item, let its review reject it or its validity lapse, then achieve the commitment).

### Filed (deferred)

- **`BcmRemediationService.transitionCapa`** (line 352) gates an ISO 22301 corrective-action CLOSURE on `a.getEvidenceId() == null` — the same presence shape — but `bcm.corrective_actions.evidence_id` is `BIGINT NULL` with **no foreign key**, no resolver, and the FE attaches it via a raw-number `prompt` (no picker). So what it references cannot be established hermetically (it may be `evidence.evidence_items`, an attachment id, or a free reference), and applying `findUsableAsEvidence` to an unconfirmed referent risks breaking every close ([[F2-214]]). It is a design/owner question — should BCM CAPA evidence go through the platform evidence subsystem with a real FK and a picker, like GHG's S-C bridge — not a hermetic fix. (`BcmCycleService`, `ContinuityStrategyService`, `BcmGovernanceRecord`, `BcmBiaAssessment`, `BcmComplianceMapping` all carry the same FK-less `evidence_id`.)
- **`NdiSubmissionPackageService.preflight`** counts `criticalNoCapa` (its one hard finalization blocker) over EVERY critical gap with no CAPA, while the adjacent `openCritical` warning scopes to the not-settled complement `{RESOLVED,CLOSED,ACCEPTED_RISK}` (the NDI gap module's own definition, [[F2-336]]). So a settled critical gap with no corrective action (cleanly, an ACCEPTED_RISK one — risk formally accepted) blocks the SDAIA submission. But whether an accepted-risk critical gap must still carry a CAPA before a regulator return is a policy question, and loosening a blocker is the dangerous (false-assurance) direction — an **owner decision** ([[F2-188]]), filed not forced. (F2-342's decider-attribution shape is **refuted** here: `NdiSubmissionPackageService` builds a signature manifest of type/id/code/status, not a governance-attestation sheet dropping a WHO, and its score aggregates are uncapped and divide-guarded.)

## F2-361 — the committee overdue sweep's query excluded DEFERRED, its own writer's accepted state

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a governance-accountability blind spot on the committee action register (`admin.committee`, CMA CG / SAMA RGov). `CommitteeActionItemRepository.findShouldBeOverdue` (the query feeding the scheduled overdue sweep) selected `status IN ('OPEN','IN_PROGRESS')`. But `defer(id, newDueDate, reason)` reschedules the deadline and moves the item to DEFERRED ("revisit by newDueDate"), `startProgress` accepts only OPEN/OVERDUE (so a DEFERRED item cannot be resumed), and `markOverdue` — the sole writer that flips an item to OVERDUE — bars only `{COMPLETED, CANCELLED, OVERDUE}`, i.e. it ACCEPTS DEFERRED. So when a deferred committee/board action's revised deadline passed, the sweep never selected it, `markOverdue` was never called, no F8 escalation fired, and it never returned to matters-arising (which lists OVERDUE). Deferral became a permanent escape from overdue accountability. |
| **Registers** | none — a repository `@Query` (`tss-grc-backend/.../admin/committee/repository/CommitteeActionItemRepository.java`) + a hermetic contract gate. No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-177]] (two artefacts — here a query and its writer — that disagree, with nobody maintaining the agreement); [[F2-196]] ("open/should-be-overdue" is the complement of a declared closed set, never a hand-typed inclusion list); [[F2-343]] (the hermetic `@Query`-vs-machine contract idiom); [[F2-299]] (a second copy of a vocabulary must be pinned so it cannot drift); [[F2-322]] / [[F2-324]] (the same sweep's transaction boundary and audit row — fixed earlier, its query scope untouched). |
| **Found by** | An inclusion-list status-count sweep ([[F2-196]]) across cold modules: reading the committee action-item machine (create → OPEN, start, complete, cancel, defer, markOverdue) against the sweep query showed `markOverdue` accepts DEFERRED while `findShouldBeOverdue` excludes it. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (source contract, no DB — the `@Query`'s row selection is SQL and only a live probe could count rows, [[F2-320]]/[[F2-325]]). `CommitteeOverdueSweepScopeTest`: derives the vocabulary (every `setStatus("X")` literal + the resolved `INITIAL_STATUS` constant) and `markOverdue`'s barred set (its `"X".equals(prev)` guard, scoped to that method's brace-balanced body), then asserts the sweep `@Query`'s `status IN (...)` set equals `vocabulary − barred` — both derived, so a new status forces the assertion and the `@Query` cannot silently drift. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): reverting only the query makes both legs RED (sweep `{OPEN, IN_PROGRESS}` ≠ accepted `{DEFERRED, IN_PROGRESS, OPEN}`). |

### Fix

Add `DEFERRED` to `findShouldBeOverdue`'s `@Query` so the sweep selects exactly the states `markOverdue` accepts. `findOpenByCommittee` / `findOpenByOwner` (the "matters arising" / "my open actions" lists, `{OPEN, IN_PROGRESS, OVERDUE}`) are deliberately left unchanged: a not-yet-due DEFERRED item should stay dormant until its rescheduled date, and once that date passes the fixed sweep flips it to OVERDUE — which those lists already include — so it resurfaces then. Only the sweep query needed the state.

### Note on the gate's first draft

The vocabulary extraction initially missed OPEN, because the create assigns the initial state via `ServerOwnedState.requireInitial(in.getStatus(), INITIAL_STATUS, …)` — a declared CONSTANT, not a string literal. Resolving `INITIAL_STATUS = "OPEN"` (rather than parsing the `requireInitial` call) fixed it — a reminder that the action-item "machine" here is implicit and its initial state hides behind a constant reference.

### Filed (deferred)

- **The outsourcing "active material" inclusion list** (`OutsourcingArrangementRepository.findActiveMaterial` / `countActiveMaterial`, `status IN ('BOARD_APPROVED','SAMA_NOTIFIED','LIVE','UNDER_REVIEW')`) excludes `SUSPENDED`, a non-terminal state. Whether a *suspended* material outsourcing arrangement counts as "active" for SAMA oversight is a semantic/owner call (no dead token, no obviously-active state dropped), so it was read and left rather than forced ([[F2-188]]).

## F2-360 — three readers of "open" on IncidentsPage disagreed; one isIncidentOpen predicate over the declared terminal set

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a pessimistic KPI over-report on the incident register (`module/incident` → `cyber.incidents`, [[F2-345]]'s register). `IncidentsPage.tsx` had THREE readers of "open/active" that disagreed: the regulator-template picker (line 282) excluded the correct terminal set `{CLOSED, RESOLVED}`; `open_count` — the "Open" KPI tile AND the OverviewStrip lifecycle it feeds — excluded `{CLOSED, RECOVERED}`, where `RECOVERED` is a phantom (0 rows, not a legal status per `IncidentService.legalStatus`, [[F2-359]]) so the 10/44 `RESOLVED` incidents leaked in; and the `critical` KPI excluded only `{CLOSED}`. So the "Open" KPI over-counted open incidents by the RESOLVED count and the critical KPI counted RESOLVED criticals as open — flatteringly the wrong direction for a governance register ([[F2-196]]'s warned direction). |
| **Registers** | none — a frontend page (`tss-grc-ui-v2/src/pages/incidents/IncidentsPage.tsx`) + a new shared predicate (`src/lib/incidentStatus.ts`) + a hermetic gate. No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-196]] ("open" = complement of a declared terminal set, never a hand-typed inclusion/exclusion list); [[F2-282]] (one predicate, N readers, never a third copy); [[F2-359]] (the sibling — `RESOLVED` is the real recovery-phase terminal, `RECOVERED` the phantom the FE knew and the backend never writes); [[F2-205]] (a leg exercising a primitive says nothing about whether the code CALLS it — the wiring proof is what matters); [[F2-180]] (FE/BE vocabulary drift). |
| **Found by** | Executing [[F2-359]]'s filed incident-KPI candidate ([[F2-188]]): reading the three `IncidentsPage` "open" readers against the backend authority `IncidentService.legalStatus` (which coerces `status` to `OPEN | INVESTIGATING | RESOLVED | CLOSED`, terminal `{RESOLVED, CLOSED}`). |
| **Verification** | hermetic (`tsc --noEmit` + vitest — no backend). New `lib/incidentStatus.ts` declares `INCIDENT_TERMINAL_STATUSES = {RESOLVED, CLOSED}` (mirroring the backend authority) and `isIncidentOpen`; `open_count`, `critical` and the regulator picker all call it. `incidentOpenPredicate.test.ts`: unit legs (terminal set = {CLOSED, RESOLVED}; RESOLVED/CLOSED terminal; OPEN/INVESTIGATING/absent open) + a source-scan wiring leg (every open-reader calls `isIncidentOpen`, `>=3` sites) + a phantom-`!== 'RECOVERED'` ban (comments stripped). Full FE suite green. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): reverting ONLY the page (predicate lib unchanged) makes the two source-scan legs RED (wiring 0<3; `!== 'RECOVERED'` present) while the two unit legs stay GREEN — the [[F2-205]] point in one run. |

### Fix

Route the three "open/active" readers through one `isIncidentOpen(status) = !{RESOLVED, CLOSED}.has(status)`. The picker's behaviour is preserved (it already excluded exactly that set); `open_count` and `critical` are corrected (they no longer count `RESOLVED` as open). `closed` (`=== 'CLOSED'`) is left counting only archived rows — `RESOLVED` is done-awaiting-formal-closure, a distinct state ([[F2-359]]). `INCIDENT_TERMINAL_STATUSES` is a MIRROR of the backend `IncidentService.legalStatus` vocabulary (the frontend cannot see the Java state machine), declared once with the authority cited — not a copy of `openbanking.ts`'s unrelated SAMA open-banking `IncidentStatus` ([[F2-282]]).

### Why a source-scan wiring gate, not a KPI-strip leaf extraction

The [[F2-359]] filing scoped this as needing "the inline KPI strip extracted to an exported leaf component ... because every render test here mounts a leaf/tab, never the monolithic self-fetching page — a page-structure decision, its own slice." That assumed the wiring proof had to be a RENDER test. It does not. A source-scan gate that asserts every open-reader calls `isIncidentOpen` (and no bare `!== 'RECOVERED'` open-comparison remains) is a valid [[F2-205]] wiring proof AND a stronger one: it covers all three readers — including the regulator picker at line 282 — where a single render test would have covered only the KPI strip. So the extraction is not required to verify the fix, and this slice needs no page-structure change.

### Filed (deferred, unchanged from [[F2-359]])

- **`STATUS_OPTIONS` (the incident edit form) offers `CONTAINED`/`ERADICATED`/`RECOVERED` and omits `RESOLVED`** — tokens `legalStatus` silently coerces to `OPEN` on save ([[F2-180]]'s shape on a form vocabulary). A form-behaviour change, deferred.

## F2-359 — the FE status vocabulary carried the phantom RECOVERED and not the real RESOLVED, so 10/44 incident rows rendered a grey, raw-token badge

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a status-badge honesty gap on the incident register (`module/incident` → `cyber.incidents`, [[F2-345]]'s register). `IncidentService.legalStatus` coerces `status` to exactly `{OPEN, INVESTIGATING, RESOLVED, CLOSED}` ("CK_incidents_status is strict"; `mapPhaseToStatus` sends the NIST RECOVERY/POST_INCIDENT phases to `RESOLVED`), so `RESOLVED` is the real recovery-phase terminal and `RECOVERED` is not a legal status at all. Yet `lib/labels.ts` carried `RECOVERED` in BOTH `STATUS_KEY` and `STATUS_TONE` (a phantom — 0 rows) and `RESOLVED` in NEITHER. So a `RESOLVED` incident (10 of 44 register rows, dev = prod per [[F2-345]]) rendered `STATUS_TONE['RESOLVED'] ?? 'neutral'` = a GREY badge indistinguishable from `CLOSED`/`DRAFT`, labelled with the raw English token `RESOLVED` (`statusLabel` falls back to the token) on an Arabic-primary UI (house rule 7). |
| **Registers** | none — a frontend shared vocabulary map (`tss-grc-ui-v2/src/lib/labels.ts`) + the two i18n dictionaries (`src/translations/en.ts`, `ar.ts`). No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-357]] (the sibling "fixed the label, left the lookup" family — F2-357 completed `STATUS_TONE` for the five PDPL breach statuses and built the completeness gate; this is the same family, one register over); [[F2-211]] (a status in the data with no label key → raw token); [[F2-196]] / [[F2-180]] (FE/BE vocabulary drift — the screen knows a token the column never stores and not one it does); [[F2-198]] (the F2-357 gate's population is the keys of one map, so a status in neither map is invisible to it). |
| **Found by** | Re-verifying [[F2-358]]'s filed incident-KPI candidate against the code ([[F2-188]]): reading the three `IncidentsPage` "open" readers surfaced the backend vocabulary (`legalStatus` / `mapPhaseToStatus`), which showed `RESOLVED` real and `RECOVERED` phantom — and grepping `lib/labels.ts` showed `RESOLVED` absent from both maps while `RECOVERED` was present in both. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (`tsc --noEmit` + vitest — no backend). Additive: `STATUS_KEY.RESOLVED = 'statusResolved'`, `STATUS_TONE.RESOLVED = 'success'`, `statusResolved` in en (`Resolved`) and ar (`محلولة`). `breachStatusToneCompleteness.test.ts` extended with a `RESOLVED` pin (label key + tone); `translationKeysDeclared.test.ts` green (en/ar key sets stay identical). Full FE suite green. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): removing both `RESOLVED` entries from `labels.ts` makes the pin leg RED (`expected "statusResolved", received undefined`) while the completeness leg stays GREEN — demonstrating the [[F2-198]] blind spot in the same run (RESOLVED removed from `STATUS_KEY` → outside `STATUS_KEY ⊆ STATUS_TONE`'s population). |

### Fix

Add `RESOLVED` to the two shared status maps in `lib/labels.ts` and the label key to both dictionaries — the exact [[F2-357]] shape (a status live in the data, missing from the FE vocabulary). Tone `'success'` follows the platform convention (done, awaiting formal closure — matching `RECOVERED`, distinct from `CLOSED`'s `neutral` for archived). `RECOVERED` is deliberately LEFT in both maps: `STATUS_TONE`/`STATUS_KEY` are platform-wide shared maps and `RECOVERED` may be a legal status in another register, so removing it is not this slice's call. Additive and behaviour-preserving for every working row — a `RESOLVED` badge goes from grey/raw to green/localised; nothing else changes.

### Filed (deferred)

The [[F2-196]] fix is to route all three through one `isIncidentOpen` predicate keyed on the declared terminal set `{RESOLVED, CLOSED}` — but a proper [[F2-205]] wiring proof needs the inline KPI strip (lines 567–582) extracted into an exported leaf component, because every render test in this codebase mounts a leaf/tab (`SubmissionAnalyticsCard`, `MatrixTab`, `OverviewTab`), never the monolithic self-fetching page. That extraction is a page-structure decision, so it is its own slice, not a side effect of a labels fix.
- **`STATUS_OPTIONS` (the incident edit form) offers `CONTAINED`/`ERADICATED`/`RECOVERED` and omits `RESOLVED`** — tokens `legalStatus` silently coerces to `OPEN` on save (F2-180's shape on a form vocabulary). A form-behaviour change, deferred.

## F2-358 — the "Open for review" KPI read 0 / "No pending submissions" on the reviewer's own pending queue (openCount swept into the review-mean's divide-by-zero guard)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P2 — a KPI that under-reports pending work in the flattering direction, on the reviewer's own queue. `SubmissionAnalyticsCard` computes `ttrStats` in one `useMemo` returning both the mean time-to-review (`avgHours`, denominator `reviewed.length`) and `openCount` (submissions `SUBMITTED`/`UNDER_REVIEW`, independent of any review). `openCount` was computed AFTER `if (reviewed.length === 0) return { avgHours: null, count: 0, openCount: 0 }` — the mean's divide-by-zero guard — so whenever the visible set held no reviewed row, the "Open for review" KPI read **0** with the sub-label **"No pending submissions"** while submissions were genuinely pending. ⚠ Not merely a fresh tenant: `WorkflowSubmissionsPage:485` passes the *client-side-filtered* `visibleItems`, and its `OPEN` status filter is exactly `SUBMITTED \| UNDER_REVIEW` (`matchesStatus`, line 56). So selecting the reviewer's own pending queue (`?status=OPEN` or `?status=SUBMITTED`) yields a set with zero reviewed rows, and the KPI read "Open for review: 0 / No pending submissions" directly above a table full of pending rows. The card hides itself only when `items.length === 0`, so the state renders. Flattering under-report ([[F2-193]] / [[F2-195]] / [[F2-210]]): the queue says "nothing to do" when there is. |
| **Registers** | none — a frontend KPI computation (`tss-grc-ui-v2/src/components/workflows/SubmissionAnalyticsCard.tsx`). No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-357]] (filed this exact defect — the "Filed / not done" of the same read-only sweep); [[F2-193]] / [[F2-195]] / [[F2-210]] (an aggregate that errs in the flattering direction); the same-directory `ProcessLifecycleBar` precedent (KPIs computed from the already-fetched list are extracted as pure, exported, unit-tested functions). |
| **Found by** | Executing [[F2-357]]'s filing and re-verifying it against the code ([[F2-188]]): the `openCount` line (a filter over `items`, no dependency on `reviewed`) sits below the `reviewed.length === 0` early return that exists only for the mean. Re-verification also sharpened the live path — the card receives the filtered `visibleItems`, so the `OPEN`/`SUBMITTED` filter is the primary trigger, not just a fresh tenant. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (`tsc --noEmit` + vitest — no backend). `computeTtrStats` extracted as an exported pure function; `SubmissionAnalyticsCard.test.tsx` 5/5 — four pure legs (openCount survives the no-review path; openCount counts only `SUBMITTED`/`UNDER_REVIEW`; a genuine zero stays 0; the mean averages over the reviewed set only) and one render leg proving the "Open for review" KPI reads `openCount` (5 pending / 0 reviewed renders "5" + "awaiting reviewer decision", not "0" / "No pending submissions"). Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): moving `openCount` back below the early return makes exactly the two discriminating legs RED (`expected +0 to be 5`; the render leg renders "No pending submissions") while the other three stay green. Full frontend suite green. |

### Fix

Extract `computeTtrStats(items)` as an exported pure function — the same-directory `ProcessLifecycleBar` idiom, where KPIs computed from the already-fetched list are pure functions of `items` and therefore testable without a render — and compute `openCount` BEFORE the mean's `reviewed.length === 0` guard. That guard is scoped to `avgHours`, whose denominator is `reviewed.length`; `openCount` (a filter over `items`) never needed it. The component's `useMemo` now just calls `computeTtrStats(items)`; the KPI wiring is unchanged. The extraction is what makes the invariant testable — the defect lived precisely because the KPI computation had no test.

## F2-357 — the five PDPL breach statuses localised but rendered a GREY badge (STATUS_KEY completed, STATUS_TONE not)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a wrong badge TONE (not a wrong label) on the PDPL Article 20 breach register. `lib/labels.ts` has two maps: `STATUS_KEY` (status → i18n label) and `STATUS_TONE` (status → badge colour). F2-211 added the five breach statuses `NOTIFIED` / `INVESTIGATING` / `INVESTIGATED` / `ESCALATED` / `REMEDIATED` to `STATUS_KEY` (so `statusLabel` localises them) but never to `STATUS_TONE`. Badges render `STATUS_TONE[status] ?? 'neutral'`, so on the `privacy.data_breaches` register (`PrivacyPage.tsx:293`) and `PdplBreachConsole` all five rendered a grey/neutral badge — an `ESCALATED` breach visually indistinguishable from a `CLOSED` one, `INVESTIGATING`/`NOTIFIED` stripped of their warning/info tone, `REMEDIATED` of its success tone — on a register where an operator scans tone to spot the urgent rows. F2-211 measured these statuses on 11 of 17 live breaches, so it was live in both databases. |
| **Registers** | none — a frontend label/tone map (`tss-grc-ui-v2/src/lib/labels.ts`). No data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | PDPL Article 20 (breach register); [[F2-205]] / [[F2-211]] (the "fixed the label, left the lookup" half-fix — a status→map completed on one map and not its sibling); [[F2-266]] (count the population — here, gate the completeness). |
| **Found by** | A read-only frontend sweep for label-vs-predicate and status-map-gap defects. `STATUS_TONE` (14 keys) was exactly `STATUS_KEY` (19 keys) minus the five F2-211 breach statuses; `PrivacyPage` and `PdplBreachConsole` both consume it via `STATUS_TONE[status] ?? 'neutral'`, and no breach-specific tone map exists anywhere, so the grey fallback was the only tone those five ever got. |
| **Verification** | hermetic (`tsc --noEmit` + vitest — no backend). `breachStatusToneCompleteness.test.ts` 3/3: a completeness leg (every `STATUS_KEY` status has a `STATUS_TONE` entry — the durable invariant, so a future label-only addition fails here), a pin leg (the five breach tones), and an anti-vacuity floor (≥ 15 keys, so a rotted import cannot pass vacuously — [[F2-195]]). Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): removing the five tones makes all three legs RED (the completeness leg names the five missing statuses, the pin fails on `undefined`, the floor drops to 14). Full frontend suite green. |

### Fix

Add the five tones to `STATUS_TONE` in `lib/labels.ts`, following the existing convention (`danger` = urgent/bad, `warning` = active, `info` = in-progress, `success` = done): `ESCALATED` → danger, `INVESTIGATING` → warning, `NOTIFIED` / `INVESTIGATED` → info, `REMEDIATED` → success. Export `STATUS_KEY` (previously private) so the completeness gate can assert `STATUS_KEY ⊆ STATUS_TONE` with types rather than parsing the source. One source of truth fixes both the register and the console.

**Filed / not done.** A separate genuine frontend defect surfaced by the same sweep, in `components/workflows/SubmissionAnalyticsCard.tsx` (rendered by `WorkflowSubmissionsPage`): the "Open for review" KPI is computed as `openCount` inside a `useMemo` whose FIRST statement is `if (reviewed.length === 0) return { avgHours: null, count: 0, openCount: 0 }` — but `openCount` (count of `SUBMITTED`/`UNDER_REVIEW`) does not depend on `reviewed`; it was swept into the divide-by-zero guard meant for `avgHours`. So when nothing has been reviewed yet (a fresh tenant, or a `SUBMITTED`-filtered view), the KPI reads **"Open for review: 0"** with the sub-label **"No pending submissions"** — a false statement, in the state where the KPI matters most. The fix is to move the `openCount` computation above the early return; verifiable with a render test. Deferred to keep this slice to one bounded fix.

## F2-356 — a gate: a server-minted reference ordinal seeds from a MAX, never from a live COUNT (the count-minter capstone)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | N/A — a preventive instrument, not a defect fix. The F2-266 capstone for the count-minter population: five registers were fixed one slice at a time (F2-337 `OBI-`, F2-351 `RUN-`, F2-353 `CP-`, F2-354 `OSI-`, F2-355 `DR-`) for the same collision — a `count(...) + 1` ordinal seed re-mints an in-use ordinal past a query window, after a soft-delete gap (the derived `countBy…` respects `@Where(is_deleted = 0)`), or under a concurrent create → a 500 on a filtered unique index, a silent duplicate without one. This gate sweeps the shape so the sixth instance fails the build instead of waiting for a sixth slice. |
| **Registers** | none — a hermetic test-source gate over `src/main/java`. No production code changed, no data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | [[F2-266]] (filings one at a time is what a population looks like when nothing counts it); [[F2-208]] (`ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest` — the sibling source-reading reference-minter ratchet, the precedent); [[F2-195]] (a corpus assertion needs a self-test or it passes when the detector rots); [[F2-205]] (say what the instrument cannot see). |
| **Found by** | [[F2-355]] filed the durable resolution: "a gate correlating a `count…() + 1` reference seed with a filtered unique index on that column." This is that gate, in its pragmatic form — it gates the count-seed-minter SHAPE (a method that both count-seeds and builds a reference), without the migration correlation, because the shape alone is what all five fixes shared and the shape is what a sixth would repeat. |
| **Verification** | hermetic — the gate itself. `CountBasedReferenceMinterRatchetTest` 3/3: an exact-set leg (the detected count-seed minters equal the two enumerated survivors, both directions), a reverse leg (each enumerated survivor is still detected, so the map cannot rot), and a synthetic self-test driving the extracted `scan()` over count-seed / MAX-seed / array-size / count-without-reference input so the corpus assertion is not vacuous ([[F2-195]]). Control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]]): dropping a `KNOWN_COUNT_SEED_MINTERS` entry makes the exact-set leg RED (the detector still finds it, the expected set no longer lists it) while the other two legs stay green. Full backend suite green. |

### The gate

`CountBasedReferenceMinterRatchetTest` (in `com.tss.grc.security`, beside `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest`) walks `*Service.java`, strips comments (one left-to-right alternation, preserving newlines — [[F2-198]]), and flags any method whose brace-balanced body BOTH computes a count-seed (`count…() + 1`, `.size() + 1`, `.count() + 1`) AND builds a reference in the same method (a zero-padded `String.format("…%0Nd…")` or a `set…Reference` / `set…Code` call). The current matches are exactly the two mitigated survivors — `CrisisAarService#nextReportCode` and `MtpdInheritanceService#generateAssessmentCode` — enumerated with a reason each (both carry bounded skip-loops and their authors accepted the residual race for their cadence). The correct idiom to reach for instead is `ComplaintService#generateNextComplaintNo` (MAX seed + skip-loop).

**Two documented blind spots ([[F2-205]]).** (1) A split-method minter — `RrpService#nextOrdinal` computes `.count() + 1L` and returns a long its caller formats, so the count-seed and the reference build are in different methods and no single-method scan matches it; it is one-per-fiscal-year, filed low-risk. (2) A match is not by itself a defect — the two survivors are mitigated, so the gate counts them with reasons rather than banning them; the point is that a NEW count-seed minter (or a mitigated one whose cadence rises) is surfaced at build time.

**Filed / not done.** The stronger form — correlating the count-seed with a filtered unique index on the target column, and reshaping the two mitigated survivors + `RrpService` to MAX seeds — is deferred: it must fix each instance it reshapes ([[F2-188]]), which is its own slice. This gate's value is that the population is now counted and a regression fails the build.

## F2-355 — the document-request reference minter seeded from a live COUNT re-mints an ordinal, producing a DUPLICATE reference (no unique index)

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-25 |
| **Severity** | P3 (latent, concurrency-only, no 500) — `RegInspectService.createDocumentRequest()` minted the document-request reference `<inspRef>-DR-NNN` from `findByInspectionIdAndOrganisationIdOrderByRequestedAtDesc(i.getId(), org()).size() + 1L`. The derived finder respects `@Where(is_deleted = 0)` (LIVE rows only), so a soft-delete gap or a concurrent create re-mints an ordinal already held by a live DR. Unlike F2-354's inspection reference, `reginspect.reginspect_document_request.reference` carries **no unique index**, so the collision is a **silent DUPLICATE** reference — a regulator citing `<inspRef>-DR-003` would then be ambiguous — rather than a 500. The F2-337 / F2-351 / F2-353 / F2-354 count-minter shape, completing the actionable members of the measured population. |
| **Registers** | `reginspect.reginspect_document_request` — read-path minting defect; no data change, no migration. |
| **Standards** | SAMA / NCA on-site-inspection document-request workspace; [[F2-354]] (same service, same idiom, the inspection-reference sibling); [[F2-310]] (format-preserving → no owner decision). |
| **Found by** | Executing [[F2-353]] / [[F2-354]]'s filed count-minter population. F2-354 classified `RegInspectService:189` as the milder member (no unique index → silent duplicate, not a 500). Confirmed: `RegDocumentRequest` soft-deletes (`@Where`), the reference has no unique index, and there is no DR delete route — so the gap-collision is concurrency-only (two DRs added to one inspection at once both read the same live count). |
| **Verification** | hermetic ([[F2-320]] / [[F2-325]]) — a unit test cannot exercise a real concurrency race, so `RegInspectServiceTest` (+3 DR legs) pins the minting logic: the ordinal seeds from `findMaxDrOrdinal` (value 8 from MAX 7, not 1 from the empty live-count list), and the skip-loop steps over a live collision. Pre-fix control ([[F2-274]] / [[F2-287]], fix committed first — [[F2-297]]): reverting to the `.size() + 1` body makes the three DR legs RED (the MAX/exists stubs go unused under strict stubbing; the reverted `.size()` over the empty list yields ordinal 1, not the asserted 8/007) while the four inspection legs stay green. `RegInspectServiceTest` 7/7 + full backend suite green. Latent (concurrency-only, no 500); no dev backend to live-probe. No migration. |

### Fix

Mirror F2-354's MAX-seed idiom in the same service. Two new `RegDocumentRequestRepository` finders: a native `findMaxDrOrdinal(inspectionId, org)` = `SELECT ISNULL(MAX(TRY_CAST(RIGHT(reference, CHARINDEX('-', REVERSE(reference)) - 1) AS INT)), 0) FROM reginspect.reginspect_document_request WHERE inspection_id = :insp AND organisation_id = :org` — the MAX of the last `-NNN` segment across ALL DRs for the inspection including soft-deleted ones, so a used ordinal is never re-issued (every DR reference ends `-NNN`; `TRY_CAST` ignores a non-numeric backstop tail; `ISNULL(…, 0)` seeds the first DR at 1) — and a derived `existsByInspectionIdAndOrganisationIdAndReference` (live-only, `@Where`-scoped) for the skip-loop. `createDocumentRequest` calls a new private `nextDrReference(RegInspection)` that seeds `MAX + 1`, steps over any live collision, backstopped by a random suffix. Format-preserving (`<inspRef>-DR-NNN`), so no owner decision ([[F2-310]]).

**Filed / not done.** The remaining count-minter members are mitigated or milder and are recorded rather than forced ([[F2-188]]): `CrisisAarService.nextReportCode` and `MtpdInheritanceService.generateAssessmentCode` are count-seeded but already carry bounded skip-loops (author-accepted for their cadence); `RrpService.nextOrdinal` is one-per-fiscal-year. With F2-337 (`OBI-`), F2-351 (`RUN-`), F2-353 (`CP-`), F2-354 (`OSI-`) and F2-355 (`DR-`), every genuine unmitigated count-minter is now closed; the durable resolution for the mitigated tail is a gate correlating a `count…() + 1` reference seed with a filtered unique index on that column ([[F2-266]]), deferred as its own slice.
