* **The narrow rule cannot see a shadow that is not schema-prefixed** (`bcm.exercises_old` would
  pass), and it is scoped that way deliberately because the loose form fails on 34 legitimate
  parent/child pairs. Said out loud, because a hard assertion over a population the instrument
  cannot see is the most reassuring possible artefact ([[F2-205]]).

## F2-300 — two tables differing by a prefix, one live and one orphaned, and the orphan sorts first in a name search

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 |
| **Severity** | P3 — **two latent hazards closed, and a measurement error that produced four wrong conclusions.** `completeExercise` owns the pair *(status = COMPLETED, executedDate stamped from the clock)*; the entity-bound create and full-replace PUT wrote both fields independently and unconditionally, so either could produce a COMPLETED exercise with **no execution date** — the evidence an ISO 22301 / NCEMA reviewer reads to accept the exercise took place. And `BcmExercise#status` carried `= "SCHEDULED"`, so a partial PUT **silently reset a COMPLETED exercise**. Both reachable only by a partial-body caller, which `BcmPage`'s form is not — so latent, and saying so is the point ([[F2-283]]). |
| **Registers** | `bcm.exercises` — **13 rows, COMPLETED ×12 / SCHEDULED ×1, three CHECK constraints, 0 COMPLETED without a date**, identical in dev and prod |
| **Standards** | ISO 22301 §8.5 / NCEMA (the exercise programme the execution date evidences) |
| **Found by** | Executing [[F2-299]]'s filing (*"`bia_records` and `bcm_exercises` have no CHECK and both take a caller's status"*) and re-deriving it ([[F2-221]]), which split the two registers apart and refuted half the premise. |
| **Verification** | suite **4664 → 4672/0/0**; probe **12/12** as `compliance`, never `admin`; register restored to 13 rows with 0 tagged rows in either database |

### The headline is my own measurement error, and it was the expensive part

`BcmExercise` maps `@Table(name = "exercises")`. I measured **`bcm.bcm_exercises`** by name and drew
four wrong conclusions: *zero CHECK constraints*, *a column default of `PLANNED`*, *`PLANNED` is a
seed-only synonym of SCHEDULED*, and *2 COMPLETED rows with no execution date*. The real table has
**three** CHECKs — including `CK_bcm_exer_status`, which admits exactly the four tokens the form
offers — a status default of `SCHEDULED` matching the entity, and **zero** COMPLETED rows without a
date. So there was no four-way disagreement, no synonym problem, and no live data defect.

🔑🔑 **`bcm.bcm_exercises` is a V1-era orphan: no `@Entity` maps it**, 14 rows, zero CHECKs, holding
a `PLANNED` status the real register's CHECK would refuse — while `DashboardService` correctly reads
`bcm.exercises`. **Two tables differing by a prefix, one live and one orphaned, and the orphan sorts
FIRST in a name search.** Third instance of the guessed-identifier landmine in this programme after
[[F2-297]]'s `ndi.gaps` and [[F2-283]]'s `bcm.business_process`, and by far the most expensive,
because **the wrong table answered every question plausibly** — a missing table gives an error, a
*different* table gives data.

⚠ It cost real residue too. The probe's cleanup matched the wrong table, so its first run left 3
rows in `bcm.exercises`. The tell was the cleanup reporting **"deleted 0" against a register whose
count had not moved**; re-pointed and re-run it deleted 3 and the register returned to 13.
🔑 **A cleanup reporting zero against an unchanged count is not a clean register — it is a cleanup
looking somewhere else.**

### The guard placement needed correcting mid-slice, and the first version failed on correct usage

With `executedDate` still written unconditionally, a partial edit of a COMPLETED exercise nulled the
date and then tripped the new invariant — **a 400 on renaming a completed exercise**, which is
exactly the trap [[F2-297]] and [[F2-298]] were about. Both fields are null-guarded now, so
*omitted* means *leave alone* — the semantics this codebase's PUTs settled on — and the pair moves
together. Clearing an execution date is therefore not expressible through the PUT, which is the
right answer for the field that evidences the exercise happened. **The test asserting the old 400
was rewritten rather than kept**, because it was asserting the wrong contract.

### The reset half is the sixth instance of one family

`= "SCHEDULED"` on an entity-bound update whose status write was unconditional is [[F2-238]]'s reset
shape, after `CrisisEvent` / `Issue` / `BcmBiaAssessment` (F2-238), `BcpPlan` (F2-297) and `BcmPlan`
(F2-298). It matters more than the row count suggests: **12 of the 13 live rows are COMPLETED**, so
the population a partial PUT could reset is nearly the whole register. `createExercise` owns the
default now — as a **default**, not `requireInitial`, because recording an exercise run offline
(created straight into COMPLETED with its date) is legitimate and the create form offers the full
select, so a refusal would break working usage ([[F2-214]]).

### No migration, and two things deliberately not done

* **No new CHECK**: `CK_bcm_exer_status` already constrains the column and already agrees with the
  form. The invariant this slice adds — *COMPLETED implies an execution date* — is expressible as
  `NOT (status = 'COMPLETED' AND executed_date IS NULL)` and is deliberately enforced in the service
  instead, because a service refusal names the field **and** the `/complete` route ([[F2-180]])
  where a 547 names neither.
* **`bcm.bia_records` was left alone, and that is F2-183's rule rather than reticence.** It
  genuinely has no CHECK and no machine — `createBia` sets no status at all, `updateBia` copies the
  caller's unconditionally, and there is no transition route — so its status is free text. But
  **nothing declares a vocabulary for it anywhere**, and the stored values (APPROVED 6 /
  IN_PROGRESS 2 / UNDER_REVIEW 1 / DRAFT 1) are data rather than a declaration, so a CHECK there
  would invent a lifecycle nobody designed — V375's `consumer.complaint.subcategory` precedent.

### Filed

* **`bcm.bcm_exercises`, the orphan** — 14 rows, no entity, no CHECKs, reachable by nothing. Either
  it is dead schema to drop or a register somebody meant to keep; both are owner decisions, and
  dropping a table in a customer database is not a side effect of a service fix.
  ⚠ **Corrected by [[F2-301]]: this filing was redundant.** `TABLE_DISPOSITION.md` has recorded the
  table since [[F2-141]] and `BASELINE_NO_CODE_TABLES = 36` counts it, so its *disposition* was never
  the open question. What was genuinely unmeasured was the **name hazard** — that the shadow returns
  14 rows where the live register has 13, so a lookup by name succeeds with the wrong data instead of
  failing. 🔑 **A filing is worth checking against the instruments that already exist before it is
  written**, which is [[F2-299]]'s lesson one artefact over.
* **`bcm.bia_records.status` as free text**, above — needs a declared lifecycle before a constraint.
* **`bcm.bia_records` has no transition route at all**, so its status is pure data entry while three
  services read the register ([[F2-282]]) — and F2-282 deliberately left those readers not
  consulting status, which is still the right call and still an owner decision.

## F2-299 — the vocabulary I documented one slice earlier had five tokens and the machine has four, and the citation is what made it credible

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a **constraint closure with a documentation defect inside it**. `bcm.bcm_plans` had **zero CHECK constraints**, so `status` was narrowed only by `BcmService`'s five writers. No live defect: every writer is a literal from the machine or `ServerOwnedState.requireInitial`, so nothing reachable could store an out-of-vocabulary value. The defect is that **the artefact a reader would have written the constraint from was wrong.** |
| **Registers** | `bcm.bcm_plans` — **10 rows in each database (8 live + 2 soft-deleted), DRAFT ×7 / APPROVED ×3, 0 NULLs, 0 non-canonical casings, 0 outside the four-token vocabulary** |
| **Standards** | ISO 22301 (the plan lifecycle the CHECK's four tokens belong to) |
| **Found by** | Executing [[F2-298]]'s own filing — *"zero CHECKs on `status`, cheapest now that the writers were touched"* — and re-deriving the writers first ([[F2-221]]) rather than trusting it. |
| **Verification** | suite **4660 → 4664/0/0**; V395 applied **twice** to dev, idempotent, enabled and **trusted**, register unchanged; probe **12/12** as `compliance`, never `admin`, driving all four tokens through their real routes |

### The headline: my own javadoc named a fifth state, and cited the file that does not have it

`BcmPlan#status`'s javadoc read `DRAFT | UNDER_REVIEW | APPROVED | INVOKED | ARCHIVED (see
BcmService)`. Measured: **`ARCHIVED` appears 0 times in `BcmService`, 0 times in its controller,
0 times in `BcmPage.tsx`.** I wrote that line **one slice earlier** (F2-298) by copying the
vocabulary of the *canonical* register, `BcpPlan`, which really does have ARCHIVED — along with
PUBLISHED, SUPERSEDED and CANCELLED. So [[F2-234]]'s two-registers-for-one-concept hazard bit the
**documentation** before it bit any code.

🔑🔑 **The citation is what made it credible: *"see BcmService"* invites the reader not to look.**
And it would have been load-bearing — **writing V395's CHECK from that line would have admitted a
token no route can produce.** That is worse than [[F2-296]]'s *"a CHECK admitting today's values
blesses the synonyms"*, because a token nothing writes makes the vocabulary look like **five**:
a later reader counting the CHECK would conclude the machine has an archive state, and the one
place that says otherwise is the code they were told they need not read.

### The gate therefore derives the vocabulary instead of holding a list

`BcmPlanStatusVocabularyTest` reads the **writers** — every `setStatus("LITERAL")` on a local of
type `BcmPlan`, plus `INITIAL_PLAN_STATUS` by reflection — and asserts that set equals the tokens
parsed out of V395 by `MigrationVocabularies`, **in both directions**:

* a token the CHECK admits that no writer produces is a **blessed unreachable state** — the
  ARCHIVED defect, and precisely what a hand-written list would not have caught, because the
  hand-written list *was* the defect;
* a token a writer produces that the CHECK refuses turns a legal transition into a **547** at run
  time, which surfaces as a 409 naming no field ([[F2-230]]).

⚠ **The scan is scoped by the RECEIVER's declared type, and that is not tidiness.** `BcmService`
also writes `e.setStatus("COMPLETED")` on a `BcmExercise` and copies a caller's status onto a
`BiaRecord`. A bare `setStatus\("([A-Z_]+)"\)` sweep of that file would have put **COMPLETED** in
the plan's vocabulary and then demanded the CHECK admit it — a gate failing on correct code, the
one thing a gate must never do ([[F2-214]]). Pinned against the live file, because that literal is
really there and its presence is the whole reason the scoping exists.

### F2-183's sequence, done in order for once

That rule — *a constraint and its writers land in the same commit* — is why this could not have
been done two slices ago and can be done now. [[F2-296]] gave the register an echo-tolerant,
change-refusing guard on the entity-bound PUT; [[F2-298]] removed the `= "DRAFT"` initialiser that
made that guard fire on every non-DRAFT plan. With those closed, **all five writers are literals
or `requireInitial`**, and nothing outside `BcmService` writes the column (checked, not assumed).
🔑 **F2-296's own finding was a filing that claimed this state of affairs before it was true; the
difference here is that the claim was re-derived rather than quoted.**

### Measured over ALL rows, because `ADD CONSTRAINT` verifies soft-deleted ones too

**10 rows in each database, of which 2 are soft-deleted** — a live-only count would have reported
8 and missed them. They happen to be DRAFT so nothing was at risk, but the method matters: a
constraint does not respect `@Where(is_deleted = 0)`, and one out-of-vocabulary archived row would
have failed Flyway and blocked every later migration on the deployed server ([[F2-183]]).

### The migration's self-checks, and the one that is deliberately skippable

V395 THROWs on: a pre-flight offender scan that **names the rows** (a bare *"constraint violated"*
sends the reader nowhere and this file blocks every later migration until resolved); the
constraint being missing, disabled, **or not trusted** (`is_not_trusted = 1` is what a
`WITH NOCHECK` add leaves behind and looks identical to a verified constraint in any listing that
only checks the name); all four tokens being accepted; and **`ARCHIVED` being refused** — a
negative control, so a later hand-edit cannot widen the CHECK to match the prose this finding is
about ([[F2-197]]).

⚠ The last two probe an existing row inside a rolled-back transaction, so **on an empty table they
verify nothing** — [[F2-183]]'s no-op-branch hazard. They are deliberately **not** made to fail
there: a fresh install runs this before any plan exists, and requiring rows would be a migration
asserting **tenant data** rather than its own writes, which is the check [[F2-260]] had to delete
from V383 because it would have blocked the whole chain. What covers the empty case is the
hermetic gate, which needs no rows at all.

### Filed

* **`bcm.bcp_plans`** — the canonical sibling — still has `ck_bcp_status`, so it is already
  constrained; but its vocabulary is **seven** tokens against this register's four, for what the
  platform presents as one concept. Reconciling them is [[F2-234]]'s filed owner decision and this
  slice deliberately did not touch it: the point of the ARCHIVED finding is that the two
  vocabularies are genuinely different, not that one is wrong.
* **`bcm.bia_records` and `bcm.bcm_exercises` have no CHECK either**, and both take a caller's
  status through `BcmService` (lines 313 and 375) — so unlike the plan register their writers are
  **open**, and F2-183's rule says the constraint cannot go first. Reading those two writers is
  the next unit of work here.

## F2-298 — the fifth instance of one initialiser, and the gate population boundary that let four of them recur

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 |
| **Severity** | P3 — a **latent-hazard closure, not a defect discovery**, and saying which is the point ([[F2-283]]). `BcmPlan#status` carried `= "DRAFT"` and `PUT /api/v1/bcm/legacy-plans/{id}` binds the entity, so a body that omitted `status` deserialised to "DRAFT", was read as a request to move the plan back, and answered **400 *"A BCM plan's status is not editable here (APPROVED → DRAFT)"*** — naming a transition the caller never asked for. **API-reachable only**: the screen echoes the stored status (see below). Same `BCM:WRITE` on the create, the PUT and every lifecycle route, so no privilege escalation ([[F2-219]]'s shape). |
| **Registers** | `bcm.bcm_plans` — **8 live rows, DRAFT ×5 / APPROVED ×3, zero CHECKs on `status`, 0 non-canonical case**, identical in dev and prod. So **3 of 8 could not take a partial body.** |
| **Standards** | ISO 22301 (the BCM plan lifecycle the refusal defers to) |
| **Found by** | Executing [[F2-297]]'s own filing — *"looks like a live twin; **measure it, do not assume**"* — and re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]). The measurement refuted half of it and confirmed the other half. |
| **Verification** | suite **4654 → 4660/0/0**; gates green; probe **12/12 post-fix** as `compliance`, never `admin`, against a plan it planted itself ([[F2-206]]); **pre-fix control 10/12** with exactly the two partial-body legs failing and the other ten passing identically |

### The filing said "measure it", and the measurement went both ways

**REFUTED — it is not screen-reachable.** `BcmPage`'s plan form seeds its edit modal through
`planToReq`, which copies `status: p.status`, and `FormModal` submits its whole seeded state — so
the screen **echoes** the stored status, and F2-296 made this route tolerate an echo. That is the
same reason F2-292's disclosure register survived: the form round-trips the field.
🔑 **Recording the refutation is the result** ([[F2-283]]) — it stops the next reader re-deriving
it, and it is why this is a latent-hazard closure rather than the live twin the filing suspected.

**CONFIRMED — the hazard is real, API-reachable, and the FIFTH instance of one residue.**
[[F2-238]] removed this initialiser from `CrisisEvent`, `Issue` and `BcmBiaAssessment`;
[[F2-297]] found the fourth on `BcpPlan`; this is the fifth. `createPlan` already owned the
default through `ServerOwnedState.requireInitial`, so the initialiser was pure residue on create
and a refusal on update — exactly as on `BcpPlan`, one register over.

### Why four of them recurred: a population boundary at the shape of the *condition*

`NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` exists for precisely this defect and [[F2-294]] promoted it to
an invariant — and it was a **hard zero over `BcpPlan` and `BcmPlan` both**, because `measure()`'s
pattern needs a `)` immediately after `null`, so the null test must be the **whole** condition,
and both guards are **conjunctive**. F2-297 filed the widening rather than doing it, because the
raw conjunctive shape matched **4 sites that had to be read first**. Read, they are **1 real and
3 refuted**, and the discriminator is mechanical — *what the other conjunct compares against*:

| site | verdict | why |
|---|---|---|
| `BcmService#updatePlan` | **REAL** | compares against the **loaded row**, so an initialiser makes the REFUSAL fire on every non-initial row |
| `ConsentRecordService#grant` ×2 | refuted | a **create** (loads no row); its conjuncts are vocabulary **validations**, and an initialiser makes them always *run* — stronger, not weaker |
| `DetectionRuleService#save` | refuted | compares against a **constant vocabulary** and normalises to upper case first — the idiom CLAUDE.md names as the pattern to copy — with no guarded lifecycle route on the register to bypass |

So the new leg is scoped to the **row-comparing** form: it finds the real site and **not** the two
refuted ones, because a gate that fails on correct code trains the next reader to edit the
assertion ([[F2-214]]). Hard zero, **no exemption map** — removing the initialiser and letting the
create own the default is always available, so there is no correct code for it to fail on.

### ⚠⚠ My synthetic self-test passed while that leg was vacuous on the live tree

`loadedLocalOf` demanded a **receiver** (`repo.getX(...)`). `BcmService#updatePlan` loads its row
with a bare `getPlan(id)`, so the site was skipped, **the new hard zero passed with the defect
still in the tree** — and the synthetic fixture passed too, because I had written it to match my
regex rather than the real code. Only restoring the initialiser and re-running against the real
tree found it, and it then named exactly `BcmService#updatePlan :: BcmPlan#status`.
🔑 **A positive control written against the shape you imagine certifies nothing** ([[F2-208]]).
The bare-call form and the two-line guard wrap are must-match cases now, with the
receiver-bearing form as a second one.

### Two things the probe corrected about my model of the defect

* A body carrying only `planNameEn` answers **400 *"A required field was not supplied"*** —
  `plan_type` and `version` are **NOT NULL** and this full-replace PUT writes them
  unconditionally, so the status guard is never reached. "Partial" here therefore has to mean
  *every editable field except the lifecycle one*, which is what a client editing the record's
  data actually sends. 🔑 **The probe found the shape of the request the defect needs; reading
  alone had given me a body the column refuses first.**
* `updatePlan` had **no test of any kind** before this, which is not the same as a path somebody
  decided was safe ([[F2-248]]).

### Registered in the declared-removal map — including F2-297's own omission

`everyRemovedInitialiserHasAWriterOnTheCreatePath` now holds **both** `BcpPlan` (F2-297, which
removed an initialiser and did **not** register it — exactly what that map exists to catch) and
`BcmPlan`. A removed initialiser whose create path does not own the default turns a silent
refusal into a **500 on a NOT NULL column**, and nothing else in the tree would notice under
`ddl-auto=none`.

### Filed

* **`bcm.bcm_plans` has zero CHECK constraints on `status`** — cheaper now that this slice
  touched the writers, but the vocabulary (`DRAFT | UNDER_REVIEW | APPROVED | INVOKED |
  ARCHIVED`) lives only in `BcmService`, and [[F2-183]]'s rule is that the constraint and its
  writers land in one commit.
* **The full-replace PUT itself.** `updatePlan` writes five fields unconditionally, so a client
  must send all of them or lose the ones it omits — [[F2-213]]'s structural root, and
  `FullReplaceUpdateContractTest` already carries this route in `DERIVED_IGNORED_FIELDS`. A
  purpose-built request record per endpoint would make the whole family unrepresentable.
* **Two plan registers for one concept** (`bcm.bcm_plans` legacy, `bcm.bcp_plans` canonical),
  unchanged from [[F2-234]]'s filing and now with a fifth shared defect between them.

## F2-297 — a census that names its members and gives them no verdicts is a list nobody reads, and four of these seven were copies of the rule the slice that filed them had just shared

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 |
| **Severity** | P2 — live and **screen-reachable**. The BCP Builder's "Edit plan" form sends `titleEn`/`titleAr`/`rtoHours`/`rpoHours`/`mtpdHours`/`responseTeamRole`/`nextReviewDate` and **no status**; `PATCH /api/v1/bcm/plans/{id}` binds the entity, whose `status` field carried `= "DRAFT"`, so an omitted status arrived as "DRAFT" and the guard read it as a request to move the plan back. Clicking **Save** on any plan that was neither DRAFT nor already locked answered **400 "Use transition() to change status"** — naming a state the form does not offer. Same `BCM:WRITE` on create, PATCH and `/transition`, so no privilege escalation: the object-level guard was the only control ([[F2-219]]'s shape). |
| **Registers** | `bcm.bcp_plans` (10 rows, 1 `UNDER_REVIEW` — the affected state — in **both** databases), `bcm.crisis_events` (7), `platform.issues` (13), `bcm.bia_assessments` (8), `sust.cma_disclosure` (91), `sust.tcfd_item` (85), `ndi.gap` (18) |
| **Standards** | ISO 22301 §8.4.2 (BCP), NCEMA (crisis events), CMA Article 92 / IFRS S2 (the two disclosure registers) |
| **Found by** | Executing [[F2-296]]'s own filed 7-site census and **re-deriving it first** ([[F2-221]]) — the gate asserts a COUNT and prints nothing, so the sites came from a scan mirroring its detector, which agreed with it at 7. Reading each site with its enclosing method is what split them. |
| **Verification** | full hermetic suite **4648 → 4654/0/0**; gate 10/10; live probe **15/15 post-fix** as `compliance`, never `admin`, against a plan it planted itself ([[F2-206]]); **pre-fix control 8/15**, reproducing the 400 on the BCP Builder's exact payload; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean |

### The census had three buckets and a count could rank none of them

`ServerOwnedStateContractTest.censusOfHandRolledLifecycleComparisons` shipped with F2-296 as a
decrease-only work list of **7 services, deliberately with no verdicts** ([[F2-188]]) — and its own
assertion message names the reading job: *"a comparison against the CURRENT row is this slice's
defect, and a comparison against a target inside a transition is the machine doing its job."* A
list of service names cannot settle that. The matched expression plus its enclosing method can, and
it split **three** ways:

**Bucket A — four hand-rolled copies of the rule F2-296 had just shared.** `BcpPlanService`,
`CrisisEventService`, `IssueService` and `BcmBiaAssessmentService` each carried, byte for byte:

```java
if (patch.getStatus() != null && !patch.getStatus().equals(existing.getStatus()))
    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Use transition() to change status");
```

The **rule** was right — tolerate an echo, refuse a change — and three things about the copy were
not. The bare `equals` cannot see that these columns collate case-insensitively, so a case-variant
echo read as a change and was refused ([[F2-179]]; **latent — 0 non-canonical values on all seven
columns in both databases**, so what made it harmless was the data and not the code, [[F2-182]]).
The message named a **Java method a caller cannot call** rather than the route ([[F2-210]]'s shape,
and `BcmBiaAssessmentService`'s said `"status"` while its request carries `approvalStatus`, which is
the very defect F2-296 found *inside the primitive*). And on `BcpPlanService` it sat over an
initialised entity field, which is what made it live.

🔑🔑 **F2-238 removed exactly that initialiser from the three PATCH-bound siblings and left the
fourth.** Its own finding reads *"5 of 5 crisis events, 4 of 7 BIA assessments, 6 of 13 issues could
not be PATCHed at all"* — and `BcpPlanController#update` is a `@PatchMapping` too, so this was
squarely inside its declared population, not a boundary gap. [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N, at the widest
range yet: **the remedy was applied three times, in the same module, and the fourth site kept the
defect while every artefact around it looked finished.**

**Bucket B — two deliberate [[F2-231]] change-detection branches that are CORRECT and must never be
converted**, and the same bare `equals` inside them fails in the **opposite** direction.
`CmaDisclosureService#update` and `TcfdItemService#update` legitimately accept `disclosureStatus`
(F2-231 established why: the entity's field initialiser makes an omitted key indistinguishable from
a real `UNDER_REVIEW`, so the ESG tab echoes it back) and route a *change* through `markReviewed` so
the review clock and the audit row move together. But a case-variant echo read as a **change**, so
`markReviewed` would stamp a CMA Article 92 / IFRS S2 review that never happened and the audit row
would record a `TRANSITION` that never occurred. 🔑 **Bucket A's failure is a false 400 — annoying
and safe. Bucket B's manufactures a governance record.** One line each: `sameState`, which is public
for exactly this — the comparison is shared, the refusal is not.

**Bucket C — one unconditional write, and BOTH of my first two readings of it were wrong.**
`NdiGapService#updateGap` writes `if (body.getStatus() != null) g.setStatus(body.getStatus())`
unconditionally and then publishes a `TRANSITION` audit row when the value differs.

* I first called it *"a PUT that is a reverse edge past whatever the transition route enforces"*.
  **Refuted:** that service has no `transition()` and no state machine at all — `setStatus` is
  written on the update path and by three derivations, and its controller maps only
  `/api/ndi/gaps`. There is no machine to bypass, so it is [[F2-221]]'s shape and not F2-296's.
* I then measured `ndi.gaps` and got **TABLE ABSENT in both databases**, which reads exactly like
  *the register does not exist*. **That was my own guessed table name** — `@Table(name = "gap")`,
  singular. The recurring guessed-identifier landmine, one step from a filed false finding.
  Resolved properly: **18 rows in both databases, a CHECK on `status` present, 0 non-canonical
  case, storing only `OPEN` ×9 and `IN_PROGRESS` ×9.**

So the arbitrary-string harm is **absent** there (the CHECK narrows it) and what remains is the
question a CHECK cannot answer — whether that vocabulary permits a **jump** past the three
derivations. Filed, unread, and the census ceiling is **7 → 1** so it cannot be lost.

### The test that could have caught it built the exact triggering payload and passed

`BcpPlanServiceTest.update_cannotEditApprovedPlan` constructs `new BcpPlan()` with only a title —
**precisely the partial patch that tripped this defect** — and passed, because `isLocked()` fires
first on an APPROVED plan. The case that was broken is a plan that is neither locked nor in the
initial state, and no fixture reached it. [[F2-293]]'s shape: **an earlier check masking the one
under test, in a fixture that otherwise looks like exactly the right coverage.**

### The harness predicted a gap before it ran, because F2-231 had already recorded it

My own comment on the CMA fix said F2-231 *"already recorded that closing one instance of a shape in
this pair is not closing the shape"* — and F2-231's register entry records that reverting its CMA
half **SURVIVED** because only the TCFD half had behaviour tests. I had added the case-variant test
to TCFD only, so that mutation would have survived for the identical reason, two slices apart. The
CMA test was written **before** the harness ran, and M6 is what proves it load-bearing.
🔑 **A recorded failure mode is a prediction, and the cheapest time to act on it is before the
harness tells you again.**

### The stale claim was in the frontend, where no code-scoped gate can see it

`CrisisRoomPage.tsx` carried a comment stating that the PATCH body **must** echo the current status
*"because the endpoint binds a JPA entity whose status field defaults to `DETECTED`"*. F2-238 removed
that initialiser, so the claim had been false ever since — and it is the kind of false claim that
propagates, because it tells the next reader to keep a workaround forever ([[F2-184]]'s shape, in
the place written to be read — [[F2-205]]). Corrected in place rather than deleted: the echo is
harmless and the form round-trips the record, so what needed fixing was the *reason*. It was also
the artefact that revealed the whole finding — the comment named the defect precisely, in a file
nobody had reason to connect to a BCM service.

### Why no gate caught it: the hard zero's population stops at the shape of the *condition*

`NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` exists for precisely this defect — `if (req.getX() != null)` on
a field the entity initialises — and F2-294 promoted it to an **invariant** with the words *"Keep it
empty. There is no correct code for a hard zero here to fail on."* It passed 15/15 both before and
after this slice. Its guard pattern is:

```
if\s*\(\s*<param>\s*\.\s*(?:get|is)([A-Z]\w*)\s*\(\s*\)\s*!=\s*null\s*\)
```

which requires a `)` **immediately after `null`** — i.e. the null test must be the *entire*
condition. All four bucket-A guards are **conjunctive** (`!= null && !…equals(…)`), so there is
` && ` there instead and they are outside that gate's population **by construction**.
🔑 **That is why F2-238's member list did not name `BcpPlan`: not an oversight, a population
boundary at the shape of the condition** — [[F2-198]]'s shape, where the narrowing is neither a
filename nor an allow-list nor a verb but **how much of the `if` the null test occupies**.

⚠ **Widening it is NOT a free closure, which is why it is filed rather than done here.** Measured:
the conjunctive shape over an initialised field of the parameter's own type matches **4 sites** —
`BcmService#updatePlan` (`BcmPlan#status = "DRAFT"`), `ConsentRecordService#grant` (two fields) and
`DetectionRuleService#save`. Two of those are plausibly legitimate create-or-update paths ([[F2-213]]
already refuted `DetectionRuleService#save` for a different family), so widening surfaces a
population that must be **read**, and manufacturing four reasons is [[F2-188]]'s failure mode.

⚠⚠ **And my measuring scanner reproduced a bug that gate's own comment records fixing.** It reported
**1 SIMPLE-shape site** — `CloudServiceService#update` over `CloudService#status = "ONBOARDING"` —
against a gate that is a hard zero for that shape. The gate is right and my scan was wrong: I keyed
initialised fields by **simple class name**, so the two `CloudService` entities (`module/cyber` and
`module/outsourcing`) collapsed and the outsourcing one's initialiser was attributed to the cyber
service. F2-238's own javadoc describes fixing exactly that, by fully-qualified name. 🔑 **CLAUDE.md's
rule verbatim — before writing a scanner, read the scanner this repo already has — and the phantom
is the reason the conjunctive figure of 4 is stated as "must be read" rather than as four defects.**

### Errors of mine, each caught by running something

* **My kill predicate was an `-or` whose first branch had no narrowing**, so a pattern meant to match
  the dev JVM by its `-Djava.io.tmpdir` argument matched **every shell whose command line mentioned
  that path** — including the harness's own wrappers — and, unlike the reporting version of this
  mistake ([[F2-193]], [[F2-295]]), it **acted** on the over-match. The prod-port guard held (8676
  was skipped and is alive), the repo and both databases were untouched, and the intended outcome
  was reached by a sloppier route than intended. 🔑 **In a compound kill predicate every branch needs
  the narrowing, not just the one you wrote last.**
* **I nearly filed "TABLE ABSENT" as a finding** — see bucket C. Resolve a table from `@Table`, never
  from a plausible plural.
* **The `-Dtest=A+B` selector**, again: surefire wants a comma, and `A+B` produces `BUILD FAILURE`
  with **no `Tests run:` line**, which is [[F2-255]]'s tell that nothing ran.

### Filed

* **`NdiGapService#updateGap`** — the last census member, unread: does `ndi.gap.status`'s CHECK
  vocabulary permit a jump past the service's three derivations, and should that register have a
  transition route at all?
* ⚠⚠ **`bcm.bcm_plans` looks like a live twin of what this slice just fixed, and it needs its own
  measurement.** `BcmPlan#status` is **still** `= "DRAFT"` (one entity class, so no simple-name
  collapse — this hit is real), `PUT /api/v1/bcm/legacy-plans/{id}` binds the entity, and
  [[F2-296]] made that route tolerate an ECHO and refuse a CHANGE — so a body omitting `status`
  arrives as "DRAFT" and is refused on any plan not already in DRAFT, exactly as here. What is NOT
  yet known is whether it is **screen-reachable**: `bcmApi.updatePlan` is called from `BcmPage`
  with form `values`, and [[F2-293]]'s rule is that this question is **per call site**, so the
  payload builder has to be read. It is also a `PUT` rather than a `PATCH`, where full-replace
  semantics make "omitted means default" a defensible reading — the distinction [[F2-238]] used as
  its slice boundary. **Do not assume it is the same defect; measure it.**
* **Widening `NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` to the conjunctive shape** — 4 sites to read, above.
* **`bcm.bia_assessments.approval_status` has zero CHECK constraints in both databases** — now
  cheaper, since this slice closed one of its writers, but the create path needs reading first
  ([[F2-183]]: the constraint and its writers land in one commit).
* **dev and prod disagree on two CHECKs** — `bcm.crisis_events.status` and `platform.issues.status`
  are constrained in dev and not in prod, because those constraints sit inside the pending
  **V345–V394** range. Recorded so nobody files it as a defect ([[F2-255]]'s reading).
* **The four machines declare themselves as inline `switch` + `Set.of(...).contains(...)`**
  ([[F2-284]]'s shape), so the legal-target list is not derivable at runtime and all four refusals
  pass `null` for the `allowed` sentence. Converting those to a declared `Map<String, Set<String>>`
  would let every refusal name the moves the machine would actually accept — a real improvement, and
  one that must not be smuggled into a slice about something else.

## F2-296 — one question, four mechanisms, and the artefact that documents two of them describes them identically without noticing they are the same rule

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 |
| **Severity** | P2 — live. A CLOSED external-audit engagement could be walked back to PLANNED through the entity-bound `PUT`, past an `advance()` that is explicitly forward-only; and any string ≤40 chars could be stored on a NOT NULL column with **zero** CHECK constraints. Same `COMPLIANCE:WRITE` on the create, the PUT and `/advance`, so no privilege escalation: the object-level machine was the only control and this route sat beside it without one ([[F2-219]]'s shape). |
| **Registers** | `compliance.audit_engagements` (12 live rows, dev = prod) · `ethics.cases` · `ethics.disclosures` · `bcm.bcm_plans` |
| **Standards** | IIA Standards 2200/2300 (engagement planning and performance) — the register records where an external audit has got to |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-294]]'s filed *"`compliance.audit_engagements` still has zero CHECKs on `status` — cheap now that this slice closed its only open writers"* and re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]) |
| **Verification** | full hermetic suite **4635 → 4648/0/0**; new gate 10/10; live probe as `compliance`, never `admin`, against a planted row |

### The filed premise was wrong, and it was wrong in the direction that mattered

F2-294 recommended this CHECK **on the strength of having closed the register's writers**. Re-derived,
`apply()` still read:

```java
if (src.getStatus() != null) target.setStatus(src.getStatus());
```

with **no vocabulary check and no direction check**. F2-294 removed the entity's `= "PLANNED"`
initialiser, which genuinely fixed the *omitted*-status half — a partial body now means *leave it
alone* — and left this line, so a body that **stated** a status still performed an arbitrary
transition.

🔑🔑 **That is precisely the sequence [[F2-183]] warns about**: adding a CHECK to a column whose
writer is still open converts silently-stored junk into a constraint violation. Executing the filing
as written would have shipped the constraint over an open writer, on the authority of a sentence the
same slice wrote about itself.

⚠ **And a CHECK could not have closed it anyway.** `CLOSED → PLANNED` is made of two legal members,
so V394 refuses nothing about it. The reverse edge is closed by the Java guard, in the same commit —
[[F2-183]]'s rule one noun over: there the CHECK could not see **case**, here it cannot see
**direction**, and a migration that adds it and stops leaves the defect intact *while appearing to
guard it*.

### One question, four mechanisms

*May the caller name the lifecycle state?* The CREATE half has had a shared answer since [[F2-218]]
(`ServerOwnedState.requireInitial`, 28 call sites). The UPDATE half had none:

| register | update-side rule | comparison |
|---|---|---|
| `ethics.disclosures` | hand-rolled ([[F2-292]]) | through a `normalise` helper — **case-insensitive** |
| `ethics.cases` | hand-rolled ([[F2-291]]) | bare `equals` on `status` **and** `outcome` |
| `bcm.bcm_plans` | hand-rolled ([[F2-234]]) | bare `equals` |
| `compliance.audit_engagements` | **none at all** | — |

🔑 **`DisclosureService` carries a paragraph explaining why a bare equals is not a comparison** — the
column collates `Latin1_General_100_CI_AS_SC_UTF8`, the table has no CHECK, so `'approved'` is
storable and a bare equals would refuse an echo differing only in case ([[F2-179]]). The reasoning was
reached, written down, applied to its own copy, and **not carried next door in the same package.**
[[F2-215]]'s two-of-N, where what stops the next reader asking is that the reasoning is *visibly
present in the module*.

🔑🔑 **The fourth site was found by my own new census, and it was already documented.**
`FullReplaceUpdateContractTest.DERIVED_IGNORED_FIELDS` carried
`/api/v1/bcm/legacy-plans/{} :: status` with a reason in these very terms — *"F2-234 made this route
accept an ECHO of the stored status and refuse a CHANGE … so a PUT-driven DRAFT → APPROVED skipped
the machine entirely"* — and this slice's fix made the audit-engagement entry appear beside it,
**described identically, with neither naming the other.** The artefact that documents the rule twice
is where you can see it is one rule.

⚠ **The case-sensitivity half is LATENT and was closed anyway.** Measured 2026-08-23 over both
databases: **0 non-canonical values** on all four guarded columns (`ethics.cases.status` 30 rows,
`.outcome` 1 of 30 non-null, `ethics.disclosures.status` 18, `compliance.audit_engagements.status`
12). What made three of the four harmless was the **data, not the code** ([[F2-182]]).

### The create-side fourth copy, and the reason it existed

`BcmCycleService.requireInitialState` was a fourth mechanism for the *create* half, and its own
javadoc documents its `field` parameter as *"the field name, so the message names what the caller
actually sent"* — while the shared primitive hard-coded `"status: "`.

⚠⚠ **So three of that primitive's own callers were emitting a 400 naming a field the request never
carried**: `BcmComplianceMappingService` writes `complianceStatus`, `ContinuityStrategyService`
`approvalStatus`, `ControlLibraryService` `workflowStatus`. A caller who sent
`approvalStatus=APPROVED` to `POST /api/v1/bcm/strategies` read a message whose first token was
`status`. [[F2-210]]'s shape — a diagnostic that sends the reader somewhere wrong — **in the message of
the primitive built to send them somewhere right.**

🔑 **A primitive that cannot express what a caller needs is a primitive callers route around**
([[F2-190]]), and the divergence that follows is invisible: two mechanisms, one question, nobody
maintaining the agreement ([[F2-177]]). The primitive takes a field name now, the fourth copy is
retired, and `requireCreatable` was normalised too — leaving one of three siblings case-sensitive
would have shipped F2-215's two-of-N *inside the class whose whole subject is one-question-one-answer*.

### The test that could have caught it asserted the rule and exercised the case where it held

`AuditEngagementPartialUpdateTest.aPartialBodyCannotUndoTheForwardOnlyMachineFromEitherEnd` opens
with the comment *"the PUT must not be able to do what `advance` is written to forbid"*, asserts that
`advance` refuses a backwards move — and then sends a body with **no status at all**. Its sibling
`anEchoOfTheStoredStatusIsStillAccepted` covered the echo. **The case in between — an explicit,
different status on the PUT — was never exercised.**

🔑 [[F2-293]]'s shape: *the one test that could have caught the reset picked the fields where the
principle held.* Here it is inside a **single method whose comment states the whole rule**, which is
the strongest form of it — the reader has been told the rule is tested.

### Four of my own errors, each caught by running something

⚠⚠ **(a) My ban leg fired on the platform's own recommended idiom: 5 of 5 false positives.** Its
first draft banned any `private normalise*()` containing `toUpperCase` in a service, and caught
`ExerciseObserverService` — which CLAUDE.md names as **"the pattern to copy"** for F2-179 —
`BcpBinderService.normaliseLanguage`, `ExerciseRuntimeService`, `CyberAssessmentService` and
`VulnerabilitySlaComputeService`. 🔑 **Those helpers canonicalise an INPUT; the defect is comparing a
REQUEST value against a STORED one.** A leg keyed on the helper measured the house idiom rather than
the defect. Rescoped to the shape of the claim, with the recommended idiom as an explicit
must-not-match control ([[F2-214]], [[F2-206]]).

⚠⚠ **(b) I grepped ONE fragment of a message and concluded it was free to change.** Searching for
`"was rejected because reaching"` returned nothing, so I converted `BcmCycleService` — and three
tests failed on `"status=UNDER_REVIEW"`, `"approvalStatus=ACTIVE"` and `"created at DRAFT"`. 🔑 **A
message has several fragments and asserting any one of them makes the whole wording load-bearing.**
Fixed by re-pointing those assertions at the *information* the refusal must carry rather than its
phrasing — the wording is the one part of a diagnostic that should stay free to improve.

⚠ **(c) The census ceiling was a prediction.** I wrote 6; the detector returned **8**; converting the
fourth site took it to **7**. [[F2-195]]: a baseline lifted from a guess is worse than none, because it
looks measured. Lowered in the same commit as the sweep (house rule 3).

⚠ **(d) Both new files landed LF in a CRLF tree** — sixth instance in this lineage. Every one of the
17 touched files is now verified CRLF with zero bare LF, because the bytes a green build verified must
be the bytes that ship.

### What the gate asserts

`ServerOwnedStateContractTest` (10 legs, hermetic):

- the services guarding a lifecycle update through the shared rule, **exactly** — so a register that
  stops calling it fails, and a new one has to be added, which is the moment a reader is forced to ask
  whether its own update is an unguarded transition route;
- none of them hand-rolls the comparison (hard zero — `sameState` and `requireUnchanged` are both
  available, so there is no correct code for it to fail on);
- a **census with no verdicts** ([[F2-188]]) of services still comparing a request-side lifecycle
  getter against a non-literal, decrease-only at 7 — some will be legitimate branch tests inside a
  transition, which is a reading job a regex cannot adjudicate ([[F2-182]]);
- no service declares its own create-side initial-state guard (the retired fourth copy);
- every `requireInitial` call whose setter is not `setStatus` **names its field**, with an
  anti-vacuity floor on the site scan;
- all three entry points compare case-insensitively and return the **canonical** spelling;
- V394's CHECK admits **exactly** `STATUS_ORDER`, read by reflection against the migration SQL —
  constraining to the 7 states that happen to be stored would refuse `FOLLOW_UP`, which
  `scheduleFollowUp()` writes, i.e. [[F2-180]]'s defect;
- and a self-test driving every detector over the literal pre-fix and post-fix shapes, including the
  comma-inside-a-string-literal case, because counting one as an argument separator would report a
  4-argument call as compliant — the quiet direction.

### Filed

⚠ **`FullReplaceUpdateContractTest`'s vocabulary has no bucket for what this route now does.** Its map
is *"either a form input that silently does nothing, or a deliberate immutable"*, and `status` here is
neither: it is **consulted and never written**. Calling it *ignored* understates the route. Recorded in
the entry rather than papered over.

⚠ The **7-site census**, with no verdicts — read each before closing; a comparison against the CURRENT
row is this slice's defect and one against a target inside a transition is the machine doing its job.

⚠ `ethics.cases` and `ethics.disclosures` still have **zero CHECK constraints** ([[F2-290]], [[F2-292]]
filed both); `bcm.bcm_plans` likewise ([[F2-234]]). All three are now cheaper, since this slice closed
or shared their status writers — but `ethics.cases` is blocked on [[F2-289]]/[[F2-290]]'s finding that
**11 of 30 rows already hold a status the register's own machine does not declare**, so a CHECK
admitting today's values would bless the synonyms.

⚠ `AuditEngagementRequest` still declares no `findingsCount` while `apply()` copies it, so the field
is settable through the entity-bound route and by nothing else ([[F2-278]] filed it as FROZEN from the
other direction, and the sibling register derives the same figure from its linked finding ids —
[[F2-197]]: a computed count is not a measured one).

## F2-295 — the gate dropped three whole services rather than mis-attributing one, and the filing that recorded the hazard described the variant nobody was running

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`36384bd1`) |
| **Severity** | P3 — a **latent-hazard closure, not a defect discovery** ([[F2-283]]). Three of the platform's 327 service sources were never scanned by a hard-zero security invariant; none holds a member of that invariant's defect family today, so nothing was live. The zero it was reporting is now the gate's own over the whole tree rather than over 324 files of it. |
| **Instrument** | `NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` — the gate F2-237 opened, F2-238/239/240 emptied, F2-240 promoted to an invariant, and F2-291 found green over 42 sites |
| **Standards** | none directly — this is instrument integrity for the family that has produced [[F2-291]]'s KYC sanctions bypass, [[F2-292]]'s NAZAHA disclosure reset, [[F2-293]]'s regulator-report reset and [[F2-294]]'s 27-site sweep |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-292]]'s filed *"module-aware pairing for both source maps"* and re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]) |
| **Verification** | full hermetic suite **4633 → 4635/0/0**; gate **15/15**; mutations **9 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss / 0 did-not-compile**, plus one withdrawn as INVALID. No production code changed and no probe was run — there is nothing to probe. |

### The filing was half already true, and its stated hazard was the wrong one

[[F2-292]] filed *"the real fix is module-aware pairing on BOTH maps — key by fully-qualified name
and pair a service with the entity in its own module."* Re-derived:

- **The entity side has paired by module since [[F2-238]].** `measure()` derives `pkgOf` per entry
  and `initialisersFor` picks the same-named entity whose package shares the longest prefix. That
  half needed nothing.
- **The service side keys on the file's SIMPLE name over a `.sorted()` walk.** So where two files
  share a simple name the last path wins the `put` and **the other file is never scanned at all.**

Four files today, three of them real services:

| shadowed | kept |
|---|---|
| `module/audit_eng/service/AuditEngagementService.java` | `module/compliance/service/…` |
| `module/board_pack/service/BoardPackService.java` | `module/reporting/service/…` |
| `module/compliance/service/RegulatoryChangeService.java` | `module/regchange/service/…` |
| `module/cyber/entity/CloudService.java` | `module/outsourcing/entity/…` |

⚙ The fourth is an **entity**, which the `Service.java` suffix catches anyway — its presence in a
map called *services* is its own small finding, and it is named in the assertion so nobody has to
rediscover it.

🔑🔑 **F2-292 measured the MERGE variant and its conclusion is right about merging and silent about
the status quo.** That slice concatenated the colliding sources, watched one phantom finding appear
naming the wrong table, reverted it and wrote *"the hazard is cross-attribution, not omission."*
True of merging. **Under `put`, the loser's whole file is outside the population**, which is
omission — and omission is the quiet direction, because a smaller population reads exactly like a
cleaner tree.

🔑 **Keying by fully-qualified name has neither failure mode.** Nothing is dropped, and a merged
value would have defeated the entity pairing that already worked, because `pkgOf` of two
concatenated files returns whichever `package` line comes first.

### Why the assertion is about the denominator and not the site set

The gate's own measurement over the now-complete population is **still empty**. That is a result
([[F2-216]]) and it is only trustworthy *because* it now comes from the whole tree — [[F2-205]]'s
rule that **a hard zero over a population the instrument cannot see is the most reassuring possible
artefact.**

So `theServiceMapScansEveryServiceSource` asserts:

- the FQN map's size **equals** the `*Service.java` file count — nothing dropped, a hard zero;
- the simple-name map is **exactly four short** — the drop is real, so a reader cannot mistake the
  leg for decoration, and reverting `measure()`'s argument is what this catches;
- the four shadowed paths **by name**, so a NEW collision fails the leg and forces the next reader
  to ask whether the newly shadowed file holds a guard — the question nobody was in a position to
  ask while three files were silently outside the population.

⚠ **The reported LABEL stays the simple name**, module-qualified only when that simple name is
declared twice. Qualifying unconditionally would rename all 38 `CLOSED_BY_F2_291/292/293/294`
entries, and **a keying fix that renames what a reader has been told is held is indistinguishable
from a slice that changed what those entries mean.** No ambiguous name produces a site today, so
the ambiguous branch is unreachable from the live tree and is pinned against a synthetic corpus in
**both** directions ([[F2-195]]: a branch nothing reaches is a branch nothing checks).

### Three of my own errors, each caught by running something

⚠⚠ **[[F2-274]]'s trap, in a slice written to close a keying hole.** Everything above tests the two
**accessors** and none of it tests which one the measurement **calls** — so the production path
could revert one argument with every size assertion green, and the site set cannot see it either,
because the measured set is empty both ways. 🔑 **A leg that exercises a primitive says nothing
about whether the code under review CALLS it.** A structural call-site ban was added, and the
harness confirms it is the only leg that kills that mutation.

⚠⚠ **That ban then matched its own assertion message.** It read comment-stripped source, and the
assertions quote the very call shapes they are about — [[F2-193]]'s rule that **a detector which
cannot tell a quotation from a claim forces every correction to paraphrase away its own evidence**,
landing on a leg written after quoting it. String literals are stripped now.

⚠⚠ **And the stripper's first draft INVERTED ITSELF.** Its own body contains `'"'` — a
single-quoted double-quote — so the scanner toggled on it and **everything after that point was
inverted**: real code blanked, string literals preserved. The tell was the *wrong half* of a pair of
assertions failing, and only the leg's own count caught it. 🔑 **A stripper that mis-identifies one
span does not degrade, it inverts** — the same family as [[F2-198]]'s two-pass comment stripper and
[[F2-211]]'s branch order. Char literals are skipped now, with a pin carrying the exact shape.

⚙ **No production code changed, and inventing some to justify the measurement would have been the
error** ([[F2-284]]'s precedent). There is nothing to probe: the change is entirely to an
instrument, and its verification is the mutation harness plus the unchanged zero over a wider
population.

⚙ **M1's first run was an ANCHOR MISS at 2 matches rather than a survivor** — two identical
call-site lines, and replacing only the first is the point, so the harness declares `want=2`.
Keeping *did-not-run* distinct from *survived* is what made that legible ([[F2-212]]).

⚙ **`BUILD FAILURE` with no `Tests run:` line, from the working directory drifting to the repo
root**, where there is no POM — [[F2-255]]'s tell, and the reason every `mvn` command in this
programme carries the absolute path.

### The other keyed map, closed rather than filed

Shipping a slice about keying ambiguity that closes **one of two** keyed maps is [[F2-215]]'s
two-of-N in exactly the shape this lineage keeps finding, so `liveWriters()` was closed here.

Simple-name keying is **right** for it — it is a lookup map and a `Moved` record names its writer by
simple name — but a lookup of an **ambiguous** name silently returns whichever path sorted last.
[[F2-287]]'s rule: an unresolved ambiguity must never fall back to something confident, because an
entry resolved against the wrong module reads exactly like one resolved against the right one. Three
service simple names collide today and no held record names one, so the leg is a tripwire on the
direction that fails confidently rather than loudly.

⚠⚠ **And the harness found that leg was VACUOUS.** Blinding the detector **SURVIVED**, because
*"collect the violations, assert the list empty"* produces an empty list whether it is working or
dead — 🔑 **on a clean corpus an empty list is what a correct detector and a rotted one both
return** ([[F2-250]]). Extracted as `ambiguousLookupsIn(code, ambiguousNames)` so the leg drives it
over a **synthetic** corpus in both directions: it must flag `services.get("BoardPackService")` and
must **not** flag `services.get("KycService")`, because a tripwire that fires on an unambiguous
lookup fails on correct code ([[F2-214]]).

### Filed

⚠ `sources("Service.java")` matches by suffix, so two **entity** files named `CloudService.java` are
in a map called *services*. Harmless — an entity declares no null guards, so it contributes nothing
— and it means the map's name overstates its contents. Narrowing the glob to `/service/` packages
would be a change to a shipped gate's population for no measured gain, so it is named in the
assertion instead.

⚠ `*Request.java` is **58 files with 58 distinct names**, so the writer half's collision hazard is
absent by **data** rather than by construction — a fact about today ([[F2-182]]), which is why the
tripwire above is keyed on the *service* collision set that is non-empty and asserted to stay so.

### Why a sweep, and why that is not the same judgement F2-293 made

[[F2-240]] swept this population once before, for a stated reason: *when every remaining member is
latent-by-caller, reach has nothing left to rank.* That is the condition again. The divergence
ordering is real and identical in dev and prod:

| site | initialiser | differs on | what the reset asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Control#controlType` | `PREVENTIVE` | **15 / 32** | 9 DETECTIVE + 4 CORRECTIVE + 2 RECOVERY controls read as preventive |
| `Control#automationLevel` | `MANUAL` | **12 / 32** | 4 AUTOMATED + 8 SEMI controls read as manual |

| 11 × `BcmSettings` tolerance | factory value | 0 / 1 | every ISO 22301 tolerance reverts |
| 4 others | — | 0 | latent |

⚠⚠ **And reach is uniformly zero through the screen, which is what makes ordering impossible.**
Every call site of all eleven routes was read. **Five of the seven highest-divergence sites have no
frontend caller at all** — `lib/controlLibrary.ts#updateControl`, `lib/bcmCycle.ts#updateCapa`,
`frameworkApi.updateMapping` and `amlApi.update` are dark clients — and the rest echo the whole
record back (`engagementToReq` names every field including `status`; `toBackendPlan`/`toBackendWp`
name `budgetHours`/`hours`; both `changeApi.update` callers spread `{...c}`).

🔑 [[F2-237]]'s rule applies with more force here than it did there: **a defence in one client is
not a defence, and five of these had no client to be defended by.** `frameworkApi.updateMapping`'s
declared body type is `{ clauseRef?, satisfaction?, notes? }` — an explicit invitation to send the
partial body the server could not survive, on a route with no call site, which is [[F2-214]]'s
invitation-to-build shape. Removing the initialiser makes the hazard **absent** rather than latent
([[F2-213]]).

### 🔑🔑 The remedy was already written at nine of the 27 sites and could not run

`AmlAlertService#create` ended `if (a.getCurrency() == null) a.setCurrency("SAR")`.
`AuditEngagementService#create` had `if (e.getStatus() == null) e.setStatus("PLANNED")`.
`createCapa` defaulted **and** range-checked both its fields; `createControl` defaulted **and**
vocabulary-checked both of its; `createGovernance`, `ChangeManagementService#create` and
`addMapping` likewise.

Every one of those guards was **dead**, because `apply` copies the request's value and the request's
own initialiser made it non-null. [[F2-292]] found this on one register and called it *"the create's
own default was dead too"*; measured across a population it is **a third of the sites**.

🔑 **A reader auditing such a create finds the default present and correct, and has no reason to ask
whether its guard can fire.** That is [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N one level down — not a mechanism present
on two fields of three, but a mechanism present and *inert*, which is strictly more reassuring than
one that is missing.

### ⚠⚠ A third kind, where deleting the initialiser would have been wrong

Thirteen of the 27 sites are on the two settings registers, and there the initialisers were the
register's **declared factory defaults**. `BcmSettingsService#getOrInit()` carried the comment *"every
default is set in the entity constructor"*, and `reset()` read `new BcmSettings()` field by field as
its source of truth. Deleting them would have left eleven NOT NULL columns with no writer and broken
the reset control outright.

So the declaration **moved** to a `defaults()` factory that both readers name — one declaration, two
readers ([[F2-217]]'s rule).

🔑 **That relocation closed a drift the initialisers were hiding.**
`OrganisationSettingsService#resetToDefaults` writes its defaults as **literals** and never touched
`carbonOffsetCapPct` at all, so *"reset to defaults"* left the carbon-offset cap wherever it happened
to be. The entity's initialisers and that literal list were two copies of one fact with nobody
maintaining the agreement ([[F2-177]]), and the **third** copy going is what made the gap visible.

### The sharpest site, and the reason it is sharp

`AuditEngagementService#advance` is explicitly forward-only — `if (to <= from) throw "must advance
forward only"` — so the entity-bound `PUT` was **the only reverse edge in the register**. It carries
the same `COMPLIANCE:WRITE` permission as the create and `/advance`, so there is no privilege
escalation: the object-level machine was the only control and the PUT sat beside it without one
([[F2-219]]'s shape). `compliance.audit_engagements` has **zero CHECK constraints**, so nothing else
narrowed the column either. Probed live: a create naming `CLOSED` returned **201 storing CLOSED**, and
a partial `PUT` took a CLOSED engagement to **PLANNED** with `findings_count` **9 → 0**.

### ⚠ Directions are MIXED, and this register's recent history says otherwise

Five resets are **flattering** — a CRITICAL AML alert reading MEDIUM; a CRITICAL ISO 22301 corrective
action reading MEDIUM; the one EMERGENCY change reading NORMAL, which removes it from the population
an ADR-017 §D-3 reviewer examines; 9 DETECTIVE + 4 CORRECTIVE + 2 RECOVERY controls reading
PREVENTIVE; a CLOSED audit engagement reading PLANNED. Four are **pessimistic** — 10 FULL framework
satisfactions reading PARTIAL; 4 AUTOMATED + 8 SEMI controls reading MANUAL; every working paper's
hours and both annual plans' budgets reading 0.

[[F2-193]], [[F2-195]] and [[F2-205]] were uniformly flattering and [[F2-210]] uniformly pessimistic.
🔑 [[F2-196]]'s rule is the one that holds: **a reset has no direction until you look.**

### Instrument work, all of it in the same commit

⚠⚠ **`methodBody`'s resolver required an access modifier**, so a package-private `static defaults()`
was invisible and the `Moved` leg reported **13 writers as "no such method"**. [[F2-291]]'s shape
inside this gate's own resolver, one slice after that finding. It failed **loudly**, which is the only
reason it cost nothing — 🔑 **a resolver that silently returned null would have reported the
create-path default as PRESENT**, i.e. would have certified thirteen fixes it could not see.

⚠ **The anti-vacuity floor counted `WORK_LIST` and went vacuous the moment the list emptied** —
exactly as its own comment predicted when [[F2-293]] wrote that prediction down ([[F2-219]]).
Re-scoped to the `CLOSED_BY_*` union, with the floor taken from **the gate's own output** (21 of 44)
after a sentinel run rather than from a prediction ([[F2-195]]), and the largest wrong answer — zero —
named in place ([[F2-215]]).

⚠ **The javadoc's first draft said "9 DETECTIVE and 2 RECOVERY" against a measured 15 of 32.**

right is what stops anybody checking the list — inside the comment recording the measurement. Both
enumerations are spelled out now.

describes a row that cannot exist in either database.

revert would not compile: the fix introduces `INITIAL_STATUS`, `DEFAULT_FINDINGS_COUNT` and two

⚠ `compliance.audit_engagements` has **zero CHECK constraints** on `status`, over a 7-value stored
