## F2-293 — the first screen-reachable member of this population, and the reachability question is per call site rather than per page

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`452cc31b`) |
| **Severity** | P1 — clicking **Pause** or **Resume** on a scheduled regulatory report rewrote its **format, language, cadence and delivery time**, and the report kept being emailed to its recipients on the new schedule. A body omitting `isActive` **resumed a paused report**. Separately, the semi-annual ISO 22301 / NCEMA BCM readiness report was being **retried daily** — 13 consecutive FAILED runs in both databases. All probed live. |
| **Register** | `reporting.report_schedules` (11 live rows, byte-identical in dev and prod) |
| **Standards** | the register carries the tenant's board and regulator reporting pack — NCA ECC posture, SAMA/CMA board risk-and-compliance, PDPL DSR/breach tracking, ISO 22301 / NCEMA BCM readiness, IIA audit-plan progress, ESG annex |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-292]]'s own 32-site work list, re-derived before executing ([[F2-221]]) because correcting the previous filing's ranking was that slice's whole finding |
| **Verification** | live probe **14/14 pre-fix · 14/14 post-fix** as `compliance`, never `admin`; mutations **13/13 killed, 0 survived, 0 anchor-miss**; backend **4602 → 4614/0/0**; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; register back at 11 live rows with 0 tagged rows left |

### The defect

`ReportScheduleController` binds the `ReportSchedule` **entity** on POST and PUT. Jackson
deserialises an omitted key into `new ReportSchedule()`, and the entity declared
`format = "PDF"`, `language = "en"`, `cadence = "WEEKLY"`, `timeOfDay = "06:00"` and
`isActive = true` — so every `if (s.getX() != null)` in `apply` was **true on every request**, and a
partial `PUT` rewrote all five.

🔑🔑 **THE FIRST SCREEN-REACHABLE MEMBER OF THIS POPULATION, AND BY A ONE-CLICK CONTROL.**
`ReportSchedulesPage` holds **two** update call sites:

- `submitForm` sends `{...values}`, seeded from `reqFromDto`'s `{...s}` — the edit modal echoes every
  field back, so it is safe. This is exactly the shape [[F2-291]] and [[F2-292]] both measured, and
  why both of those were **API-reachable only**.
- `togglePause` sends `{ isActive: !s.isActive }` **and nothing else**.

So one page was simultaneously safe and destructive. Probed live as `compliance` — the only non-admin
holder of `REPORTING:WRITE` — a schedule stored as `XLSX / ar / QUARTERLY / 22:00` became
`PDF / en / WEEKLY / 06:00` after a single Pause click, while `cadenceAnchor` and `nameAr` survived:
those two are guarded **and uninitialised**, which is the control showing the reset came from the
initialisers rather than from the guards.

🔑 **[[F2-283]]'s screen-reachable / API-reachable distinction is per CALL SITE, not per page.** Two
slices in a row concluded *"the screen echoes the whole DTO, so this is API-reachable only"* from
reading `reqFromDto`. This page's `reqFromDto` also echoes, and the defect is live anyway because a
**different handler on the same page** builds its own body. Reading one payload builder is one file
short — the same error shape as [[F2-187]]'s *"one file short is the whole error"*.

### The measurement, and the third consecutive inverted ranking

Identical in dev and prod over 11 live rows — rows a partial `PUT` would rewrite:

| field | initialiser | differs on | what the reset asserts |
|---|---|---|---|
| `cadence` | `WEEKLY` | **10 / 11** | a quarterly regulator return becomes weekly |
| `language` | `en` | **9 / 11** | an Arabic report reverts to English (house rule 7) |
| `time_of_day` | `06:00` | **9 / 11** | the delivery time moves |
| `format` | `PDF` | 1 / 11 | an XLSX tracker becomes a PDF |
| `is_active` | `true` | **0 / 11** | a paused report resumes |

🔑 **`isActive` differs on 0 rows because the toggle is the one caller that always sends it** — so the
field [[F2-292]]'s filing ranked sharpest is the one this defect could not reach through the screen,
and the four it listed as collateral were the live ones. It is closed anyway: a body that omits it
resumed a paused report (probed, `PUT {"cadence":"MONTHLY"}` took `is_active` false → true), and a
reset that **restarts delivery manufactures an assurance** rather than losing a fact ([[F2-240]]).

**Third slice running where the filing's ranking and the executing slice's measurement disagree.**
[[F2-291]]'s filing was corrected by [[F2-292]], and [[F2-292]]'s by this one. The pattern is
structural rather than careless: **a filing ranks by what the initialiser asserts, because that is
all it can see without reading the callers; the executing slice ranks by the caller.** Expect to
re-derive, and expect the answer to move.

⚠ No privilege escalation: `REPORTING:WRITE` guards the create, the PUT and `/run-now` alike, so the
object-level behaviour was the only control ([[F2-219]]'s shape). `REPORTING:DELETE` is held only by
`ORG_ADMIN`, which has **0 active holders**, so nobody but a platform administrator can delete a
schedule ([[F2-253]]'s shape) — filed.

### The adjacent defect the same measurement exposed, and why it had to land in this commit

`reporting.report_schedules` has **zero CHECK constraints**, and `seed_real_data.py` wrote
**`SEMIANNUAL`** onto the *"Semi-annual ISO 22301 / NCEMA BCM readiness"* schedule — a token
`advanceNextRun`'s `switch` did not name, so its `default` arm rescheduled it `now.plusDays(1)`.
Measured in both databases: **13 consecutive FAILED runs, 2026-08-11 to 2026-08-23**.

⚠⚠ **Pre-fix, the pause toggle would have "healed" it by accident** — resetting the cadence to
`WEEKLY`, a token the scheduler handles. So *this slice's own fix makes the daily retry permanent*.
That is [[F2-203]]'s detonation (fixing one defect is what arms the next), and it is why the
`SEMIANNUAL` arm is in the same commit rather than filed.

🔑🔑 **EVERY READER AGREED AND THE STORED DATA WAS THE OUTLIER.** `CADENCE_OPTIONS` offers exactly the
four the switch handled; `REPORT_TYPE_OPTIONS` offers exactly the five `renderBody` handles. So the
screen and the server were consistent, and consistency among readers is what made a third value
invisible. [[F2-205]]'s question — *how many things read this, and which of them is the server?* —
assumes the disagreement is **between readers**; here there was none. [[F2-180]]'s mirror: there the
screen offered categories the column's CHECK refused, here the column holds tokens every reader
refuses — one **loudly** (`default -> throw` on `report_type`) and one **silently**
(`default -> plusDays(1)` on `cadence`).

`SUPPORTED_CADENCES` is now one declaration with two readers: the switch, and a write-boundary
refusal that turns a silently-daily schedule into a **400 naming the field**. The frontend list is a
third copy and is checked against it by `ReportCadenceContractTest`, cross-codebase in the way
`ConnectorBackingContractTest` reads a `.ts` file ([[F2-193]]).

⚠ Deliberately **not** a `ClosedVocabulary`: that primitive *requires* the name of a CHECK it mirrors
and there is none on this table. The claim here is not about the schema — it is *the scheduler can
compute a next run for every one of these* — which is checkable in Java, and is checked
**behaviourally** rather than by matching `case` labels. `require` not `coerce` ([[F2-182]]): every
stored value is already a member and the frontend offers exactly this set, so nothing that works
today starts failing. The `default` arm keeps its one-day fallback — throwing would break the run
loop, which calls `advanceNextRun` from its catch path too — but now **WARNs naming the token**, so
an unrecognised cadence is chased rather than excused ([[F2-196]]).

⚠ **No CHECK migration rides with this, and the reason is recorded rather than assumed:**
`report_type` is the larger open vocabulary on the same table, and constraining `cadence` alone would
leave the table's real vocabulary problem open while looking addressed. Both want one migration once
the report-type question has an owner decision ([[F2-183]]: a constraint and its writers land
together).

### The test that could have caught it picked the two fields where the principle held

`ReportScheduleBilingualTest.anOmittedArabicFieldIsLeftAloneRatherThanBlanked` states the general
rule in its own javadoc — *"`apply()` treats null as 'leave alone' so a partial PATCH-style body
cannot wipe fields"* — and exercised it on `nameAr` and `descriptionAr`, **two of the only guarded
fields on this entity with no initialiser**. For the five that had one, the rule was **false**.

🔑 **A partial-update test that picks the uninitialised fields proves the principle on exactly the
fields where it holds.** [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N inside a test fixture, which is the artefact a reader
trusts most. Corrected in place and extended to the other five — and a mocked repository cannot see
this at all, which is why it was probed live (house rule 4).

### Three of my own assertions were wrong, and each was caught by running something

⚠ **(a) Distance cannot discriminate the fallback arm.** The first cadence leg asserted that no
non-daily cadence lands within two days, and it **failed on correct code**: `nextWeekly` reads the
anchor as a day-of-week, so a WEEKLY schedule legitimately lands tomorrow whenever tomorrow is the
anchor day. A gate that fails on working code trains the next reader to edit the assertion
([[F2-214]]), and a red leg is a finding only when the code is actually wrong ([[F2-206]]). Replaced
by per-cadence **properties the default arm cannot produce** — the anchor's own day-of-week or
day-of-month, and the month a period must start in, with every anchor chosen so tomorrow's date
cannot satisfy it by coincidence.

⚠⚠ **(b) The probe then reproduced that exact error one file over.** It asserted the `SEMIANNUAL`
next-run was `>= 150` days out and failed at **145** — `2027-01-15`, which is precisely the next
half-year start after 2026-08-23 for anchor 15. A half-year boundary is between 1 and ~183 days away
depending where in the half you stand, so a distance threshold is only right for part of the year.
🔑 **Naming a trap does not exempt you from it**, and I had fixed the identical mistake minutes
earlier in the unit test.

⚠ **(c) I replaced the last element of a hard-asserted work list with a member I had never
measured** — a phantom in exactly the artefact [[F2-292]] recorded the hazard for. Caught before the
build ran, by re-reading the edit.

### 🔑 A test whose strength depends on the month it runs in

The mutation harness found the sharpest instrument defect here: a mutant computing the **quarterly**
start instead of the half-year start **SURVIVED**. Quarters begin Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct and halves Jan/Jul,
so the two **agree in six months of twelve** — and the run was in August, where both answer July. So
`isIn(1, 7)` passes over a quarterly implementation for Jan–Mar and Jul–Sep.

🔑 **A test whose strength depends on the month it runs in is strong on the day you write it and weak
on the day it matters.** No single instant can separate the two functions, so the fix is not a better
assertion at *now*: `theSemiannualArithmeticHoldsInEveryMonthOfTheYear` drives `nextSemiannual`
across **all twelve months**. It takes `now` as a parameter, which is why this is a unit assertion
rather than a probe.

### Harness landmines

⚠ **`os._exit()` skips stdout flushing**, so the first piped probe run printed **nothing** and read
exactly like a probe that never executed. It had in fact run — it planted and cleaned its rows.

⚠⚠ **A wholesale pre-fix revert is the wrong control for a fix that INTRODUCES a symbol.** The new
gate references `ReportSchedulerService.SUPPORTED_CADENCES`, so reverting the service made the test
fail to **compile** — and a control that cannot run reads exactly like a gate that passed
([[F2-287]], which recorded this same shape). Surgical mutations instead, which is the right
instrument anyway because it says *which* leg sees *which* half.

⚠ **A mutation anchor that is a PREFIX of its line leaves the tail dangling.** M1's anchor stopped
before `(see ReportSchedulerService#renderBody)`, so the mutant did not compile and reported as
inconclusive — **neither a kill nor a hole**. Anchor on the whole line, and keep
*did-not-run* distinct from *survived*.

⚠ **The helper-only floor was re-measured 8 → 5, and which it is matters.** All five members closed
here were helper-only — their guards live in a private `apply` — so the population fell **because of
the fix** rather than because the detector rotted ([[F2-213]]: a population that falls after a fix is
not automatically rot, but it is always worth asking which). That floor also has a shape problem in
its future, recorded in place: it counts `WORK_LIST`, so when the work list reaches zero the count is
zero too and the leg goes vacuous ([[F2-219]]).

### Filed

⚠⚠ **Seven of eleven scheduled regulatory reports have never been delivered.** `renderBody` handles
`RISK_REGISTER | FINDINGS_AGING | KRI_DASHBOARD | BOARD_PACK | AI_MODEL_REGISTRY` and answers
`default -> throw`; the register holds seven other types, all written by the seed and none offered by
`REPORT_TYPE_OPTIONS`: `BOARD_RISK_COMPLIANCE_PACK`, `CYBER_POSTURE_ECC`, `TPRM_RISK_POSTURE`,
`AUDIT_PLAN_PROGRESS`, `ESG_ANNEX`, `PDPL_DSR_BREACH_TRACKER`, `BCM_READINESS`. Every one carries
`last_run_status = FAILED` with `Unknown report type: …`, in **both** databases. `ExportService` has
no generator for any of them, so this is seven new report builders — a **build plus an owner
decision** (which framework each pack must satisfy), not a slice. It is also why no CHECK migration
rode with this fix.

⚠ **`FORMAT_OPTIONS` offers DOCX and PPTX and the renderer cannot produce either for most types.**
`renderBody` is `"PDF".equalsIgnoreCase(fmt) ? …Pdf(lang) : …Xlsx()` for four of the five types, and
`mimeFor` maps anything unrecognised to `application/pdf` — so choosing **DOCX** yields **XLSX bytes
labelled as a PDF with a `.pdf` extension**. PPTX is real for `BOARD_PACK` only, and its label already
says so. Latent: 10 of 11 live rows are PDF and one is XLSX. Deciding which formats each report type
supports is a product matrix ([[F2-193]]'s rule that a catalogue must not claim a capability that
does not exist).

⚠ `reporting.report_schedules` has **zero CHECK constraints** on `report_type`, `format`, `language`
or `cadence`; the cadence writer is closed now, the other three are not.

⚠ `REPORTING:DELETE` is held only by `ORG_ADMIN`, which has **0 active holders** in either database.


## F2-292 — the sharpest member of a work list was not its widest, and the derivation that closed the last register could not be copied to this one

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`81547da5`) |
| **Severity** | P1 — every conflict-of-interest disclosure in the register was **destroyable by a body carrying only `titleEn`**, which reverted it to DRAFT and escaped a TERMINAL state; and a disclosure could be **filed already APPROVED** with no decider, skipping the whole review chain. Both probed live. |
| **Register** | `ethics.disclosures` (18 live rows, byte-identical in dev and prod) |
| **Standards** | NAZAHA and the Saudi anti-bribery regime; SAMA and CMA corporate-governance conflict-of-interest declaration requirements |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-291]]'s own 34-site work list, ranked by what the initialiser **asserts** ([[F2-239]]) rather than by count — and the measurement **inverted the ranking** |
| **Verification** | live probe **7/12 pre-fix · 12/12 post-fix** as `compliance`, never `admin`; gate control **5 of 12 legs discriminate**, the other 7 named; backend **4595 → 4602/0/0**; both databases back at 18 / 30 / 16 / 12 with **0** tagged rows across 245 swept text columns |

### The defect

`DisclosureController` binds the `Disclosure` **entity** on POST and PUT. Jackson deserialises an
omitted key into `new Disclosure()`, and the entity declared `private String status = "DRAFT"` — so
`apply`'s `if (src.getStatus() != null) target.setStatus(...)` was **true on every request**, and a
partial update reverted the disclosure.

Measured identically in dev and the deployed database: **18 live rows, 18 of them non-DRAFT** —
APPROVED 11, REVIEW 4, SUBMITTED 2, REJECTED 1 — so every disclosure in the register was destroyable
this way.

🔑 **APPROVED, RECUSED and MITIGATED are TERMINAL in `DisclosureService.TRANSITIONS`** (`Set.of()`,
no outgoing edges), so the reset **escaped a terminal state by a route the machine cannot see** — and
`DRAFT → SUBMITTED` exists, so the whole review cycle became re-runnable on a decided disclosure.
There is no privilege escalation: `COMPLIANCE:WRITE` guards the create, the PUT and `/transition`
alike, so the object-level machine was the only control and the PUT sat beside it without one
([[F2-219]]'s shape).

⚠ **API-reachable, not screen-reachable, and saying which is the point** ([[F2-283]]).
`EthicsPage`'s disclosure form declares **no** status field among its sixteen, but `reqFromDto`
spreads the whole DTO into the edit modal, so the screen's PUT **echoed** the stored status and those
18 rows survived. The reachable caller is anything sending a genuinely partial body — which is
exactly what the client's own `Partial<DisclosureDto>` type invites, and where machine callers live
([[F2-179]]). That echo is also why the fix must **tolerate** one rather than refuse the field: a
refusal would break the screen that works today, the one failure a fix must never have ([[F2-214]]).

### The second half: the create's own default was dead too

`create()` read `apply(d, req); if (d.getStatus() == null) d.setStatus("DRAFT");` — and `apply` copied
a status that was never null, so **that default was dead code and the create accepted the caller's
value**. Probed pre-fix: `POST` with `status: "APPROVED"` returned **201 storing APPROVED**, skipping
`DRAFT → SUBMITTED → REVIEW` and the transition route that is the **only writer** of `decision`,
`decisionNotes`, `decidedByName` and `decidedAt` ([[F2-220]]'s shape, [[F2-223]]'s attribution). The
create now forces the initial state and refuses a contradicting one.

### 🔑🔑 The ranking inverted, and breadth was the wrong axis

`BcmSettingsService#update` contributes **11 of the 34** work-list entries — the RTO/RPO warning and
critical hours, the exercise cadences, the evidence-expiry warning, the CAPA grace days, the risk
matrix maxima — i.e. every ISO 22301 tolerance the BCM controls compare against. Measured: **0 of 1
rows differ from the initialiser, on all eleven.** Entirely latent; nothing to destroy.

The two-entry member differs on **18 of 18**. [[F2-239]]'s rule for the third time: **harm-if-reached
and reach are two orderings and they disagree** — and the member a count would have picked has the
widest apparent blast radius and the smallest real one.

### 🔑🔑 A derivation cannot be copied to a machine with a different topology

[[F2-291]] derived `EthicsCaseLifecycle.INITIAL` as *the one state that is never a transition target*.
That derivation **yields nothing here**: this machine has `REJECTED → DRAFT`, so DRAFT **is** a target
and the root set is **empty**. Copying it would have made every disclosure start nowhere.

[[F2-290]]'s rule — **copying a derivation copies its convention** — with this as the case where the
convention does not hold. So `INITIAL_STATUS` is **declared**, and a static block asserts *both* halves
of the reasoning: that the literal is a state the machine knows, and that the root set really is empty,
**so a reader can see the derivation was tried rather than overlooked**. It is also a tripwire: it
throws the moment this machine gains a state that is never a target, telling the next reader to switch
to the derivation.

### Refuted, and worth recording so nobody re-derives them

- **`analytics()`'s inclusion lists are exhaustive today.** `byStatus` loops 7 tokens and `byType` 8;
  measured, **0 rows fall outside either** in both databases, and every listed token is stored. So
  [[F2-290]]'s `byCategory` defect — the adjacent register, the same module — is **absent here**. Still
  an inclusion list over a CHECK-less column, so latent; not a live defect, and "fixing" it would be a
  latent-hazard closure rather than a discovery.
- **`currency` is 0 of 18.** All eighteen rows hold `SAR`, so what made that half harmless was the
  **data and not the code** ([[F2-182]]). Closed anyway — and the probe's own row, created with `USD`,
  showed the reset live, which is what the seeded rows could not.

### The instrument finding: a merge that manufactured a phantom

`NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` keys its service-source map by **file simple name into a
`LinkedHashMap`**, so where two files share a name the second visited **replaces** the first —
[[F2-276]]'s exact defect, which failed in the quiet direction there. Three `*Service` names collide
under a `/service/` package: `AuditEngagementService` (audit_eng | compliance), `BoardPackService`
(board_pack | reporting), `RegulatoryChangeService` (compliance | regchange). And the **entity** map in
the same class was **already fixed** for it with `computeIfAbsent` — [[F2-215]]'s two-of-N inside the
instrument, with the fixed half visibly present.

🔑🔑 **So I changed it to merge, and the merge surfaced exactly one new site — a phantom.**
`AuditEngagementService#update :: AuditEngagement#auditType`: `audit_eng`'s entity initialises
`auditType = "INTERNAL"` and its service has **no `update` at all**, while `compliance`'s service
guards `auditType` and its entity declares **no initialiser**, so that guard can fire. Two different
classes, two different tables, one manufactured finding — and the entity map's pre-existing
`computeIfAbsent` union is what supplied the other half.

**The hazard here is CROSS-ATTRIBUTION, not omission**, and it is [[F2-287]]'s rule verbatim: a
fallback for an unresolved type reintroduces the ambiguity the resolution removed, and **it fails in
the confident direction — a finding naming the wrong table**. A gate that reports a defect where none
exists is worse than one that misses ([[F2-214]]), so the merge is **reverted** and the phantom is
pinned by `theDuplicateNameHazardIsCrossAttributionNotOmission`, which fails if anybody reintroduces
it. The real fix is module-aware pairing on **both** maps, which is a change to a shipped security
gate and is **filed** rather than smuggled into a slice about a different register.

⚠ **What made the merge look safe was my own measurement.** `f292_dupsvc.py` looked for guards inside
a **private helper**, which is narrower than this gate's population, and concluded *"no pair collapses
today"*. 🔑 **A hazard measured with a narrower population than the instrument's reads as latent when
it is not.**

### My own errors, all caught by running something

- ⚠⚠ **A member regex anchored on the previous member's `;` cannot match a field preceded by a
  comment**, and this codebase comments heavily between fields. **13 of 34 initialisers read as
  absent** — and a field with no initialiser is not in this population at all, so the miss read
  exactly like *nothing to see here* ([[F2-206]]). Stripping comments first — the rule already on the
  record — took it to **0 unresolved**. The tell was `rtoCriticalHours` resolving while
  `rtoWarningHours`, on the adjacent identical line, did not.
- My `src()` resolver returned a **3-tuple** on its unresolvable path, and [[F2-287]]'s rule is that
  ambiguity must **throw** rather than resolve by luck. Corrected, it fired immediately on
  `AuditEngagementService` — the exact pair F2-287 lost a hypothesis to — and resolving the twin by
  *which one declares the method* is what settled it.
- **A piped build's exit code is the pipe's, not Maven's.** `mvn … | grep` reported `exited with
  code 0` over a `BUILD FAILURE`, and I had edited the gate mid-build, so the failure was
  attributable to neither. Redirect to a file and read `$?`.
- **The jar lock, twice.** `mvn clean` cannot delete a jar a running JVM holds open, and the probe
  jar was mine both times. Kill by CommandLine, guarded on the session id and on the target not
  owning 8090/8091.
- Guessed the repository finder (`findByIdAndOrganisationIdAndIsDeletedFalse`); it is `findById(id)`
  with an in-memory tenant filter. Guessed nothing else after resolving `target` and `accessToken`
  from the controller and `AuthController` respectively.
- The transition leg failed because `CurrentActor.username()` returns null with no principal —
  a leg failing for a reason unrelated to its claim ([[F2-244]]). Fixed by installing the house
  `GrcUserDetails` fixture ([[F2-261]]), not by weakening the assertion.
- The victim create failed on `description`, **NOT NULL with no default**, and the diagnostic reads
  *"A required field was not supplied"* naming **no field** — [[F2-210]]/[[F2-214]]'s shape, which
  cost one probe iteration. Resolved from `sys.columns`.

### Filed

- The **32** remaining work-list sites, no reasons ([[F2-188]]). By what the initialiser asserts:
  `ReportSchedule#isActive = true` **manufactures an assurance** — a paused regulator report resumes
  — beside `cadence = "WEEKLY"`, `language = "en"` (an Arabic report reverting to English, house
  rule 7) and `format`/`timeOfDay`, measured **10/11, 9/11, 1/11, 9/11** differing; `Control#controlType
  = "PREVENTIVE"` and `#automationLevel = "MANUAL"` at **15/32 and 12/32**;
  `AuditEngagement#status = "PLANNED"` at 10/12; `ChangeRequest#changeType = "NORMAL"` at 6/17 dev and
  6/15 prod. `BcmSettings`' eleven are **0/1 and latent**.
- **Module-aware pairing** for both of this gate's source maps.
- `ethics.disclosures` has **zero CHECK constraints** — now cheap, since this slice closed its only
  open status writer ([[F2-183]]) — and `title_ar` is **not NOT NULL**, so a statutory disclosure can
  be filed with no Arabic title (house rule 7).
- **7 of the 11 APPROVED rows carry no `decided_by_name` and no `decided_at`**, identical in both
  databases: seed-origin, since `transition` has stamped both since F2-223, so those approvals record
  no approver. Repair rewrites live governance rows — **owner decision**.
- `apply` still copies `disclosureCode`, so a caller can rename the reference an auditor cites
  ([[F2-172]](d)'s family, outside `ClientSuppliedReferenceRatchetTest`'s setter key).

## F2-291 — a hard-zero invariant whose population was `publicMethods`, over a codebase whose house idiom is a private `apply(target, src)` helper

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`6a6f017c`) |
| **Severity** | P1 — a KYC subject with a confirmed OFAC SDN sanctions match was **approved for business** by an edit that changed only its name, and a whistleblowing case was **de-anonymised** the same way. Live, probed, identical in dev and prod |
| **Registers** | `ethics.cases` (30 live rows), `ethics.kyc_subjects` (16), both byte-identical in dev and prod |
| **Standards** | NAZAHA / the Saudi Whistleblower Protection Law; FATF R.12 and SAMA AML/CFT for the PEP and sanctions flags |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-290]]'s filing of `intake_channel` and re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]) — which **refuted the filing's figure** and, while reading the writers, found the mechanism one level up |
| **Verification** | live probe **7/12 and 5/11 pre-fix**, **12/12 and 11/11 post-fix**, as `compliance` and never `admin`; gate control **7 of 12 legs discriminate**, the other 5 named as pins, self-tests and measurements ([[F2-225]]); mutations **13 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss**; backend **4583 -> 4595/0/0**, frontend 818/818, `tsc` clean; both databases back at 30 / 16 / 12 with zero probe residue |

### The defect

`EthicsCaseController` and `KycController` bind their **entity** on POST and PUT. Jackson
deserialises an omitted key into `new T()`, so a field initialiser is indistinguishable from a value
the caller stated — and both services copy under `if (src.getX() != null)`, which an initialiser
makes true on **every** request. A partial `PUT` was therefore a full replace with the initialisers.

Probed live as `compliance` (which holds `COMPLIANCE:WRITE`, the permission on every one of these
routes, so **there is no privilege escalation here** — the object-level state was the only control):

* `PUT /api/v1/ethics/cases/{id} {"titleEn": "…"}` on a case at INTAKE → **200**, and
  `severity` CRITICAL → **MEDIUM**, `intake_channel` IN_PERSON → **HOTLINE**, `is_anonymous`
  TRUE → **FALSE**. The reporter's name and email columns sit two fields above that flag.
* `PUT /api/v1/ethics/kyc/{id} {"fullName": "…"}` → **200**, and `is_sanctioned` TRUE → **FALSE**,
  `risk_rating` PROHIBITED → **STANDARD**, `edd_required` TRUE → **FALSE**, `cdd_level`
  ENHANCED → **STANDARD**. `POST /{id}/approve` then answered **200** and stored `APPROVED`,
  with the screening hit still on the register reading `TRUE_MATCH`.

🔑🔑 **The KYC half defeats the control [[F2-288]] armed one slice earlier.** `approve()` has always
refused a sanctioned subject; F2-288 was the slice that made anything write the flag it reads. That
flag was then cleared by the adjacent route, under the same permission — and F2-288's own gate leg
says `apply()` *"legitimately copies all four flags because the subject form lets an operator flag a
PEP or a sanctioned party by hand."* True of a **full-echo** form. **The initialiser is what made a
legitimate copy a reset**, and F2-288 read that method, scoped a gate leg around it, and could not
see it.

### 🔑🔑 The instrument finding: two stacked narrowings, and the hard zero read as a finished sweep

`NeverFiringNullGuardContractTest` exists for exactly this defect. F2-237 opened it at 50 sites,
F2-238/239/240 took it to **0**, and F2-240 promoted it from a decreasing work list to an
**invariant** with the words *"Keep it empty. There is no correct code for a hard zero here to fail
on."* It was green over **42 sites**.

1. **`measure()` walked `publicMethods` only.** The house idiom in this codebase is
   `update(id, body)` delegating to a private `apply(target, src)` that holds every null guard, so
   the whole idiom was outside the population **by construction**. [[F2-198]]'s shape at an access
   modifier — and the **third** time this family has been bitten by that exact narrowing: [[F2-237]]
   recorded it for `EvidenceItemService#transitionStatus` against the **sibling** gate,
   [[F2-231]] then built that gate a one-hop private-helper follow and documented it at length, and
   this gate never inherited it ([[F2-190]]) although it already imports `stripComments`,
   `publicMethods` and `requestParamTypes` **from that same class**.
2. **The "did it load a row?" test was a name vocabulary**, `get|find\w*` — and the ethics and KYC
   services call their loader `require(id)`, so every update method in those modules read as a
   *create*, where writing the initialiser is exactly what is meant to happen. [[F2-217]]'s headline.
   ⚠ [[F2-278]] had already recorded this precise limitation for the sibling gate's `loadsARow`
   (`get|mustGet|find*|load*|fetch*`, *"it cannot see `frameworks.require(...)`"*) and **measured
   that porting it changed nothing there** — so the limit was known, filed against one gate, and
   never asked of this one.

Neither narrowing alone would have hidden these two registers; both together did. The load test is
now **structural** — a local of the entity's type initialised from something that is not `new` —
which needs no vocabulary and cannot be defeated by naming a loader something new.

⚠⚠ **And the first structural draft reproduced [[F2-213]]'s recorded detector bug**:
`ChangeRequest saved = changeRepo.save(c);` made a **create** read as a method that had loaded a
row, and F2-213's own first draft counted the same shape and reported 41 sites, nearly all creates.
Naming a trap does not exempt you from it. Both shapes are must-not-match cases in the self-test.

### The fix

[[F2-238]]'s established remedy: **remove the initialiser, own the default on the create path.**
Ten fields across two entities, with `everyRemovedInitialiserHasAWriterOnTheCreatePath` asserting
the (entity, field, writer, method) quadruple in both directions — every one of these columns is
NOT NULL, so a create that stops setting one turns a silent reset into a 500, and nothing else in
the tree can see that under `ddl-auto=none`.

⚠ **`EthicsCase#status` was not a reset, it was a REFUSAL, and it was holding the others shut.**
`apply` never copies `status` ([[F2-22b]](v) moved it to `transition()`), but
`requireLifecycleIsNotBodySet` compares the body's value against the stored one — so with
`= "INTAKE"` a body that omitted `status` looked like a request to move the case **back**, and a
partial PUT on a case at TRIAGE answered **400 "Case 50 is at TRIAGE and cannot be moved to INTAKE
by an update"**, naming a state the caller never sent. 🔑 That refusal is also why the three resets
were live on only the **2 of 30** cases at INTAKE: **fixing the obviously-wrong refusal alone would
have detonated the resets on all 30** ([[F2-203]]: a latent defect in a path is held shut by
whatever else is broken around it). The two halves had to land together.

⚠ The method's javadoc is corrected rather than deleted. It reasons carefully about why a **present**
value must be tolerated (*"`EthicsPage`'s edit modal seeds itself with `reqFromDto(c) = { ...c }`"* —
verified, and `FormModal` submits its whole seeded state, so the edit form really does echo) and had
**no vocabulary for an ABSENT one**. [[F2-184]]'s shape: the paragraph answers the question a reader
was about to ask.

⚙ `EthicsCaseLifecycle.INITIAL` is now **derived** — the one state that is a key and never a target,
with the static block throwing if the machine ever admits two roots or none. It gained a second
reader in this slice (the create default and the create-side comparison), and two copies of one fact
is the shape [[F2-217]] measured.

### What is filed rather than fixed

The corrected population is **34 remaining sites**, held as a decrease-only work list with **no
reasons attached** ([[F2-188]] measured what happens otherwise: five claims, five false). They are
to be read and closed the way F2-238/239/240 closed the first population — ordered by reach, entity
by entity. **Do not write 34 reasons.** The nine pairs this slice fixed are held separately by name,
so a revert FAILS rather than being absorbed by a tolerated list.

Sharpest unread members, by what the initialiser ASSERTS ([[F2-238]]'s ordering):
`AuditEngagementService#update :: AuditEngagement#findingsCount` (resets an IIA engagement's finding
count to **0** — and [[F2-278]] already filed that field for a different reason);
`DisclosureService#update :: Disclosure#status` (a conflict-of-interest disclosure reverts to
**DRAFT**); `ChangeManagementService#update :: ChangeRequest#changeType` (an **EMERGENCY** change
becomes **NORMAL**); `ReportScheduleService#update :: ReportSchedule#isActive` (resets to **true**,
so a paused regulator report starts sending again); the **eleven** `BcmSettingsService#update` thresholds ⚠ **corrected by [[F2-292]], which re-derived the list before executing it ([[F2-221]]):** this said *"nine `BcmSettingsService#update` thresholds"*, and there are **eleven** — and all eleven differ from their initialiser on **0 of 1 rows**, so the member with 11 of the 34 entries is entirely **latent** while the two-entry `Disclosure` member behind it was **18 of 18**. Breadth was the wrong axis.

### ⚠ My own errors, all caught by running something

* **The em-dash trap, in PowerShell this time.** Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a script file as ANSI
  unless it carries a BOM, so a UTF-8 em-dash in a comment became three bytes it could not parse and
  the whole kill script failed to compile with five cascading errors pointing at unrelated lines.
  [[F2-271]] recorded the same trap for a Python patch script; **a PowerShell script must be pure
  ASCII.**
* **My extraction of the gate's own output dropped the first element of the list.** AssertJ prints
  the first member of a set on the `["…` line, and my grep asked for lines starting with whitespace
  and a quote — so a 34-member population read as 33, which is exactly the failure mode this slice
  is about, in the harness reading it. The gate refused it; the count came from the gate.
* **The `mvn` launcher is on D:**, and the Bash cwd drifts after a `cd` in an earlier command, so
  `sed`/`grep` against a relative path failed with a misleading usage error. Use absolute paths.

### ⚙ Filed

* The **34-site** work list above.
* **[[F2-290]]'s `intake_channel` figure was wrong in one direction.** Re-derived: `CHANNEL_OPTIONS`
  offers **16** values, the register stores **13**, they intersect in **4** (`HOTLINE`, `EMAIL`,
  `IN_PERSON`, `WEB_FORM`, 17 of 30 rows). So the 9 stored-and-not-offered is right and the
  "6 offered-never-stored" is **12**. Still display-only: nothing counts the column, `list()` has no
  channel filter, and the register cell renders the raw token through `.replace(/_/g, ' ')` — so 9
  of 13 stored values appear as unlabelled English words on an Arabic-primary UI (house rule 7).
* **`KycService#apply` copies `status` at all**, so a caller who *sends* a status still overwrites
  the lifecycle — [[F2-22b]](v)'s defect, which `EthicsCaseService` has a guard for and this register
  never got. Deciding whether an operator may set a KYC status directly is not a side effect of
  removing an initialiser.
* `ethics.cases` and `ethics.kyc_subjects` both still have **zero CHECK constraints**; `cddLevel` is
  copied unvalidated where `riskRating` goes through a `ClosedVocabulary`. Cheap now that this slice
  touched both writers ([[F2-183]]), and blocked on [[F2-290]]'s finding that 11 of 30 ethics rows
  already hold statuses outside the machine.
* Neither register's edit form offers a control for the flags it round-trips (`isAnonymous`,
  `isSanctioned`), so they are settable only at creation or through the API — [[F2-278]]'s
  frozen-field shape, and offering them is a product change.

## F2-290 — three artefacts answered "is this case still open?", and the one that emits a board pack was the narrowest of the three

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`d7362902`) |
| **Severity** | P2 — the misconduct / whistleblowing caseload was reported as **10 open where 26 are open**, on the analytics panel and in the board-pack PDF and PPTX. Live, not latent, and identical in dev and prod |
| **Register** | `ethics.cases` (30 live rows, byte-identical in dev and prod) |
| **Standards** | NAZAHA, the Saudi Whistleblower Protection Law, SAMA AML/CFT for the financial-crime categories; the figure is rendered into the board pack a board reads |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-289]]'s filing of *"the rest of the `ethics` schema's unconstrained columns"* and re-deriving it first ([[F2-221]]) — which **refuted the filing's framing** and pointed one level up, at the readers |
| **Verification** | live probe **11/11 pre-fix · 13/13 post-fix** as `auditor` and `compliance`, never `admin`; gate control **6 of 11 legs discriminate**, the other 5 named as pins and measurements ([[F2-225]]); mutation harness **12 killed / 0 survived / 0 anchor-miss**, each by the leg named for it; backend **4567 → 4583 / 0 / 0**, frontend 818/818, `tsc` clean |

### The defect

Three artefacts answered whether an ethics case is still open. No two agreed. Measured
2026-08-23, identically in dev and the deployed database — 30 live cases, 4 terminal, so **26
open**:

| reader | predicate | answer |
|---|---|---|
| `EthicsPage` (the client) | complement of `{CLOSED, DISMISSED}` | **26** ← the only correct one |
| `EthicsCaseService.analytics()` | inclusion list of **five** open states | **10** |
| `BoardPackAggregateService.ethics()` | inclusion list of **three** | **10** ← **emits a document** |

The third is printed by `BoardPackService` into the board-pack **PDF** and by
`BoardPackPptxService` into the **PPTX**, in both languages, as `"Cases: 30 · Open 10 · …"`. So the
register screen showed 26 open beside a board pack reporting 10, for the same tenant, at the same
moment.

The two server answers coincide **only because `REMEDIATION` and `ESCALATED` hold no rows today**,
so their disagreement with each other is latent while the understatement is live. Say which is
which ([[F2-283]]).

### 🔑🔑 The client was right and the server was wrong, twice

[[F2-205]]'s question — *"how many things read this status, and **which of them is the server?**"* —
with the answer **inverted**. There the server was authoritative and five clients had drifted;
here the two server readers were the drifted ones, and the narrowest of the three is the one whose
figure **leaves the platform**. 🔑 **"Which of them is the server?" is a question about
authority, not about correctness — and this register is the counter-example that stops the two being
conflated.**

### 🔑 Why an inclusion list is the defect and not a style

`ethics.cases` has **no CHECK constraint** on `status`, and it holds `INVESTIGATING` (8 rows) and
`TRIAGED` (3) — near-synonyms of two declared states — so **11 of 30 rows were invisible to every
bucket**. An inclusion list silently drops every token nobody remembered; the complement of a
declared terminal set counts it as open, so it is **chased rather than excused**, which for a
misconduct caseload is the safe direction: under-reporting the open caseload is the finding an
examiner writes up. [[F2-196]]'s rule, unapplied at three sites in a module [[F2-289]] had just
worked in.

Same shape one column over: `byCategory` looped a 13-token list while the register holds 17
categories, so `AML` (2), `POLICY_BREACH`, `GIFTS_HOSPITALITY`, `ABUSE_OF_OFFICE` and
`DATA_PRIVACY` — **6 of 30 rows** — were in no bucket and in no dropdown.

### ⚠⚠ The derivation had to read edge-emptiness, not key-absence

`EthicsCaseLifecycle.TERMINAL` is derived from `ALLOWED` as *the states with no outgoing edges*.
[[F2-196]]'s `DsrCaseLifecycle` derives it as *mentioned minus keys*, which is correct **there**
because that machine omits its terminal states from the map entirely. This machine gives them an
explicit empty entry — so **the same reading returns an EMPTY terminal set here, and an empty
terminal set makes every case open and `closed` permanently zero**.

🔑 **Copying a derivation copies its convention.** The wrong reading fails in the reassuring
direction (a bigger "open" number on a register where bigger was the correction), so
`theDerivationReadsEdgeEmptinessNotKeyAbsence` asserts the counter-factual explicitly: the
key-absence answer **must** be empty on this machine, and edge-emptiness **must** still find both
states. A negative control that does not actually break the thing proves nothing ([[F2-197]]).

### ⚠ Where the predicate lives — and the two recorded rules that pull against each other

The obvious placement is `EthicsCaseLifecycle` imported by `module/reporting`, which is an ADR-002
inversion `ModuleGraphRatchetTest` refuses. [[F2-196]] established the answer: put it behind a
**repository default method** the out-of-module caller already imports, because a caller that
cannot name a status cannot invent its own idea of open. But [[F2-282]] established the opposite
hazard — **a Mockito mock does not execute default methods**, so a decision on one is a decision
every mocking test silently loses.

🔑 **The reconciliation is the split, and it is worth stating because the two rules read as
contradictory:** the **decision** (which states are terminal) is a pure static, so it is mock-immune
and unit-tested; the **query** (count the rows not in that set) is the repository default, because
it must touch the database and holds no judgement — it names the constant and delegates. Checked
rather than assumed: no existing test mocks `EthicsCaseRepository` and calls `analytics()`, so
nothing was already silently asserting a mock.

### ⚠ What was deliberately NOT changed

* **`substantiated`** stays a two-token status sum. That is a narrower question, not a restatement
  ([[F2-250]]) — a case in REMEDIATION is still a substantiated one. `outcome` was checked as a
  durable alternative and **refuted**: it holds the *remediation* result (`POLICY_UPDATE`, 1 of 30
  rows), not a verdict, so there is no column to count instead and inventing one to make the figure
  stable would be [[F2-196]]'s own defect. Consequence stated rather than glossed: the count falls
  when a substantiated case is closed.
* **The client's tile**, which was the correct reader. It is now **pinned**, because a later slice
  reconciling three figures would align it *downward* — the two server readers were the lower ones.
* **The board pack's `amlSuspicion`** stays `AML_SUSPICION` only, reporting 1 where 3 rows are
  AML-categorised. Treating `AML` as a synonym is a semantic judgement about a customer's register.
* **No migration.** Adding a CHECK to either column would refuse the 11 + 6 rows that already
  exist ([[F2-183]]), and one admitting both spellings would *bless* the synonyms.
* **The 11 stuck rows stay stuck**, and `EthicsCaseLifecycleTest` asserts it, so nobody reads this
  disclosure as having closed [[F2-221]]'s finding. They are now **counted and surfaced**, which is
  what lets an owner see the population the decision is about.

### ⚠ My own errors, all caught by running something

* **My harness reported "THE CONTROL DID NOT FIRE — the gate is vacuous" while six legs were
  failing.** The failure-name regex was guessed rather than read off surefire's real output, and the
  harness's own message then accused the gate. 🔑 **A harness that cannot read its own output reads
  exactly like a broken gate** ([[F2-257]]'s shape, in the instrument rather than the gate). Dump
  the log and derive the names from it.
* **My revert guard fired on correct code**: it asserted `countOpen` was absent from master's
  `BoardPackAggregateService`, and master contains `findingRepo.countOpenByOrganisationId` — an
  audit-findings method for a different register. 🔑 **A guard whose token also occurs innocently
  rejects the fix and leaves the defect** ([[F2-267]], verbatim, in a revert script).
* **The `mvn` launcher path**: guessed as `C:\Sources\…` where it is on **D:**. Recorded by
  [[F2-288]] and repeated anyway.
* **The escape-collapse landmine on an inline `py -c` inside Bash** — a Windows path's backslashes
  collapsed into a `SyntaxError`. The rule is recorded and names heredocs; **it applies to any inline
  script carrying escapes**, and the remedy is the Write tool.
* **Both new files landed LF in a CRLF tree** and git warned it would convert them, which would mean
  the bytes the gate was verified against are not the bytes that ship. Normalised before merge;
  fifth instance of the line-ending trap in this lineage.

### ⚙ Filed

* **The 11 `INVESTIGATING` / `TRIAGED` rows and the 6 out-of-taxonomy categories** — near-synonyms
  of declared values, so collapsing them rewrites live rows in two real databases. **Owner
  decision** ([[F2-183]]/[[F2-196]]/[[F2-203]]). Now measured and disclosed on screen rather than
  inferred from a total that does not add up.
* **`ethics.cases` has zero CHECK constraints** over 8 stored statuses, 17 categories and 13 intake
  channels — and the schema is otherwise well constrained (**17 CHECKs**, including a
  CHECK-constrained `status` vocabulary on `whistleblower_case`, *the same concept*). So this is
  [[F2-196]]'s two-registers-for-one-concept shape with the constrained half being the one the UI
  does **not** drive, and [[F2-289]]'s filing understated it by saying "the rest of the schema's
  unconstrained columns" when most of the schema is constrained.
* **`intake_channel` holds 9 values the dropdown does not offer** (`PORTAL`, `HR_DIRECT`,
  `WHISTLEBLOWER_HOTLINE`, `ACCOUNTING_REVIEW`, `ANALYTICS`, `SCREENING`,
  `TRANSACTION_MONITORING`, `INTERNAL_AUDIT`, `MANAGER_REPORT`) and the dropdown offers **12**
  the register has never stored. ⚠ **Corrected by [[F2-291]], which re-derived this before
  executing it ([[F2-221]]):** this said *"the dropdown offers 6 the register has never
  stored"*. `CHANNEL_OPTIONS` declares **16** values and the register stores **13**; they
  intersect in **4** (`HOTLINE`, `EMAIL`, `IN_PERSON`, `WEB_FORM`, 17 of 30 rows), so the 9
  stored-and-not-offered stands and the other side is 12. The register cell also renders the
  raw token through `.replace(/_/g, ' ')`, so those 9 appear as unlabelled English words on
  an Arabic-primary UI (house rule 7). Nothing counts that column, so it is display-only today —
  [[F2-180]]'s shape in both directions.
* **`substantiated` is not stable across the lifecycle** — the figure falls when a substantiated
  case is closed, and recording the verdict durably needs a column. **Owner decision.**
* **The board pack's `amlSuspicion` / `briberyOrKickback` / `retaliation`** are three more
  category-token selections; they are legitimate narrower questions, and the AML one under-reports
  by two thirds for the synonym reason above.
* `mockEthics.ts`'s `ETHICS_ANALYTICS` corpus buckets `OUTCOME`, `BRIBERY_KICKBACK`,
  `HARASSMENT_DISCRIMINATION` and `IP_DATA_THEFT` — **tokens the server can never produce**. A
  `Record<string, number>` admits any key, so [[F2-211]]'s corpus gate cannot see it by
  construction.

## F2-289 — the decider was recorded on TWO of one switch's THREE decision branches, and the comment explaining it was duplicated in the two that had it

| | |
|---|---|
| **Status** | ✅ CLOSED 2026-08-23 (`6ae807c6`) |
| **Severity** | P2 — an AML alert could be escalated as a confirmed true positive and closed with no decider recorded anywhere, permanently. Latent (0 `ESCALATED` rows) and reachable from the platform's own screen (3 `INVESTIGATING` alerts in both databases) |
| **Register** | `ethics.aml_alerts` (10 rows, byte-identical in dev and prod) |
| **Standards** | SAMA AML/CFT Rules, FATF R.20 (STR reporting), Saudi FIU |
| **Found by** | executing [[F2-288]]'s filing of *"the `ethics` schema's remaining unconstrained columns, sharpest being `aml_alerts.disposition`"*, and then reading the method the filing pointed at rather than only the line it named |
| **Verification** | live probe **16/16 pre-fix · 16/16 post-fix** on a freshly restarted listener, **6 of 16 legs discriminating**; gate control **21 of 32 legs fire** across four classes; mutation harness **2/2 killed**; backend **4544 → 4567 / 0 / 0** |

### The defect

`AmlAlertService#transition` stamped `decidedByName` and `decidedAt` in **two of its three**
decision branches. `ESCALATED` — which records a `TRUE_POSITIVE` disposition, i.e. the analyst's
conclusion that a monitored transaction is genuinely suspicious, and the referral an MLRO acts on
— stamped neither. `ESCALATED → CLOSED` is a declared edge and the `CLOSED` branch keeps decision
metadata as-is, so the absence was **preserved rather than corrected**: escalate and close, and the
alert is shut as a confirmed true positive with no decider and no route left that could add one.

Probed live as `auditor` (COMPLIANCE:WRITE — the permission on create, update, assign *and*
transition alike, so there is **no escalation** to report: the object-level machine was the only
control on this register and the attribution sat inside it, which is [[F2-219]]'s shape) against
alerts the probe plants itself ([[F2-206]]):

| leg | pre-fix | post-fix |
|---|---|---|
| `INVESTIGATING → ESCALATED` | 200, disposition `TRUE_POSITIVE` | 200, disposition `TRUE_POSITIVE` |
| ↳ the decider | **`NULL`** | `auditor` |
| ↳ the decision timestamp | **`NULL`** | stamped |
| **then `→ CLOSED`** | **closed, `TRUE_POSITIVE`, decider still `NULL`** | closed, decider preserved |
| `→ CLEARED` (sibling branch) | decider `auditor` | decider `auditor` |
| `→ STR_FILED` (sibling branch) | decider `auditor` | decider `auditor` |
| `disposition: "PROBABLY_FINE"` | **200, stored verbatim** | 400 naming the field |
| `disposition: "true_positive"` | **200, stored verbatim** | 200, stored `TRUE_POSITIVE` |
| `PUT {"severity": "SEVERE"}` | **200, stored** | 400 naming the field |

🔑 **The two sibling rows are the finding as much as the first three are.** One probe run, one
persona, three branches of one switch: two stamped the decider and the third did not.

### 🔑🔑 Repetition reads as a rule

The five-line comment explaining the attribution was **byte-identical** in `CLEARED` and
`STR_FILED`, and the gap sat between them — so a reader scrolling the switch met the mechanism
twice and its absence once. Worse, the duplicated comment's own worked example was *"the STR filed
with the Saudi FIU could be attributed to the empty string"*, i.e. **one of the two branches it
appeared in**, so its subject reinforced exactly the coverage it did not have.

[[F2-215]]'s two-of-N, sharpened: **a comment duplicated across the branches that have a mechanism
is stronger evidence of coverage than one stated once.** A single explanatory comment invites the
question *"does this apply elsewhere?"*; two identical ones answer it.

### 🔑 And F2-223 wrote the comment

[[F2-223]] is the slice that introduced the attribution — to two of the three branches, with the
comment naming itself in both. That is [[F2-287]]'s headline again: **the slice that establishes a
rule is the worst-placed slice to apply it to its own leftovers**, because the branch it did not
touch is the one its new comment makes look finished. The frontend carries the same shape: the
handler's comment says *"the decision-maker is NOT asked for. The server records the authenticated
principal (AmlAlertService#transition)"* — a claim about the server that was true for two of the
three branches the same function drives ([[F2-184]]).

### Latent, and that is stated rather than implied

0 rows are `ESCALATED`; both rows carrying a disposition also carry a decider. Identical in dev and
prod. The Escalate control is offered on the register for every `INVESTIGATING` alert and **three
real alerts are in that state in both databases**, so it is reachable from the platform's own screen
today — a fact about today, not a property of the control ([[F2-182]]). Per [[F2-283]]: **this is a
latent-hazard closure, not a defect discovery**, and reporting it as the latter is the error this
register keeps warning about.

### The fix

One private `recordDisposition(alert, body, fallback)` is the **sole writer** of the four-column
tuple — disposition, notes, decider, clock — reached by all three branches ([[F2-245]]: the claim
that prevents drift is about *where* the writes live).

- **`requireUsername`, never `username()`.** The method stamps the clock from the server, which is
  the service declaring that *it* is the recorder of the act, so a blank name beside a real
  timestamp would read as an attribution ([[F2-236]], whose javadoc states exactly this rule).
- **All four move together, latest decision wins.** `STR_FILED` used to preserve an existing
  `decidedAt` while overwriting `decidedByName` unconditionally — [[F2-223]]'s split waiting for a
  second decision (name from decision 2, clock from decision 1). `ESCALATED → STR_FILED` is the only
  two-disposition path the machine allows, and because `ESCALATED` wrote no clock the old
  conditional always fired: **behaviour-identical on every reachable path today, and the split
  removed.** Nothing is lost — `str_filed_at` records when the STR was filed.
- **`require` not `coerce`** ([[F2-182]]'s third case, as [[F2-288]] stated it): no coercion exists
  upstream *and* the column had no CHECK, so out-of-vocabulary values genuinely succeeded — but
  every stored value is already a member, so nothing that works today starts failing, and an
  unrecognised AML disposition does not degrade gracefully, it becomes a conclusion the register
  cannot report.
- **A caller may still choose within the vocabulary.** Escalating an alert the analyst believes is a
  false positive — for a second opinion — is a real thing; whether it should be refused is a product
  question about AML practice, not a side effect of an attribution fix. The boundary is pinned in
  both directions so the next reader has to decide it deliberately.

### What else the same commit closed, because F2-183 ties a constraint to its writer

| column | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `disposition` | `body.get("disposition").toString()` at **three** sites, table had **zero** CHECKs | one writer, `ClosedVocabulary.require`, `CK_aml_alerts_disposition` |
| `severity` | copied straight out of an entity-bound PUT | `SEVERITY.require`, `CK_aml_alerts_severity` |
| `status` | four writers, **all already closed** before this slice | `CK_aml_alerts_status`, mirrored against `TRANSITIONS` |
| `analytics()` | two **typed inclusion lists** — a third and fourth copy of vocabularies this file declares | derived from `TRANSITIONS.keySet()` and `SEVERITY.tokens()` |
| `alert_type` | open | **still open, and asserted as a decision** |

`alert_type` is the [[F2-183]] `consumer.complaint.subcategory` precedent: 10 distinct values are
stored and **no vocabulary for it is declared anywhere in either codebase** — no reader's inclusion
list, no dropdown, no CHECK — so constraining it would mean inventing one. Recorded as a decision
rather than left as an absence.

V393 measured both databases first (10 rows each, 0 violations, 0 non-canonical casings), so no
`WITH NOCHECK` and no casing UPDATE; applied twice to dev; four self-checks that `THROW`, including
the mirror of the pre-flight — *every token the service can write must still be admitted*.

### ⚠ The gate could not see this register at all, and the narrowing was a Java type

`StateMachineColumnMirrorTest.constantValue` cast the vocabulary constant to `Set<String>`. A
machine that declares its states as `Map<String, Set<String>>` — i.e. **with their edges, the more
precise form** — was therefore structurally excluded from `MIRRORED`: not a smaller answer, a
`ClassCastException`. **So the more precisely a machine declared itself, the less that gate could
check it.** [[F2-198]]'s shape inside the gate, where the narrowing is neither a filename nor an
allow-list nor a module name but the Java type the resolver happens to cast to.

`AmlAlert#status` is the first Map-shaped entry in that bucket, and
`theResolverHandlesAMapShapedMachineAndSomethingActuallyUsesIt` asserts the widening is
load-bearing — [[F2-248]]'s rule, where deleting a token SURVIVED because the anti-vacuity list had
not grown with the vocabulary. `BASELINE_UNCONSTRAINED` **5 → 4**, re-derived from the map's own
size rather than subtracted ([[F2-207]]), and lowered in the same commit as the sweep.

⚙ [[F2-221]]'s own entry for this register said it was left unconstrained *"because the create path
was not read in this slice — F2-183 ties the constraint to the writer."* That was an accurate,
honest reason, and the shape was never the stated obstacle **because nothing had tried**. Reading
the create path is what surfaced the attribution gap; the constraint was the by-product.

### ⚠ Two of my own gate legs failed on correct code, both scans wider than their claim

- The analytics leg banned the literal `"INVESTIGATING"` anywhere in `analytics()` and fired on
  `openAlerts = getOrDefault("OPEN") + getOrDefault("INVESTIGATING")` — a deliberately **narrower**
  question than the machine's non-terminal complement (*"awaiting disposition"*, not *"not
  closed"*), which [[F2-250]] had already recorded on this very service.
- The frontend leg compared `EthicsPage`'s `disposition:` literals against this register's
  vocabulary **file-wide**, and fired on the screening-hit draft further down the same component —
  whose vocabulary (`NEEDS_REVIEW`/`TRUE_MATCH`) belongs to the sibling register. That is
  [[F2-288]]'s two-registers-one-word finding, in one file, and a file-scoped scan therefore
  compares one register's literals against the other register's CHECK and reports a defect that is
  not there.

🔑 **A gate that fails on correct code trains the next reader to edit the assertion rather than the
code** ([[F2-214]]), and both were caught by *running* it. Scope a scan to the shape of its claim
([[F2-192]]) — third and fourth instance in two slices.

### ⚠ A behavioural leg that could not see the defect it is named for

The mutation harness's first run killed the `decidedAt`-preservation mutation with the **structural**
leg only: `aSecondDecisionMovesBothHalves` asserted `isAfterOrEqualTo(firstClock)`, which a
**preserved** clock satisfies. 🔑 **A leg whose name claims more than its assertion can see is the
family this register keeps catching** ([[F2-159]], [[F2-279]]) — and only the harness could tell,
because on the fixed tree it passes either way. Now compared against a reading taken *between* the
two decisions. 2/2 killed after.

### ⚠ Measured and deliberately NOT done

`KycService#disposition` — the sibling AML register, same package, same concept — hand-rolls the
same *"no principal to record"* refusal instead of calling `CurrentActor.requireUsername`. That is
[[F2-190]]'s shape, and converting it was measured rather than assumed: **21 sites use the
primitive and there is a substantial population of hand-rolled refusals with bespoke messages**
across `approvals`, `audit_lc`, `bcm`, `board_pack`, `capa`, `change_mgmt`, `compliance` and
`cyber_lc`. Converting one arbitrary member would invent a rule that only one file follows, so the
population is filed and nothing was changed ([[F2-278]]: sometimes the right answer is *measure it
and do not make it*).

### Filed

- **`ethics.cases.status`** — [[F2-221]]'s finding, re-confirmed live: **11 of 30 rows** hold
  `INVESTIGATING` or `TRIAGED`, which are not keys of that register's machine, so those cases cannot
  be advanced by any route. Near-synonyms of real keys, so collapsing them rewrites live rows in two
  databases — **owner decision**.
- **The remaining unconstrained `ethics` columns**: `cases` (8 status values, 17 categories, 13
  intake channels — all with **zero** CHECKs), `disclosures` (4 statuses, 8 types, 2 decisions),
  `case_actions.action_type`, `case_links.entity_type`/`link_type`, `coi_recusal_event`. Each needs
  its writers read first.
- **`aml_alerts.alert_type`**, above — closing it means declaring the vocabulary *with the owner*.
- **The hand-rolled-refusal population**, above.
- **Two screening registers for one concept** ([[F2-288]]'s filing, unchanged and now sharper: this
  slice declared `aml_alerts`' own two-token vocabulary and deliberately did **not** reconcile it
  with `screening_hits`' four, because that changes what the platform reports to the Saudi FIU) —
  **owner decision**.
- **`str_filed = true` with a caller-supplied `FALSE_POSITIVE`** is storable: an STR filed with the
  FIU while the alert records no suspicion. The frontend cannot produce it; a machine caller can.
  Whether that combination should be refused is AML practice — **owner decision**.
